• Root directory: "/" in Unix, "C:\" in Windows.
• All directories branch from root.
• Path starts from root (absolute path).

q: What is the primary advantage of using a virtual file system (VFS) layer within an operating system?
o: To directly manage the physical storage devices
To handle the low-level details of file storage and retrieval for a single file system
To optimise disk access speeds for specific file system types
To provide a consistent interface for applications to access different file systems
exp:
A Virtual File System gives applications one consistent interface to access different file systems (NTFS, FAT, ext4, network drives) without knowing their details.
★ Exam Points:
• VFS is used in Linux and Unix.
• It abstracts physical storage differences.
• Applications use the same open/read/write calls.

q: What is the primary advantage of using a Directory Acyclic Graph (DAG) structure for file systems compared to a simple tree structure?
o: DAGs enable the creation of hard links, allowing a single file to have multiple directory entries.
DAGs inherently provide better data security and access control.
DAGs allow for faster traversal and searching of files.
DAGs reduce disk fragmentation and improve storage efficiency.
exp:
A directed acyclic graph allows one file or directory to appear in several places through links, which a simple tree cannot.
★ Exam Points:
• DAG file systems allow shared files/sub-directories via links.
• Tree structure gives each file one path.
• Hard links point to the same data.

q: Which of the following scheduling algorithms is most prone to convoy effect, where a long-running process blocks shorter processes behind it?
exp:
The convoy effect occurs in First-Come, First-Served scheduling, when one long process holds the CPU and shorter processes wait behind it.
★ Exam Points:
• Convoy effect: short processes wait behind a long one in FCFS.
• SJF minimises average waiting time.
• Round Robin uses a time quantum (time-sharing).

q: In most Unix-based operating systems, which command is used to create an empty file if the file does not already exist?
exp:
The touch command creates an empty file if it does not exist (and updates timestamps otherwise).
★ Exam Points:
• touch creates empty file / updates timestamp.
• mkdir creates directory.
• cp copies files.

q: In the context of file systems, what is the primary purpose of a file system 'metadata'?
o: To optimise the physical storage of file data on the storage device for faster access
To define the graphical representation of files and folders for the user
To store the actual content and data of the files
To record information about the files and directories, such as their names, sizes, timestamps and permissions
exp:
File system metadata stores information about files (name, size, timestamps, permissions), not the content.
★ Exam Points:
• Metadata: name, size, type, timestamps, permissions, owner.
• Stored in inodes (Unix) or MFT (NTFS).
• Content is stored in data blocks.

q: Consider a hierarchical file system. If a user attempts to delete a non-empty directory using a standard 'delete directory' command without any recursive options, what is the most likely outcome?
o: The operating system will automatically delete all files and subdirectories within it.
The operating system will prompt the user for confirmation to delete each item within the directory.
Only the directory structure will be removed, leaving the files and subdirectories orphaned.
The operating system will return an error indicating that the directory is not empty.
exp:
The OS refuses with an error such as "Directory not empty"; a recursive option (rm -r, rmdir /s) is needed to delete it with its contents.
★ Exam Points:
• Linux: rmdir works only on empty directories.
• rm -r deletes recursively.
• Windows: rmdir /s.

q: Which of the following is an example of an operating system commonly used on desktop computers?
exp:
Windows 10 is a desktop operating system; Word, Photoshop and Chrome are application programs.
★ Exam Points:
• Desktop OS: Windows, macOS, Linux.
• Mobile OS: Android, iOS.
• Word, Photoshop, Chrome are applications.

q: Which of the following best encapsulates the role of an operating system's kernel?
o: Providing the graphical user interface for user interaction
Acting as the core interface between applications and the system hardware
Managing user accounts and access permissions
Offering a suite of utility programs for file management and system configuration
exp:
The kernel is the core of the OS and acts as the interface between applications and hardware, managing memory, processes and devices.
★ Exam Points:
• Kernel manages CPU, memory and devices.
• Shell is the user interface layer.
• Linux kernel created by Linus Torvalds (1991).

q: What is the primary function of an operating system in a laptop?
o: To manage hardware and software resources
exp:
An operating system manages hardware and software resources of the computer.
★ Exam Points:
• OS functions: process, memory, file, device management, security.
• OS provides a user interface.
• Without an OS, applications cannot run.

q: What is the function of Alt + F2 in the Linux GNOME desktop environment?
o: Toggles between full-screen and windowed mode
Opens the Run Command dialog box
exp:
Alt + F2 opens the Run Command dialog in GNOME.
★ Exam Points:
• GNOME is a Linux desktop environment.
• Alt + F2 – Run command.
• Super key opens Activities overview.

q: A game installed on your computer belongs to:
exp:
A game is application software.
★ Exam Points:
• Games are application software.
• Device drivers are system software.
• Game engines include Unity, Unreal.

q: The development of high-level programming languages such as FORTRAN and COBOL changed computer use in which significant way?
o: It forced all programmers to use binary numbers only.
It allowed programs to be written in more human- readable forms, making complex software easier to develop.
It eliminated the need for compilers.
It made computers work only for scientific calculations.
exp:
High-level languages like FORTRAN and COBOL let programs be written in human-readable form, replacing machine code.
★ Exam Points:
• FORTRAN (1957, IBM, John Backus) – scientific use.
• COBOL (1959, Grace Hopper's influence) – business use.
• HLLs are portable and easy to learn.

q: A certain software component is critical for memory management and process scheduling, allowing multiple programs to run concurrently, and it is the first program loaded by the boot process. It generally operates in a privileged mode (kernel mode). Based on this description, which category of software does this component belong to?
exp:
The OS is system software: it handles memory and process scheduling and is the first program loaded at boot.
★ Exam Points:
• OS is the first program loaded at boot (after BIOS).
• OS handles memory management and process scheduling.
• Kernel stays in memory while computer runs.

q: Which of the following tasks is exclusive to the role of System Software and cannot be performed by an Application Software program?
o: Managing data storage and retrieval on a hard disk drive.
Executing a pre-written script to automate a series of repetitive tasks.
Accepting user input from a keyboard and displaying output on a monitor.
Allocating a specific block of the CPUs processing time to a newly launched program.
exp:
Allocating CPU time to a new program is an operating-system (system software) task that application programs cannot do.
★ Exam Points:
• CPU time allocation is done by the OS scheduler.
• Applications request resources from the OS.
• Only the kernel has full hardware access.

q: Which of the following statements correctly highlights the primary difference between System Software and Application Software?
o: Application software is required to start the computer, whereas system software is used only after the computer has fully booted up.
System software is always free and open- source, but application software must always be purchased with a license.
System software manages the computers core resources and provides a platform for other programs, while application software is designed to perform specific tasks for the user.
System software is developed by large companies, while application software is developed only by individual programmers.
exp:
System software manages the computer's core resources and provides a platform, while application software performs specific tasks for the user.
★ Exam Points:
• OS is needed to start the computer.
• System software can be proprietary or open source.
• Applications run on top of system software.

q: Which function is primarily handled by system software in a computer system?
o: Coordinating hardware and running core system processes
exp:
System software coordinates the hardware and runs core system processes.
★ Exam Points:
• System software coordinates hardware.
• Applications handle user documents and media.
• Background services are part of OS.

q: Which software helps in maintaining and optimizing the system e.g., disk cleanup?
exp:
Utility software, such as disk cleanup, maintains and optimises the system.
★ Exam Points:
• Utility software maintains and optimises.
• Examples: antivirus, file compression, backup.
• Firmware is embedded in hardware.

q: Which user interface requires users to type instructions using the keyboard to perform tasks?
exp:
A Command-based (Command Line/Character User) Interface requires users to type commands using the keyboard.
★ Exam Points:
• Example: MS-DOS, Linux terminal.
• GUI uses icons and mouse.
• CLI needs memorising commands.

q: Which one of the following best describes system software? .
o: Software that manages hardware and provides platform for application software
exp:
System software manages hardware and provides a platform for application software.
★ Exam Points:
• System software manages hardware and supports applications.
• Examples: OS, drivers, utilities.
• Application software is user-oriented.

q: Programs like MS Word, MS Excel, and PowerPoint fall into which group?
exp:
MS Word, Excel and PowerPoint are application software.
★ Exam Points:
• MS Office applications are application software.
• Office suite launched in 1990.
• Booting programs are system software.

q: Which of the following correctly describes the role of the Windows operating system?
exp:
The Windows operating system manages files and folders (along with hardware and memory).
★ Exam Points:
• OS manages files, memory, processes and devices.
• Windows is by Microsoft (first version 1985).
• Editing audio needs application software.

q: A disk defragmenter rearranges file fragments on a hard drive for faster access. Why is this tool classified as system software rather than application software?
o: It only works on removable media.
It is always visible to the user.
It requires Internet access to run.
It primarily maintains and optimizes storage resources, not domain tasks like writing letters.
exp:
A defragmenter is a utility (system software) because it maintains and optimises the computer's storage resources rather than performing a user task.
★ Exam Points:
• Defragmentation is not needed for SSDs.
• Windows: "Defragment and Optimize Drives".
• Fragmentation slows HDD access.

q: A computer lab server handles login requests from many students at the same time without confusion. Which characteristic does this scenario mainly highlight?
exp:
Handling many users' logins at once without confusion shows multitasking and reliability.
★ Exam Points:
• Multitasking = running many tasks/users at once.
• Servers use multi-user operating systems.
• Reliability = consistent, error-free operation.

q: Which of the following is not an application software?
exp:
An operating system is system software, not application software.
★ Exam Points:
• OS is system software.
• Publisher, Excel, Photoshop are applications.
• Photoshop is by Adobe.

q: 1. Application Software depends on System Software like the OS to be loaded and access hardware. 2. The failure of one application always causes the OS to crash.
exp:
Application software depends on system software for loading and hardware access, so (i) is true; one application crash does not always crash the OS, so (ii) is false.
★ Exam Points:
• Applications depend on the OS.
• Modern OS isolates apps, so one app crashing doesn't crash the OS.
• Protected memory prevents interference.

q: computers core resources and provides a platform for other programs, while application software is designed to perform specific tasks for the user. A web browser such as Chrome is used to access the internet. This makes it a/an:
exp:
A web browser such as Chrome is application software, used for a specific user task.
★ Exam Points:
• Browsers are application software.
• System software manages core resources.
• Chrome is developed by Google.

q: Which of the following is the main function of system software?
o: To manage computer hardware and run applications.
exp:
System software manages the computer hardware and provides a platform to run applications.
★ Exam Points:
• System software runs the hardware and provides a platform.
• Application software performs specific user tasks.
• OS is the most important system software.

q: In the architecture of the Windows Operating System, which crucial component acts as the bridge between the application programs and the core hardware, operating in a protected mode to manage process scheduling, memory allocation, and interrupt handling?
o: Kernel, which contains the executive services, process manager, and security reference monitor.
Win32 Subsystem, which translates instructions for 32-bit applications and manages display output.
Windows Shell (Explorer), which manages the desktop, taskbar, and file system user interface.
Hardware Abstraction Layer (HAL), which isolates the kernel from platform-specific hardware differences.
exp:
The kernel is the core component that sits between application programs and hardware and runs in privileged mode (the shell only provides the user interface).
★ Exam Points:
• Windows kernel (ntoskrnl.exe) runs in kernel mode.
• HAL isolates hardware differences.
• User mode apps cannot directly access hardware.

q: An image-editing program and a video-editing program both use the same shared library for color correction. Which advantage of modular application software does this situation show?
exp:
Sharing one colour-correction library across two programs shows code reusability in modular software.
★ Exam Points:
• Code reusability via shared libraries (DLLs).
• Modular design simplifies updates.
• Libraries reduce duplication.

q: A device driver acts as an interface between which two components?
exp:
A device driver is the interface between the operating system and the hardware device.
★ Exam Points:
• Driver = OS ↔ hardware interface.
• Printer driver converts data into printer language.
• Drivers are system software.

q: Which of the following is an example of GeneralPurpose Software?
o: Accounting Software made for a company
exp:
LibreOffice Calc is general-purpose software, usable by anyone; the others are made for specific clients.
★ Exam Points:
• General-purpose software: MS Office, LibreOffice, browsers.
• Customised software: payroll for a specific company.
• LibreOffice is free and open source.

q: Which software type helps the operating system to manage hardware and provide services to applications?
exp:
System software (mainly the OS) manages hardware and provides basic services to application programs.
★ Exam Points:
• Examples: Windows, Linux, drivers.
• Utilities are a sub-type of system software.
• Applications rely on system services.

q: Which function of the Operating System deals with allocation of CPU time among different running processes?
exp:
Process management handles CPU time allocation among running processes (scheduling).
★ Exam Points:
• Process management handles CPU scheduling.
• Memory management allocates RAM.
• Device management controls I/O devices.

q: In FIFO scheduling, which process is executed first?
o: The process with the shortest execution time
The process with the highest priority
exp:
FIFO scheduling runs the process that arrived first, like a queue.
★ Exam Points:
• FIFO = First In First Out (same as FCFS).
• Queue data structure follows FIFO.
• Stack follows LIFO.

q: What does GUI stand for in an operating system context?
exp:
GUI stands for Graphical User Interface, which uses icons, windows and menus instead of typed commands.
★ Exam Points:
• GUI uses windows, icons, menus and pointer (WIMP).
• First commercial GUI: Xerox Star (1981); popularised by Apple Macintosh (1984).
• CLI/CUI uses typed commands (MS-DOS).

q: What is the function of device drivers in an operating system?
o: To manage communication between OS and hardware
exp:
A device driver manages communication between the OS and a hardware device.
★ Exam Points:
• Device drivers translate OS commands for hardware.
• Each device needs a specific driver.
• Plug and Play installs drivers automatically.

q: Select the INCORRECT operating system used in computers and laptops.
exp:
Android is primarily a mobile operating system, so it is the incorrect choice for computers and laptops.
★ Exam Points:
• Android is for smartphones and tablets.
• Unix and Linux run on servers and desktops.
• Windows dominates desktop market.

q: Which of the following is an example of an operating system commonly used on laptops?
exp:
Windows 11 is an operating system; the others are applications.
★ Exam Points:
• Windows 11 is a laptop/desktop OS.
• Word, Chrome, Photoshop are applications.
• Linux and macOS are other laptop OSs.

q: Which of the following operating systems is NOT typically used on desktop or laptop computers?
exp:
Android is a mobile OS, not normally used on desktops or laptops.
★ Exam Points:
• Android is a mobile OS by Google (Linux-based).
• Desktop OS: Windows, macOS, Linux.
• ChromeOS runs on Chromebooks.

q: Which type of software manages hardware resources, provides a user interface and allows applications to run?
exp:
The OS manages CPU, memory, storage and devices and provides the platform for applications.
★ Exam Points:
• Examples: Windows, Linux, macOS, Android.
• Kernel is the core of OS.
• BOSS is India's Linux OS.

q: Why do desktop and laptop operating systems require more advanced memory management than embedded systems?
o: Memory management is not necessary for them
They rely on static memory allocation
They run only one application at a time
They use more hardware resources and need dynamic memory allocation
exp:
General-purpose OSs run many programs simultaneously and must allocate and free memory dynamically (paging, virtual memory).
★ Exam Points:
• Embedded systems often use fixed/static allocation.
• Virtual memory uses disk as extra RAM.
• Paging divides memory into fixed-size pages.

q: Which file extension is most commonly used for executable installation files on Windows?
exp:
.exe files are executable programs; installers may also use .msi.
★ Exam Points:
• .jpg – image; .mp3 – audio; .txt – text.
• .bat – batch file.
• .apk – Android package.

q: Which scenario correctly illustrates the interdependence of system software and application software?
o: An antivirus program relying on system utilities to perform disk scans and remove malware
An OS requiring a media player to manage hardware
A word processor working without an operating system
A device driver operating as application software for printing
exp:
Application programs depend on the OS and system utilities to access hardware; the antivirus example shows this.
★ Exam Points:
• System software manages hardware.
• Application software performs user tasks.
• Drivers are system software.

q: In OLE, what handles object linking by maintaining persistent connections to a remote server's CLSID?
exp:
Object Linking and Embedding (OLE) is built directly atop Microsoft's Component Object Model (COM). COM uses a globally unique 128-bit CLSID (Class Identifier) stored in the Windows Registry to locate the server application and maintain persistent object links (and across networks via DCOM).
★ Exam Points:
• In Linking, the destination document stores only a reference/pointer to the source file so changes update dynamically; in Embedding, a standalone copy of the object is stored inside the document.
• CLSID is a 128-bit UUID/GUID identifying a specific COM class in Windows.
• BLOB stores binary database objects, SMTP transfers emails, and AWT is Java's GUI toolkit.

q: What is the full form of SQL?
exp:
SQL – Structured Query Language – is used to create and query relational databases.
★ Exam Points:
• Developed at IBM (1970s) as SEQUEL.
• DML: SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE.
• DDL: CREATE, ALTER, DROP.

q: Text editors and text formatters belong to which category of computing?
exp:
Programs that create, edit and format text documents are word processors.
★ Exam Points:
• Text editor examples: Notepad, Vim.
• Word processor examples: MS-Word, Writer.
• Compilers and interpreters are language translators.

q:
Identify whether the following statements are true or false.
(i) Assembly language is a low-level programming language.
(ii) An interpreter translates each statement into machine code and runs it.
(iii) The output of the assembler is in binary code.
exp:
All three statements are correct: assembly is low-level, an interpreter translates and executes line by line, and an assembler produces binary machine code.
★ Exam Points:
• Assembly uses mnemonics (ADD, MOV).
• Compiler translates the whole program at once.
• Python and BASIC are commonly interpreted.

q:
Identify whether the statements are true or false.
(i) An assembler converts instructions written in low-level assembly code into machine code.
(ii) An assembler converts assembly code into machine code line by line.
(iii) Types of assemblers include one-pass and load-and-go assemblers.
exp:
All three statements are correct as per standard definitions of an assembler.
★ Exam Points:
• Two-pass assemblers are also common.
• Assembler output = object code.
• Disassembler converts machine code back to assembly.

q:
Match the stages of compiler design with their descriptions.
(a) Lexical analysis (b) Syntax analysis (c) Semantic analysis (d) Code generation
(i) Translates the parse tree into machine code (ii) Reads source code character by character and breaks it into tokens (iii) Checks syntax against grammar rules of the language (iv) Checks the meaning of the code (types, declarations)
exp:
Lexical analysis produces tokens; syntax analysis (parsing) builds the parse tree; semantic analysis checks meaning; code generation produces target code.
★ Exam Points:
• Phases: Lexical → Syntax → Semantic → Intermediate code → Optimisation → Code generation.
• Lexical analyser is also called scanner.
• Symbol table is used in all phases.

q: The output of the assembler program is called the ____ relative to the input source program.
exp:
An assembler converts an assembly-language source program into machine-code object program.
★ Exam Points:
• Compiler output is also an object code.
• Linker combines object files into an executable.
• Byte code is produced by the Java compiler (run by JVM).

q: WinZip software is an example of ____ software.
exp:
WinZip is distributed as shareware – free to try for a trial period, after which a licence must be purchased.
★ Exam Points:
• Freeware is free forever but closed source.
• Open source (7-Zip) gives source code freely.
• WinZip creates .zip compressed archives.

q: When a Windows computer is in Sleep mode, which common user action will typically bring the system back to an active state?
exp:
Moving the mouse or pressing a key wakes a computer from sleep.
★ Exam Points:
• Mouse movement or key press wakes from Sleep.
• Power button wakes from Hibernate.
• Wake timers can wake the PC.

q: What is the primary function of the keyboard shortcut Alt + F4 in Windows?
exp:
Alt + F4 closes the active window.
★ Exam Points:
• Alt + F4 closes the active window; on desktop it opens Shut Down dialog.
• Ctrl + W closes a document/tab.
• Windows + D shows desktop.

q: Which of the following wildcards is used for finding the files matching a pattern?
exp:
The asterisk (*) wildcard matches any characters, as in *.txt.
★ Exam Points:
• * matches any number of characters (*.txt).
• ? matches a single character.
• Wildcards are used in search and command line.

q: Under which section can we find the total processor utilization across all cores on a computer?
exp:
Task Manager shows total processor utilisation across all cores.
★ Exam Points:
• Task Manager → Performance tab shows CPU, memory, disk, network.
• Resource Monitor gives detailed usage.
• Logical processors include hyper-threads.

q: In Windows 11, which built-in tool opens immediately when a user presses the keyboard shortcut Ctrl + Shift + Esc?
exp:
Ctrl + Shift + Esc opens Task Manager.
★ Exam Points:
• Ctrl + Shift + Esc – Task Manager directly.
• Ctrl + Alt + Del – security screen.
• Task Manager shows CPU, memory, disk usage.

q: Which is the latest version of Windows?
exp:
Windows 11 is the latest version of Windows among the options.
★ Exam Points:
• Windows 11 released 5 October 2021.
• Windows 10 support ended 14 Oct 2025.
• Windows 11 25H2 released Sept 2025.

q: Which shortcut opens the Properties of the selected item?
exp:
Alt + Enter opens Properties of the selected item.
★ Exam Points:
• Alt + Enter – Properties.
• In Excel, Alt + Enter – new line in cell.
• Alt + double-click also opens Properties.

q: Restarting a computer means:
o: Turning it off and on again automatically
exp:
Restarting turns the computer off and on again automatically.
★ Exam Points:
• Restart = warm boot.
• Shutdown turns the PC off completely.
• Restart applies updates.

q: Which of the following locations stores recently opened files in Windows for quick access?
exp:
Quick Access lists recent files and frequent folders.
★ Exam Points:
• Quick Access shows recent files and pinned folders.
• Windows 11 calls it Home.
• Pin folders for faster access.

q: Maria wants to manage startup programs and services that run automatically when Windows 11 starts. Which Windows utility provides dedicated "Startup" and "Services" task for this purpose?
exp:
MSConfig (System Configuration) has Services and Startup tabs for managing programs and services at start-up.
★ Exam Points:
• MSConfig = System Configuration utility (Run: msconfig).
• Startup apps are now managed in Task Manager.
• Selective startup helps troubleshooting.

q: Which tab in the Windows 11 Task Manager allows a user to change the priority of a running application?'
exp:
In Task Manager's Details tab you can set a process's priority.
★ Exam Points:
• Details tab → right-click → Set priority.
• Priorities: Realtime, High, Above normal, Normal, Below normal, Low.
• Ctrl + Shift + Esc opens Task Manager.

q: Which power mode uses the least electricity while maintaining an open session?
exp:
Sleep uses little power while keeping the session open in RAM.
★ Exam Points:
• Sleep keeps session in RAM with low power.
• Hibernate saves session to disk and powers off.
• Hybrid sleep combines both.

q: What is the primary function of Ctrl + Y in most Windows applications?
exp:
Ctrl + Y redoes the last undone action (or repeats the last action) in most Windows applications.
★ Exam Points:
• Ctrl + Z – undo.
• Ctrl + C – copy.
• Ctrl + V – paste.

q: Which file type is most likely to be classified as a system file in Windows
exp:
.dll (Dynamic Link Library) files are system files in Windows.
★ Exam Points:
• .dll = Dynamic Link Library.
• .sys and .ini are also system files.
• .mp3 audio; .docx Word; .zip archive.

q: Which of the following is correct about Hibernation mode in computers?
exp:
Hibernation uses the least power, as the session is saved to disk and the machine powers off.
★ Exam Points:
• Hibernate saves RAM content to disk (hiberfil.sys).
• Hibernate uses almost zero power.
• Sleep uses low power and resumes faster.

q: Where is Recycle Bin located?
exp:
The Recycle Bin icon is located on the Desktop.
★ Exam Points:
• Recycle Bin icon sits on the desktop.
• It can also be pinned to Quick Access.
• Restore via right-click.

q: What will the following PowerShell command in Windows OS do? Command: Remove-Item C:\Logs -Recurse -Force
o: Delete only empty folders under C:\Logs
Move the C:\Logs folder to the Recycle Bin
Only delete files, leave folders intact
Delete all files and subfolders inside C:\Logs, including the folder itself
exp:
Remove-Item with -Recurse -Force deletes the folder C:\Logs along with all files and subfolders, without prompting.
★ Exam Points:
• Remove-Item deletes files/folders in PowerShell.
• -Recurse includes subfolders; -Force removes hidden/read-only items.
• PowerShell deletions bypass the Recycle Bin.

q: Which of the following methods is the easiest way to sort files by name in File Explorer in Windows 11 OS?
o: Click the Name column header in File Explorer
Drag files into alphabetical order manually
exp:
Clicking the Name column header in File Explorer's Details view is the easiest way to sort files by name.
★ Exam Points:
• Click a column header to sort; click again to reverse.
• Details view shows columns.
• Sort by Name, Date, Type, Size.

q: Which method allows you to create a new text file inside a specific folder in Windows?
o: Open the folder and right-click New Text Document
Press Ctrl + F while in the folder.
Start a new task from Task Manager.
Restore a file from the Recycle Bin.
exp:
Open the folder, right-click an empty area and choose New → Text Document to create a .txt file there.
★ Exam Points:
• Default name: New Text Document.txt.
• Notepad opens .txt files.
• Ctrl + Shift + N creates a folder, not a file.

q: Which statement best explains why removing all desktop icons does NOT impact the functionality of the applications in Windows OS?
o: The desktop is a virtual memory area where applications run in the background.
Desktop icons are system-critical files required to run applications.
Desktop icons are only visual shortcuts and not the actual application files.
Windows OS duplicates all application files in the desktop directory.
exp:
Desktop icons are only visual shortcuts to programs, so removing them does not affect the applications.
★ Exam Points:
• Shortcut icons point to actual program files.
• Deleting a shortcut doesn't uninstall the program.
• Shortcuts have .lnk extension.

q: Which of the following key combinations is used to paste copied content?
exp:
Ctrl + V pastes the copied content.
★ Exam Points:
• Ctrl + V – paste; Ctrl + C – copy; Ctrl + X – cut.
• Ctrl + P – print; Ctrl + K – hyperlink.
• Ctrl + B – bold.

q: Which keyboard shortcut is typically used to paste copied content?
exp:
Ctrl + V pastes copied content.
★ Exam Points:
• Ctrl + V – paste.
• Ctrl + C – copy.
• Ctrl + F – find.

q: Which of the following methods is the simplest way to rename a file or folder in Windows?
o: Double-click the file to open it
Drag the file to the Recycle Bin
exp:
Right-click on the file or folder and select Rename (F2 also works).
★ Exam Points:
• F2 renames the selected item.
• Right-click → Rename.
• Click twice slowly on the name also renames.

q: What is the function of the keyboard shortcut Ctrl + F in Windows OS?
o: It forwards an email message to another recipient.
It checks and corrects spelling errors in text.
It formats content in a document or application.
It opens a search or find feature to locate text or items in files, webpages or applications.
exp:
Ctrl + F opens the Find or Search box.
★ Exam Points:
• Ctrl + F – Find.
• Ctrl + H – Replace (Office).
• F3 – search in Explorer.

q: Which of the following conditions will prevent a file from being renamed in a Windows-based operating system?
o: The file is currently opened in another application.
The file is located in the Recycle Bin.
The file has a long name exceeding 255 characters.
The file has the 'Read-only' attribute enabled.
exp:
A file open in another application is locked and cannot be renamed until it is closed.
★ Exam Points:
• Open files are locked by the application.
• Close the program to rename.
• Read-only files can still be renamed.

q: Which component of Windows OS allows users to modify system settings such as display resolution, sound preferences and user accounts?
exp:
The Control Panel lets users modify system settings such as display, sound and user accounts.
★ Exam Points:
• Control Panel: Display, Sound, User Accounts, Programs.
• Settings app (Windows + I) is the modern equivalent.
• Open via "control" in Run.

q: What is the default name given to a folder on Windows systems?
exp:
Windows names a new folder 'New folder' by default.
★ Exam Points:
• Default new folder name: New folder.
• Second becomes "New folder (2)".
• Rename with F2.

q: Which desktop element in Windows OS allows users to restore deleted files and folders?
exp:
The Recycle Bin allows deleted files and folders to be restored.
★ Exam Points:
• Recycle Bin – restore deleted items.
• Restore puts item back to original location.
• Empty Recycle Bin deletes permanently.

q: In Windows 11, why might you receive an 'Access is denied' error when trying to rename a file?
o: You are renaming from the Recycle Bin.
You are using the wrong drive letter.
exp:
An 'Access is denied' error on renaming usually points to permission or ownership problems on the file.
★ Exam Points:
• Access denied errors relate to permissions/ownership.
• Administrator rights may be needed.
• Take ownership via Properties → Security.

q: Which of the following is the most effective method for organizing files and folders in a computer's operating system?
o: Creating a logical folder structure that reflects the content, using clear, descriptive names
Naming files and folders with random characters to avoid confusion
Renaming folders frequently to prevent them from becoming cluttered
Storing all files and folders in one directory to save space
exp:
Creating a logical folder structure that reflects how the files are used (by project, date or type) is the best way to organise files.
★ Exam Points:
• Use meaningful names.
• Avoid dumping everything on the Desktop.
• Use sub-folders for categories.

q: Which of the following key combinations is primarily used to access the File menu in most legacy and standard Windows applications?
exp:
Alt + F opens the File menu in most Windows applications.
★ Exam Points:
• Alt + F – File menu.
• Alt + E – Edit menu (legacy).
• Alt + H – Home tab in Office.

q: Which of the following actions will create a new folder on a Windows desktop?
o: Clicking on the Recycle Bin icon
Right-clicking on the desktop and selecting 'New' 'Folder'
exp:
Right-clicking the desktop and choosing New then Folder creates a new folder.
★ Exam Points:
• New folder shortcut: Ctrl + Shift + N.
• Right-click → New → Folder.
• Default name: "New folder".

q: Where do deleted files go by default in Windows OS?
exp:
Deleted files go by default to the Recycle Bin.
★ Exam Points:
• Recycle Bin holds deleted files temporarily.
• Default size is a % of drive space.
• Files larger than the bin are deleted permanently.

q: In Windows-based systems, which Alt key combination is most likely to display the contextual control menu of the active window, especially when the title bar is inaccessible?
exp:
Alt + Space displays the control (system) menu of the active window.
★ Exam Points:
• Alt + Space – window control menu (Restore, Move, Size, Minimize, Maximize, Close).
• Alt + F4 – close.
• Alt + F10 / F10 activates menu bar.

q: Which keyboard shortcut opens the Windows 11 OS Settings menu to change system settings?
exp:
Windows key + I opens Settings in Windows 11.
★ Exam Points:
• Windows + I – Settings.
• Windows + S – Search.
• Windows + A – Quick Settings (Win 11).

q: Which of the following actions is performed when the Ctrl + V shortcut is used in most computer applications?
o: Opens the new file creation dialog box
Paste the copied or cut content
exp:
Ctrl + V pastes the copied or cut content.
★ Exam Points:
• Ctrl + V – paste.
• Ctrl + Shift + V – paste without formatting (many apps).
• Windows + V – clipboard history.

q: Which feature in Windows allows you to recover files that were accidentally deleted?
exp:
The Recycle Bin recovers accidentally deleted files.
★ Exam Points:
• Recycle Bin allows restore.
• Disk Cleanup removes junk files.
• File History/backup helps recovery.

q: Which element on the Windows 11 desktop allows users to quickly access multiple open windows and virtual desktops?
exp:
Task View on the Windows 11 taskbar gives quick access to open windows and virtual desktops.
★ Exam Points:
• Task View: Windows + Tab.
• New virtual desktop: Windows + Ctrl + D.
• Switch desktops: Windows + Ctrl + Left/Right.

q: In Windows OS, which of the following actions will permanently delete a file without sending it to the Recycle Bin?
exp:
Shift + Delete bypasses the Recycle Bin and deletes permanently.
★ Exam Points:
• Shift + Delete deletes permanently (asks for confirmation).
• Delete → Recycle Bin.
• Deleted USB files skip Recycle Bin.

q: Which keyboard shortcut opens File Explorer in Windows 11 OS to navigate and create files/folders?
exp:
Windows key + E opens File Explorer.
★ Exam Points:
• Windows + E – File Explorer.
• Ctrl + Shift + N – new folder in Explorer.
• Windows + R – Run.

q: In Windows 10 File Explorer, how can you group files by their type?
o: Use the 'Group by' option and select 'Type'
Rename all files with the same type
Use the 'Sort by' option and select 'Name'
exp:
In File Explorer, 'Group by' with 'Type' groups files by type.
★ Exam Points:
• Group by: Name, Date modified, Type, Size.
• Sort by arranges items in order.
• Views: Details, List, Tiles, Icons.

q: What is the main purpose of the taskbar in the Windows desktop interface?
o: It provides access to open and frequently used programs.
It stores documents and media files.
exp:
The taskbar gives access to open and pinned (frequently used) programs.
★ Exam Points:
• Taskbar shows Start, search, pinned and open apps.
• Notification area is at the right end.
• Taskbar introduced with Windows 95.

q: In the context of file deletion, what is the typical immediate effect of moving a file to the 'Trash' or 'Recycle Bin' in a GUI-based Operating System?
o: The file's data is immediately overwritten and unrecoverable.
The file's metadata (inode or equivalent) is immediately purged from the file system.
The file is compressed and archived before being permanently deleted.
The file is moved to a special directory, and its directory entry is updated, but the data remains on the storage device.
exp:
Moving a file to the Recycle Bin only relocates it; it can be restored until the bin is emptied.

• Recycle Bin is a special hidden folder ($Recycle.Bin).
• Emptying it frees disk space.
• Files remain recoverable until emptied.

q: Which of the following characters is NOT allowed in a filename when renaming in Windows?
exp:
A filename in Windows cannot contain \ / : * ? " < >
★ Exam Points:
• Forbidden in Windows file names: \ / : * ? " < > and the vertical bar.
• Max path length traditionally 260 characters.
• Reserved names: CON, PRN, AUX, NUL.

q: What is the purpose of pressing Alt + Tab on the keyboard of a computer system?
exp:
Alt + Tab switches between open applications.
★ Exam Points:
• Alt + Tab – switch apps.
• Windows + Tab – Task View.
• Alt + F4 – close window.

q: When navigating through options in a dialog box or menu using the keyboard, what is the primary function of the Tab key?
o: To go back to the previous option or control
To close the current dialog box or menu
To move the focus to the next available option or control
To select the currently highlighted option
exp:
The Tab key moves the focus to the next available option or control in a dialog box or form.

• Tab moves forward; Shift + Tab moves backward.
• Enter selects the highlighted button.
• Esc closes/cancels the dialog.

q: What happens when you press the Delete key after selecting a file in File Explorer in Windows OS?
o: The file is sent to the Recycle Bin.
exp:
Pressing Delete on a selected file in File Explorer sends it to the Recycle Bin, from where it can be restored.
★ Exam Points:
• Delete key → Recycle Bin.
• Shift + Delete → permanent deletion.
• Restore from Recycle Bin by right-click → Restore.

q: In Windows 11, what is the purpose of using dir /s /b "syllabus.pdf" inside Command Prompt?
o: To open "syllabus.pdf" using the default PDF viewer
To copy "syllabus.pdf" into a new destination folder
To show the file size and attributes of "report.pdf"
To list full file paths of "syllabus.pdf" from all nested folders

The dir /s /b command searches subdirectories and lists the matching file's full path in bare format.

q: Which key is used to open the Start Menu in Windows 11?
exp:
The Windows key opens the Start menu.
★ Exam Points:
• Windows key opens Start menu.
• Ctrl + Esc also opens Start.
• Windows + X opens Quick Link menu.

q: When using the search term Invoice* in Windows 11 File Explorer, which files will be found?
o: Files that have "Invoice" anywhere in the name
Files that begin with the word "Invoice"
Files that contain exactly the word "Invoice"
Files that end with the word "Invoice"
exp:
The search term Invoice* finds files whose names begin with 'Invoice'.

• Invoice* = begins with "Invoice".
• *Invoice = ends with "Invoice".
• *Invoice* = contains "Invoice".

q: Which power mode is required for systems using Instant-on / Always-Connected experiences in Windows 10 and 11?
exp:
Modern Standby is the low-power mode used for Instant-on and Always-Connected experiences.
★ Exam Points:
• Modern Standby (S0 Low Power Idle) keeps network connected.
• Like a smartphone's standby.
• Traditional sleep is S3.

q: What is the primary purpose of Task Manager in Windows?
o: To monitor and manage running applications, processes and system performance
exp:
Task Manager monitors and manages running applications, processes and performance.
★ Exam Points:
• Task Manager: Ctrl + Shift + Esc.
• Shows Processes, Performance, Startup, Users, Details, Services.
• Can end tasks and set priorities.

q: The bar at the bottom of the Windows screen that shows open applications
exp:
The taskbar at the bottom of the Windows screen shows the Start button, pinned items and all open applications.
★ Exam Points:
• Notification area is at its right end.
• Taskbar can be auto-hidden.
• Pin apps for quick launch.

q: In Windows 11 File Explorer, which feature is used to quickly locate a file by typing its name?
exp:
The search box in File Explorer finds files by typing their name.
★ Exam Points:
• Search box is at the top-right of File Explorer.
• Ctrl + E or F3 focuses it.
• Wildcards * and ? can be used.

q: Which of the following key combinations is used to open the File menu in many applications?
exp:
Alt + F opens the File menu in many applications.
★ Exam Points:
• Alt + F – File menu.
• Alt + E – Edit menu.
• Alt + V – View menu.

q: When a program in Windows appears as "Not Responding" and the user ends it using Task Manager, which action is effectively being requested from the operating system?
o: Convert the program into a service
Move the program to another drive
Force the process to terminate and release its resourcesIT

Ending a non-responding program in Task Manager forces the process to terminate and releases its resources.

• End task forces process termination.
• Unsaved work may be lost.
• Not Responding = app is frozen.

q: A user wants to quickly pause work and resume in few minutes without waiting for the computer to reboot. The best option is:
exp:
Sleep mode pauses work and resumes quickly without a full reboot.

q: A document is saved on the local computer and also synchronised to a cloud service. Later, the local copy is accidentally deleted. Why might the document still be recoverable?

• Centralizing files prevents loss and makes automated data backups more efficient.

q:
Identify whether the statements about Windows XP are true or false.
(i) The taskbar is the blue bar at the bottom of the desktop containing the Start menu and Quick Launch bar.
(ii) The notification area is a portion of the taskbar that provides notifications and status.
(iii) Control Panel is used to configure system-level features.
exp:
All three statements are correct for Windows XP.
★ Exam Points:
• Windows XP was released in 2001.
• Notification area is also called the system tray.
• Quick Launch was removed in Windows 7 (pinning replaced it).

q: Which keyboard shortcut is used to copy content to the clipboard?
exp:
Ctrl + C copies the selected item to the clipboard.
★ Exam Points:
• Ctrl + V pastes; Ctrl + X cuts.
• Ctrl + Insert also copies.
• Windows + V opens clipboard history.

q: A ____ is an image that fills the screen whenever the computer is left idle for some time.
exp:
A screen saver appears after a set idle time; originally it prevented phosphor burn-in on CRT monitors.
★ Exam Points:
• Wallpaper is the desktop background image.
• System tray (notification area) is at the right of the taskbar.
• Screen saver settings are in Personalisation → Lock screen.

q: Which key will launch the Start menu in the Windows operating system?
exp:
Pressing the Windows key (or Ctrl + Esc) opens the Start menu.
★ Exam Points:
• Start menu introduced in Windows 95.
• Windows 8 replaced it with the Start screen; Windows 10 brought it back.
• Windows 11 centres the Start button by default.

q: Which combination of keys is used to undo an action in Windows 10?
exp:
Ctrl + Z undoes the last action in Windows and most applications.
★ Exam Points:
• Ctrl + Y redoes the action.
• Alt + Tab switches between open apps.
• Ctrl + Tab moves between tabs.

q: When you delete an item from a hard drive using the Delete key or right-click → Delete, the file is moved to the ____ in Windows.
exp:
Deleted files go to the Recycle Bin, from where they can be restored until the bin is emptied.
★ Exam Points:
• Shift + Delete deletes permanently, bypassing the Recycle Bin.
• Files deleted from USB drives/network drives skip the Recycle Bin.
• Recycle Bin occupies a % of disk space (configurable).

q: To select adjacent icons on the desktop, you press the ____ key and then click the icons you wish to select.
exp:
Shift + click selects a continuous (adjacent) range; Ctrl + click selects non-adjacent items one by one.
★ Exam Points:
• Ctrl + A selects all items.
• Dragging a selection rectangle also selects adjacent icons.
• Same rule applies in Word, Excel and File Explorer.

q: A student finishes typing a paragraph and wants to make a copy of a sentence to use later in the document. She first selects the sentence. Which shortcut should she press next?
exp:
Ctrl + C copies the selected sentence.
★ Exam Points:
• Select then Ctrl + C to copy.
• Paste later with Ctrl + V.
• Office Clipboard stores 24 items.

q: Which shortcut saves the current file?
exp:
Ctrl + S saves the current file.
★ Exam Points:
• Ctrl + S saves.
• Ctrl + L left align; Ctrl + R right align.
• Ctrl + P print.

q: Which pair of keyboard shortcuts is used to quickly copy and paste text?
exp:
Ctrl + C copies and Ctrl + V pastes.
★ Exam Points:
• Ctrl + X cuts.
• Ctrl + F finds; Ctrl + S saves.
• Ctrl + Tab switches tabs.

q: Which shortcut selects all content in a document?
exp:
Ctrl + A selects all content.
★ Exam Points:
• Ctrl + A – select all.
• Ctrl + E – centre; Ctrl + R – right align.
• Ctrl + S – save.

q: Which keyboard shortcut is used to cut (move) text in MS Word?
exp:
Ctrl + X cuts selected text.
★ Exam Points:
• Ctrl + X – cut; Ctrl + Z – undo.
• Ctrl + V – paste; Ctrl + C – copy.
• Cut text is held on the clipboard.

q: Which of the following is NOT a valid way to move selected text in MS Word?
exp:
Format Painter copies formatting; it does not move text.
★ Exam Points:
• Format Painter copies formatting only.
• Moving: drag-and-drop, Cut + Paste.
• Ctrl + Drag copies text.

q: How can we change the margins of a document in MS Word?
exp:
The Layout tab (Page Layout) has the Margins option.
★ Exam Points:
• Layout tab → Margins.
• Preset: Normal, Narrow, Moderate, Wide, Mirrored.
• Ruler can also adjust margins.

q: What happens when you press 'Enter' while working with a bullet or numbered list in MS Word 365?
o: It converts the list into plain text.
It deletes the previous bullet or number.
It creates a new list item with the same bullet or number.
exp:
Pressing Enter in a list creates a new item with the next bullet or number.
★ Exam Points:
• Enter adds the next list item.
• Pressing Enter twice ends the list.
• Shift + Enter adds a line without a new bullet.

q: What is the primary advantage of using 'Section Breaks' in an MS Word document compared to simply using 'Page Breaks'?
o: Section breaks automatically create a table of contents from headings
Section breaks allow different page formatting (orientation, margins, headers) in different parts, while page breaks only force content to the next page
Section breaks improve the document's security
Section breaks reduce the file size
exp:
Section breaks let different parts of a document have different page formatting (orientation, margins, headers/footers, columns), whereas page breaks only push content to the next page.
★ Exam Points:
• Types: Next Page, Continuous, Even Page, Odd Page.
• Page break: Ctrl + Enter.
• Show breaks with ¶ (Ctrl + Shift + 8).

q: What happens when a user presses the Bullets button (•) in MS Word?
o: The text alignment changes to center
The selected text is converted into a bulleted list
The selected text is converted into a numbered list
exp:
The Bullets button converts selected text into a bulleted list.
★ Exam Points:
• Bullets button creates bulleted list.
• Numbering button creates numbered list.
• Ctrl + Shift + L applies List Bullet style.

q: What is the keyboard shortcut to remove paragraph indentation in MS Word 365?
exp:
Ctrl + Shift + M removes a paragraph indent; Ctrl + M adds one.
★ Exam Points:
• Ctrl + Shift + M – decrease indent.
• Ctrl + M – increase indent.
• Ctrl + T – hanging indent.

q: In MS Word, when a user wants to move a block of text from one part of a document to another, which of the following sequences of actions should be performed?
o: Type the text Save it Retype it at the new location
Copy the text Paste the text at the desired location
Cut the text Paste the text at the desired location
Highlight the text Save it Open it in another document
exp:
Cut the text, then paste at the new location, to move it.
★ Exam Points:
• Cut (Ctrl + X) + Paste (Ctrl + V) moves text.
• Copy + Paste duplicates text.
• Drag-and-drop also moves selected text.

q: Which keyboard shortcut is used to copy selected text in MS Word 365?
exp:
Ctrl + C copies selected text.
★ Exam Points:
• Ctrl + C – copy.
• Ctrl + Insert – copy (alternate).
• Copied text stays on clipboard until replaced.

q: Which feature allows you to create a multi-level numbered list (e.g., 1.1, 1.2) in MS Word 2019?
exp:
Define New Multilevel List creates numbering like 1.1, 1.2.
★ Exam Points:
• Multilevel list: 1, 1.1, 1.1.1.
• Link levels to heading styles.
• Tab/Shift + Tab change levels.

q: How do we customise bullets in MS Word?
exp:
Home, Bullets, then Define New Bullet customises bullets.
★ Exam Points:
• Define New Bullet → Symbol/Picture/Font.
• Bullet colour via Font button.
• Picture bullets can use images.

q: Which of the following scenarios would most effectively necessitate the use of a 'Keep with Next' paragraph formatting option in MS Word?
o: Automatically indenting the first line of every paragraph in a document
Applying a consistent bullet point style to a list of items
Ensuring that a heading and the paragraph immediately following it always appear on the same page
Preventing a long paragraph from being split across multiple pages
exp:
Keep with Next keeps a heading on the same page as the paragraph that follows.
★ Exam Points:
• Keep with Next keeps a heading with the next paragraph.
• Keep lines together prevents splitting a paragraph.
• Page break before forces a new page.

q: Which of the following best describes the function of a 'Section Break (Next Page)' in MS Word?
o: It starts a new paragraph while maintaining the same formatting.
It ends the current section and starts a new section on the subsequent page.
It inserts a manual line break within the same paragraph.
It creates a visual divider between different parts of the document on the same page.
exp:
A Next Page section break ends the current section and starts a new one on the next page.
★ Exam Points:
• Section Break (Next Page) starts a new section on the next page.
• Continuous starts on same page.
• Even/Odd Page start on next even/odd page.

q: In MS Word 365, which feature allows users to set specific spacing before and after paragraphs to control the vertical space between paragraphs and improve document readability?
exp:
Paragraph Spacing sets the space before and after paragraphs.
★ Exam Points:
• Paragraph spacing: Before/After (in points).
• Line spacing is within a paragraph.
• Layout → Spacing controls.

q: In MS Word 2019, which of the following features can you use to change the page orientation of your document?
exp:
Page Layout (or Layout) then Orientation changes the page orientation.
★ Exam Points:
• Layout/Page Layout → Orientation.
• Portrait or Landscape.
• Section breaks allow mixed orientations.

q: In MS Word, if you want to duplicate a selected text without removing it from its original location, which set of commands should you use?
exp:
Copy then Paste duplicates text while leaving the original.
★ Exam Points:
• Copy + Paste duplicates text.
• Cut + Paste moves text.
• Ctrl + drag also copies.

q: Which action best describes the effect of applying bullets or numbering to a selection of text in MS Word?
o: It converts the selected text into a structured list with symbols or numbers for better organization.
It applies a background color to highlight important paragraphs.
It automatically splits the document into multiple sections.
It hides the selected content to protect it from being viewed.
exp:
Bullets or numbering convert the selected text into a structured list.
★ Exam Points:
• Bullets/numbering create structured lists.
• Lists improve readability.
• Increase/Decrease Indent changes list level.

q: What is the purpose of the Find and Replace feature (Ctrl + H) in MS Word 2019?
o: To change the font of the selected text
To search for specific text and replace it with other text
exp:
Find and Replace (Ctrl + H) searches for specific text and replaces it with other text, once or everywhere.
★ Exam Points:
• Replace All changes every instance.
• Supports formatting and special characters.
• Ctrl + F – Find only.

q: In MS Word 2019, if you want to select an entire paragraph quickly, which of the following actions should you perform?
o: Press and hold Alt while clicking the paragraph.
Right-click and choose 'Paragraph' from the available menu options.
Triple-click on any word within the paragraph.
exp:
Triple-clicking a word selects the whole paragraph.
★ Exam Points:
• Triple-click selects paragraph.
• Double-click selects a word.
• Ctrl + click selects a sentence.

q: What happens when you press Ctrl + S while working on a document in computer system?
exp:
Ctrl + S saves the current document.
★ Exam Points:
• Ctrl + S – save.
• F12 – Save As.
• Ctrl + O – open.

q: When utilising the 'Paste Special' function in MS Word to insert content copied from a spreadsheet, which of the following paste options would preserve the original formula calculations while displaying the calculated values in the Word document?
exp:
Pasting as a Microsoft Excel Worksheet Object preserves the original spreadsheet structure and formulas.
★ Exam Points:
• Excel Worksheet Object embeds the data with formulas.
• Paste Link updates with source.
• Unformatted text loses formulas.

q: What happens when you use the Format Painter tool in MS Word?
o: It copies formatting (e.g., font, color) from one piece of text to another.
exp:
Format Painter copies formatting such as font and colour from one selection to another.
★ Exam Points:
• Format Painter copies formatting.
• Double-click for multiple uses.
• Shortcut: Ctrl + Shift + C / V.

q: Which keyboard shortcut is used to make the selected text bold in MS Word 365?
exp:
Ctrl + B makes selected text bold.
★ Exam Points:
• Ctrl + B – bold; Ctrl + I – italic; Ctrl + U – underline.
• Ctrl + D – Font dialog.
• Ctrl + Shift + D – double underline.

q: In MS Word 365, which feature allows users to customise the appearance of bulleted lists by selecting different bullet styles or symbols and modifying their size and color?
exp:
The bullet library lets you choose bullet symbols and adjust their style.
★ Exam Points:
• Bullet Library shows recent bullets.
• Define New Bullet: Symbol, Picture, Font.
• Bullets are in Home → Paragraph.

q: You have applied a specific character style to several instances of a product name throughout a lengthy MS Word document. If you need to change the font and color of all these instances, what is the most efficient method?
o: Copying the formatting from one instance using the 'Format Painter' and applying it to others
Using the 'Find and Replace' function with formatting options
Modifying the definition of the character style
Manually selecting each instance and applying the new formatting
exp:
Modifying the character style's definition updates every instance that uses that style automatically – the most efficient method.
★ Exam Points:
• Styles pane → Modify.
• Avoids manual changes.
• Character styles affect selected text only.

q: Which of the following best describes the 'Gutter' margin in MS Word 2019?
o: The space at the top of the page for a header
The blank space on all four sides of the page
Extra space added for document binding
A margin applied only to odd-numbered pages
exp:
The gutter margin is extra space added for binding.
★ Exam Points:
• Gutter = extra margin for binding.
• Gutter position: Left or Top.
• Used with Mirror margins in books.

q: Which tab in MS Word 365 contains options to change page margins, orientation and size?
exp:
The Layout tab (Page Layout in older versions) contains margins, orientation and size.
★ Exam Points:
• Layout tab: Margins, Orientation, Size, Columns, Breaks.
• Home tab: font and paragraph formatting.
• Insert tab: tables, pictures.

q: When working with text wrapping around an image in MS Word, which 'Layout Option' provides the most flexibility in precisely positioning the image relative to the text and other elements, ignoring the text flow?
o: Behind Text or In Front of Text
exp:
'Behind Text' or 'In Front of Text' lets the image be positioned freely, independent of text flow.
★ Exam Points:
• Behind Text / In Front of Text allow free positioning.
• Square/Tight wrap text around.
• In Line with Text treats picture as a character.

q: If you move text using 'Cut and Paste', where does the text go before being pasted in MS Office?
exp:
Cut text goes to the Clipboard until it is pasted.
★ Exam Points:
• Cut text goes to the Clipboard.
• Office Clipboard holds 24 items.
• Recycle Bin is for files, not text.

q: In MS Word, which feature allows users to set the margins of a document, affecting the space between the text and the edges of the page?
exp:
The Margins option sets the space between the text and the page edges.
★ Exam Points:
• Margins: Layout → Margins.
• Default 1 inch on all sides.
• Custom Margins opens Page Setup.

q: In MS Word, which command allows users to duplicate a selected block of text and place the copy at a different location within the same document or another document?
exp:
Copy and Paste duplicates text to another place in the same or another document.
★ Exam Points:
• Copy (Ctrl + C) + Paste (Ctrl + V) duplicates.
• Cut + Paste moves.
• Paste Special controls format.

q: In MS Word 365, what is the shortcut to remove manual character formatting from selected text?
exp:
Ctrl + Spacebar removes manual character formatting from selected text.
★ Exam Points:
• Ctrl + Spacebar removes character formatting.
• Ctrl + Q removes paragraph formatting.
• Ctrl + Shift + N applies Normal style.

q: Which one is NOT the method to search for and replace text in Microsoft Word?
o: Press Ctrl + H to open the Find and Replace window
Click 'Edit' and then select 'Find and Replace'.
Go to the 'Home' tab and select 'Replace'.
exp:
Alt + Enter is not used for Find and Replace; Ctrl + H, Home tab then Replace, and the older Edit menu are.
★ Exam Points:
• Ctrl + H opens Replace.
• Home → Editing → Replace.
• Alt + Enter is not a replace shortcut.

q: What is the difference between dragging text with the mouse (left-click) and Ctrl + dragging text in MS Word 365?
o: Dragging moves the text; Ctrl + dragging copies it.
Dragging deletes the text; Ctrl + dragging pastes it.
Ctrl + dragging changes the font style.
exp:
Dragging selected text moves it; Ctrl + dragging copies it.
★ Exam Points:
• Drag = move; Ctrl + drag = copy.
• Right-drag shows a menu (Move/Copy/Link).
• Works in Explorer too.

q: What is the primary function of the keyboard shortcut Ctrl + H in applications like MS Word?
o: Opens the Find and Replace dialog box
exp:
Ctrl + H opens the Find and Replace dialog box.
★ Exam Points:
• Ctrl + H – Find and Replace.
• Ctrl + F – Find.
• Ctrl + G – Go To.

q: In a Word document form, when you press the Tab key after filling a name field, to which element does the focus shift?
o: Deletes all entered form data instantly
Moves cursor to subsequent input field or table cell
Prints the form with current entries
Saves document and closes the form view
exp:
Pressing Tab moves the cursor to the next input field or table cell.
★ Exam Points:
• Tab moves to the next field/table cell.
• Shift + Tab moves back.
• Forms use content controls.

q: In Microsoft Word 2016 and later versions, when text spanning multiple paragraphs is highlighted and the user presses Ctrl + C, what operation is performed?
o: Transfers the highlighted paragraphs to clipboard for duplication elsewhere
Permanently erases the highlighted paragraphs from existence
Immediately inserts the paragraphs at the documents beginning
Automatically saves the entire document with paragraphs updated
exp:
Ctrl + C copies the highlighted paragraphs to the clipboard.
★ Exam Points:
• Ctrl + C copies to clipboard.
• Original text stays unchanged.
• Ctrl + X would remove it.

q: In Google Docs, when you press Ctrl + S, what technical action occurs in the background?
o: The document is saved to local storage
The keyboard shortcut is not recognized
An immediate sync to Drive is triggered
The Save As dialog box appears on screen
exp:
In Google Docs, Ctrl + S forces an immediate sync of the document to Google Drive (it autosaves).
★ Exam Points:
• Google Docs saves automatically to Google Drive.
• Ctrl + S triggers a manual sync in Docs.
• Version history: Ctrl + Alt + Shift + H.

q: To prevent losing your current progress due to a system crash or power failure, which essential shortcut key combination should you press regularly to quickly save the document you are working on?
exp:
Press Ctrl + S regularly to save progress.
★ Exam Points:
• Save frequently with Ctrl + S.
• AutoRecover saves every 10 minutes by default.
• Use UPS to avoid power loss.

q: A file with the extension ".docx" is usually created by:
exp:
A .docx file is created by MS Word.
★ Exam Points:
• .docx – Word document.
• .txt – Notepad.
• .bmp/.png – Paint.

q: Which of the following file formats does not get affected by the destination format and version?
exp:
A PDF file preserves its layout, fonts and formatting regardless of the destination software or version, so it is not affected by destination format/version.
★ Exam Points:
• PDF = Portable Document Format (Adobe).
• .pptx/.docx may render differently in other versions.
• PDF/A is for archiving.

q: Which shortcut saves the current file in Microsoft Word or Microsoft Excel?
exp:
Ctrl + S saves the current file in Word or Excel.
★ Exam Points:
• Ctrl + S saves in all Office apps.
• AutoSave works on OneDrive files.
• Unsaved files can be recovered from AutoRecover.

q: Which of the following is an example of application software used for creating documents?
exp:
MS Word is application software for creating documents.
★ Exam Points:
• MS Word is a word processor.
• Linux and Windows are OS; BIOS is firmware.
• Google Docs is an online word processor.

q: What is the function of the keyboard shortcut Ctrl + Z?
exp:
Ctrl + Z undoes the last action.
★ Exam Points:
• Ctrl + Z – undo; Ctrl + Y – redo.
• Undo history can be many steps.
• Alt + Backspace also undoes.

q: What does Ctrl + F help users to do?
o: Find a file on the desktop
Find text in the current document or webpage
exp:
Ctrl + F finds text in the current document or web page.
★ Exam Points:
• Ctrl + F – find text.
• In browsers also finds on page.
• Ctrl + G – Go To.

q: Which shortcut key combination is used to save a file quickly?
exp:
Ctrl + S saves a file.
★ Exam Points:
• Ctrl + S – quick save.
• Shift + F12 – save.
• F12 – Save As.

q: Which feature reduces the file size of a modern Word document by compressing its XML components?
exp:
A .docx file is a ZIP-compressed package of XML files (Office Open XML), which keeps it small.
★ Exam Points:
• Rename .docx to .zip to see the XML parts.
• Introduced with Office 2007.
• Compress Pictures further reduces size.

q: Which option in MS Word aligns text to the left, centre, right or justified across the page?
exp:
Paragraph alignment buttons in the Home → Paragraph group set left, centre, right or justify.
★ Exam Points:
• Ctrl + L / E / R / J.
• Alignment applies to whole paragraphs.
• Vertical alignment is in Page Setup.

q: Which keyboard shortcut increases the indent of a paragraph in MS Word 2010?
exp:
Ctrl + M increases the left indent; Ctrl + Shift + M decreases it.
★ Exam Points:
• Ctrl + T – hanging indent.
• Ctrl + K – hyperlink.
• Ctrl + D – Font dialog.

q: Which keyboard shortcut is used for adding bullets in MS Word 2010?
exp:
Ctrl + Shift + L applies the List Bullet style to the paragraph.
★ Exam Points:
• Numbering: Home → Paragraph → Numbering.
• Typing "* " auto-creates a bulleted list.
• Ctrl + L is left align.

q: Which feature in MS Word applies a consistent look across text elements such as headings, titles and subtitles?
exp:
Styles store sets of formatting that can be applied uniformly to headings, titles, etc.
★ Exam Points:
• Styles gallery is in the Home tab.
• Heading styles power the Navigation pane and TOC.
• Templates contain styles for whole documents.

q:
Consider the following statements regarding line spacing of a paragraph in MS-Word 2010.
P: Line spacing determines the amount of vertical space between lines of text in a paragraph.
Q: Line spacing determines the amount of diagonal space between lines of text in a paragraph.
Which statement(s) is/are correct?
exp:
Line spacing is the vertical distance between lines; there is no "diagonal" spacing.
★ Exam Points:
• Single spacing: Ctrl + 1; Double: Ctrl + 2; 1.5 lines: Ctrl + 5.
• Paragraph spacing (Before/After) is different from line spacing.
• Default line spacing in Word 2010 is 1.15.

q: In MS-Word 365, Ctrl + E is the keyboard shortcut to ____.
exp:
Ctrl + E centres the selected paragraph.
★ Exam Points:
• Ctrl + L left, Ctrl + R right, Ctrl + J justify.
• Alt + F opens the File tab.
• Centre alignment is common for titles.

q: Which keyboard shortcut is used to close an MS-Word 365 document window?
exp:
Alt + F4 closes the active window (the Word document window); Ctrl + W also closes the current document.
★ Exam Points:
• Shift + F5 returns to the last edit location.
• Ctrl + F3 cuts to the Spike.
• Alt + F3 creates a Quick Part/AutoText entry.

q: Which buttons are present in the Quick Access Toolbar by default in MS-Word 2010?
exp:
By default the QAT contains Save, Undo and Redo (Repeat).
★ Exam Points:
• Ctrl + S save; Ctrl + Z undo; Ctrl + Y redo/repeat.
• QAT can be shown below the Ribbon.
• Touch/Mouse mode button is added in Word 2013+.

q:
Which of the following statements about the Quick Access Toolbar in MS-Word 2010 is/are incorrect?
P: It has Save, Undo and Redo buttons by default.
Q: It has Cut, Undo and Redo buttons by default.
R: You can place more buttons on the Quick Access Toolbar.
S: There is no option on the Quick Access Toolbar for "Show below the Ribbon".
exp:
Default QAT buttons are Save, Undo and Redo/Repeat, so Q is incorrect; the customise menu does offer "Show below the Ribbon", so S is incorrect.
★ Exam Points:
• QAT appears at the top-left, above the Ribbon by default.
• Buttons can be added through "Customize Quick Access Toolbar".
• Alt + number keys activate QAT buttons.

q: Which of the following font effects is NOT available in the MS-Word 2010 Font dialog box?
exp:
Equalize Character Height is an Asian-layout option, not a font effect; the Font dialog has Strikethrough, Double Strikethrough, Superscript, Subscript, Small Caps, All Caps and Hidden.
★ Exam Points:
• Font dialog box: Ctrl + D.
• Small Caps shortcut: Ctrl + Shift + K; All Caps: Ctrl + Shift + A.
• Superscript: Ctrl + Shift + =; Subscript: Ctrl + =.

q: Which of the following print settings is used to choose only specific pages in MS-Word 365?
exp:
Custom Print lets you type particular pages or ranges (e.g., 1,3,5-8) in the Pages box so that only those pages are printed.
★ Exam Points:
• Print dialog shortcut: Ctrl + P (also Ctrl + F2 for Print Preview).
• Print Selection prints only highlighted text; Print Current Page prints the page where the cursor is.
• Custom range syntax: comma for separate pages, hyphen for a range.

q: Which keyboard shortcut is used to insert a hyperlink for the selected text in Microsoft Word?
exp:
Ctrl + K opens the Insert Hyperlink dialog box for the selected text or object.
★ Exam Points:
• Ctrl + M increases the left indent; Ctrl + H opens Find & Replace.
• Ctrl + Z undoes the last action.
• Ctrl + Shift + F9 removes a hyperlink (unlinks fields).

q: The Shading option in MS-Word 365 is used for ____.
o: changing the colour behind the selected text
changing the colour of the selected text
making the text pop by highlighting it
changing the colour around the selected text
exp:
Shading (Home → Paragraph group) fills the background behind the selected text, paragraph or table cell with colour.
★ Exam Points:
• Font Color changes the colour of the text itself.
• Text Highlight Color marks text like a highlighter pen.
• Borders draw lines around text or a page.

q: You are editing a 50-page thesis. Changing one heading alters the font size of all headings. If you want to change only the selected heading's font size and not all similar headings, what should you do?
exp:
When all headings share a linked style (e.g., Heading 1 with 'Automatically update' enabled or style modification), modifying the style changes every heading in the document. Applying direct formatting (selecting just that single heading text and changing its font size on the Home tab / Mini Toolbar) overrides the style locally for only the selected heading.
★ Exam Points:
• Modify Style updates every paragraph tagged with that style across the entire document.
• Change Theme (Design tab) changes document-wide theme fonts and colour palettes simultaneously.
• Ctrl + Spacebar removes manual character formatting, reverting selected text back to its underlying paragraph style.

q: When a user inserts a Section Break (Next Page) in a long document, which property can typically be customized for the new section without affecting the previous sections?
exp:
Inserting a Section Break (Next Page) (Layout tab > Breaks) divides a Word document into independent layout sections, allowing section-level settings such as page orientation (Portrait/Landscape), margins, paper size, columns, page numbering, and headers/footers to be customized without affecting earlier sections.
★ Exam Points:
• To give a new section a different Header or Footer, turn off Link to Previous on the Header & Footer contextual tab.
• Types of Section Breaks in MS Word: Next Page, Continuous, Even Page, and Odd Page.
• Document Properties, Normal style font, and AutoCorrect lists are document-wide or application-wide settings, not section-specific.

q: Which keyboard shortcut is commonly used to create a new blank document while the program is already running?
exp:
Across MS Word, MS Excel, MS PowerPoint, Notepad, and most desktop applications, pressing Ctrl + N creates a new blank document/workbook/file while the application is already open.
★ Exam Points:
• Shortcut | Standard File Action
• Ctrl + N | Create a new blank document / file
• Ctrl + O | Open an existing file from storage
• Ctrl + S | Save the current file
• Ctrl + W / Ctrl + F4 | Close the active document window (app stays open)
• Ctrl + F2 / Ctrl + P | Open Print Preview / Print dialog

q: Which tab in MS Word contains options to change orientation, margins and page size?
exp:
Layout → Page Setup has Margins, Orientation, Size, Columns and Breaks.
★ Exam Points:
• Called Page Layout in Word 2010.
• Page Setup dialog has more options.
• Size options: A4, Letter, Legal.

q: In MS Word, which feature creates a list where each item starts with a dot or symbol instead of a number?
exp:
Bullets add symbols (•, ■, ✓) before list items.
★ Exam Points:
• Define New Bullet allows symbols/pictures.
• Numbering uses 1, 2, 3 or a, b, c.
