q: What is the default file extension of MS Word 2007 and later documents?
exp:
Word documents are saved as .docx by default.
★ Exam Points:
• .doc – Word 97–2003.
• .dotx – template.
• .rtf – Rich Text Format.

q: In MS Word, which feature ensures that text such as document title and page number appears at the top of every page?
exp:
A header repeats in the top margin of every page (footer repeats at the bottom).
★ Exam Points:
• Insert → Header.
• Different First Page option available.
• Different Odd & Even pages option available.

q: What is the main purpose of the Format Painter tool in the Clipboard group?
o: To copy formatting from one part of text and apply it to another
exp:
Format Painter copies the formatting of the selected text to other text.
★ Exam Points:
• Double-click to apply multiple times.
• Ctrl + Shift + C / V shortcuts.
• Icon is a paintbrush.

q: ____ is a word-processing tool for creating different types of documents used in work and school environments.
exp:
Microsoft Word is the word processor of Microsoft Office.
★ Exam Points:
• Excel – spreadsheet.
• Access – database.
• PowerPoint – presentations.

q: Which option on the Home tab changes selected text from small letters to capital letters or vice versa?
exp:
Change Case (Aa) offers UPPERCASE, lowercase, Sentence case, Capitalize Each Word and tOGGLE cASE.
★ Exam Points:
• Shift + F3 cycles cases.
• Ctrl + Shift + A applies All Caps.
• Located in the Font group.

q: Which feature in MS Word lets you see how the document will look when printed, including margins and page breaks?
o: Print Layout view or Print Preview
exp:
Print Layout and Print Preview show pages exactly as they will print.
★ Exam Points:
• Print Preview: Ctrl + F2.
• Draft hides page layout elements.
• Web Layout shows web appearance.

q: Which feature moves the cursor to the next line automatically when the end of a line is reached, without pressing Enter?
exp:
Word wrap automatically moves text that does not fit onto the next line.
★ Exam Points:
• Press Enter only to start a new paragraph.
• Shift + Enter adds a line break.
• Wrap Text in Excel works within a cell.

q: The ____ contains multiple tabs, which you can find near the top of the Word window.
exp:
The Ribbon has tabs (Home, Insert, Layout…) each containing groups of commands.
★ Exam Points:
• Introduced in Office 2007.
• Ctrl + F1 collapses/expands it.
• Contextual tabs appear for tables/pictures.

q: Which key combination moves the cursor one word to the right?
exp:
Ctrl + Right arrow jumps to the start of the next word.
★ Exam Points:
• Ctrl + Left arrow – previous word.
• Shift + Ctrl + Right selects a word.
• End – end of line.

q: How can you insert a signature line in Microsoft Word?
exp:
Insert → Text group → Signature Line adds a line for a printed or digital signature.
★ Exam Points:
• Digital signatures verify authenticity.
• Signer details can be pre-filled.
• Signed documents become read-only.

q: Which feature in MS Word inserts custom fields such as dates, document properties or user information?
exp:
Insert → Quick Parts → Field opens the Field dialog with fields like Date, Author, FileName, NumPages.
★ Exam Points:
• Ctrl + F9 inserts an empty field.
• F9 updates fields.
• Alt + F9 shows field codes.

q: Which combination of Word features is most suitable to create a professional letter with a logo, predefined layout and consistent heading styles?
o: Insert Picture, a suitable Template and Styles for headings
Only Normal style and no images
exp:
Templates give layout, Insert Picture adds the logo and Styles keep headings consistent.
★ Exam Points:
• Letterhead templates are available.
• Save company template as .dotx.
• Styles ensure uniformity.

q: To view formatting for the current selection, press ____ to open Reveal Formatting.
exp:
Shift + F1 opens the Reveal Formatting pane showing font, paragraph and section formatting.
★ Exam Points:
• Shift + F3 – change case.
• Shift + F2 – copy text (Word).
• Useful to compare formatting.

q: Which key in MS Word deletes the character to the left of the insertion point?
exp:
Backspace removes the character to the left; Delete removes the one to the right.
★ Exam Points:
• Ctrl + Backspace deletes previous word.
• Enter starts a new paragraph.
• Tab inserts a tab space.

q: Which is the primary MS Word view in which the document looks the same as when printed?
exp:
Print Layout (default) shows margins, headers, footers and page breaks as they will print.
★ Exam Points:
• Read Mode is for comfortable reading.
• Web Layout shows as a web page.
• Draft hides headers and images.

q: Who developed Microsoft Word?
exp:
Microsoft Word was developed by Charles Simonyi and Richard Brodie and released in 1983 (as Multi-Tool Word).
★ Exam Points:
• First version ran on Xenix/MS-DOS.
• Dennis Ritchie created C language.
• Bill Gates co-founded Microsoft.

q: In a Table of Contents (TOC), the hierarchy of headings is controlled by ____.
exp:
Each heading style has an outline level (Level 1, 2, 3…) that determines its position in the TOC.
★ Exam Points:
• Heading 1 = Level 1.
• Add Text (References tab) sets levels.
• Update TOC after edits.

q: For a large document with many headings, which combination is most effective for navigation and automatic table of contents?
o: Applying built-in Heading styles and using the Navigation pane
exp:
Heading styles appear in the Navigation pane and are used to build an automatic TOC.
★ Exam Points:
• Navigation pane: Ctrl + F → Headings.
• TOC: References → Table of Contents.
• Drag headings to reorganise.

q: In MS Word, which feature automatically moves text to the next page when the current page is full?
exp:
Word inserts soft (automatic) page breaks as pages fill; they move as text changes.
★ Exam Points:
• Manual (hard) break: Ctrl + Enter.
• Keep with next prevents awkward breaks.
• Widow/Orphan control is on by default.

q: The ____ option protects a Word document: you can set a password so nobody can open it, or lock it so nobody can edit it.
exp:
File → Info → Protect Document offers Mark as Final, Encrypt with Password, Restrict Editing and Add Digital Signature.
★ Exam Points:
• Restrict Editing limits changes.
• Encrypt sets an open-password.
• Digital signature verifies authenticity.

q: Which command converts selected text to uppercase, lowercase or sentence case?
exp:
Home → Font → Change Case (Aa) offers Sentence case, lowercase, UPPERCASE, Capitalize Each Word and tOGGLE cASE.
★ Exam Points:
• Shortcut: Shift + F3.
• Ctrl + Shift + A – all caps.
• Excel uses UPPER/LOWER/PROPER functions.

q: Which Word feature helps you view two parts of a long document simultaneously?
exp:
View → Split divides the window into two panes showing different parts of the same document.
★ Exam Points:
• Shortcut: Alt + Ctrl + S.
• View Side by Side compares two documents.
• New Window opens another view.

q: What is the purpose of the "Compare" feature in Microsoft Word?
o: To compare two documents for differences
To create a table of contents
exp:
Review → Compare → Compare shows differences between two versions as tracked changes.
★ Exam Points:
• Combine merges revisions from several reviewers.
• Results open in a new document.
• Useful for legal documents.

q: Which is NOT a valid section break type in MS Word?
exp:
Section breaks are Next Page, Continuous, Even Page and Odd Page; there is no "Top Page".
★ Exam Points:
• Layout → Breaks.
• Sections can have different headers/orientation.
• Continuous starts a section on the same page.

q: Clicking on each menu bar option opens a list of commands called a ____.
exp:
A pull-down (drop-down) menu lists commands when a menu-bar item is clicked.
★ Exam Points:
• Shortcut (context) menu appears on right-click.
• Cascading menus open sub-menus.
• Greyed commands are unavailable.

q: What is the purpose of the “Smart Lookup” feature in Word?
o: Search the web for the selected text
exp:
Smart Lookup (now Search/Researcher) shows web definitions and information for selected text using Bing.
★ Exam Points:
• Right-click → Smart Lookup.
• Introduced in Office 2016.
• Translate is a separate feature.

q: How can you create a custom style based on a paragraph style in MS Word?
o: Home → Styles → Create a Style (New Style)
exp:
Use Home → Styles → Create a Style (or New Style in the Styles pane) and set "Style based on".
★ Exam Points:
• Styles pane: Ctrl + Alt + Shift + S.
• Style types: Paragraph, Character, Linked, Table, List.
• Modify updates all text using the style.

q: Which button is used to make text appear slanted or tilted?
exp:
Italic (Ctrl + I) slants the text to the right.
★ Exam Points:
• Bold: Ctrl + B.
• Underline: Ctrl + U.
• Italics are used for titles and emphasis.

q: Which section manages version history in Word for the web/Microsoft 365?
exp:
File → Info → Version History lists earlier saved versions of a file stored on OneDrive/SharePoint.
★ Exam Points:
• AutoSave creates versions automatically.
• Older versions can be restored.
• Requires cloud storage.

q: When you use the ‘Open’ command, which device is MS Word primarily accessing to find a saved file?
exp:
Saved files are stored permanently on storage devices; Open reads them from there into RAM.
★ Exam Points:
• RAM is temporary (volatile).
• Files can also be opened from OneDrive.
• Ctrl + O opens files.

q: A footer is text that appears at the ____ of every page of a document.
exp:
Footers appear in the bottom margin; headers appear in the top margin.
★ Exam Points:
• Insert → Footer.
• Often contains page numbers.
• Double-click footer area to edit.

q: What is the use of a "Macro" in Word?
o: To automate repetitive tasks by recording a sequence of commands
exp:
A macro records a series of actions (in VBA) that can be replayed with one click or shortcut.
★ Exam Points:
• View → Macros → Record Macro.
• Macro-enabled files: .docm.
• Macros can carry viruses – enable carefully.

q: What is the extension of an MS Word file (2007 and later)?
exp:
Word documents are saved as .docx (older .doc).
★ Exam Points:
• .png – image.
• .xlsx – Excel.
• .pptx – PowerPoint.

q: What is the purpose of the "Building Blocks" feature in Microsoft Word?
o: To store and reuse pre-formatted content such as cover pages, headers and text boxes
exp:
Building Blocks are reusable pieces of content (AutoText, cover pages, headers/footers) inserted via Quick Parts.
★ Exam Points:
• Building Blocks Organizer manages them.
• Alt + F3 saves selection as a building block.
• Stored in Building Blocks.dotx.

q: Which statement describes the difference between Save and Save As once a document already has a name?
o: Save creates a copy; Save As exits
Save stores changes in the same file; Save As saves a new copy with a different name or location
exp:
Save updates the existing file; Save As creates a new file with a new name/location/format.
★ Exam Points:
• Save: Ctrl + S; Save As: F12.
• First-time Save opens Save As.
• Save As can convert to PDF.

q: In MS Word, which mode makes existing characters move forward instead of being overwritten when you type?
exp:
In Insert mode (default) new text is inserted and existing text shifts right; Overtype replaces characters.
★ Exam Points:
• Insert key toggles Overtype (if enabled in Options).
• Status bar can show Insert/Overtype.
• Overtype was default in old typewriter-style editors.

q: Which bar lies below the Title bar and provides categorised options (in menu-based programs)?
exp:
The menu bar (File, Edit, View, Insert…) sits just below the title bar in classic interfaces.
★ Exam Points:
• Clicking a menu opens a pull-down menu.
• Office 2007+ replaced menus with the Ribbon.
• Status bar is at the bottom.

q: Which shortcut key applies Small Caps formatting in MS Word?
exp:
Ctrl + Shift + K converts lowercase letters into small capital letters.
★ Exam Points:
• Ctrl + Shift + A – All Caps.
• Ctrl + K – hyperlink.
• Small Caps is in the Font dialog.

q: Which alignment makes both left and right edges of a paragraph flush with the margins (used in books and newspapers)?
exp:
Justify spaces words so that lines touch both margins.
★ Exam Points:
• Shortcut: Ctrl + J.
• Last line stays left-aligned.
• Hyphenation reduces large gaps.

q: Which of the following allows you to link content from Excel into Word so it updates automatically?
exp:
OLE lets you link or embed objects (e.g., Excel charts) in Word; linked objects update when the source changes.
★ Exam Points:
• Paste Special → Paste Link.
• Embedded objects are stored inside the document.
• OLE was developed by Microsoft.

q: Which feature allows text to flow around images or shapes?
exp:
Wrap Text options (Square, Tight, Through, Top and Bottom, Behind, In Front) control how text flows around objects.
★ Exam Points:
• Default for pictures: In Line with Text.
• Layout Options button appears next to picture.
• Found in Picture Format → Wrap Text.

q: Which option is used to protect a Word document with a password?
o: File → Info → Protect Document → Encrypt with Password
exp:
Encrypt with Password in File → Info → Protect Document sets an opening password.
★ Exam Points:
• Restrict Editing limits changes, not opening.
• Passwords are case-sensitive.
• Mark as Final is not real protection.

q: What is the purpose of the Recent option in MS Word?
exp:
File → Open/Recent shows recently used documents for quick access.
★ Exam Points:
• Documents can be pinned to the Recent list.
• Number of recent files is configurable.
• Also shows recent folders.

q: What is the difference between normal text and a saved "Building Block" (Quick Parts/AutoText) in Word?
o: Building blocks lose formatting when reused
A building block is reusable content that keeps formatting (text, graphics, tables)
Building blocks double file size each time
They can store only single words

Building Blocks store pre-formatted content (cover pages, headers, text boxes, AutoText) for quick reuse.
★ Exam Points:
• Insert → Quick Parts → Building Blocks Organizer.
• Alt + F3 creates a new building block.
• Stored in Building Blocks.dotx.

q: In MS Word, to remove changes keep clicking the ____ button till you reach the original form of the document.

Undo (Ctrl + Z) reverses actions one by one.
★ Exam Points:
• Redo: Ctrl + Y.
• Undo list shows multiple actions.
• Undo history is lost after closing.

q: Which format preserves a Word document's layout and is best for sharing?

PDF (Portable Document Format) keeps fonts, images and layout identical on all devices.

• PDF developed by Adobe (1993).
• Save As → PDF in Word 2010+.
• PDF/A is for archiving.

q: What is the primary function of the Styles group on the Home tab?

exp:
Styles apply predefined formatting combinations consistently in one click.

• Heading styles enable automatic TOC.
• Modify a style to update all text using it.

• Page formatting: margins, orientation, size.

Paste inserts what was copied or cut onto the clipboard.

• Paste Options button appears after pasting.

q: ____ are reduced-size versions of images used in Word 2016 and other programs.

Thumbnails are small preview images of pictures or pages.

• File Explorer shows thumbnails in large icon view.
• Thumb drive = pen drive.

q: How can you create a drop cap in Microsoft Word?

Insert → Text group → Drop Cap enlarges the first letter of a paragraph.
★ Exam Points:
• Options: Dropped, In Margin.
• Lines to drop can be set.
• Common in newspapers.

q: The default line spacing for a new document in MS Word 2007/2010 is ____.

• Word 2003 default: single.
• Spacing after paragraph default: 10 pt (2010).
• Change defaults via Paragraph → Set As Default.

• Ctrl + Q – remove paragraph formatting.
• Highlight is not removed by it.

q: Which feature lets you create personalised letters or envelopes using a list of names/addresses?

• Merge fields insert names/addresses.

q: The feature used to apply artistic or decorative effects to text, such as shadows or reflections, is called ____.
exp:
Home → Font → Text Effects and Typography applies outline, shadow, reflection and glow to text.

• WordArt also gives decorative text.
• Effects are found in the Font dialog too.
• Reflection and glow came in Word 2010.

q: Which option in MS Word allows you to add a watermark to the document?

Watermark is in the Design tab (Page Layout tab in Word 2010).

• Built-in: CONFIDENTIAL, DRAFT, ASAP.
• Custom picture watermark is possible.
• Remove Watermark option is in the same menu.

q: In Word Print settings, which option prints multiple pages reduced in size onto a single sheet of paper?
exp:
The Pages Per Sheet option (1, 2, 4, 6, 8, 16) prints several pages on one sheet.

• Saves paper for drafts.
• Found under zoom settings in Print.
• Scale to paper size fits pages to paper.

q: The feature used to create a numbered or bulleted list in MS Word is found in which group of the Home tab?
exp:
Bullets, Numbering and Multilevel List are in the Paragraph group.

• Paragraph group also has alignment and line spacing.
• Typing "1. " starts automatic numbering.
• Ctrl + Shift + L – bullets.

q: Which option inserts the date and time in a Word document?
exp:
Insert → Text group → Date & Time inserts the current date/time in a chosen format.
★ Exam Points:
• Alt + Shift + D – insert date field.
• Alt + Shift + T – insert time field.
• "Update automatically" makes it a field.

q: How can you insert a section break in MS Word?
exp:
Layout (Page Layout) → Breaks offers Next Page, Continuous, Even Page and Odd Page section breaks.
★ Exam Points:
• Page break: Ctrl + Enter.
• Sections allow different orientation/headers.
• Column break: Ctrl + Shift + Enter.

q: If a Word document is protected with a password, what is the procedure to change or remove that password?

Rename to .zip and edit internal files

The open-password is set and removed from File → Info → Protect Document → Encrypt with Password; clear the box and save.
★ Exam Points:
• Restrict Editing handles editing permissions, not open-passwords.
• Passwords are case-sensitive.
• Forgotten passwords cannot be recovered by Microsoft.

q: How can you change the case of selected text in MS Word using the keyboard?
exp:
Shift + F3 cycles through lowercase, UPPERCASE and Capitalize Each Word.
★ Exam Points:
• Change Case button is in Home → Font.
• Ctrl + Shift + A – All Caps.
• Alt + F3 – create Quick Part.

q: In a standard menu-driven application, how do you display different toolbars?
o: Edit → Toolbars, then uncheck the toolbar
Format → Toolbars, then click to hide
File → Toolbars, then check a toolbar
View → Toolbars, then click the name of an unchecked toolbar to display it
exp:
In menu-based versions (e.g., Word 2003), View → Toolbars lists toolbars; clicking an unchecked one displays it.
★ Exam Points:
• Standard and Formatting were default toolbars.
• Office 2007 replaced toolbars with the Ribbon.
• Right-click a toolbar area also shows the list.

q: What does the ‘Insert Footnote’ feature do in MS Word?
o: Adds a footer on every page
Inserts a superscript reference mark and creates a note at the bottom of the current page
Converts text into a margin comment
exp:
A footnote places a numbered mark in the text and the corresponding note at the bottom of that page.
★ Exam Points:
• Shortcut: Ctrl + Alt + F.
• Endnotes appear at the document end.
• References tab → Footnotes group.

q: What is the purpose of the "Master Document" feature in Microsoft Word?
o: To create a table of contents
To manage multiple documents (subdocuments) as a single document
exp:
A master document links several subdocuments (e.g., chapters) so they can be managed, numbered and printed as one.
★ Exam Points:
• Available in Outline view.
• Useful for long books and theses.
• Subdocuments remain separate files.

q: What is the file extension of a standard MS Word document created in Word 2007 and later?
exp:
Word 2007+ uses the XML-based .docx format.
★ Exam Points:
• .doc was used up to Word 2003.
• .docm – macro-enabled.
• .dotx – template.

q: Which is the correct method to remove a hyperlink in MS Word?
exp:
Right-clicking the link and choosing Remove Hyperlink keeps the text but removes the link.
★ Exam Points:
• Ctrl + Shift + F9 also unlinks.
• Ctrl + K edits the hyperlink.
• Ctrl + click follows the link.

q: In Microsoft Word, what is the primary function of inserting a Non-Breaking Space (Ctrl + Shift + Space)?
o: To automatically capitalise the next word
To keep the two words on the same line, preventing a line break between them
To remove formatting from the space
To justify and centre the paragraph

A non-breaking space joins two words (e.g., "Mr. Sharma", "10 kg") so Word never splits them across lines.
★ Exam Points:
• Shortcut: Ctrl + Shift + Space.
• Shown as a small degree-like symbol with ¶ marks on.
• Non-breaking hyphen: Ctrl + Shift + -.

q: Which shortcut key can be used to go to a specific page in MS Word?
exp:
Ctrl + G (or F5) opens the Go To tab of Find and Replace.
★ Exam Points:
• Go To can jump to page, section, line, bookmark.
• Ctrl + H – Replace.
• Ctrl + J – justify.

q: What is the standard term for light-coloured text or image appearing semi-transparently behind the main content of every page?
exp:
A watermark (e.g., CONFIDENTIAL, a logo) is placed behind text on every page.
★ Exam Points:
• Design → Watermark (Page Layout in Word 2010).
• Custom watermark can use pictures.
• Page Color changes the background colour.

q: Which feature allows you to add a citation in MS Word?
exp:
References → Citations & Bibliography → Insert Citation adds a source reference.
★ Exam Points:
• Citation styles: APA, MLA, Chicago.
• Manage Sources stores references.
• Bibliography is generated automatically.

q: What is the standard file extension for a Word document template (2007 and later)?
exp:
Word templates are saved as .dotx (.dotm if they contain macros).
★ Exam Points:
• .docx – document; .docm – macro-enabled document.
• Normal.dotm is the default template.
• .dot was the template format before 2007.

q: Which command places a selected block of text in a different location, removing it from its original position?
exp:
Cut (Ctrl + X) removes the text to the clipboard; Paste (Ctrl + V) places it elsewhere – i.e., moving.
★ Exam Points:
• Drag and drop also moves text.
• Ctrl + drag copies text.
• F2 then Enter moves text in Word.

q: Which tab in MS Word provides options for inserting footnotes and endnotes?
exp:
The References tab contains Footnotes, Table of Contents, Citations, Captions and Index groups.
★ Exam Points:
• Insert Footnote: Ctrl + Alt + F.
• Insert Endnote: Ctrl + Alt + D.
• Bibliography is also in References.

q: What is the default page orientation for a new document in MS Word?
exp:
New documents use Portrait orientation (taller than wide) by default.
★ Exam Points:
• Change via Layout → Orientation.
• Default paper: Letter (US) / A4 (India).
• Default margins: 1 inch.

q: Which feature in MS Word creates and formats a Table of Contents automatically?
exp:
References → Table of Contents builds a TOC from heading styles.
★ Exam Points:
• Update TOC with F9 / Update Table.
• TOC entries link to headings.
• Uses Heading 1–3 by default.

q: A user sees only the horizontal ruler although the Ruler is turned on. Which view mode might the person be using?
exp:
The vertical ruler appears only in Print Layout view; Normal/Draft view shows only the horizontal ruler.
★ Exam Points:
• Views: Read Mode, Print Layout, Web Layout, Outline, Draft.
• Show rulers: View → Ruler.
• Draft view hides headers and pictures.

q: Which option in MS Word sets automatic numbering for headings in a document?
o: Heading Styles in the Home tab
Multilevel List in the Home tab
exp:
Multilevel List (Home → Paragraph) can be linked to heading styles to number headings as 1, 1.1, 1.1.1 automatically.
★ Exam Points:
• Define New Multilevel List links levels to Heading 1, 2, 3.
• Used in reports and theses.
• Numbering updates automatically.

q: The primary purpose of displaying toolbars with shortcut buttons in document editing is to ____.
o: provide detailed descriptions of complex commands
facilitate quicker and easier editing and formatting operations
exp:
Toolbars give one-click access to common commands, making editing faster.
★ Exam Points:
• Quick Access Toolbar can be customised.
• Mini toolbar appears on text selection.
• Ribbon replaced menus in Office 2007.

q: What does it mean when text is displayed with a red wavy underline in MS Word?
o: The word is not properly capitalised
The text is marked for deletion
exp:
Red wavy underline marks possible spelling errors; blue double underline marks grammar issues.
★ Exam Points:
• F7 runs Spelling & Grammar.
• Right-click shows suggestions.
• Add to Dictionary stops flagging a word.

q: What is the function of the ‘Merge’ (Combine) feature in MS Word?
o: To combine multiple documents into one
exp:
Review → Compare → Combine merges revisions from multiple documents into one.
★ Exam Points:
• Mail Merge combines a letter with a data list.
• Insert → Object → Text from File also merges.
• Compare shows differences between two versions.

q: What is the default interval of tab stops in a standard MS Word document when no custom tabs are set?
exp:
Word places default tab stops every 0.5 inch (1.27 cm).

• Tab types: Left, Center, Right, Decimal, Bar.
• Set tabs with Ruler or Paragraph → Tabs.
• Default tab interval can be changed.

q: Which feature is used to copy formatting (font style, colour, size) from one text to another?
exp:
Format Painter copies formatting from selected text and applies it to other text.
★ Exam Points:
• Single-click – apply once; double-click – apply repeatedly.
• Shortcut: Ctrl + Shift + C / Ctrl + Shift + V.
• Icon is a paintbrush.

q: While setting a password in Word using "General Options", which statement is FALSE?

The password is case-sensitive and may include numbers, spaces and symbols
The password to open must be retyped in Confirm Password
As the password is typed, the actual characters are displayed to prevent mistyping
exp:
Passwords are masked (shown as dots/asterisks) while typing, not displayed as actual characters.
★ Exam Points:
• General Options is in Save As → Tools.
• Two passwords: to open and to modify.
• Passwords are case-sensitive.

q: Which option in MS Word lets you apply a style to text?
exp:
The Styles group in the Home tab contains the Styles gallery to apply styles.
★ Exam Points:
• Ctrl + Shift + S – Apply Styles pane.
• Ctrl + Alt + 1/2/3 – Heading 1/2/3.
• Modify style to change all instances.

q: Which command should be used to create a brand-new, blank document?
exp:
File → New → Blank document (Ctrl + N) creates a new document.
★ Exam Points:
• Open – existing file.
• Save As – save with new name.
• Templates also start new documents.

q: Which non-printing character is represented by the ¶ (pilcrow) symbol when Show/Hide formatting marks is on in MS Word?
exp:
¶ marks the end of a paragraph (where Enter was pressed).
★ Exam Points:
• Show/Hide: Ctrl + Shift + 8.
• Tab shows as →; space as a dot.
• Paragraph formatting is stored in the ¶ mark.

q: What is the keyboard shortcut for opening the ‘Find’ feature in MS Word/Excel?
exp:
Ctrl + F opens Find (Navigation pane in Word, Find dialog in Excel).
★ Exam Points:
• Ctrl + H – Replace.
• Ctrl + G – Go To.
• Ctrl + D – Font dialog (Word).

q: Where in Microsoft Word can you adjust indentation options, such as creating a hanging indent?
exp:
The Paragraph dialog box (Indents and Spacing → Special) offers First line and Hanging indent.
★ Exam Points:
• Open via Home → Paragraph launcher.
• Ruler markers also adjust indents.
• Hanging indent: Ctrl + T.

q: How do you access the ‘Find and Replace’ feature in MS Word?
exp:
Ctrl + H opens Find and Replace on the Replace tab.
★ Exam Points:
• Home → Editing → Replace.
• More >> shows Match case, Wildcards.
• Replace All changes every instance.

q: Which tab in MS Word contains the “Margins” option?
exp:
Layout (Page Layout) → Page Setup → Margins.
★ Exam Points:
• Preset margins: Normal, Narrow, Wide.
• Custom Margins opens Page Setup.
• Gutter adds binding space.

q: Which feature lets you create fillable forms in Word?
exp:
Content Controls (Developer tab) add text boxes, check boxes, drop-downs and date pickers to create forms.
★ Exam Points:
• Show Developer tab via File → Options → Customize Ribbon.
• Restrict Editing → Filling in forms protects the form.
• Legacy form fields also exist.

q: Which MS Word view displays the document as it would look in a web browser, fitting the text to the window width?
exp:
Web Layout shows how the document looks as a web page, wrapping text to the window.
★ Exam Points:
• Print Layout – as printed.
• Outline – heading structure.
• Read Mode – comfortable reading.

q: What is the purpose of the "AutoCorrect" feature in MS Word?
o: To automatically correct common typing errors as you type
exp:
AutoCorrect fixes common misspellings (teh → the), capitalisation and can insert symbols automatically.
★ Exam Points:
• Settings: File → Options → Proofing → AutoCorrect Options.
• (c) becomes ©.
• Custom entries can be added.

q: During the ____ operation, no duplicate copy of the text is made.
exp:
Cut removes the original and places it on the clipboard (moving it), so no duplicate remains in the document.
★ Exam Points:
• Copy leaves the original in place.
• Cut: Ctrl + X.
• Paste inserts clipboard content.

q: Which tool helps identify inconsistencies in formatting across a Word document?
exp:
The Style Inspector shows paragraph and text-level formatting so you can spot and clear inconsistent formatting.
★ Exam Points:
• Open from Styles pane → Style Inspector.
• Reveal Formatting: Shift + F1.
• Mark formatting inconsistencies option exists in Options.

q: Which option applies a gradient background to a page in MS Word?
exp:
Design → Page Color → Fill Effects → Gradient tab applies a gradient page background.
★ Exam Points:
• Page Color is in Page Layout tab in Word 2010.
• Fill Effects also offers texture, pattern, picture.
• Page colour is not printed by default.

q: Which button is used to set the size of letters (characters)?
exp:
The Font Size box/button in Home → Font sets the character size in points.
★ Exam Points:
• 1 point = 1/72 inch.
• Ctrl + ] / Ctrl + [ change size by 1 pt.
• Default size: 11 pt.

q: What does the “Inspect Document” feature check for?
exp:
Document Inspector finds and removes hidden data like comments, revisions, document properties and personal information.
★ Exam Points:
• File → Info → Check for Issues → Inspect Document.
• Use before sharing externally.
• Also checks hidden text and headers.

q: Which ribbon tab contains the options for changing the font, font size, and text color?
exp:
In MS Word (and Office apps), the Home tab houses the Font group containing options for changing the font family, font size, font color, Bold, Italic, Underline, Text Highlight Color, and Change Case.
★ Exam Points:
• Groups on the MS Word Home tab: Clipboard, Font, Paragraph, Styles, and Editing.
• Shortcut to open the full Font dialog box: Ctrl + D (or Ctrl + Shift + F).

q: The primary purpose of displaying toolbars with shortcut buttons, as described in the paragraph, is to achieve which of the following goals in document editing?
o: To provide detailed descriptions of complex commands and menus.
To manage file operations such as saving and opening documents securely.
To facilitate quicker and easier editing and formatting operations.
To allow the user to change the visual themes and background colors of the application window.
exp:
Displaying toolbars with graphical shortcut buttons (icons for Save, Bold, Copy, Print, etc.) allows users to execute frequent commands in a single click without drilling through multi-level menus—facilitating quicker and easier document editing and formatting.
★ Exam Points:
• In modern MS Office (2007+), traditional toolbars were consolidated into the tabbed Ribbon plus the customizable Quick Access Toolbar (QAT).
• Shortcut to collapse/expand the Ribbon in Word & Excel: Ctrl + F1.

q: Which of the following is used to format text into a superscript in MS Word?
exp:
In MS Word, pressing Ctrl + Shift + + (i.e., holding Ctrl + Shift and pressing the =/+ key) toggles Superscript formatting, raising selected text slightly above the baseline (e.g., x², 10th).
★ Exam Points:
• Shortcut for Subscript (e.g., H O) in MS Word: Ctrl + = 2 (without Shift).
• Both Superscript (x²) and Subscript (x ) buttons are lo- 2 cated in the Home tab > Font group.

q: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: - Delete paragraph D Ctrl + N - Numbering list
exp:
Checking each shortcut pair in MS Word: • Ctrl + F – Find text is correctly matched (opens the Navigation search pane). • Ctrl + H opens Find and Replace (not Highlight text). • Ctrl + D opens the Font dialog box (not Delete paragraph). • Ctrl + N creates a New blank document (not Numbering list).
★ Exam Points:
• Shortcut to delete an entire word to the left/right: Ctrl + Backspace / Ctrl + Delete.

q: The presence of the vertical ruler depends upon which 'View' mode is currently active within the application. Assuming a user currently can only see the horizontal ruler, even though the Ruler option has been turned on, which of the View modes might that person be using?
exp:
In word-processing / classic Office view modes, both horizontal and vertical rulers appear only in Print Layout / Page Layout View. When the user is in Normal View (called Draft View in newer Word versions), page top/bottom margins are suppressed, so only the horizontal ruler is displayed even when the Ruler checkbox is enabled.
★ Exam Points:
• MS Word View | Primary Purpose
• Print Layout | Default view; shows margins, headers/footers & printed page look
• Read Mode | Column screen layout optimized for distraction-free reading
• Web Layout | Displays document as a bor-derless webpage
• Outline / Draft | Hierarchy structure (Outline) or fast text editing without headers/images (Draft)

q: What is the keyboard shortcut used to centre-align a selected paragraph or line of text in MS Word?
exp:
In MS Word, pressing Ctrl + E center-aligns the selected paragraph or line horizontally between the left and right margins. (Ctrl + C is already reserved for Copy, so 'E' from center is used.)
★ Exam Points:
• Shortcut | Alignment Effect
• Ctrl + L | Align Left (default in MS Word)
• Ctrl + E | Center Align
• Ctrl + R | Align Right
• Ctrl + J | Justify (even left & right margins)

q: In Microsoft Word, what is the primary function of inserting a Non-Breaking Space (often created using the keyboard shortcut Ctrl + Shift + Spacebar)?
o: To automatically capitalize the first letter of the following word.
To ensure that the two words separated by the space remain on the same line, preventing an awkward line break between them.
To remove all formatting from the space, making it invisible to the user.
To force the entire paragraph to be justified and centered simultaneously.
exp:
In MS Word, inserting a Non-Breaking Space (shortcut Ctrl + Shift + Spacebar) glues two words together (e.g., Rs. 500, 100 km, Mr. Sharma) so Word will never split them across two lines at the end of a line.
★ Exam Points:
• When Show/Hide ¶ (Ctrl + Shift + 8) is enabled, a non-breaking space appears as a small degree-like circle (°) between words instead of a regular dot (·).
• Shortcut for a Non-Breaking Hyphen in MS Word: Ctrl + Shift + Hyphen (-).

q: To make a document private or restrict who can edit it, which tab should you use to find the Protect Document feature?
exp:
In MS Word, the Protect Document command (including Encrypt with Password, Restrict Editing, and Mark as Final) is located in Backstage View under File > Info > Protect Document.
★ Exam Points:
• Restrict Editing alone can also be accessed from the Review tab, while full file-open password encryption (AES) is under File > Info > Protect Document > Encrypt with Password.

q: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
exp:
Checking each shortcut pair: • Ctrl + P – Print document is correctly matched. • Ctrl + S = Save document (not Select all). • Ctrl + A = Select all text (not Save document). • Ctrl + F = Find text (not Format text).
★ Exam Points:
• Shortcut for Print Preview in MS Word/Excel: Ctrl + F2 (modern Office combines Print & Print Preview under Ctrl + P).

q: What is the standard file extension for a Word Document Template?
exp:
In modern MS Word (2007 and later), a reusable Word Document Template is saved with the standard XML-based file extension .dotx.
★ Exam Points:
• MS Word Extension | File Type
• .docx | Standard Word Document (2007+)
• .docm | Macro-Enabled Word Document
• .dotx | Word Document Template (no macros)
• .dotm | Macro-Enabled Word Template
• .doc / .dot | Legacy Word 97–2003 Document / Template

q: How can you change the case of selected text in MS Word?
exp:
In MS Word, pressing Shift + F3 cycles the capitalization of selected text sequentially through three states: lowercase → UPPERCASE → Capitalize Each Word (Title Case) (or Sentence case when a full sentence is selected).
★ Exam Points:
• The Ribbon command Change Case (Aa) in Home > Font offers 5 options: Sentence case, lowercase, UPPERCASE, Capitalize Each Word, and tOGGLE cASE.
• Ctrl + Shift + A converts selected text directly to ALL CAPS.

q: According to the provided text, which sequence of actions is the correct method for a user to manage the display of different toolbars in a standard menu-driven application interface?
o: Select Edit Toolbars command and then uncheck the name of the toolbar to add it.
Select Format Toolbars command and then click the name of an unchecked toolbar to hide it.
Select File Toolbars command and then check the name of a toolbar to display its shortcut buttons.
Select View Toolbars command and then click the name of an unchecked toolbar to display it.
exp:
In a classic menu-driven application interface (such as MS Word/Excel 2003 or LibreOffice), toolbars are toggled from the View menu: select the View > Toolbars command and click the name of an unchecked toolbar to check and display it (clicking a checked toolbar hides it).
★ Exam Points:
• Checked items (✓) next to toolbar names indicate currently visible toolbars; unchecked items are hidden.

q: A user has selected a section of text and wishes to increase its font size by one increment without navigating to the Font Size dropdown menu. Which shortcut achieves this action?
exp:
In MS Word, pressing Ctrl + Shift + > increases the selected text's font size by one preset increment on the Font Size dropdown list (e.g., 11 → 12 → 14 → 16 → 18 pt) without opening the menu.
★ Exam Points:
• MS Word Font Size Shortcut | Exact Change
• Ctrl + Shift + > | Increases font size to the next preset dropdown step
• Ctrl + Shift + < | Decreases font size to the previous preset dropdown step
• Ctrl + ] | Increases font size by exactly 1 point (1 pt)
• Ctrl + [ | Decreases font size by exactly 1 point (1 pt)

q: According to the standard procedure to open the 'Customize' dialog box, which of the following is the correct navigational hierarchy?
exp:
In classic menu-based Office / word-processing interfaces, opening the toolbar Customize dialog box follows the menu path View > Toolbars > Customize, allowing users to show/hide toolbars, add/remove command buttons, and assign keyboard shortcuts.
★ Exam Points:
• In modern Ribbon-based MS Word/Excel, customization is found via File > Options > Customize Ribbon / Quick Access Toolbar.

q: What is the shortcut key combination to make the selected text Bold?
exp:
In MS Word, MS Excel, MS PowerPoint, and rich-text editors, pressing Ctrl + B toggles Bold formatting on the selected text.
★ Exam Points:
• Core font style shortcuts: Ctrl + B = Bold; Ctrl + I = Italic; Ctrl + U = Underline; Ctrl + Shift + D = Double Underline (Word); Ctrl + Shift + W = Underline words only (not spaces).

q: If a Microsoft Word document is protected with a password, what is the procedure to modify (change or remove) that existing password?
o: Open the document >go to File Info> Protect Document Encrypt with Password clear the password and click OK.
Open the document Review Restrict Editing Stop Protection enter the password save the document.
Close the document rename the file extension to .zip edit internal files to remove password data rename back to.docx.
Open the document use "Save As" to save in plain text format the new file will have no password.
exp:
To change or remove an existing open-password on an encrypted MS Word document: 1. Open the document using the current password. 2. Go to File > Info > Protect Document > Encrypt with Password. 3. Clear the password box (to remove protection) or type a new password, click OK, and save the document.
★ Exam Points:
• MS Word encrypts password-protected .docx files using strong AES (128-bit / 256-bit) encryption—if the password is forgotten, Microsoft Word cannot recover it.

q: Which feature is used to copy the formatting (like font style, colour, and size) from one section of text and apply it to another section?
exp:
Format Painter (paintbrush icon in Home tab > Clipboard group) copies visual formatting—font family, size, colour, bold/italic, borders, and paragraph alignment—from selected text/cells and paints it onto another selection without copying the text itself.
★ Exam Points:
• Single-click Format Painter to apply formatting once; double-click Format Painter to lock it and apply formatting to multiple places (press Esc to turn off).
• MS Word keyboard shortcuts: Ctrl + Shift + C (Copy Formatting) and Ctrl + Shift + V (Paste Formatting).

q: What does the 'Shrink One Page' feature do in MS Word?
o: Moves all text to the second page
Shrinks the document to fit it onto one page
exp:
In MS Word, the Shrink One Page command (available via Customize Quick Access Toolbar > All Commands) automatically makes subtle adjustments to font sizes and spacing across the document to shrink a document that spills slightly onto an extra page so it fits neatly onto one fewer page (e.g., onto a single page).
★ Exam Points:
• It eliminates awkward 'trailing lines' where just 2–3 lines spill onto Page 2.

q: While setting a security layer for a Microsoft Word document using the "General Options" feature, which of the following statements regarding the password is FALSE based on the provided instructions?
o: The maximum length of the password is limited to 15 characters.
The password is case-sensitive and may include numerals, spaces, and symbols.
The "Password to open" must be retyped in a subsequent "Confirm Password" dialog box for verification.
As the password is typed, it is displayed as the actual characters to prevent mistyping.
exp:
When setting a document password under MS Word's Save As > Tools > General Options, typed password characters are masked as asterisks (*) or bullets (•) for shoulder-surf-ing security—they are NEVER shown in plain text. Hence, the statement that 'as the password is typed, it is displayed as the actual characters to prevent mistyping' is FALSE.
★ Exam Points:
• True rules in Word's General Options dialog: passwords are case-sensitive, can contain letters/numerals/spaces/symbols (up to 15 characters in classic General Options), and require re-entering in a Confirm Password box precisely because characters are masked!

q: What is the primary function of the non-printing End-of- Document Marker in Microsoft Word?
o: It marks the end of a paragraph and forces a page break when printing.
It ensures footnotes and endnotes are placed correctly at the bottom of the last page.
It signifies the absolute end of the document's editable content, preventing further text insertion.
It converts the document to read-only to prevent further edits.
exp:
Visible in MS Word's Draft / Normal View as a short thick horizontal black bar, the non-printing End-of-Document Markermarks the absolute end of the document's editable text stream—nothing can be typed or placed below this marker.
★ Exam Points:
• Unlike a paragraph mark (¶), the End-of-Document Marker cannot be deleted.

q: How can you insert a footnote in Microsoft Word?
exp:
On the MS Word Ribbon, a footnote is inserted via References > Insert Footnote (in the Footnotes group). (Note: Question asks the Ribbon path, and Option 1 gives the exact menu path; the keyboard shortcut in Word is Alt + Ctrl + F.)
★ Exam Points:
• Footnotes appear at the bottom of the current page, whereas References > Insert Endnote (Alt + Ctrl + D) places notes at the end of the document.

q: The default line spacing for a new document in modern versions of MS Word (after the first paragraph) is typically:
exp:
Starting with MS Word 2007 (Word 2007/2010 classic modern default; 1.08 in newer 2013+ Calibri/Aptos templates, tested across SSC/DP exams as 1.15), Microsoft changed the default line spacing of a new document from legacy 1.0 (Single) to 1.15 lines (with extra space after each paragraph) for cleaner readability.
★ Exam Points:
• Quick line-spacing shortcuts in MS Word: Ctrl + 1 = Single (1.0); Ctrl + 2 = Double (2.0); Ctrl + 5 = 1.5 line spacing.

q: A user wants to quickly link a piece of text (e.g., "Click Here") to an external website URL within their MS Word document. Which single keyboard shortcut key combination should they use to open the Insert Hyperlink dialog box?
exp:
Across MS Word, MS Excel, MS PowerPoint, Outlook, and modern editors, pressing Ctrl + K opens the Insert Hyperlink dialog box to attach a web URL, file link, or bookmark to selected text.
★ Exam Points:
• To follow a hyperlink inside an editable MS Word document, hold Ctrl + Left-Click on the linked text.

q: What is the shortcut to insert a hyperlink in Word?
exp:
In MS Word, pressing Ctrl + K opens the Insert Hyperlink dialog box to link selected text or an image to a webpage URL, file, email address, or document bookmark.
★ Exam Points:
• Compare: Ctrl + H = Find & Replace; Alt + H = Activates the Home tab KeyTips on the Ribbon.

q: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
exp:
Checking each shortcut pair in MS Word: • Ctrl + L – Left align text is correctly matched. • Ctrl + R = Right align text (not Remove formatting, which is Ctrl + Spacebar). • Ctrl + J = Justify paragraph (not Jump to header). • Ctrl + T = Create Hanging Indent in Word (not Table insert).
★ Exam Points:
• Shortcut | Alignment Effect
• Ctrl + L | Align Left (default in MS Word)
• Ctrl + E | Center Align
• Ctrl + R | Align Right
• Ctrl + J | Justify (even left & right margins)

q: __________ are used in Word 2016 for reduced size versions of images.
exp:
In MS Word 2016 (e.g., in the Navigation Pane > Pages tab and media galleries), small reduced-size preview versions of pages or images that help users scan and jump through visual content quickly are called Thumbnails.
★ Exam Points:
• Thumbnails consume minimal screen space and memory compared to rendering full-resolution images.

q: Which of the following allows you to link content from Excel into Word?
exp:
Object Linking and Embedding (OLE) (developed by Microsoft) allows an Excel table or chart to be embedded or dynamically linked inside an MS Word document (via Paste Special > Paste Link or Insert > Object) so updates in the source Excel workbook automatically reflect in Word.
★ Exam Points:
• Difference: Linking keeps a live connection to the external .xlsx file; Embedding stores an independent copy of the Excel object inside the .docx file.

q: Which of the following options is used to protect a Word document with a password?
o: File > Protect Document > Encrypt with Password
exp:
To lock a Microsoft Word document with an encryption password so unauthorized users cannot open it, navigate to Backstage View: File > Protect Document > Encrypt with Password (under File > Info).
★ Exam Points:
• Word uses modern AES encryption for password-protected .docx files.

q: What is extension of MS word file?
exp:
Among the four given options (.xlm, .doc, .png, .txt), .doc is the native file extension of an MS Word document (legacy Word 97–2003 format; modern Word 2007+ uses .docx).
★ Exam Points:
• Other options: .xlm = Excel 4.0 Macro sheet; .png = Portable Network Graphics image; .txt = unformatted plain text file (Notepad).

q: How do you insert a non-breaking space in Word?
exp:
In MS Word, pressing Ctrl + Shift + Space (Ctrl + Shift + Spacebar) inserts a non-breaking space that keeps two adjacent words (like 'Dr. Verma' or '25 December') together on the same line.
★ Exam Points:
• Do NOT confuse with Ctrl + Space (without Shift), which clears character formatting in MS Word, or Shift + Space in MS Excel, which selects the entire row!

q: In MS Word, which feature ensures that when text is typed, existing characters move forward instead of being overwritten by new characters?
exp:
In MS Word (and text editors), default Insert mode ensures that newly typed characters are inserted at the cursor while pushing existing characters to the right/forward without erasing them.
★ Exam Points:
• Contrast: In Overtype mode (toggled by the Insert key if enabled under File > Options > Advanced), newly typed characters overwrite and replace existing characters to the right of the cursor!

q: Which shortcut key is used for small-cap?
exp:
In MS Word, pressing Ctrl + Shift + K applies Small Caps formatting—rendering lowercase letters as smaller-sized capital letters while keeping true uppercase letters full height.
★ Exam Points:
• Compare MS Word case/underline shortcuts: Ctrl + Shift + K = Small Caps; Ctrl + Shift + A = ALL CAPS; Shift + F3 = Cycle Change Case; Ctrl + Shift + D = Double Underline.

q: Which one of the following buttons is used to make some text appear slanted or tilted?
exp:
Clicking the Italic button (I icon in Home > Font, shortcut Ctrl + I) formats selected text so the characters appear slightly slanted or tilted to the right for emphasis, book titles, or scientific names.
★ Exam Points:
• Compare: Bold (Ctrl + B) makes strokes thicker/darker; Underline (Ctrl + U) draws a line beneath text.

q: Which section manages version history in Word online?
exp:
In Word for the Web (Word Online) and modern desktop MS Word, Version History (allowing you to view, compare, and restore earlier saved snapshots of a cloud document) is accessed under File > Info > Version History.
★ Exam Points:
• Clicking the document title on the top Title Bar in Word/OneDrive also gives a quick shortcut to Version History.

q: Which MS Word feature allows you to automatically update the page number formatting if you add or delete pages?
exp:
Behind the scenes in MS Word, dynamic elements such as automatic page numbers ({ PAGE }), total page counts ({ NUMPAGES }), tables of contents, and auto-updating dates are powered by Field Codes—dynamic placeholders that recalculate automatically whenever pages are added or deleted.
★ Exam Points:
• Shortcuts for MS Word Field Codes: Alt + F9 toggles viewing Field Codes vs results; Ctrl + F9 inserts empty field braces { }; F9 updates selected fields.

q: __________ option is to protect your word document. You can set a password so that nobody can open your document, or you can lock the document so that nobody can edit your document.
exp:
In MS Word's Backstage View (File > Info, historically labeled Permissions / Protect Document), the Permissions section controls document security—allowing you to encrypt the file with an open-password so nobody can open it without authorization, or restrict editing/formatting so nobody can modify it.
★ Exam Points:
• Options inside Permissions / Protect Document include Encrypt with Password, Restrict Editing, Restrict Access, Add a Digital Signature, and Mark as Final.

q: Which key combination is used to open a new document in MS Word?
exp:
In MS Word, pressing Ctrl + N creates and opens a brand-new blank document immediately.
★ Exam Points:
• Compare: Ctrl + N = New blank document; Ctrl + O = Open an existing saved document; Ctrl + P = Print; Ctrl + S = Save.

q: When preparing a large document with many headings and subheadings, which combination of features is most effective for navigation and automatic table of contents creation?
o: Manually enlarging text and pressing Enter several times
Applying built-in Heading styles and using the Navigation pane
Using only bold formatting without any styles
Typing a list of contents manually without page numbers
exp:
When authoring a long multi-chapter report in MS Word, applying built-in Heading styles (Heading 1, Heading 2, Heading 3) combined with the Navigation Pane (Ctrl + F / View > Navigation Pane) lets you jump across chapters in one click, drag-and-drop sections to reorganize them, and generate an automatic Table of Contents instantly.
★ Exam Points:
• Manually bolding or enlarging text (Options 1 & 3) stays invisible to both the Navigation Pane's Headings view and automatic TOC!

q: Which key is used to move the cursor one word right?
exp:
In MS Word (and Windows text editors), holding Ctrl and pressing the Right Arrow key—Ctrl + Right arrow—jumps the text cursor forward one whole word to the right at a time (instead of one character).
★ Exam Points:
• MS Word Cursor Shortcut | Cursor Movement
• Left / Right Arrow | One character left / right
• Ctrl + Left / Ctrl + Right Arrow | One whole word left / right
• Up / Down Arrow | One line up / down
• Ctrl + Up / Ctrl + Down Arrow | One paragraph up / down
• Home / End | Start / End of current line

q: Which Microsoft Word feature allows you to create a shortcut to frequently used formatting options?
exp:
In Microsoft Word, recording a Macro (View > Macros > Record Macro) bundles multiple frequently used formatting steps (such as setting a specific font, size, colour, margins, and border together) and assigns them to a single custom keyboard shortcut or button.
★ Exam Points:
• Note distinction: The Quick Access Toolbar pins individual built-in commands as top-corner icons, whereas a Macro lets you create your own custom keyboard shortcut executing a multi-step formatting sequence in one stroke.

q: When creating text in MS Word, which method is best for selecting a sentence quickly using the mouse?
o: Double-click any word in the sentence
Drag the mouse from the first character to the last
exp:
Among the four pure mouse actions listed (without keyboard modifier keys): • Single-click only places the insertion point (selects nothing). • Double-click selects only a single word. • Manual character-by-character dragging is slow and error-prone. • Triple-click anywhere in the sentence/paragraph instantly selects the entire block cleanly in one rapid action.
★ Exam Points:
• Pro MS Word note: When a paragraph contains multiple sentences and you want to select only one specific sentence inside it, hold Ctrl + Single-click anywhere in that sentence!

q: Which mode is the primary display in MS word that would look the same when print?
exp:
In MS Word, Print Layout view is the default primary editing and display view that shows the document on screen— complete with margins, headers, footers, columns, and graphics—exactly as it will appear on printed paper (WYSIWYG).
★ Exam Points:
• Note distinction: Print Preview (Ctrl + F2 / Ctrl + P) is a pre-printing inspection screen in Backstage View rather than Word's primary everyday editing display mode.

q: Which tab in MS Word contains the options to change page orientation (Portrait/Landscape), margins and page size, which affect the presentation of the document on paper?
exp:
In MS Word, all paper-presentation settings—Orientation (Portrait/Landscape), Margins, Paper Size (A4/Letter), Columns, and Section Breaks—are grouped inside the Page Setup group on the Layout / Page Layout tab.
★ Exam Points:
• Named 'Page Layout' in Word 2007–2013 and concisely labeled 'Layout' in Word 2016/2019/2021/365.

q: In MS Word, which feature lets you create a list where each item starts with a dot or symbol rather than a number?
exp:
In MS Word (Home tab > Paragraph group), the Bullets feature creates an unordered list where each item begins with a graphical symbol—such as a solid dot (•), hollow circle, square, arrow, or checkmark—instead of sequential numbers or letters.
★ Exam Points:
• Quick keyboard shortcut to start a bulleted list in MS Word: type an asterisk (*) at the start of a line and press Spacebar (or press Ctrl + Shift + L).

q: Which tool is used that number, figure, symbol, or indicator that is smaller than the normal line of type and is set slightly above its like X²?
exp:
Formatting a character, number, or symbol smaller than normal body text and raising it slightly above the baseline— such as the exponent 2 in X² or ordinal 1st—uses the Superscript tool (Home > Font, shortcut Ctrl + Shift + +).
★ Exam Points:
• Contrast: Subscript (shortcut Ctrl + =) sets a smaller character slightly below the baseline, as in chemical formulas like H O or CO . 2 2

q: What is the file extension of MS Word?
exp:
Among the four options (.doc, .pdf, .html, .txt), .doc is the native file extension of Microsoft Word (used as default up to Word 2003, with .docx used in Word 2007 and newer).
★ Exam Points:
• Compare the other three extensions: .pdf = Portable Document Format; .html = HyperText Markup Language webpage; .txt = unformatted plain text file.

q: In MS Word, which feature should be used to ensure that headings printed at the top of each page (such as document title and page number) are the same throughout the document?
exp:
In MS Word, the Header and Footer feature (Insert tab > Header & Footer group) lets you place repeating content— such as a document title, chapter name, company logo, date, and automatic page numbers—in the top margin (Header) and bottom margin (Footer) consistently across every page.
★ Exam Points:
• Double-clicking inside the top or bottom margin of any page in Print Layout view opens the Header & Footer editing mode directly (press Esc to exit).
• Checking Different First Page suppresses the header/footer on a cover/title page.

q: Which option on the Home tab in MS Word is used to change all letters of selected text from small letters to capital letters or vice versa?
exp:
On MS Word's Home tab (in the Font group), clicking the Change Case (Aa) button converts selected text between lowercase, UPPERCASE, Sentence case, Capitalize Each Word, and tOGGLE cASE.
★ Exam Points:
• Keyboard shortcut to cycle Change Case in MS Word: Shift + F3.

q: Which tool moves the cursor to the next line when reaching the end without requiring you to press Enter?
exp:
In word processors (like MS Word) and text editors, Word Wrap is the automatic text-flow feature that moves the cursor and overflowing word onto the next line automatically upon reaching the right margin without requiring you to press the Enter key at the end of every line.
★ Exam Points:
• In MS Word, Word Wrap is always active automatically; you press Enter only when you want to start a new paragraph!
• (In MS Excel cells, the analogous feature for multi-line cell display is Wrap Text on the Home tab.)

q: When a document is wider than the screen, which control lets you move left and right to view hidden parts?
exp:
The horizontal scroll bar at the bottom scrolls content sideways.
★ Exam Points:
• Vertical scroll bar moves up/down.
• Shift + mouse wheel scrolls horizontally.
• Zoom out to see more.

q: In MS Word, which shortcut moves the insertion point directly to the beginning of the document?
exp:
Ctrl + Home jumps to the start of the document; Ctrl + End to the end.
★ Exam Points:
• Home – start of the current line.
• Ctrl + Page Up – previous page/object.
• Shift + Ctrl + Home selects to start.

q: Which key combination deletes the whole word immediately to the right of the insertion point?
exp:
Ctrl + Delete removes the next word.
★ Exam Points:
• Ctrl + Backspace removes the previous word.
• Shift + Delete cuts the selection.
• Delete removes one character.

q: Which feature automatically changes typed text like "teh" into "the" as soon as you press the Spacebar?
exp:
AutoCorrect replaces common typos and abbreviations as you type.
★ Exam Points:
• Options in File → Options → Proofing.
• You can add your own entries.
• Undo (Ctrl + Z) reverses a correction.

q: A student wants all month names in a selected paragraph to appear in ALL CAPS. Which is the best quick approach?
o: Use the Change Case command on the selected paragraph and choose UPPERCASE
exp:
Change Case → UPPERCASE converts the selection at once.
★ Exam Points:
• Shift + F3 cycles cases.
• Ctrl + Shift + A applies All Caps formatting.
• Change Case is in Home → Font.

q: While copying text from a website into Word, a user wants the pasted text to match the current document's font and style. Which paste option should be chosen?
exp:
Merge Formatting adopts the destination's formatting while keeping basic emphasis like bold/italic.
★ Exam Points:
• Keep Text Only strips all formatting.
• Keep Source keeps web formatting.
• Paste Options button appears after pasting.

q: Which key combination deletes the entire word to the left of the insertion point in one step?
exp:
Ctrl + Backspace deletes the previous word; Ctrl + Delete deletes the next word.
★ Exam Points:
• Backspace deletes one character left.
• Delete removes one character right.
• Ctrl + Z undoes deletion.

q: Which list on the File tab shows recently opened documents for quick reopening?
exp:
File → Open → Recent lists recently used documents; items can be pinned.
★ Exam Points:
• Number shown is configurable.
• Also shows recent folders.
• Pinned items stay at top.

q: What is a main advantage of word processors over handwritten documents?
o: Word processors allow easy editing, formatting, copying and printing of the same content
exp:
Content can be corrected, reformatted, saved and printed many times without rewriting.
★ Exam Points:
• Spell check improves accuracy.
• Templates speed up work.
• Files can be shared electronically.

q: Why is it useful to understand export options such as "Save as PDF" or "Export to PDF/XPS"?
o: They create high-quality fixed-layout versions for printing or sharing while keeping the editable Word file
exp:
Exporting to PDF/XPS creates a non-editable, layout-preserving copy; the .docx stays editable.
★ Exam Points:
• XPS is Microsoft's fixed-layout format.
• PDF is universal.
• Hyperlinks can be preserved in PDF.

q: Which view is designed for comfortable on-screen reading with columns and larger text, hiding editing tools?
exp:
Read Mode (Full Screen Reading in 2010) shows pages like a book for easy reading.
★ Exam Points:
• Esc exits Read Mode.
• Arrows turn pages.
• Editing is limited.

q: You need to share a Word document so recipients can read but not easily edit it. Which approach is most appropriate?
o: Keep it as .docx and rely on honesty
Convert it to PDF and optionally mark the original Word document as final
exp:
PDF preserves layout and is not easily editable; Mark as Final discourages editing of the original.
★ Exam Points:
• Save As → PDF.
• Restrict Editing gives stronger control.
• PDF/A for archiving.

q: When you start Word and see a screen offering Blank document and recently used files, what is this screen called?
exp:
The Start screen (Office 2013+) appears at launch with templates and recent files.
★ Exam Points:
• Can be disabled in Options.
• Backstage view is File tab.
• Recent list helps reopen files.

q: When a Word document is opened on a device with different fonts installed, why might the layout look different?
o: Font availability affects how text is rendered and substituted
exp:
If a font is missing, Word substitutes another font with different widths, shifting the layout.
★ Exam Points:
• Embed fonts via File → Options → Save.
• PDF preserves fonts.
• Use common fonts for sharing.

q: What best describes word processing?
o: Entering, editing, formatting and saving text using a computer program
Entering text without formatting or saving
exp:
Word processing is creating, editing, formatting, saving and printing text documents using software like MS Word.
★ Exam Points:
• Examples: MS Word, Google Docs, Writer.
• WYSIWYG display.
• Spell check, mail merge are features.

q: A document is saved locally and synchronised to a cloud service. Later the local copy is accidentally deleted. Why might it still be recoverable?
o: Cloud synchronisation keeps a copy on the remote service that can be downloaded again
exp:
Cloud services like OneDrive/Google Drive keep their own copy (and recycle bin/version history).
★ Exam Points:
• OneDrive keeps deleted files for 30 days.
• Version history restores older versions.
• Follow 3-2-1 backup rule.

q: Which statement best describes the relationship between a paragraph mark (¶) and formatting in MS Word?
o: Paragraph marks do not affect formatting
Many formatting settings of a paragraph are stored with the paragraph mark
They exist only in printed output
exp:
Paragraph formatting (alignment, spacing, indents, style) is stored in the ¶ mark at the end of the paragraph.
★ Exam Points:
• Deleting ¶ merges paragraphs and formatting.
• Show marks: Ctrl + Shift + 8.
• Section formatting is stored in section breaks.

q: Why are shortcuts such as Ctrl + S, Ctrl + O and Ctrl + P useful?
o: They allow quick access to common commands without navigating menus, saving time
exp:
Keyboard shortcuts speed up frequent tasks.
★ Exam Points:
• Ctrl + S save; Ctrl + O open; Ctrl + P print.
• Alt shows KeyTips for Ribbon.
• Custom shortcuts can be assigned.

q: Which paragraph option prevents a single line of a paragraph from being left alone at the top or bottom of a page?
exp:
Widow/Orphan control (on by default) avoids single lines stranded on a page.
★ Exam Points:
• Widow – last line alone at top of page.
• Orphan – first line alone at bottom.
• Paragraph → Line and Page Breaks tab.

q: Which operation adds content from the clipboard to your MS-Word 2010 document?
exp:
Paste (Ctrl + V) inserts the clipboard content at the cursor.
★ Exam Points:
• Paste options: Keep Source Formatting, Merge Formatting, Keep Text Only.
• Paste Special: Ctrl + Alt + V.
• Copy places content on the clipboard.

q: After creating a table in MS-Word 2010, to insert a new row below a particular row, which option is used?
exp:
Table Tools → Layout → Insert Below adds a row beneath the current row.
★ Exam Points:
• Tab in the last cell adds a row at the end.
• Insert Above adds a row above.
• Delete → Delete Rows removes rows.

q: Which keyboard shortcut moves to the previous cell in a row of a table in MS-Word 2010?
exp:
Shift + Tab moves to the previous cell; Tab moves to the next cell.
★ Exam Points:
• Ctrl + Tab inserts a tab inside a cell.
• Alt + Home – first cell of the row.
• Alt + End – last cell of the row.

q:
State whether the statements about MS-Word 2010 are true or false.
(i) In Landscape orientation, the height of a page is larger than its width.
(ii) In Portrait orientation, the width of a page is larger than its height.
exp:
Both are reversed: Landscape is wider than tall, Portrait is taller than wide.
★ Exam Points:
• Portrait is default.
• Orientation is in Layout/Page Layout tab.
• A4 size: 210 × 297 mm.

q: The distance between the written text and the edge of the paper in MS-Word 2010 is called ____.
exp:
Margins are the blank spaces between text and the paper edges (top, bottom, left, right).
★ Exam Points:
• Default margins: 1 inch (2.54 cm) all sides.
• Gutter margin is extra space for binding.
• Layout → Margins.

q: The keyboard shortcut to close an MS-Word 2010 document is ____.
exp:
Ctrl + W (or Ctrl + F4) closes the current document.
★ Exam Points:
• Alt + F4 closes the Word window.
• Ctrl + Z – undo.
• Ctrl + X – cut.

q: What is the maximum number of columns that can be inserted in a table in MS-Word?
exp:
A Word table can contain up to 63 columns.
★ Exam Points:
• Rows are practically unlimited.
• Insert → Table → Insert Table dialog.
• Excel has 16,384 columns.

q:
State whether the statements are true or false.
(i) In MS Word, all paragraphs can have right alignment.
(ii) In MS Word, all paragraphs cannot have the same hanging indent.
exp:
Any formatting, including right alignment or the same hanging indent, can be applied to all paragraphs at once, so (i) is true and (ii) is false.
★ Exam Points:
• Select all (Ctrl + A) then apply formatting.
• Hanging indent: Ctrl + T.
• Right align: Ctrl + R.

q: Which statement about an MS Word table is FALSE?
o: The first and last cells of a table can be merged.
Alternate cells of a row or column cannot be merged.
Two or more consecutive cells of a column can be merged.
Two or more consecutive cells of a row can be merged.
exp:
Only adjacent cells forming a rectangle can be merged; the first and last cells of a table are not adjacent.
★ Exam Points:
• Merge: Table Layout → Merge Cells.
• Eraser tool removes borders to merge.
• Split Cells does the opposite.

q: Which of the following is NOT an option in the ‘Table’ menu of the ‘Insert’ tab in MS-Word 2007?
exp:
The Table menu offers Insert Table, Draw Table, Convert Text to Table, Excel Spreadsheet and Quick Tables; there is no Remove Header.
★ Exam Points:
• Quick Tables are pre-formatted tables (calendars etc.).
• Excel Spreadsheet embeds a sheet.
• Header Row option is in Table Design.

q: In MS-Word 2010, a large capital letter used as a decorative element at the beginning of a paragraph is called ____.
exp:
Drop Cap (Insert → Text group) makes the first letter large, spanning several lines.
★ Exam Points:
• Options: Dropped, In margin.
• Common in magazines and books.
• Default lines to drop: 3.

q: In MS-Word 2010, the Page Down key is used to ____.
o: move the cursor one line down
move the cursor to the last page
move the cursor one paragraph down
move the cursor one screen down
exp:
Page Down scrolls the view (and cursor) down by one screen.
★ Exam Points:
• Ctrl + Page Down – next page (browse object).
• Ctrl + End – end of document.
• Down arrow – one line down.

q: In MS-Word, the function key F12 is used to ____.
o: open the Save As dialog box
exp:
F12 opens the Save As dialog box.
★ Exam Points:
• Shift + F12 – Save.
• Ctrl + F12 – Open.
• Ctrl + Shift + F12 – Print.

q: A table in MS-Word 2010 can have unlimited rows and a maximum of ____ columns.
exp:
Word tables support a maximum of 63 columns.
★ Exam Points:
• Excel has 16,384 columns.
• PowerPoint table max: 75 rows × 75 columns.
• Insert Table grid shows up to 10 × 8.

q: Which of the following is NOT a word processor?
exp:
Chrome is a web browser; the others are used to type and edit text.
★ Exam Points:
• Notepad is a basic text editor.
• Google Docs is an online word processor.
• WordStar was an early word processor.

q: Which shortcut is used in MS-Word 2010 to open the File tab (Backstage view)?
exp:
Alt + F opens the File tab/Backstage view.
★ Exam Points:
• Alt + H – Home tab.
• Alt + N – Insert tab.
• Alt + P – Page Layout tab.

q: Which shortcut key is used to apply superscript formatting in MS-Word 2010?
exp:
Ctrl + Shift + = (the plus key) toggles superscript.
★ Exam Points:
• Subscript: Ctrl + =.
• Ctrl + Shift + < / > shrink/grow font.
• Superscript example: E = mc².

q: In MS-Word 2010, which shortcut key deletes one word to the right?
exp:
Ctrl + Delete deletes the word to the right of the cursor; Ctrl + Backspace deletes the word to the left.
★ Exam Points:
• Delete removes one character to the right.
• Backspace removes one character to the left.
• Alt + Backspace = undo in many apps.

q: In MS-Word 2010, which key deletes one character to the left of the cursor?
exp:
Backspace deletes the character to the left; Delete removes the character to the right.
★ Exam Points:
• Ctrl + Backspace deletes the previous word.
• Ctrl + Delete deletes the next word.
• Shift + Delete cuts the selection.

q: Which of the following is NOT a document processing (word processing) software?
exp:
OpenOffice Impress is presentation software (like PowerPoint); the others are text/word processors.
★ Exam Points:
• OpenOffice Writer is its word processor.
• Calc is the spreadsheet.
• Base is the database program.

q: Which of the following effects is NOT available in the MS-Word 2010 Font dialog box?
exp:
There is no "Fancy" effect; font styles are Regular, Italic, Bold, Bold Italic and effects include Subscript, Superscript, Strikethrough, etc.
★ Exam Points:
• Ctrl + D opens the Font dialog.
• Subscript: Ctrl + =.
• Hidden text is also a font effect.

q: Which shortcut key is used in MS-Word 2010 to apply double line spacing to a paragraph?
exp:
Ctrl + 2 applies double spacing; Ctrl + 5 gives 1.5 spacing; Ctrl + 1 single spacing.
★ Exam Points:
• Ctrl + 0 adds/removes 12 pt space before a paragraph.
• Line spacing options are in Home → Paragraph.
• Default Word 2013+ spacing: 1.08.

q: In MS-Word 2010, if you press the Tab key within a table, the cursor moves to the next ____ of the table.
exp:
Tab moves to the next cell; Shift + Tab moves to the previous cell; Tab in the last cell adds a new row.
★ Exam Points:
• Ctrl + Tab inserts a tab character inside a cell.
• Alt + Shift + Up/Down moves rows.
• Table max columns in Word: 63.

q: Which feature in MS-Word 2010 draws a straight line through the middle of selected text?
exp:
Strikethrough draws a horizontal line through the text (abc), used to show deleted content.
★ Exam Points:
• Double strikethrough is in the Font dialog.
• Format Painter copies formatting.
• Strikethrough button is in Home → Font group.

q: Which shortcut key is used to align a paragraph to the right in MS-Word 2010?
exp:
Ctrl + R right-aligns the paragraph.
★ Exam Points:
• Ctrl + Shift + M reduces hanging indent.
• Ctrl + J justifies.
• Ctrl + L aligns left.

q: Which keyboard shortcut is equivalent to Ctrl + S for saving an open file in MS-Word 2010?
exp:
Shift + F12 performs Save, same as Ctrl + S.
★ Exam Points:
• F12 – Save As.
• Ctrl + F12 – Open.
• Shift + F5 – go to previous edit.

q: In MS-Word 2010, ____ cells means adjacent cells are thereafter treated as a single cell.
exp:
Merge Cells combines selected adjacent cells into one cell.
★ Exam Points:
• Merge Cells is in Table Tools → Layout.
• Split Cells divides a cell.
• Excel equivalent: Merge & Center.

q: Which alignment option distributes text evenly between the left and right margins in MS-Word 2010?
exp:
Justify aligns text to both margins by adjusting the spaces between words.
★ Exam Points:
• Shortcut: Ctrl + J.
• Newspapers commonly use justified text.
• Distributed alignment also spreads characters.

q: In MS-Word 2010, the ____ contains frequently used commands and can be customised.
exp:
The Quick Access Toolbar holds frequently used commands (Save, Undo, Redo) and can be customised.
★ Exam Points:
• QAT is above or below the Ribbon.
• Right-click any command → Add to QAT.
• Title bar shows document name.

q: When an MS-Word 2010 document is already open, which keyboard shortcut is used to open a new document?
exp:
Ctrl + N creates a new blank document in a new window.
★ Exam Points:
• Ctrl + Y – redo/repeat.
• Ctrl + X – cut; Ctrl + V – paste.
• Normal.dotm is the default template.

q: In MS-Word 2010, which key deletes a character to the right of the cursor?
exp:
The Delete key removes the character to the right of the cursor.
★ Exam Points:
• Backspace removes the character to the left.
• Ctrl + Delete removes the word to the right.
• Insert key toggles overtype mode (if enabled).

q: Which key is used to run spell check in MS-Word 2010?
exp:
F7 starts the Spelling & Grammar check.
★ Exam Points:
• F1 – Help; F5 – Go To; F3 – AutoText.
• Shift + F7 – Thesaurus.
• Alt + F7 – next spelling error.

q: Which shortcut key increases the font size to the next larger size in the Font Size list of MS-Word 2010?
exp:
Ctrl + Shift + > grows the font to the next size; Ctrl + Shift + < shrinks it.
★ Exam Points:
• Ctrl + ] increases size by 1 point.
• Ctrl + [ decreases size by 1 point.
• Ctrl + Shift + P selects the Font Size box.

q: Which feature in MS-Word 2010 types small letters or numbers set slightly above the normal line of text?
exp:
Superscript raises small characters above the baseline, e.g. x², 1st.
★ Exam Points:
• Superscript: Ctrl + Shift + =.
• Subscript (H₂O): Ctrl + =.
• Both are in Home → Font group.

q: The arrangement of data in rows and columns in MS-Word 2010 is called a ____.
exp:
A table organises data in rows and columns; each intersection is a cell.
★ Exam Points:
• Insert → Table.
• Convert Text to Table is also available.
• Table Styles format the table quickly.

q: Which keyboard shortcut in MS-Word 2010 changes paragraph spacing to 1.5-line spacing?
exp:
Ctrl + 5 applies 1.5 line spacing.
★ Exam Points:
• Ctrl + 1 – single.
• Ctrl + 2 – double.
• Ctrl + 0 – toggle 12 pt space before.

q: In MS-Word 2010, the keyboard shortcut Ctrl + X is used to ____.
o: cut the selected items to the clipboard
exp:
Ctrl + X cuts the selected item and stores it on the clipboard.
★ Exam Points:
• Ctrl + B – bold; Ctrl + A – select all.
• Paste: Ctrl + V.
• Spike (Ctrl + F3) collects multiple cuts.

q: Which shortcut key is used to align text to the left in MS-Word 2010?
exp:
Ctrl + L left-aligns the paragraph (default alignment).
★ Exam Points:
• Ctrl + Shift + L applies List Bullet style.
• Ctrl + M increases indent.
• Ctrl + Shift + M decreases indent.

q: What is the default font face in an MS-Word 2010 document?
exp:
Calibri (11 pt) was the default font from Word 2007 to 2021; Microsoft 365 now uses Aptos.
★ Exam Points:
• Word 2003 default: Times New Roman 12.
• Default heading font in 2010: Cambria.
• Aptos became default in 2023-24.

q: In paragraph formatting of MS-Word 2010, the shortcut Ctrl + Q is used to ____.
o: remove paragraph formatting from the highlighted paragraph
open the Apply Styles task pane
exp:
Ctrl + Q resets paragraph formatting (alignment, indents, spacing) to the style default.
★ Exam Points:
• Ctrl + Space removes character formatting.
• Ctrl + Shift + S opens Apply Styles pane.
• Ctrl + Shift + N applies Normal style.

q: The ____ displays the application name and document name in MS-Word 2010.
exp:
The title bar at the top shows the document name followed by the program name, e.g., Document1 – Microsoft Word.
★ Exam Points:
• Minimise, maximise and close buttons are at the right of the title bar.
• QAT sits on the title bar by default.
• Ribbon is below the title bar.

q: In ____ in MS-Word 2010, all lines other than the first line are indented.
exp:
A hanging indent keeps the first line at the margin and indents the following lines (used in bibliographies).
★ Exam Points:
• Shortcut: Ctrl + T (Ctrl + Shift + T to remove).
• First-line indent indents only the first line.
• Set using Ruler or Paragraph dialog.

q: MS-Word 2010 opens a new document with the temporary name ____.
exp:
New Word documents are named Document1, Document2, etc. until saved.
★ Exam Points:
• Excel: Book1.
• PowerPoint: Presentation1.
• Access requires naming at creation.

q: Which of the following is NOT present in the Quick Access Toolbar by default in MS-Word 2010?
exp:
Default QAT buttons are Save, Undo and Redo/Repeat; Cut is in Home → Clipboard.
★ Exam Points:
• Cut shortcut: Ctrl + X.
• Customize QAT using its drop-down arrow.
• QAT can hold any Ribbon command.

q: In MS-Word 2010, which statement is incorrect about the Ruler?
o: It helps to change a line's indentation.
It helps to change font styles.
It helps to control page margins.
exp:
The Ruler is used for tabs, indents and margins; font styles are changed from the Font group.
★ Exam Points:
• Show Ruler: View → Ruler.
