• Horizontal and vertical rulers exist.
• Indent markers: first-line, hanging, left, right.

q: The ____ tab in MS-Word 2010 is the default tab that appears when you open a document.
exp:
The Home tab, with Clipboard, Font, Paragraph, Styles and Editing groups, is active by default.
★ Exam Points:
• Alt + H activates Home.
• Ribbon introduced in Office 2007.
• Home has the most frequently used commands.

q: In MS-Word 2010, when you cut text, it is stored on the ____.
exp:
Cut or copied items are temporarily stored on the clipboard until pasted.
★ Exam Points:
• Office Clipboard holds 24 items.
• Windows clipboard history: Windows + V.
• Paste: Ctrl + V.

q:
Which is true about ‘Styles’ in MS-Word 2010?
(i) Styles are named definitions of how text should appear.
(ii) Styles allow quick formatting changes throughout the document.
exp:
A style is a named set of formatting; changing the style updates all text using it.
★ Exam Points:
• Built-in styles: Normal, Heading 1, Title.
• Headings styles help create Table of Contents.
• Ctrl + Alt + 1 applies Heading 1.

q:
Which is a valid page orientation in MS-Word 2010?
(i) Landscape (ii) Portrait
exp:
Word supports Portrait (vertical) and Landscape (horizontal) orientation in Page Layout → Orientation.
★ Exam Points:
• Portrait is the default.
• Different sections can have different orientations.
• Landscape is wider than tall.

q: In the context of MS Word, what does the term "word processing" primarily mean or describe as a digital activity?
o: Manually writing text on paper with a pen
Entering, editing, formatting and saving text using a computer program
Entering, editing, text without formatting and without saving text using a computer program
Only creating slides with pictures and animations
exp:
Word processing refers to the digital creation, manipulation, and storage of text using software like MS Word. It allows users to perform various operations including typing, revis-ing, applying visual formatting, and saving documents elec-tronically.
★ Exam Points:
• Word processors replaced traditional typewriters by providing editing flexibility.
• Standard features include spell check, text formatting, and document layout controls.
• MS Word is one of the most widely used word processing software applications.
• Output can be saved in various formats like .docx and .pdf.

q: Which statement best explains why using shortcuts such as Ctrl+S, Ctrl+O and Ctrl+P in MS Word is valuable for efficiency?
o: Keyboard shortcuts allow quick access to common commands without navigating menus, saving time during frequent operations
To indicate that the document is considered complete and discourage further editing
exp:
Keyboard shortcuts streamline document editing by executing commands directly through keystrokes. This reduces reliance on mouse navigation through ribbon tabs, leading to increased productivity and faster workflow during repetitive tasks.
★ Exam Points:
• Ctrl + S saves the active document.
• Ctrl + O opens the file picker/open document dialog.
• Ctrl + P opens the Print preview and printing interface.
• Using keyboard shortcuts reduces operational fatigue caused by switching between keyboard and mouse.

q: Which keyboard shortcut closes the current document but does not quit the Word application, provided no other documents are open?
exp:
The Ctrl + W shortcut (as well as Ctrl + F4) closes the active document window in MS Word without shutting down the entire program instance. If changes were made, it prompts the user to save before closing.
★ Exam Points:
• Alt + F4 closes the active application window entirely, quit-ting the Word program.
• Ctrl + W is standard across many Windows programs, including closing tabs in web browsers.
• Ctrl + N opens a brand new blank document.
• Ctrl + S saves the current file before closing.

q: In MS Word, what action or change does the Redo command mainly perform on recently undone work?
o: It repeats an action that was undone using Undo
It converts the document to PDF format
It closes the current document immediately
It removes all formatting from the text
exp:
The Redo command reverses a previously executed Undo action, restoring the document to the state it was in before the Undo operation was applied.
★ Exam Points:
• The keyboard shortcut for Redo is Ctrl + Y (or Alt + Shift + Backspace).
• The keyboard shortcut for Undo is Ctrl + Z.
• Redo is only available immediately after an Undo command has been performed.
• The Redo button is located on the Quick Access Toolbar at the top of the Word interface.

q: When sharing a Word document that must not be altered by recipients, which sequence of actions is most appropriate?
o: The document is kept in .docx format and depends on the recipients' honesty not to make any edits. This approach does not enforce restrictions
Convert it to PDF and optionally mark the original Word document as final
Save it as plain text and tell recipients to reformat it
exp:
Converting a document to PDF (Portable Document Format) locks the visual elements and structure, making casual editing difficult while preserving formatting across all devices. Marking as final adds a read-only metadata flag.
★ Exam Points:
• PDF was created by Adobe to ensure consistent document rendering on any device.
• The Mark as Final feature disables typing, editing commands, and proofing marks in Word.
• Word documents can be saved as PDF using File -> Save As / Export -> Create PDF/XPS.
• Password protection and restrict editing options can also be applied under the Review / Info menu.

q: Which option in the Paragraph dialog allows only the first line of a paragraph to be indented from the left margin, leaving the rest aligned with the margin?
exp:
A First Line Indent offsets only the initial line of a paragraph to the right by a specified distance, leaving all subsequent lines flush with the standard left page margin.
★ Exam Points:
• Hanging Indent does the opposite: the first line stays at the margin while subsequent lines are indented.
• Shortcut to apply a Hanging Indent is Ctrl + T.
• Indents can be quickly set using the Ruler or via the Paragraph Dialog Box.
• Pressing the Tab key at the start of a paragraph creates a default 0.5-inch First Line Indent.

q: When you start the program and see a screen that offers choices such as Blank document and recently used files, what is this first screen commonly called?
exp:
The Start Screen appears when opening Microsoft Office applications like Word or Excel, providing immediate access to new templates, a Blank document, and recent files without opening the full editing interface directly.
★ Exam Points:
• The Start screen can be bypassed in Options > General settings.
• It provides direct access to the Backstage View via the File menu.
• Users can pin frequent documents on this screen for permanent fast access.
• It features pre-configured online templates for invoices, resumes, and reports.

q: Which window arrangement feature lets you divide a single document window into two panes so that you can scroll and edit different parts of the same document at the same time?
exp:
The Split feature located under the View tab divides the current document window into two independent panes. Edits made in either pane automatically reflect across the entire document in real-time.
★ Exam Points:
• Access split controls via View tab > Window group > Split.
• Keyboard shortcut to split/unsplit a Word document window is Alt + Ctrl + S.
• New Window opens a duplicate instance of the file in a separate window.
• View Side by Side compares two entirely different files simultaneously.

q: In MS Word, which command from the File menu would you use to produce a hard copy on paper?
exp:
The Print command (accessible via File -> Print or Ctrl + P) sends the document data to a physical printer device to produce a physical hard copy printout on paper.
★ Exam Points:
• Keyboard shortcut for Print is Ctrl + P.
• The Print interface includes a Print Preview window to check layout before printing.
• Settings allow selecting specific page ranges, orientation (Portrait/Landscape), and copies.
• Print to PDF creates a digital document file instead of a physical paper copy.

q: When a Word document is opened on a device with different fonts installed, why might the layout look slightly different from the original?
o: Font availability affects how text is rendered and substituted
Word always rearranges text randomly on new devices
The printer settings delete fonts from the document
exp:
If a document utilizes a specific font that is missing on the viewing computer, MS Word performs font substitution. Because replacement fonts vary in character width and spacing metrics, text pagination and overall page layout shift slightly.
★ Exam Points:
• Font Embedding can be enabled under File Options -> Save to store fonts within the .docx file.
• Standard universal fonts (e.g., Arial, Times New Roman) reduce font substitution problems across systems.
• Converting documents to PDF format preserves original typography visually across all machines.
• Font substitution can alter character spacing, line wrapping, and overall document page counts.

q: Which action in MS Word can help avoid overwriting a master document while experimenting with major formatting changes?
o: Close without saving and reopen later
Use Save As to create a separate experimental copy
exp:
Using the Save As feature allows users to duplicate the original document under a different filename. This pre-serves the primary master file intact while allowing safe testing and formatting experimentation on the new secondary copy.
★ Exam Points:
• Save As shortcut key is F12.
• Save (Ctrl + S) overwrites existing file content directly on the storage disk.
• Creating experimental copies prevents accidental data loss during structural revisions.
• Document versions can also be managed using cloud version history features.

q: What is the main advantage of using a word processor like MS Word instead of handwritten documents for creating long reports?
o: Entering, editing, text without formatting and without saving text using a computer program
Word processors allow easy editing, formatting, copying and printing of the same content
Word processors prevent storing documents on disk
Handwritten documents are automatically scanned by MS Word
exp:
Word processors like MS Word offer advanced digital capa-bilities including effortless text editing, dynamic formatting, copying, proofreading tools, and high-quality printing, which makes long document creation significantly faster and cleaner compared to handwriting.
★ Exam Points:
• Features built-in Spell Check (F7) and Grammar check tools.
• Supports non-destructive digital editing and automatic document recovery.
• Offers structured document styling via Styles gallery (Headings, Titles).
• Facilitates collaborative working through Track Changes and comments.

q: When preparing for important written work in MS Word, why is it useful to understand export options such as "Save as PDF" or "Export to PDF/XPS"?
o: Export options always delete the original file
They allow producing high-quality fixed-layout versions suitable for printing or online sharing while keeping the original editable Word file
They transform the document into an audio file automatically
Maintain one official shared file with Track Changes enabled, and store a separate personal copy for independent work
exp:
Exporting a Word document to PDF (Portable Document Format) locks fonts, styling, and structural layout, ensuring that the file appears identical across all devices, operating systems, and printers, while preserving the source .docx file for editing.
★ Exam Points:
• PDF was created by Adobe to preserve formatting across platforms.
• XPS is Microsoft's fixed-layout document format alternative to PDF.
• Exporting prevents accidental modifications during file distribution.
• PDF files can be opened natively in most modern web browsers.

q: Which option in MS Word allows the user to view a list of recently opened documents for quick access?
o: File tab Recent or Open section
exp:
Navigating to File tab > Open (or Recent) accesses the Backstage View menu, which tracks and displays a histori-cal list of recently modified or opened document paths for quick one-click reopening.
★ Exam Points:
• Part of the Microsoft Office Backstage View architecture.
• Frequently accessed files can be pinned to stay permanently at the top of the list.
• Users can clear unpinned recent files to protect privacy on shared computers.
• Displays the exact file storage location path under each filename.

q: Which of the following statements correctly explains what happens when the Delete key is pressed while text is selected in MS Word?
o: Only the last character of the selection is removed
The font size of the selection is increased
exp:
Pressing either the Delete or Backspace key when a block of text is active and highlighted in MS Word completely removes the entire selected block at once.
★ Exam Points:
• Removed text can be instantly restored using the Undo command (Ctrl + Z).
• Pressing Delete with no text selected deletes one character to the right of the cursor.
• Pressing Backspace with no text selected deletes one character to the left of the cursor.
• Typing any new character while text is selected replaces the selected text immediately.

q: A student accidentally minimized the Ribbon in MS Word, so that only the tab names like Home and Insert are visible. Which mouse action will quickly bring back the full Ribbon with its command groups?
exp:
Double-clicking any top tab (e.g., Home, Insert, View) toggles the expanded display state of the Microsoft Office Ribbon, switching between collapsed (tab names only) and pinned full view.
★ Exam Points:
• Keyboard shortcut to collapse or expand the Ribbon is Ctrl + F1.
• Clicking the pin icon at the bottom-right of the Ribbon pins it permanently.
• Collapsing the Ribbon expands the available document editing canvas area.
• Single-clicking a tab in collapsed state opens the ribbon temporarily until an action is performed.

q: Which part of the document window is mainly used to move quickly up and down through pages when the text is longer than the visible area on the screen?
exp:
The vertical scroll bar is located on the right side of the document window and allows users to navigate up and down through pages when content exceeds the visible screen area. It contains a scroll box (thumb) and arrows for precise or rapid vertical movement.
★ Exam Points:
• The horizontal scroll bar is used to shift the document view left and right when pages are wider than the screen.
• Dragging the scroll box allows faster navigation through lengthy multi-page documents.
• Clicking in the empty track above or below the scroll box scrolls the document page-by-page.
• Modern word processors also support mouse wheel scrolling and keyboard shortcuts like Page Up and Page Down for vertical navigation.

q: Dragging the small box inside the vertical scroll bar is most useful for which type of action in a long document?
o: Moving the insertion point one character
Jumping quickly to another page area
Changing the font size of selected text
Turning spell check on or off
exp:
Dragging the scroll box (thumb) inside the vertical scroll bar allows users to navigate rapidly through long documents and jump directly to specific distant page sections. The position of the scroll box reflects the relative location within the document.
★ Exam Points:
• The size of the scroll box is inversely proportional to document length—it gets smaller as document length increases.
• Dragging the scroll box changes the displayed view but does not move the text insertion point (cursor).
• Word displays ScreenTips showing the current page number as the scroll box is dragged in long documents.
• The Navigation Pane (Ctrl + F) provides another efficient method for jumping between document headings and pages.

q: In MS Word, which keyboard shortcut deletes the entire word to the left of the cursor in one step, instead of deleting it letter by letter?
exp:
Executing Ctrl + Backspace in MS Word removes the full word located directly to the left of the insertion point at once. This significantly improves editing efficiency when removing multi-letter words or preceding terms.
★ Exam Points:
• Ctrl + Delete erases the full word located immediately to the right of the insertion point.
• Standard Backspace deletes only one character to the left of the insertion point.
• Ctrl + Shift + Left Arrow selects the entire word to the left without immediately deleting it.
• Holding Ctrl while using directional arrow keys moves cursor focus word-by-word across text.

q: Which list on the File tab shows you a history of documents you have opened recently and lets you reopen them quickly without browsing folders again?
exp:
The Recent documents list located in the File menu (Backstage view) stores short-cut paths to recently opened workbooks. Users can click any file in this list to reopen it instantly without manually navigating through folder directories.
★ Exam Points:
• Clicking the pin icon next to a document in the Recent list pins it permanently to the top.
• The number of recent items shown can be configured in Excel Options > Advanced > Display.
• In recent Office versions, the Home tab in Backstage view combines Recent, Pinned, and Shared files.
• Hovering over a file entry displays its full file system storage path.

q: A user rolls the mouse wheel toward themselves while the pointer is over the document text. What usually happens to the visible part of the document?
o: The text scrolls down to later content
The text scrolls up to earlier content
The page switches to a new orientation
exp:
Rolling the mouse wheel backward (toward the user) triggers vertical downward scrolling, bringing later document content into view. Rolling the wheel forward moves the document upward toward earlier pages.
★ Exam Points:
• Holding Ctrl while rolling the mouse wheel adjusts the document Zoom level (in/out).
• Holding Shift while rolling the mouse wheel performs horizontal scrolling in supported software.
• Scrolling moves the viewport display without changing the active text cursor position.
• Mouse wheel scrolling speed can be customized within the operating system device settings.

q: If some text in MS Word has many different fonts, sizes and colors applied and you want to remove all formatting at once but keep the text, which command should you use?
exp:
The Clear All Formatting button (represented by an 'A' with an eraser icon on the Home tab) strips away all manual inline formatting, fonts, sizes, colors, and styles, resetting the selected text back to the document's default Normal style.
★ Exam Points:
• The keyboard shortcut for Clear All Formatting in MS Word is Ctrl + Spacebar for character formatting.
• Ctrl + Q resets paragraph formatting back to the default style parameters.
• Clear All Formatting leaves plain raw text intact while removing highlights, bold, italics, and custom fonts.
• It is located in the Font group on the Home tab.

q: Which cloud-related feature automatically saves changes to a document stored in an online location, reducing the risk of losing work if the computer closes unexpectedly?
exp:
AutoSave is a cloud-integrated feature in Microsoft 365 that continuously saves edits every few seconds as you work on files stored in OneDrive or SharePoint. This eliminates manual saving and prevents data loss during system crashes or power outages.
★ Exam Points:
• AutoSave toggle switch is located in the top-left corner of the title bar in Word, Excel, and PowerPoint.
• AutoSave requires files to be hosted on OneDrive or SharePoint rather than local hard drives.
• It tracks incremental edits, allowing real-time co-authoring and Version History navigation.
• AutoRecover is a separate local feature that periodically saves recovery files for unsaved local documents.

q: When a document is wider than the screen, which control lets you move left and right to see text that is currently hidden off the edge of the window?
exp:
The horizontal scroll bar is situated at the bottom of the document window and enables sideways panning. It allows users to scroll left and right when document pages or wide table columns extend beyond the horizontal boundaries of the display monitor.
★ Exam Points:
• The vertical scroll bar handles up and down movement through document pages.
• Zooming out (reducing zoom percentage) fits wider pages into the window, reducing the need for horizontal scrolling.
• Touchpads and tilt-wheel mice support horizontal panning gestures directly.
• Page Width view automatically scales document magnification so that horizontal margins fit the window bounds.

q: In MS Word, which keyboard shortcut is used to move the insertion point directly to the beginning of the document?
exp:
Pressing Ctrl + Home instantly relocates the cursor to the very start of an MS Word document (before the first character on page 1). Conversely, Ctrl + End moves the cursor directly to the end of the document.
★ Exam Points:
• Standard Home key moves the cursor to the beginning of the current line.
• Standard End key moves the cursor to the end of the current line.
• Ctrl + Shift + Home selects all text from the current cursor position up to the beginning of the document.
• Ctrl + Page Up moves the cursor to the top of the previous page.

q: Which key combination removes the whole word immediately to the right of the insertion point, helping you quickly delete the next word in a sentence?
exp:
Executing Ctrl + Delete erases the complete word positioned immediately to the right of the text cursor. It streamlines forward text editing by eliminating whole words ahead of the insertion point in a single keystroke.
★ Exam Points:
• Ctrl + Backspace deletes the full word positioned directly to the left of the insertion point.
• Standard Delete removes one character at a time to the right of the cursor.
• Shift + Delete in file explorer permanently deletes selected files bypassing the Recycle Bin.
• Ctrl + Shift + Right Arrow highlights the next word to the right for review before deletion.

q: Which button on the Home tab displays hidden items such as spaces, tab marks and paragraph marks so that a user can see the exact structure of the text?
exp:
The Show/Hide ¶ button (located in the Paragraph group on the Home tab) toggles non-printing formatting characters on screen. It reveals spaces (dots), tabs (arrows), and paragraph breaks (pilcrows ¶) to reveal document layout details.
★ Exam Points:
• The keyboard shortcut to toggle formatting marks in MS Word is Ctrl + Shift + 8 (or Ctrl + *).
• Non-printing formatting marks appear on screen for editing guidance but never print on paper.
• Revealing formatting marks helps troubleshoot extra spaces, unintended page breaks, and section alignment issues.
• Individual formatting symbols can also be toggled permanently via File > Options > Display.

q: Which feature will automatically change typed text like "teh" into the correctly spelled the as soon as you press the spacebar or punctuation?
exp:
AutoCorrect automatically replaces predefined mis-spellings, typos, and shorthand symbols (such as replacing "teh" with "the" or "(c)" with "©") the moment the user presses the spacebar or punctuation mark.
★ Exam Points:
• AutoCorrect entries can be customized under File > Options > Proofing > AutoCorrect Options.
• It automatically capitalizes the first letter of sentences and names of days.
• Spell Checker (F7) flags errors manually or underlines them with squiggly lines, whereas AutoCorrect fixes them instantly.
• Pressing Ctrl + Z immediately undoes an automated AutoCorrect substitution.

q: A student typed the name of a month in lowercase, and AutoCorrect changed it to start with a capital letter. Later the student decides that all month names in a selected paragraph should appear in ALL CAPS for emphasis. Which is the best approach for making this change quickly and consistently?
o: Retype every month name manually in capital letters
Turn off AutoCorrect and then re-enter the paragraph
Use the Change Case command on the selected paragraph and choose the UPPERCASE option
Apply a watermark with the month names across the page
exp:
The Change Case command (or Shift + F3 shortcut) instantly transforms text capitalization across highlighted selections into Sentence case, lowercase, UPPERCASE, Title Case, or TOGGLE cASE without manual retyping.
★ Exam Points:
• The Change Case button is located in the Font group on the Home tab in MS Word.
• Pressing Shift + F3 repeatedly cycles through UPPERCASE, lowercase, and Title Case for selected text.
• UPPERCASE option converts every selected letter into capital format instantly.
• Using Change Case prevents manual typing errors and maintains font styling.

q: The ‘Open’ command used to open an MS-Word 2010 document is found in which tab?
exp:
Open, Save, Save As, Print and New are in the File tab (Backstage view).
★ Exam Points:
• Ctrl + O – Open.
• Recent documents are listed in File → Recent.
• Backstage view introduced in Office 2010.

q: Which built-in function is used to generate random text in an MS-Word 2010 document?
exp:
Typing =rand() and pressing Enter inserts sample paragraphs; =rand(p,s) sets paragraphs and sentences.
★ Exam Points:
• =lorem() inserts Lorem Ipsum text.
• =rand.old() inserts "The quick brown fox…".
• Useful for testing formatting.

q: Which text formatting is achieved with the keyboard shortcut Ctrl + E in MS-Word 2010?
exp:
Ctrl + E centres the paragraph.
★ Exam Points:
• Ctrl + J justify; Ctrl + R right; Ctrl + L left.
• Alignment buttons are in Home → Paragraph group.
• Justify aligns text to both margins.

q: The ____ keyboard shortcut is used to cut the selected data in MS-Word 2010.
exp:
Ctrl + X removes the selection and places it on the clipboard.
★ Exam Points:
• Cut + Paste = moving text.
• Shift + Delete also cuts in Word.
• Ctrl + U underlines text.

q: Which option in MS-Word 2010 removes all formatting from the selection, leaving only plain text?
exp:
Clear All Formatting (Home → Font group) removes font and paragraph formatting, leaving plain Normal text.
★ Exam Points:
• Ctrl + Space removes character formatting.
• Ctrl + Q removes paragraph formatting.
• Its icon is an "A" with an eraser.

q: Which option is used to specify the number of prints required in the Print option of MS-Word 2010?
exp:
The Copies box sets how many copies of the document will be printed.
★ Exam Points:
• Collated option prints full sets in order.
• Orientation: Portrait or Landscape.
• Default paper size (India/UK): A4; (US): Letter.

q: Which option of the Draw Borders group in Table Tools Design tab is used to remove a specific border in a table to create merged cells in MS-Word 2010?
exp:
The Eraser tool erases individual cell borders, effectively merging adjacent cells.
★ Exam Points:
• Draw Table tool draws borders.
• Merge Cells is in the Layout tab.
• Split Cells divides one cell into many.

q: In MS-Word 2010, ____ is used to check all printing settings so the print is accurate without cuts or lost formatting.
exp:
Print Preview shows how the document will look on paper before printing.
★ Exam Points:
• Shortcut: Ctrl + F2 / Ctrl + P.
• From Word 2010, preview appears on the Print screen in Backstage view.
• Helps avoid wasting paper.

q: A file "Draft.docx" is renamed to "Final.docx" in the file system without opening it. What has changed inside the document?
o: Only the file name in the storage system has changed
exp:
Renaming changes only the name entry in the file system; contents remain the same.
★ Exam Points:
• Changing extension may break file association.
• Properties like modified date may stay.
• Use Save As to change format.

q: Which mouse action quickly selects a single word in a document?
exp:
Double-clicking selects a word; triple-clicking selects the paragraph.
★ Exam Points:
• Ctrl + click selects a sentence.
• Click in left margin selects a line.
• Ctrl + A selects all.

q: A user edits a shared report on a network location and saves over it without coordination. What is the risk?
o: Other contributors' work may be overwritten or lost
exp:
Uncoordinated saving can overwrite colleagues' changes.
★ Exam Points:
• Use co-authoring in OneDrive/SharePoint.
• Track Changes records edits.
• Keep version backups.

q: A user has several Word files named “Resume.docx” in different folders. What problem can this create and what is a good solution?
o: It can become unclear which version is current; adding dates or descriptive words to names helps
exp:
Identical names cause confusion; versioned names (Resume_2026_Jan.docx) solve it.
★ Exam Points:
• Use one master folder.
• Cloud version history also helps.
• Avoid "final_final" names.

q: Which mouse action selects an entire paragraph at once?
exp:
Triple-clicking selects the whole paragraph.
★ Exam Points:
• Double-click selects a word.
• Triple-click in left margin selects the whole document.
• Ctrl + click selects a sentence.

q: A person always saves essays on the desktop with names like “NewDocument1”. What problem may appear after some time?
o: It becomes difficult to identify which file contains which content/version
exp:
Generic names make it hard to find and distinguish documents later.
★ Exam Points:
• Use descriptive names.
• Organise in folders.
• Desktop clutter slows navigation.

q: In MS Word, what is the blinking vertical line that shows the current typing position called?
exp:
The insertion point (text cursor) marks where typed text will appear.
★ Exam Points:
• Mouse pointer becomes an I-beam over text.
• Arrow keys move the insertion point.
• Home/End move to line start/end.

q: In MS Word, which paragraph setting indents only the first line of each paragraph while other lines stay at the margin?
exp:
First Line indent (Paragraph → Special) moves only the first line inward.
★ Exam Points:
• Hanging indent is the opposite.
• Ruler top triangle sets first-line indent.
• Tab at paragraph start may also indent.

q: When you select text, a small semi-transparent bar with common formatting buttons (Bold, Font Size) appears near the pointer. What is it called?
exp:
The Mini Toolbar gives quick formatting options near the selection.
★ Exam Points:
• Introduced in Office 2007.
• Also appears on right-click.
• Can be disabled in Options.

q: A company wants printed reports to have a faint "Confidential" background, a thin decorative line around each page and consistent fonts and colours. Which combination achieves this?
o: Page Color, Drop Cap, Styles gallery
exp:
Watermark adds background text, Page Borders add a line around pages and Themes set consistent fonts and colours.
★ Exam Points:
• All are in the Design tab.
• Themes include colours, fonts, effects.
• Page Borders are in Borders and Shading dialog.

q: Which part of the MS Word window usually contains frequently used commands such as Save, Undo and Redo can be customised by the user?
exp:
The Quick Access Toolbar (QAT) sits at the top-left of the MS Word window (above or below the Ribbon) and provides single-click access to frequently used commands—by default Save, Undo, and Redo—independent of which Ribbon tab is currently active.
★ Exam Points:
• Users can add or remove any Word command on the QAT via the Customize Quick Access Toolbar drop-down arrow.
• Status Bar (bottom) shows page count, word count, proofing status, views, and zoom slider.
• Navigation Pane (Ctrl + F) allows browsing headings, pages, and search matches.

q: Which action with the mouse will quickly select a single word in a document without using the keyboard?
exp:
In MS Word (and standard text editors), double-clicking on any word with the left mouse button selects that entire single word instantly without using the keyboard.
★ Exam Points:
• Mouse Action in MS Word | Text Selected
• Double-click on a word | Selects that single word
• Triple-click inside a paragraph | Selects the entire paragraph
• Ctrl + Single-click anywhere in a sentence | Selects that entire sentence
• Single/Double/Triple-click in left selection bar | Selects line / paragraph / entire document

q: In MS Word, which statement correctly explains the purpose or function of the Quick Access Toolbar?
o: A bottom-fixed toolbar that stays visible while scrolling, clearly shows page numbers for moving between sections
A customisable toolbar that holds frequently used commands for easy access
A ribbon tab used only for inserting images
A bar that controls sound volume
exp:
In MS Word, the Quick Access Toolbar is a customizable toolbar positioned at the top-left of the application window that keeps frequently used commands (Save, Undo, Redo, Print Preview, etc.) accessible in one click regardless of the active Ribbon tab.
★ Exam Points:
• Pressing the Alt key displays keyboard KeyTips (numbers/letters) on Quick Access Toolbar icons and Ribbon tabs.
• The QAT can be placed either above the Ribbon (default) or below the Ribbon.

q: Which mouse action is used to select an entire paragraph at once when the insertion point is inside that paragraph?
exp:
In MS Word, triple-clicking anywhere inside a paragraph with the left mouse button instantly selects the entire paragraph.
★ Exam Points:
• Double-click selects a single word; Ctrl + Click selects a full sentence; Ctrl + A selects the entire document.
• Keyboard paragraph selection: Ctrl + Shift + Down Arrow / Up Arrow selects from the cursor to the end/start of the paragraph.

q: In MS Word, which paragraph setting should be used to move only the first line of each paragraph slightly inside from the left margin, while keeping the remaining lines aligned with the margin?
exp:
In MS Word's Paragraph settings (Home / Layout > Paragraph dialog > Indents and Spacing > Special), First line indent shifts only the first line of each paragraph inward from the left margin while keeping all subsequent lines flush with the margin.
★ Exam Points:
• Indent Type | Effect on Paragraph Lines
• First line indent | Indents ONLY the first line inward (standard book/essay paragraphs)
• Hanging indent (Ctrl + T) | First line stays at margin; all remaining lines indent inward (bibliographies)
• Left indent (Ctrl + M) | Moves the entire paragraph inward from the left margin
• Right indent | Moves the entire paragraph inward from the right margin

q: When you select text and then point to it, a small semitransparent bar with common formatting buttons like Bold and Font Size appears near the pointer. What is this feature called?
exp:
In MS Word (and Office apps), selecting text and hovering the pointer over it displays a compact, semi-transparent floating bar called the Mini toolbar containing quick character/paragraph commands like Bold, Italic, Font, Font Size, Text Highlight Color, and Bullets.
★ Exam Points:
• The Mini toolbar also appears automatically alongside the context menu whenever you right-click selected text.
• It can be enabled/disabled under File > Options > General > Show Mini Toolbar on selection.

q: A company wants its printed reports to show a faint Confidential background, a thin decorative line around each page, and a consistent set of fonts and colours for all headings and body text. Which combination of features would most efficiently achieve all three requirements?
o: Page color, Drop Cap, Styles gallery
exp:
All three requirements map directly to features on MS Word's Design tab: • Watermark adds faint ghosted text ('Confidential') behind page text, • Page Border draws a thin decorative frame around every page, and • Theme applies a coordinated set of heading/body fonts and colours across the whole report.
★ Exam Points:
• In MS Word 2013 and newer, Themes, Watermark, Page Color, and Page Borders are all grouped on the Design tab (in Word 2007/2010 they were on the Page Layout tab).

q: What is the purpose of the MS-Word keyboard shortcut Ctrl + F?
o: To open the Paragraph dialog box
exp:
Ctrl + F opens Find (Navigation pane) to search text in the document.
★ Exam Points:
• Ctrl + D opens the Font dialog box.
• Ctrl + A selects the whole document.
• Ctrl + H – Find and Replace.

q:
Identify whether the following statements are true or false.
(i) The MS-Word 365 Clipboard stores text and graphics you copy or cut, and lets you paste them into any other Office file.
(ii) Watermarks in MS-Word 365 are used to add a logo, image or identifying text behind page content, e.g. to show a document's status.
exp:
Both statements correctly describe the Office Clipboard (holds up to 24 items) and watermarks (Design tab → Watermark).
★ Exam Points:
• Office Clipboard holds up to 24 items.
• Common watermarks: CONFIDENTIAL, DRAFT, DO NOT COPY.
• Watermark is in Design tab (Page Layout tab in Word 2010).

q: Identify the INCORRECT statement about proofing in MS-Word 365.
o: The Spelling and Grammar tool identifies words with capitalisation problems.
To start a Spelling and Grammar check, press F7.
The Spelling and Grammar group has three separate options: Spelling, Grammar, and Spelling & Grammar.
The Word Count icon is available in the Review tab.
exp:
There is no group with three such options; Spelling & Grammar is a single command in the Proofing group of the Review tab.
★ Exam Points:
• F7 – Spelling & Grammar; Shift + F7 – Thesaurus.
• Red wavy underline = spelling; blue double underline = grammar (Word 2013+).
• Word Count: Ctrl + Shift + G.

q: Which keyboard shortcut opens the ‘Find and Replace’ dialog box in MS-Word?
exp:
Ctrl + H opens the Replace tab of the Find and Replace dialog box.
★ Exam Points:
• Ctrl + F – Find (Navigation pane).
• Ctrl + G – Go To.
• Ctrl + Alt + F – insert footnote.

q: Which of the following is NOT available under the ‘Tracking’ group of the ‘Review’ tab in MS-Word 365?
exp:
Previous/Next change are in the Changes group (with Accept and Reject); Tracking has Track Changes, markup view, Show Markup and Reviewing Pane.
★ Exam Points:
• Track Changes: Ctrl + Shift + E.
• Markup views: Simple, All, No Markup, Original.
• Compare is in the Compare group.

q: The MS-Word 365 shortcut key Ctrl + C is used to ____.
o: copy the selected content to the clipboard
paste the contents of the clipboard
exp:
Ctrl + C copies the selection to the clipboard without removing it.
★ Exam Points:
• Ctrl + V pastes; Ctrl + X cuts.
• Ctrl + Shift + C copies formatting.
• Ctrl + B bold; Ctrl + A select all.

q: The keyboard shortcuts for ‘Navigation’ and ‘Find and Replace’ in Microsoft Word are ____.
exp:
Ctrl + F opens the Navigation pane (Find) and Ctrl + H opens Find and Replace.
★ Exam Points:
• Ctrl + N – new document.
• Ctrl + R – right align.
• Ctrl + A – select all.

q: Select the INCORRECT statement about MS-Word 365.
o: To change AutoCorrect settings, go to View → Window → Split.
To start a Spelling and Grammar check, press F7.
The Spelling & Grammar icon is in the Review tab.
Using Thesaurus, we can look up synonyms and antonyms.
exp:
AutoCorrect settings are in File → Options → Proofing → AutoCorrect Options; View → Window → Split divides the document window.
★ Exam Points:
• AutoCorrect fixes typos as you type (e.g., teh → the).
• Thesaurus: Shift + F7.
• Split window: Alt + Ctrl + S.

q: The MS-Word 365 Office Clipboard allows us to store up to ____.
exp:
The Office Clipboard can hold up to 24 copied or cut items, which can be pasted in any Office program.
★ Exam Points:
• Earlier Office 2000 clipboard held 12 items.
• Open Clipboard pane: Home → Clipboard dialog launcher.
• Windows clipboard history: Windows + V (25 items).

q: Which keyboard shortcut in MS-Word 2010 is used to go to the File tab?
exp:
Alt + F opens the File tab (Backstage view).
★ Exam Points:
• Alt + H – Home tab; Alt + N – Insert tab.
• Alt + G – Design tab (Word 2013+).
• Alt + W – View tab; Alt + R – Review tab.

q: Which of the following is NOT an example of a word processor?
exp:
MS-Access is a database management system (DBMS), not a word processor.
★ Exam Points:
• Other word processors: LibreOffice Writer, WPS Writer, Apple Pages.
• Notepad is a plain-text editor.
• Access file extension: .accdb.

q: Which option best describes the Delete Cells dialog box (Home → Cells → Delete → Delete Cells)?
o: It deletes the workbook from disk
It deletes selected cells and gives options to shift remaining cells left or up
exp:
The dialog offers Shift cells left, Shift cells up, Entire row and Entire column.
★ Exam Points:
• Shortcut: Ctrl + -.
• Insert Cells dialog: Ctrl + Shift + +.
• Deleting can cause #REF! errors.

q: ____ are often used to find out whether there is a relationship between variables X and Y.
exp:
A scatter (XY) chart plots pairs of values to show correlation between two variables.
★ Exam Points:
• Trendline shows the relationship.
• CORREL calculates correlation coefficient.
• Bubble chart adds a third variable.

q: What does the =INDIRECT() function do in Excel?
o: Converts a text string into a valid cell reference
Creates a direct reference to a range
exp:
INDIRECT("B"&2) returns the reference B2, allowing references to be built from text.
★ Exam Points:
• Useful for dynamic sheet references.
• INDIRECT is volatile.
• OFFSET also builds dynamic ranges.

q: When a formula with relative references is copied to another cell, how do the references behave?
o: They adjust based on the relative position of the new cell
They change only on another sheet
exp:
Relative references shift by the same number of rows/columns as the formula moves.
★ Exam Points:
• Default reference type is relative.
• Absolute ($) references do not change.
• Moving (cut) a formula keeps references.

q: Which formula calculates the average of B2:B10 excluding zeros using SUM and COUNTIF?
exp:
Dividing the total by the count of non-zero cells gives the average excluding zeros.
★ Exam Points:
• AVERAGEIF(B2:B10,"<>0") does it directly.
• "<>" means "not equal to".
• Zeros pull down a normal average.

q: ____ is a feature in Excel used to control what a user can enter into a cell.
exp:
Data Validation restricts input (whole numbers, dates, lists) and shows error alerts.
★ Exam Points:
• Data → Data Tools → Data Validation.
• Creates drop-down lists.
• Input message guides the user.

q: What is the purpose of the =IFERROR() function in Excel?
o: Checks for errors and returns a custom value/message if there is an error
exp:
IFERROR(value, value_if_error) shows a chosen result instead of #DIV/0!, #N/A, etc.
★ Exam Points:
• IFNA handles only #N/A.
• Common with VLOOKUP.
• ISERROR checks for errors.

q: What is the best way to delete only the contents and formatting of selected cells while keeping rows and columns unchanged?
o: Clear All on the Home tab
exp:
Home → Editing → Clear → Clear All removes contents, formats and comments but keeps the cells in place.
★ Exam Points:
• Clear Formats / Clear Contents remove one part.
• Delete key clears only contents.
• Delete Cells shifts other cells.

q: What does the 'Flash Fill' feature in Excel do?
o: Automatically fills data in cells based on detected patterns
Fills a table with column names
exp:
Flash Fill (Ctrl + E) recognises the pattern from your examples and fills the rest (e.g., splitting first names).
★ Exam Points:
• Introduced in Excel 2013.
• Found in Data → Data Tools.
• Results are static values, not formulas.

q: What is the function of a Slicer in MS Excel?
o: Quickly and easily filter PivotTables (and tables) using buttons
exp:
Slicers are visual button filters for PivotTables and tables.
★ Exam Points:
• Insert → Slicer.
• Timeline slicer filters by dates.
• One slicer can control multiple PivotTables.

q: What does the formula =RANK(A1, A1:A10) do?
o: Returns the rank of the value in A1 within A1:A10
exp:
RANK returns the position of a number in a list (default descending: largest = 1).
★ Exam Points:
• RANK.EQ and RANK.AVG are newer versions.
• Third argument 1 = ascending.
• Ties get the same rank.

q: How do you select multiple non-adjacent cells or ranges in Excel?
o: Click and drag across all cells
Hold Ctrl and click each cell or range separately
Use Shift + Enter on each cell
exp:
Ctrl + click/drag adds separate cells or ranges to the selection.
★ Exam Points:
• Shift + click selects a continuous range.
• Shift + F8 adds to selection without holding Ctrl.
• Some commands don't work on multiple selections.

q: What is the function of Ctrl + 0 in MS Excel?
exp:
Ctrl + 0 hides the selected columns; Ctrl + 9 hides rows.
★ Exam Points:
• Ctrl + Shift + 0 unhides columns.
• Ctrl + Shift + 9 unhides rows.
• Hidden data still participates in formulas.

q: What does the =NOW() function return in Excel?
exp:
NOW returns the current date and time and updates on recalculation.
★ Exam Points:
• TODAY returns only the date.
• NOW is a volatile function.
• Ctrl + ; and Ctrl + Shift + ; insert static date/time.

q: To resize a column to fit its longest entry, which mouse action is most appropriate?
o: Double-click the boundary on the right side of the column header
exp:
Double-clicking the column's right boundary AutoFits the width to the longest entry.
★ Exam Points:
• Home → Format → AutoFit Column Width.
• Same works for row heights.
• Alt + H, O, I shortcut.

q: Which function introduced in Excel 2021 returns unique values from a list or range?
exp:
UNIQUE returns the distinct values of a range as a spilled array.
★ Exam Points:
• Other dynamic functions: SORT, FILTER, SEQUENCE.
• Remove Duplicates is the menu alternative.
• #SPILL! occurs if output cells are blocked.

q: What is the function of Shift + F9 in Excel?
o: Full calculation of all cells in all workbooks
exp:
Shift + F9 recalculates only the active worksheet; F9 recalculates all open workbooks.
★ Exam Points:
• Ctrl + Alt + F9 – full calculation.
• Useful in Manual calculation mode.
• Formulas → Calculation Options.

q: Which is the best description of using "Find" while editing a large spreadsheet?
o: It searches for specific text or values so the user can review or edit those cells
exp:
Find locates cells containing given text/values; Find All lists every match.
★ Exam Points:
• Shortcut: Ctrl + F.
• Can search values, formulas or comments.
• Wildcards * and ? allowed.

q: What is the role of brackets in the formula =(A1+A2)*(B1-B2)?
o: They change the natural order so the additions/subtractions are done before multiplication
exp:
Without brackets multiplication would happen first; brackets ensure the sums are calculated before multiplying.
★ Exam Points:
• Brackets have highest precedence.
• Nested brackets are evaluated inside-out.
• Excel colour-codes matching brackets.

q: The ____ in Excel lets you add, edit and delete records (rows) and display only records meeting certain criteria.
exp:
A Data Form shows one record at a time in a dialog with New, Delete and Criteria buttons.
★ Exam Points:
• Add "Form" to QAT to use it.
• Works with list/table data.
• Maximum 32 fields.

q: How are rows and columns labelled in an MS Excel worksheet?
o: Rows use letters and columns use numbers
Rows use numbers and columns use letters
exp:
Rows are numbered (1, 2, 3) and columns are lettered (A, B, C) in A1 style.
★ Exam Points:
• R1C1 style uses numbers for both.
• Last column: XFD.
• Last row: 1,048,576.

q: Why is using cell references in formulas better than typing actual numbers?
o: It makes formulas harder to read
It ensures formulas update automatically when the referenced cells change
exp:
Formulas with references recalculate automatically whenever source values change.
★ Exam Points:
• Hard-coded numbers need manual updates.
• Automatic calculation is default.
• F9 forces recalculation.

q: What does the =TEXT() function do in Excel?
o: Converts a numeric value into text in a specific format
Converts text into a numeric value
exp:
=TEXT(value, format_text) returns the number as formatted text, e.g., =TEXT(1234.5,"₹#,##0.00").
★ Exam Points:
• VALUE converts text to number.
• SUBSTITUTE/REPLACE change text.
• Result of TEXT is left-aligned (text).

q: Which MS Excel function returns the number of complete months between two dates?
exp:
=DATEDIF(start, end, "M") returns completed months; "Y" years and "D" days.
★ Exam Points:
• DATEDIF is an undocumented (hidden) function.
• EOMONTH gives month-end date.
• NETWORKDAYS counts working days.

q: When editing a cell containing a formula, which part of the Excel window is most useful for carefully changing the formula?
exp:
The formula bar shows the full formula and allows precise editing.
★ Exam Points:
• Expand it with Ctrl + Shift + U.
• Colour-coded references appear while editing.
• F2 also edits in-cell.

q: Which function returns the largest number from a range of cells?
exp:
=MAX(range) returns the largest value.
★ Exam Points:
• LARGE(range,1) also returns the largest but needs k.
• MIN returns the smallest.
• MAXIFS adds conditions.

q: Which element selects the entire worksheet at once?
o: The Select All button at the top-left corner of the grid (above row 1, left of column A)
exp:
Clicking the Select All button (triangle at the corner of row and column headers) selects every cell.
★ Exam Points:
• Ctrl + A also selects all.
• Useful to change font for the whole sheet.
• Ctrl + Shift + Space also works.

q: Which formula demonstrates a nested IF inside another function to count how many values in A1:A10 are "Pass"?
exp:
SUM wraps an IF that returns 1 for each "Pass" and 0 otherwise – IF nested inside SUM.
★ Exam Points:
• COUNTIF gives the same count without nesting.
• Older Excel needed Ctrl + Shift + Enter for array formulas.
• Excel 365 handles arrays natively.

q: If you have data in columns that you need to rotate to rearrange in rows, use the ____ feature.
exp:
Paste Special → Transpose switches rows to columns and vice versa.
★ Exam Points:
• TRANSPOSE function does it by formula.
• Ctrl + Alt + V then E selects Transpose.
• Data must be copied, not cut.

q: What does the =LEFT(text, num_chars) function do?
o: Extracts the first num_chars characters from the left of the text
exp:
=LEFT("Restart",3) → "Res".
★ Exam Points:
• RIGHT takes characters from the end.
• MID takes characters from the middle.
• num_chars defaults to 1.

q: What is the small dark square in the lower-right corner of the active cell that can be dragged to fill adjacent cells?
exp:
The fill handle copies data or extends series (1, 2, 3; Jan, Feb…) when dragged.
★ Exam Points:
• Double-click fill handle to fill down to the end of data.
• Ctrl + D fills down.
• AutoFill Options button appears after filling.

q: What is the default alignment of data in an Excel cell?
o: Left for text, right for numbers
Right for text, left for numbers
exp:
Excel’s General alignment left-aligns text and right-aligns numbers and dates.
★ Exam Points:
• Logical values are centred.
• Change via Home → Alignment.
• Numbers stored as text are left-aligned.

q: A cell A1 contains =B$2 + $C3. If this formula is copied to cell D4, what will the formula in D4 be?
exp:
Moving 3 columns right and 3 rows down: in B$2 only the column changes (B→E); in $C3 only the row changes (3→6).
★ Exam Points:
• $ locks the part that follows it.
• Mixed references are used in tables.
• Check each part separately.

q: Which formula calculates the total of A2:A6 and then adds a constant bonus of 5 to the result?
exp:
SUM(A2:A6) gives the total and +5 is added once at the end.
★ Exam Points:
• =SUM(A2:A6,5) would also add 5.
• A2:A6+5 adds 5 to each cell (array).
• Brackets control order.

q: What is the function of F11 in an Excel sheet?
o: Creating a chart from the selected cells (on a new chart sheet)
exp:
F11 instantly creates a default chart from the selected data on a separate chart sheet.
★ Exam Points:
• Alt + F1 – embedded chart.
• Shift + F11 – new worksheet.
• Alt + F11 – VBA editor.

q: What is =COUNTIF(A1:A10, "apple") used for?
o: To count the occurrences of "apple" in A1:A10
To check if any cell contains "apple"
exp:
COUNTIF counts the cells in A1:A10 equal to "apple".
★ Exam Points:
• Not case-sensitive.
• Use "*apple*" for partial matches.
• SUMIF adds based on a condition.

q: Which best describes the basic purpose of a spreadsheet?
o: A tool only for drawing pictures
A grid-based program used to organise, calculate and analyse data in rows and columns
exp:
Spreadsheets arrange data in cells of rows and columns for calculations and analysis.
★ Exam Points:
• First spreadsheet: VisiCalc (1979).
• Examples: Excel, Calc, Google Sheets.
• Charts and PivotTables analyse data.

q: Which type of chart is best suited to display the proportion of different categories in a dataset?
exp:
A pie chart shows each category as a slice of the whole (100%).
★ Exam Points:
• Doughnut chart is similar.
• Line chart shows trends.
• Scatter chart shows relationships.

q: To extract the n-th largest unique value from a range without duplicates, which combination is most appropriate?
exp:
=LARGE(UNIQUE(range), n) first removes duplicates, then picks the n-th largest.
★ Exam Points:
• UNIQUE is a dynamic array function (365).
• SMALL gives n-th smallest.
• MAX returns only the largest.

q: In Excel, how do you insert a new column between existing columns B and C?
o: Right-click the column C header and choose Insert
Right-click the column B header and choose Delete
Double-click between B and C headers
exp:
Inserting at column C places a new blank column before C, i.e., between B and C.
★ Exam Points:
• New columns appear to the left of selection.
• Shortcut: Ctrl + Shift + + with column selected.
• Double-click border = AutoFit.

q: What is the shortcut key to hide the entire row in Excel?
exp:
Ctrl + 9 hides selected rows.
★ Exam Points:
• Ctrl + 0 hides columns.
• Ctrl + Shift + 9 unhides rows.
• Ctrl + - deletes cells.

q: What is the correct way to reference cell A1 from a different sheet named "Sheet2"?
exp:
Other-sheet references use an exclamation mark: SheetName!Cell.
★ Exam Points:
• Names with spaces need quotes: 'Sales Data'!A1.
• Other workbook: [Book1.xlsx]Sheet2!A1.
• 3D: Sheet1:Sheet3!A1.

q: What happens when an entire column is deleted from an Excel worksheet?
o: The column and all its data are removed, and columns to the right shift left
A new column is inserted at the end
exp:
Deleting a column removes it entirely and the columns to its right move left.
★ Exam Points:
• Shortcut: select column, Ctrl + -.
• Formulas referring to it show #REF!.
• Total column count stays 16,384.

q: Which tool is used to rearrange data to find values quickly?
exp:
Sorting arranges data in ascending or descending order, making values easier to locate.
★ Exam Points:
• Sort A to Z / Z to A.
• Custom sort by multiple columns.
• Sort by colour is possible.

q: Which function in Excel returns the current time (with date)?
exp:
=NOW() returns the current date and time; format the cell as time to show only time.
★ Exam Points:
• TIME(h,m,s) builds a time.
• TODAY() returns date only.
• Ctrl + Shift + ; enters static time.

q: Which edit can be performed using the Format Painter tool in Excel?
o: Copy formatting such as font, border and colour from one cell to another
exp:
Format Painter copies formatting only, not cell values.
★ Exam Points:
• Double-click to apply to many places.
• Esc stops Format Painter.
• Paste Special → Formats is an alternative.

q: If A1 contains text instead of a number, what problem is most likely with the formula =A1+10?
exp:
Arithmetic on text that cannot be read as a number produces the #VALUE! error.
★ Exam Points:
• #DIV/0! – division by zero.
• #NAME? – unknown function/name.
• SUM ignores text instead of erroring.

q: How do we insert a formula in a cell?
exp:
Every formula must begin with an equal sign (=).
★ Exam Points:
• + or - can also start formulas (legacy Lotus style).
• Ctrl + ` shows formulas.
• Functions are used inside formulas.

q: While editing a formula in the formula bar, which key switches a cell reference between relative, absolute and mixed modes?
exp:
Pressing F4 cycles A1 → $A$1 → A$1 → $A1 → A1.
★ Exam Points:
• F4 outside editing repeats the last action.
• F5 – Go To.
• F11 – chart sheet.

q: Which function checks whether a cell contains a logical value (TRUE or FALSE) in Excel?
exp:
ISLOGICAL returns TRUE if the value is TRUE or FALSE.
★ Exam Points:
• ISTEXT – text check.
• ISNUMBER – numeric check.
• ISFORMULA – checks for a formula.

q: In a report, you need to show day-wise temperature and humidity. The best way is to insert ____.
exp:
A chart (e.g., a line chart) clearly shows day-wise changes in temperature and humidity.
★ Exam Points:
• Line charts show trends over time.
• Combo charts use two axes.
• Secondary axis helps different scales.

q: Which function in Excel counts non-empty cells in a range?
exp:
COUNTA counts all cells that are not empty (numbers, text, errors).
★ Exam Points:
• COUNT – numbers only.
• COUNTBLANK – empty cells.
• COUNTIF – with condition.

q: Which of the following helps in creating charts for a set of numbers (older Excel versions)?
exp:
In Excel 2003 and earlier, the Chart Wizard guided users step by step to create charts.
★ Exam Points:
• Excel 2007+ uses Insert → Charts.
• F11 creates a default chart.
• Recommended Charts helps choose type.

q: Which function in MS Excel returns the ISO week number of a given date?
exp:
ISOWEEKNUM returns the ISO 8601 week number (weeks start on Monday).
★ Exam Points:
• Introduced in Excel 2013.
• WEEKNUM(date,21) also gives ISO week.
• Best single answer: ISOWEEKNUM.

q: In Excel, which element lets the user switch quickly between worksheets in the same workbook?
o: Sheet tabs at the bottom of the window
exp:
Sheet tabs at the bottom let you click to switch sheets (or use Ctrl + Page Up/Down).
★ Exam Points:
• Right-click tab scroll arrows to list all sheets.
• Tab colour can be changed.
• Double-click tab to rename.

q: You can resize a chart in a worksheet using the sizing handles (dots) on its border. How many such handles are given?
exp:
A selected chart shows eight sizing handles – four at the corners and four at the middle of the sides.
★ Exam Points:
• Corner handles resize proportionally with Shift.
• Charts can also be moved by dragging.
• Format Chart Area sets exact size.

q: In Excel, how would you change the text in cell A1 to uppercase?
exp:
=UPPER(A1) returns the text in capital letters.
★ Exam Points:
• There is no CHANGECASE function.
• TEXT formats numbers.
• Copy and Paste Values to replace original text.

q: Which MS Excel function looks up a value in a dynamic array using approximate matching, searching from the bottom of the range?
exp:
XLOOKUP's 5th argument sets match mode (1 = next larger approximate) and 6th argument search mode (-1 = last to first).
★ Exam Points:
• Search mode 1 = first to last (default).
• Match mode 0 = exact (default).
• XLOOKUP is in Excel 365/2021.

q: To prevent users from changing the formatting or structure of a worksheet without preventing them from entering data, you should use ____.
exp:
Protect Sheet (Review tab) lets you allow only selected actions, such as editing unlocked cells, while blocking formatting and structural changes.
★ Exam Points:
• Unlock input cells first via Format Cells → Protection.
• Protect Workbook protects structure (sheets).
• Mark as Final is a read-only hint.

q: In the mixed reference =B$4, what is held constant when the formula is copied?
o: Nothing – it becomes C$4 when copied down
exp:
The $ sign before 4 locks the row; the column B can change when copied across.
★ Exam Points:
• $B4 – column locked.
• $B$4 – both locked.
• F4 cycles reference types.

q: Which feature is used to create a data table in Excel?
exp:
Insert → Table (Ctrl + T) converts a range into a structured table; What-If Analysis → Data Table creates sensitivity tables.
★ Exam Points:
• Tables auto-expand.
• Structured references use column names.
• Banded rows improve readability.

q: What does the =AND() function do in Excel?
o: Returns TRUE if all conditions are TRUE
Returns TRUE if any condition is TRUE
exp:
AND returns TRUE only when every argument is TRUE; otherwise FALSE.
★ Exam Points:
• OR – TRUE if any is TRUE.
• NOT reverses a logical value.
• XOR – TRUE if an odd number are TRUE.

q: In the formula =SUM(A1:C5), what does the colon (:) indicate?
o: A range of cells (from A1 through C5)
The start of a named range
exp:
The colon is the range operator; A1:C5 includes all cells from A1 to C5 (15 cells).
★ Exam Points:
• Comma (,) is the union operator.
• Space is the intersection operator.
• A1:C5 = 5 rows × 3 columns.

q: Formulas that are built into a spreadsheet are called ____.
exp:
Functions are predefined formulas such as SUM, AVERAGE and IF.
★ Exam Points:
• Function syntax: =NAME(arguments).
• Excel has 12+ function categories.
• User-defined functions can be made with VBA or LAMBDA.

q: Which chart lets us pivot any data that can be quantified – from currency to countable qualitative data?
exp:
A PivotChart is a graphical view of a PivotTable and can be pivoted interactively.
★ Exam Points:
• Insert → PivotChart.
• Field buttons allow filtering on the chart.
• Changes in PivotTable reflect in PivotChart.

q: In MS Excel, which LOOKUP-based formula returns the last non-empty cell in a column?
exp:
1/(range<>"") gives 1 for non-empty cells and errors for blanks; looking up 2 (larger than any 1) returns the last match.
★ Exam Points:
• LOOKUP ignores errors when searching.
• 9.99E+307 trick finds the last number.
• XLOOKUP with search_mode -1 is a modern method.

q: While editing, which action is most suitable to place a block of cells in a new position but also keep the original block?
exp:
Copy and Paste duplicates the block, leaving the original intact.
★ Exam Points:
• Cut and Paste moves the block.
• Ctrl + drag copies cells.
• Paste options control formatting.

q: Which best describes a mixed cell reference such as A$1?
o: Both column and row are fixed
The column is relative but the row is fixed
The column is fixed but the row is relative
exp:
In A$1 the $ is before the row number, so the row stays fixed and the column can change.
★ Exam Points:
• $A1 – column fixed.
• Mixed references are used in multiplication tables.
• F4 cycles through options.

q: How can you calculate data across a workbook using multiple worksheets?
exp:
A 3D reference like =SUM(Sheet1:Sheet4!B2) refers to the same cell across several sheets.
★ Exam Points:
• Useful for monthly sheet totals.
• Sheet names are separated by a colon.
• Inserting a sheet between them includes it automatically.

q: What does the "Ctrl + Alt + V" command do?
exp:
Ctrl + Alt + V opens the Paste Special dialog box (in Excel and Word).
★ Exam Points:
• Paste Values: Ctrl + Alt + V, V.
• Ctrl + Shift + V – paste as plain text (365).
• Transpose is in Paste Special.

q: What does the formula =MATCH("apple", A1:A10, 0) do?
o: Finds the position of "apple" in the range A1:A10
exp:
With match_type 0, MATCH returns the relative position of the exact match.
★ Exam Points:
• Returns #N/A if not found.
• MATCH is not case-sensitive.
• Combine with INDEX to fetch values.

q: The LET() function introduced in Excel 2021 helps a user to ____.
o: assign names to calculation results and reuse them in a formula
exp:
LET assigns names to intermediate values inside a formula, making it shorter and faster.
★ Exam Points:
• Syntax: =LET(name1, value1, calculation).
• LAMBDA creates custom functions.
• Both are Excel 365/2021 functions.

q: What is a cell reference in Excel used for?
o: Identifying a cell (its address) for use in a formula
exp:
A cell reference such as B4 tells a formula which cell’s value to use.
★ Exam Points:
• Types: relative, absolute, mixed.
• 3D references refer to other sheets.
• External references point to other workbooks.

q: When you select Format Cells → Number → Custom, what is the primary purpose?
o: To permanently convert the value to text
To define how data is displayed without changing the actual stored value
exp:
Custom number formats change only the appearance (e.g., 0.00 "kg"); the underlying value stays the same for calculations.
★ Exam Points:
• Format Cells: Ctrl + 1.
• Code 0 = digit, # = optional digit.
• "@" represents text.

q: Which function combination returns a value from a table based on matching criteria in multiple columns?
exp:
INDEX with MATCH (using array conditions) can look up based on multiple criteria and in any direction.
★ Exam Points:
• VLOOKUP searches only the first column.
• XLOOKUP is the modern alternative.
• FILTER can also return multiple-criteria results.

q: How would you use the =COUNT() function in Excel?
o: To count cells containing numerical data
exp:
COUNT counts only cells containing numbers (dates are numbers too).
★ Exam Points:
• COUNTA counts all non-empty cells.
• COUNTBLANK counts empty cells.
• Text and logical values are ignored by COUNT.

q: What is the primary function of the ‘Text to Columns’ tool in Excel?
o: Breaks cell data into separate columns using a selected separator
exp:
Data → Text to Columns splits text using delimiters (comma, space) or fixed width.
★ Exam Points:
• Useful for splitting full names.
• Flash Fill (Ctrl + E) is another way.
• TEXTSPLIT does it by formula (Excel 365).

q: Which Excel function would you use to calculate the present value of an investment?
exp:
PV returns the present value of a series of future payments at a given rate.
★ Exam Points:
• FV – future value.
• PMT – periodic payment of a loan.
• NPV – for uneven cash flows.

q: A spreadsheet consists of rows and columns. Each row and column intersection creates a ____ into which you may enter data.
exp:
The intersection of a row and a column is called a cell.
★ Exam Points:
• Each cell has a unique address like C3.
• Selected cell = active cell.
• A group of cells = range.

q: Which of the following is NOT a type of data that can be entered into a cell in Excel?
exp:
Cells hold text, numbers, dates and formulas; graphs (charts) are objects placed over the sheet, not cell data.
★ Exam Points:
• Sparklines are tiny charts inside cells.
• Charts are inserted from the Insert tab.
• Formulas begin with =.

q: Which Excel Ribbon tab contains commands for inserting, deleting and renaming individual worksheets?
exp:
Home → Cells → Insert/Delete/Format contains Insert Sheet, Delete Sheet and Rename Sheet.
★ Exam Points:
• Rename by double-clicking the sheet tab.
• Shift + F11 inserts a sheet.
• Right-click a tab for sheet options.

q: Which Excel function calculates the internal rate of return (IRR) for a series of cash flows?
exp:
=IRR(values) returns the internal rate of return for periodic cash flows.
★ Exam Points:
• NPV – net present value.
• PMT – loan instalment.
• FV – future value.

q: The ____ function takes data from a series of worksheets or workbooks and summarises it into a single worksheet that can be updated easily.
exp:
Data → Consolidate combines and summarises data (sum, average, etc.) from multiple ranges into one.
★ Exam Points:
• Can link to source data for automatic updates.
• Works by position or by category.
• Flash Fill (Ctrl + E) fills patterns.

q: In Excel, how would you round the number 5.6789 to two decimal places?
exp:
ROUND(number, 2) gives the standard rounded value 5.68.
★ Exam Points:
• ROUNDUP → 5.68 (always up); ROUNDDOWN → 5.67.
• FIXED returns text, not a number.
• Negative digits round left of decimal (=ROUND(1234,-2) → 1200).

q: In the Go To dialog box (Ctrl + G) in Excel, which reference should you enter to quickly select a previously defined block of cells?
exp:
Named ranges appear in the Go To list; selecting one jumps to and selects that block.
★ Exam Points:
• Define names with the Name Box or Ctrl + F3.
• Go To Special (Alt + S) selects blanks, formulas etc.
• F5 also opens Go To.

q: What is the collection of multiple worksheets saved together called in MS Excel?
exp:
An Excel file is a workbook containing one or more worksheets.
★ Exam Points:
• Default extension: .xlsx.
• Macro-enabled: .xlsm.
• Template: .xltx.

q: Which function is used in Excel to calculate the weighted average of a set of numbers?
exp:
Weighted average = SUMPRODUCT(values, weights) / SUM(weights).
★ Exam Points:
• There is no WEIGHTEDAVERAGE function.
• SUMPRODUCT multiplies arrays and sums results.
• AVERAGE gives equal weight.

q: When you use Paste Special and select ‘Values’, what is the result?
o: The formula and formatting are pasted exactly
The calculated result is pasted and the original formula is discarded
exp:
Paste Values pastes only the displayed result (text/number), not the formula.
★ Exam Points:
• Shortcut: Ctrl + Alt + V, then V.
• Useful to freeze calculated values.
• Paste Formats pastes only formatting.

q: What is the result of =IF(OR(A1>10, B1<5), "Yes", "No") if A1 = 12 and B1 = 3?
exp:
OR returns TRUE because A1 > 10 (and also B1 < 5), so IF returns "Yes".
★ Exam Points:
• OR is TRUE if any condition is TRUE.
• AND is TRUE only if all are TRUE.
• Text results must be in double quotes.

q: What is the primary purpose of inserting a chart or graph in an Excel worksheet?
o: To visualise data and analyse trends quickly
exp:
Charts present data visually so trends and comparisons are easy to see.
★ Exam Points:
• Line chart – trends over time.
• Pie chart – parts of a whole.
• Recommended Charts suggests suitable types.

q: A manager wants to highlight all cells containing numbers greater than 100. Which feature should be used?
exp:
Conditional Formatting → Highlight Cells Rules → Greater Than applies formatting automatically.
★ Exam Points:
• Rules update when data changes.
• Data Validation restricts entries.
• Filter hides non-matching rows.

q: What happens if you type a number, a space and then text (e.g., 50 units) into an Excel cell?
o: Excel recognises it as a number
Excel treats the entire entry as a text label
Excel treats it as a date
exp:
Any entry mixing numbers and letters is stored as text and left-aligned; it cannot be used in calculations.
★ Exam Points:
• Use custom format 0 "units" to keep numbers numeric.
• Text is left-aligned by default.
• VALUE() converts numeric text to number.

q: Which Excel formula calculates the average of cells A1 through A10?
exp:
AVERAGE is Excel's function for the arithmetic mean; MEAN and AVG do not exist.
★ Exam Points:
• =SUM(A1:A10)/COUNT(A1:A10) also gives the mean.
• Unknown functions give #NAME?.
• AVERAGEIF adds a condition.

q: Which best describes the relationship between a workbook and worksheets in Excel?
o: A workbook is a file containing one or more worksheets
A workbook is a chart with many worksheets
A workbook is a formula with many worksheets
A workbook is a single cell
exp:
A workbook (.xlsx file) holds one or more worksheets.
★ Exam Points:
• Worksheets contain cells.
• Chart sheets can also be in a workbook.
• Excel 2013+ starts with one sheet.

q: Each row in an Excel worksheet is assigned a ____.
exp:
Rows are identified by numbers (1 to 1,048,576).
★ Exam Points:
• Columns use letters.
• Row height default ≈ 15 points.
• Click a row number to select the row.

q: The powerful ____ function in Excel counts cells based on one criterion.
exp:
COUNTIF(range, criteria) counts cells meeting one condition.
★ Exam Points:
• COUNTIFS for multiple criteria.
• Criteria can use wildcards like "A*".
• =COUNTIF(A:A,">=40").

q: Which function in MS Excel determines whether a formula refers to an empty cell?
exp:
ISBLANK(value) returns TRUE if the referenced cell is empty.
★ Exam Points:
• A cell with "" formula is not blank.
• COUNTBLANK counts empty cells.
• ISERR checks errors except #N/A.

q: When the values 2, 4, 6 are selected, what happens on dragging the Fill Handle in Excel?
exp:
AutoFill detects the step (+2) and extends the series.
★ Exam Points:
• Fill Handle = small square at bottom-right of selection.
• Ctrl + drag a single number creates a series.
• Series dialog: Home → Fill → Series.

q: What does the CONCATENATE function do in Excel?
o: Merges two or more text strings into one
exp:
CONCATENATE joins text strings; =CONCATENATE(A1," ",B1).
★ Exam Points:
• & operator does the same.
• CONCAT / TEXTJOIN are newer.
• TRIM removes extra spaces.

q: In MS Excel, which function returns the k-th percentile of a dataset using the exclusive method?
exp:
PERCENTILE.EXC uses k between 0 and 1, exclusive.
★ Exam Points:
• PERCENTILE.INC includes 0 and 1.
• QUARTILE.EXC/INC are related.
• PERCENTRANK gives rank as a percentage.

q: Which method is best for copying both the value and the formatting of one cell to another cell in Excel?
exp:
Normal Copy (Ctrl + C) and Paste (Ctrl + V) copies value/formula and formatting together while leaving the original.
★ Exam Points:
• Paste Special can choose specific parts.
• Cut moves instead of copying.
• Format Painter copies only formatting.

q: To represent a group of cells in a function, we place a ____ between the first and last cell address.
exp:
A colon creates a range, e.g. =SUM(A1:A10).
★ Exam Points:
• Comma separates arguments.
• Some regional settings use semicolon as separator.
• Range A1:A10 has 10 cells.

q: Which is the correct formula for the total of cells B1 to B10?
exp:
=SUM(B1:B10) adds all ten cells; =B1+B10 adds only two cells.
★ Exam Points:
• AutoSum: Alt + =.
• There is no TOTAL function (SUBTOTAL exists).
• SUM ignores text.

q: In MS Excel, which function combines data from multiple ranges vertically and spills the combined list automatically?
exp:
VSTACK appends arrays vertically (one below the other) into a single spilled array.
★ Exam Points:
• HSTACK appends side by side.
• CHOOSECOLS returns selected columns.
• TOROW converts an array to one row.

q: Which feature in Excel is most appropriate for replacing every occurrence of the word "Pending" with "Completed" in a selected range?
exp:
Find & Replace (Ctrl + H) with Replace All updates every occurrence at once.
★ Exam Points:
• Can limit to selection or sheet.
• Match case option available.
• SUBSTITUTE does it by formula.

q: The ____ consists of an up-arrow scroll button and a down-arrow scroll button.
exp:
The vertical scroll bar on the right has up and down arrows to move through rows.
★ Exam Points:
• Horizontal scroll bar has left/right arrows.
• Scroll Lock changes arrow-key behaviour.
• Mouse wheel scrolls vertically.

q: Which Excel feature displays cell contents in a different format or colour based on a condition?
exp:
Conditional Formatting changes appearance automatically when cell values meet rules.
★ Exam Points:
• Icon sets, data bars, colour scales.
• New Rule allows formulas.
• Manage Rules sets priority.

q: In MS Excel, which function returns the numeric ASCII/ANSI code of the first character of a text string?
exp:
=CODE("A") returns 65.
★ Exam Points:
• CHAR(65) returns "A".
• UNICODE returns the Unicode code point.
• VAL is not an Excel function.

q: What is the simplest way to edit a cell so that only part of the text (e.g., a spelling mistake) is changed?
o: Retype the entire sentence and press Enter
Double-click the cell or press F2, move the cursor and correct only the mistake
Delete the cell and insert a new row
exp:
Edit mode (double-click or F2) lets you change part of the content without retyping everything.
★ Exam Points:
• Typing directly replaces the whole content.
• Esc cancels changes.
• Edit also possible in the formula bar.

q: What does D7:D15 indicate?
o: Cell D7 and cell D15 only
exp:
The colon denotes a range – all cells from D7 to D15 (9 cells).
★ Exam Points:
• D7,D15 (comma) means only the two cells.
• Range must be contiguous.
• Can be named for reuse.

q: Which function looks for a value horizontally across the first row of a table in Excel?
exp:
HLOOKUP (Horizontal lookup) searches the top row and returns a value from a specified row.
★ Exam Points:
• VLOOKUP searches the first column.
• Syntax: HLOOKUP(value, table, row_index, [range_lookup]).
• XLOOKUP works both ways.

q: In MS Excel, which function checks conditions and returns the value corresponding to the first TRUE condition?
exp:
IFS(test1, value1, test2, value2, …) returns the value of the first condition that is TRUE.
★ Exam Points:
• SWITCH matches an expression against values.
• CHOOSE picks by index number.
• IFS avoids nested IFs.

q: In Excel, what is the effect of using "Insert Cut Cells" from the right-click menu after cutting a range?
o: It pastes the content and pushes existing cells down or right
It converts cut cells into formulas
exp:
Insert Cut Cells inserts the moved cells at the destination, shifting existing cells instead of overwriting them.
★ Exam Points:
• Normal paste overwrites the destination.
• Shift + drag also inserts while moving.
• Ctrl + Shift + + inserts cells.

q: When a formula containing the absolute reference $B$2 is copied to another cell, what happens to this reference?
o: Neither the column nor the row changes
exp:
$ before both column and row makes the reference fully absolute; it stays $B$2 wherever copied.
★ Exam Points:
• Used for constants like tax rate.
• Press F4 to add $ signs.
• Mixed references lock only one part.

q: Which shortcut key inserts a comment in Excel?
exp:
Shift + F2 inserts or edits a comment (note) on the active cell.
★ Exam Points:
• In Excel 365 Ctrl + Alt + M adds a threaded comment.
• Review → New Comment.
• Red triangle marks a comment.

q: Which of the following is used to lock specific rows and columns while scrolling in Excel?
exp:
View → Freeze Panes keeps chosen rows/columns visible while scrolling.
★ Exam Points:
• Freeze Top Row / First Column options.
• Split divides the window into panes.
• Lock Cells works only with sheet protection.

q: While working on a large worksheet, which feature keeps the top heading row visible at all times while scrolling down?
exp:
View → Freeze Panes → Freeze Top Row keeps the header row visible.
★ Exam Points:
• Freeze First Column keeps column A visible.
• Unfreeze Panes removes it.
• Print Titles repeat headers on printed pages.

q: To arrange students' marks from highest to lowest, you need to sort the marks field in ____ order.
exp:
Descending order arranges values from largest to smallest (Z to A).
★ Exam Points:
• Ascending: smallest to largest.
• Sort Largest to Smallest button.
• LARGE/RANK find top values.

q: Which Excel function can be used to check whether a condition is true or false and return different results?
exp:
IF tests a condition and returns one value if TRUE and another if FALSE.
★ Exam Points:
• =IF(A1>=33,"Pass","Fail").
• TRUE() just returns TRUE.
• BOOLEAN and LOGICAL are not functions.

q: Which function finds the third lowest numerical value in the range A1:D10?
exp:
SMALL(array, k) returns the k-th smallest value.
★ Exam Points:
• LARGE returns the k-th largest.
• MIN = SMALL(range,1).
• RANK gives the position of a number.

q: What is the result of the formula =IF(OR(A1>10, B1<5), 'Yes', 'No') if A1 contains 12 and B1 contains 3?
exp:
Step-by-step evaluation of =IF(OR(A1>10, B1<5), 'Yes', 'No') for A1 = 12 and B1 = 3: 1. Check A1 > 10: 12 > 10 → TRUE 2. Check B1 < 5: 3 < 5 → TRUE 3. OR(TRUE, TRUE) returns TRUE (OR needs at least one TRUE). 4. Since the condition is TRUE, IF returns the first branch: Yes.
★ Exam Points:
• Syntax: =IF(logical_test, value_if_true, value_if_false).
• OR() returns TRUE if at least one condition is TRUE; AND() returns TRUE only if all conditions are TRUE; NOT() reverses TRUE/FALSE.

q: Which chart enhancement in Excel 2021 allows users to create visually appealing diagrams with better animations and templates?
exp:
