In Excel 2021, updated SmartArt Graphics (Insert tab > Illustrations > SmartArt) provide enriched diagram templates, modern icons, and smoother visual layouts for turning bulleted lists into process flows, hierarchies, cycles, and org charts.
★ Exam Points:
• Categories of SmartArt layouts: List, Process, Cycle, Hierarchy, Relationship, Matrix, Pyramid, and Picture.
• Funnel and Waterfall are quantitative data charts introduced earlier (Excel 2016/2019) rather than diagram template enhancements.

q: Range is a sequence of __________.
exp:
In MS Excel, a Range is a contiguous rectangular block or sequence of cell addresses specified by its top-left and bottom-right cell coordinates separated by a colon—for example, A1:D10.
★ Exam Points:
• Operators in Excel references: Colon (:) = Range operator (all cells between two endpoints); Comma (,) = Union operator (combines multiple ranges); Space ( ) = Intersection operator (overlapping cells).
• A single cell can also be treated as a 1×1 range.

q: Which primary tab on the Excel Ribbon is home to the commands for adding, removing, and renaming individual sheets within a workbook?
exp:
On the Excel Ribbon, the Home tab's Cells group contains the Insert (Insert Sheet), Delete (Delete Sheet), and Format (Rename Sheet, Move or Copy Sheet, Tab Color, Hide & Unhide) commands for managing worksheets.
★ Exam Points:
• Quick alternative: right-click any sheet tab at the bottom of the workbook to Insert, Delete, Rename, Move/Copy, or Protect a sheet.
• Shortcut to insert a new worksheet: Shift + F11.

q: If you are using the Go To dialog box (Ctrl+G), which reference type should you enter to quickly select a previously defined block of cells?
exp:
In MS Excel's Go To dialog box (opened via Ctrl + G or F5), selecting or typing a Named Range (a user-defined descriptive name assigned to a block of cells, e.g., Sales_Data) immediately jumps to and highlights that entire block of cells.
★ Exam Points:
• Named Ranges are created via the Name Box (left of Formula Bar) or Formulas tab > Define Name (shortcut Ctrl + F3 opens Name Manager).
• Named Ranges cannot contain spaces and must begin with a letter, underscore (_), or backslash (\).

q: You have the value 100 in cell A1. You enter the formula =A1 in cell B1 and then copy cell B1 and use "Paste Special" to paste only the "Formulas" into cell C1. What will be the result in cell C1?
exp:
Step-by-step relative reference trace: 1. Cell B1 holds =A1, which is a relative reference meaning 'one column to the left in the same row'. 2. Copying B1 and pasting Formulas one column right into C1 shifts the relative reference one column right from A1 to =B1.
★ Exam Points:
• Since B1 evaluates to 100 (from A1), cell C1 stores the formula =B1 (and displays 100 on screen).
• Had B1 contained the absolute reference =$A$1, pasting into C1 would have remained =$A$1.

q: If you are editing a cell and need to insert a line break (new line) within the cell text, which key combination must you use?
exp:
While editing text inside a cell in MS Excel, pressing Alt + Enter inserts a manual line break (carriage return) within that same cell.
★ Exam Points:
• Ctrl + Enter fills the same entry across all currently selected cells; Shift + Enter confirms the entry and moves one cell up.

q: What do you mean by cell references?
exp:
In MS Excel, a cell reference (such as A1, $B$2, or C1:C10) identifies a cell's coordinates on the grid so its stored value can be dynamically used inside a formula—automatically recalculating whenever that cell's value changes.
★ Exam Points:
• Reference | Type | Locked Part (F4 cycles)
• A1 | Relative | Neither column nor row changes lock; both adjust
• $A$1 | Absolute | Both column A and row 1 locked
• $A1 | Mixed | Column A locked, row 1 relative
• A$1 | Mixed | Column A relative, row 1 locked

q: When applying a filter in Excel, what happens if you filter a column that contains blank cells?
o: Excel will automatically remove the blank cells from the filtered view.
Excel will ignore the blank cells and display all other data.
Blank cells will be displayed at the top of the filtered data.
Excel will display an error message and stop the filter.
exp:
When AutoFilter is active on a column in MS Excel, the filter drop-down lists (Blanks) as a selectable item, and during filtering/ascending arrangement with blank entries included, blank cells are retained and displayed rather than deleted or throwing an error (as matched in Option 3).
★ Exam Points:
• In Excel's filter checklist, unchecking (Blanks) hides rows where that column is empty; checking only (Blanks) isolates incomplete records for cleanup.
• Shortcut to toggle AutoFilter on/off in MS Excel: Ctrl + Shift + L.

q: When you select 'Format Cells' and choose Custom under the Number tab, what is the primary purpose?
o: To permanently convert the cell's value to text so it cannot be used in calculations.
To lock the cell so that no further editing is allowed.
To define how the data is displayed without changing the actual stored value.
To automatically apply conditional formatting based on value.
exp:
Using Format Cells (Ctrl + 1) > Number > Custom lets users apply format masks (such as 0.00, "Rs"#,##0, or dd-mmm-yyyy) to customize how a value is visually displayed in the cell without altering the actual underlying number or date stored for calculations.
★ Exam Points:
• Shortcut to open the Format Cells dialog box in MS Excel: Ctrl + 1.
• Custom number formats have up to 4 sections separated by semicolons: Positive; Negative; Zero; Text.

q: Which shortcut key is used to open a new workbook?
exp:
In MS Excel, pressing Ctrl + N creates and opens a new blank workbook immediately.
★ Exam Points:
• Compare common Excel file shortcuts: Ctrl + N = New workbook; Ctrl + O = Open existing workbook; Ctrl + S = Save; Ctrl + P = Print; Shift + F11 = Insert new worksheet inside the current workbook.

q: Which of the following formulas would you use to calculate the present value of an investment?
exp:
Excel's financial function =PV(rate, nper, pmt, [fv], [type]) calculates the Present Value of a loan or investment based on a constant interest rate, total payment periods (nper), and periodic payment (pmt).
★ Exam Points:
• Companion TVM (Time Value of Money) functions: =FV() (Future Value), =PMT() (Periodic Installment), =NPER() (Number of Periods), and =RATE() (Interest Rate per period).

q: In the mixed cell reference =B4 what specifically is held constant (made absolute) when the formula is copied to a different cell?
o: Both the Column (B) and the Row (4) are locked.
The reference will change entirely to C4 when copied one cell down.
exp:
In the mixed cell reference =B$4 (printed as =B4 in the question where row 4 is the fixed part of the mixed reference), the dollar sign precedes row 4—meaning the Row number (4) is locked (held constant) while the Column letter (B) remains relative and adjusts if copied left or right.
★ Exam Points:
• Reference | Type | Locked Part (F4 cycles)
• A1 | Relative | Neither column nor row changes lock; both adjust
• $A$1 | Absolute | Both column A and row 1 locked
• $A1 | Mixed | Column A locked, row 1 relative
• A$1 | Mixed | Column A relative, row 1 locked

q: In the cell reference A1:C5, the colon (:) signifies:
o: A range of cells (from A1 through C5)
The start of a Named Range
exp:
In MS Excel, the colon (:) in A1:C5 is the range operator sig-nifying a rectangular range of all 15 cells spanning Columns A through C and Rows 1 through 5.
★ Exam Points:
• Total cells in A1:C5 = 3 columns (A, B, C)×5 rows (1..5) = 15 cells.
• Other reference operators: Comma (,) = Union of two separate ranges; Space ( ) = Intersection of overlapping ranges.

q: How can we pivot any data that can be quantified, ranging from currency or other numeric values to qualitative data that can be counted?
exp:
A Pivot Chart (linked to a PivotTable via Insert > PivotChart) dynamically aggregates, slices, cross-tabulates, and visualizes both quantitative numeric/currency sums and counted qualitative/categorical fields interactively.
★ Exam Points:
• Adding Slicers and Timelines to a PivotChart allows inter-active dashboard filtering in a single click.

q: Which of the following best describes a mixed cell reference, such as A1, in the context of editing and copying formulas in Excel?
o: Both the column and row are fixed
Both the column and row are relative
The column is relative but the row is fixed
The column is fixed but the row is relative
exp:
In a mixed cell reference of the form A$1 (printed as A1 where the row carries the absolute lock), the column (A) is relative while the row ($1) is fixed—copying across columns changes A to B, C, etc., whereas copying down rows keeps row 1 constant.
★ Exam Points:
• Reference | Type | Locked Part (F4 cycles)
• A1 | Relative | Neither column nor row changes lock; both adjust
• $A$1 | Absolute | Both column A and row 1 locked
• $A1 | Mixed | Column A locked, row 1 relative
• A$1 | Mixed | Column A relative, row 1 locked

q: How to calculate data throughout a workbook using multiple worksheets?
exp:
In MS Excel, a 3D reference refers to the same cell or range across a span of multiple consecutive worksheets in a workbook—for example, =SUM(Sheet1:Sheet4!B2:B10) adds cell range B2:B10 across Sheet1, Sheet2, Sheet3, and Sheet4 simultaneously.
★ Exam Points:
• Inserting a new worksheet physically between Sheet1 and Sheet4 automatically includes that new sheet's values in the 3D reference calculation!

q: Which view is best for quickly checking the document's structure and seeing which cells are being referenced in formulas?
exp:
In MS Excel, switching to Formula View using the shortcut Ctrl + ` (Ctrl + grave accent / tilde key, or Formulas tab > Show Formulas) displays the actual underlying formulas inside every cell instead of their calculated results and high-lights referenced cells when clicked—making formula auditing fast and transparent.
★ Exam Points:
• Pressing Ctrl + ` a second time toggles the worksheet right back to normal calculated values.

q: __________ are used to locate the source of an error to understand how formulas are arranged before making changes to the Excel worksheet.
exp:
On MS Excel's Formulas tab > Formula Auditing group, Trace Precedents draws blue arrows pointing from the input/source cells that supply data TO the currently selected formula cell, helping locate the upstream source of an error before editing.
★ Exam Points:
• Contrast: Trace Precedents = 'Which cells feed INTO this formula?'; Trace Dependents = 'Which other formulas depend ON this cell?'.
• Red dashed arrows appear when a referenced cell contains an error value.

q: In Excel, which element allows the user to switch quickly between different worksheets within the same workbook while working on different sets of data?
o: Sheet tabs at the bottom of the window
Status indicators at the bottom-left corner
exp:
In MS Excel, clicking the Sheet tabs at the bottom of the window (such as Sheet1, Sheet2, Sheet3) switches immediately between different worksheets within the same workbook.
★ Exam Points:
• Keyboard shortcuts to switch sheet tabs: Ctrl + Page Down (next sheet) and Ctrl + Page Up (previous sheet).

q: You can easily resize a chart in a worksheet. For resizing a chart, ________ dots are given on the border of the chart.
exp:
When you click on a chart in an MS Excel worksheet to select it, eight (8) sizing handles (dots/circles) appear around its rectangular border—4 at the corners (proportional diago-nal resizing) and 4 at the midpoints of the top, bottom, left, and right edges.
★ Exam Points:
• Dragging a corner handle while holding Shift maintains the chart's exact aspect ratio; holding Alt snaps the chart border neatly to worksheet cell gridlines.

q: Which of the following best describes the relationship between a workbook and worksheets in Excel as elements of a spreadsheet?
o: A workbook is a single cell, and multiple workbooks form one worksheet
A workbook is a file that contains one or more worksheets
A workbook is a chart, and each chart has several worksheets
A workbook is only a formula, and each formula contains many worksheets
exp:
In MS Excel's hierarchy, a workbook is a spreadsheet file (.xlsx) that contains one or more individual worksheets (tabs), and each worksheet consists of a grid of rows and columns intersecting into cells.
★ Exam Points:
• Hierarchy from largest to smallest in Excel: Workbook → Worksheet → Range → Cell.

q: Which of the following correctly describes the use of the Fill Handle in Excel for editing a series such as 2, 4, 6 when these three values are selected?
o: Dragging the Fill Handle will only copy the number 2
Dragging the Fill Handle will continue the pattern 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, and so on
Dragging the Fill Handle will delete all selected cells
Dragging the Fill Handle will convert numbers to text
exp:
When multiple cells showing a linear arithmetic progression —2, 4, 6 (step difference = +2)—are selected together in MS Excel, dragging the Fill Handle (the small solid square at the bottom-right corner of the selection) triggers AutoFill and continues the arithmetic pattern as 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, and so on.
★ Exam Points:
• Note: If you select only a single number (e.g., just cell A1 containing 2) and drag the Fill Handle without holding Ctrl, Excel copies 2, 2, 2... (holding Ctrl while dragging incre-ments 2, 3, 4...). Selecting two or more cells establishes the step pattern automatically!

q: While editing data, which feature in Excel is most appropriate for replacing every occurrence of the word "Pending" in a selected range with the word "Completed"?
exp:
To replace every instance of "Pending" with "Completed" across a selected Excel range in one go, open Find & Replace (Ctrl + H, or Home > Find & Select > Replace), enter "Pending" in Find what, "Completed" in Replace with, and click Replace All.
★ Exam Points:
• Checking Match entire cell contents in Find & Replace ensures partial words (like "Pending_Approval") are not accidentally altered.

q: When a formula containing an absolute reference like B2 is copied to another cell, what happens to this reference during editing?
o: Both column and row change to match the new position
Only the column changes but the row stays the same
Only the row changes but the column stays the same
Neither the column nor the row changes
exp:
In an absolute cell reference such as $B$2 (printed as B2 in the question describing an absolute reference), dollar signs lock both the column letter and row number—so when the formula is copied anywhere else on the sheet, neither the column nor the row changes.
★ Exam Points:
• Reference | Type | Locked Part (F4 cycles)
• A1 | Relative | Neither column nor row changes lock; both adjust
• $A$1 | Absolute | Both column A and row 1 locked
• $A1 | Mixed | Column A locked, row 1 relative
• A$1 | Mixed | Column A relative, row 1 locked

q: In MS Excel, which function can convert a vertical array into a single row automatically?
exp:
Introduced in Excel for Microsoft 365, the dynamic array function =TOROW(array, [ignore], [scan_by_column]) transforms a vertical column or multi-row 2D range into a single horizontal row automatically.
★ Exam Points:
• Contrast: =TRANSPOSE() flips a 1-column vertical array into 1 row, OR flips a multi-column 2D table into a multi-row table, whereas =TOROW() flattens any 1D or 2D array strictly into a single row (and =TOCOL() flattens into a single column).

q: Which of the following correctly describes what happens when an entire column is deleted from a worksheet in Excel?
o: Only the heading of the column is deleted, but data remains
The column and all its data are removed, and columns to the right shift left
Only the formatting is removed while values stay
A new column is automatically inserted at the end
exp:
When an entire column (say Column B) is deleted in MS Excel (Right-click header → Delete, or Ctrl + -), the column along with all its data and formatting is removed, and every column to its right automatically shifts one position to the left (and column letters relabel sequentially).
★ Exam Points:
• Note: Pressing the Delete key on a selected column only clears cell contents without shifting columns; choosing the Delete Column command physically removes the column and shifts right-hand columns left.

q: In MS Excel, which function returns a vertically stacked dynamic array from multiple ranges?
exp:
In MS Excel (Microsoft 365), =VSTACK(array1, [array2], ...) ('Vertical Stack') combines multiple ranges or arrays one underneath another in sequence and returns a single vertically stacked dynamic array.
★ Exam Points:
• Horizontal counterpart: =HSTACK(array1, [array2], ...) stacks arrays side-by-side across columns.
• WRAPROWS(vector, wrap_count) wraps a 1D row/column vector into a 2D array after every N elements.

q: If cell A1 contains text instead of a number, which issue is most likely when using the formula =A1+10?
o: Excel will ignore A1 and return 10 without warning
exp:
When cell A1 contains non-numeric text (e.g., "Delhi") and you use the arithmetic operator + in =A1+10, Excel cannot coerce alphabetic text into a number and immediately returns the #VALUE! error.
★ Exam Points:
• Error | Meaning / Cause
• #DIV/0! | Division by zero or empty cell
• #VALUE! | Wrong data type in formula (e.g., text + number)
• #NAME? | Misspelled function or unrecognized range name
• #REF! | Deleted or invalid cell reference
• #N/A | Lookup value not found (VLOOKUP/MATCH)
• ##### | Column too narrow or negative date/time
• Interesting exam nuance: While =A1+10 throws #VALUE!, the function =SUM(A1, 10) gracefully ignores text in range references and returns 10!

q: Which Excel feature allows you to split text across multiple columns?
exp:
Excel's Text to Columns tool (Data tab > Data Tools > Text to Columns) takes text in a single column (such as full names or comma-separated addresses) and splits it across multiple adjacent columns using delimiters or fixed column widths.
★ Exam Points:
• Contrast: Concatenate / TEXTJOIN merges columns together; AutoFit resizes column width/row height; Text to Columns splits one column into multiple columns.

q: While editing a spreadsheet, which keyboard shortcut copies cells to the clipboard without removing them from their original location?
exp:
While editing a spreadsheet in MS Excel, pressing Ctrl + C copies the selected cell(s) to the Clipboard (indicated by a moving dashed 'marching ants' border) without removing them from their original location.
★ Exam Points:
• Compare: Ctrl + X = Cut (moves); Ctrl + V = Paste; Ctrl + Z = Undo.

q: Which description best explains the difference between the Copy and Cut commands when editing cells in Excel?
o: Copy moves data and clears the original, while Cut duplicates data
Copy duplicates data and leaves original unchanged, while Cut moves data and clears original
Both Copy and Cut always delete the original data
Copy and Cut are used only for formatting, not for data
exp:
In MS Excel cell editing: • Copy (Ctrl + C) creates a duplicate of the selected cells while leaving the original cells completely unchanged. • Cut (Ctrl + X) moves the selected cells to the new Paste destination and clears the original cells.
★ Exam Points:
• Note in Excel: Unlike Word where Ctrl + X disappears immediately, Excel keeps cut cells visible inside a dashed border until you press Ctrl + V / Enter at the new spot!

q: What is the =COUNTIF(A1:A10, "apple") function used for?
o: Count the number of occurrences of "apple" in the range A1:A10
Count all cells in the range A1:A10 that are not empty
Sum all the values containing the word "apple"
Check if any cell in the range contains the word "apple"
exp:
In MS Excel, =COUNTIF(A1:A10, "apple") checks every cell in the range A1:A10 and returns the exact count of cells whose value equals "apple" (case-insensitive, so "Apple" and "APPLE" are also counted).
★ Exam Points:
• To count cells that merely contain "apple" anywhere inside longer text (e.g., "green apple"), use wildcards: =COUNTIF(A1:A10, "*apple*").

q: In MS Excel, which of the following best describes the basic purpose of a spreadsheet in terms of elements like rows, columns and cells?
o: A tool used only for drawing and painting pictures
A grid-based program used to organize, calculate and analyze data in rows and columns
A program used only for sending emails
A program used only for playing audio and video files
exp:
In MS Excel, a spreadsheet is a grid-based electronic program used to organize, store, calculate, and analyze structured data arranged in horizontal rows and vertical columns intersecting at cells.
★ Exam Points:
• Automatic formula recalculation when any input cell changes is the core strength of electronic spreadsheets.

q: How can you adjust the column width to fit the contents of a cell in Excel?
o: Right-click on the column header and select "AutoFit" only
Use the "Column Width" option from the Home tab only
exp:
In MS Excel, you can automatically adjust (AutoFit) a column's width to match its widest entry either by: • (a) Double-clicking the right boundary of the column header (e.g., between A and B), OR • (b) Using the AutoFit Column Width command (via column menu / Home > Format > AutoFit Column Width, short-cut Alt + H + O + I). Hence, Both a and b are valid methods.
★ Exam Points:
• Remember: When a numeric/date column is too narrow to show the full value, Excel displays ##### until you AutoFit the column width!

q: While working on a large worksheet, which element should be used to keep the top heading row visible at all times when scrolling down to edit data in lower rows?
exp:
When scrolling down thousands of rows in a large Excel worksheet, Freeze Panes (specifically View > Freeze Panes > Freeze Top Row) keeps the column-header row pinned at the top of the screen at all times.
★ Exam Points:
• To unpin frozen rows/columns later, go to View > Freeze Panes > Unfreeze Panes.

q: In order to arrange the marks of students in the division from those with the highest marks to those with the lowest, you need to sort on the marks field in __________.
exp:
Arranging numerical marks from the highest value at the top down to the lowest value at the bottom (Largest to Smallest, e.g., 98, 95, 89, ..., 35) is called sorting in descending order.
★ Exam Points:
• Contrast: Ascending order arranges from lowest to high-est (Smallest to Largest / A to Z).

q: Which of the following Excel functions can you use to check if a condition is true or false?
exp:
In MS Excel, the conditional function =IF(logical_test, value_if_true, value_if_false) tests whether a given condition evaluates to TRUE or FALSE and returns one specified output if TRUE and another if FALSE.
★ Exam Points:
• Excel has no built-in worksheet functions named =BOOLEAN() or =LOGICAL() (and =TRUE() simply returns the constant TRUE without checking any condition).

q: Which function would you use to return the current date in Excel?
exp:
In MS Excel, =TODAY() (with empty parentheses) returns only the current system date (dynamically updated whenever the workbook opens or recalculates).
★ Exam Points:
• Compare: =TODAY() = current Date only; =NOW() = current Date + Time; =DATE(year, month, day) = builds a date from 3 specified numbers; Excel has NO =CURRENTDATE() function.
• Static current date keyboard shortcut in Excel: Ctrl + ;.

q: Which tool allows us to automatically apply formatting like colors, icons, and data bar to one or more cells based on the apply condition?
exp:
MS Excel's Conditional formatting (Home tab > Styles group) automatically applies visual cues—cell fill colours, colour scales, directional/traffic-light Icon Sets, and in-cell Data Bars—to cells dynamically based on their numeric values or rules.
★ Exam Points:
• Cell Styles and Format as Table apply static design themes regardless of whether individual values pass a threshold condition.

q: In Excel, which element is used to select the entire worksheet at once for applying editing actions like changing font or deleting all data?
o: The small triangle or square at the top-left corner of the grid (above row 1 and left of column A)
exp:
In MS Excel, clicking the Select All button—the small grey triangle/square at the top-left corner of the worksheet grid (above Row 1 and to the left of Column A)—instantly selects every cell across the entire worksheet.
★ Exam Points:
• Keyboard shortcut equivalent: Ctrl + A (if pressed inside a contiguous data table, the first Ctrl + A selects the current data region and pressing Ctrl + A a second time selects the entire sheet; Ctrl + Shift + Spacebar also selects all).

q: If you have a worksheet with data in columns that you need to rotate to rearrange it in rows, use the ________ feature.
exp:
In MS Excel, rotating tabular data so that columns become rows and rows become columns is performed using the Transpose feature (via Copy → Paste Special (Ctrl + Alt + V) > Transpose, or dynamically using the =TRANSPOSE(array) function).
★ Exam Points:
• Difference: Paste Special > Transpose creates a one-time static rotated copy, whereas =TRANSPOSE(A1:C5) stays dynamically linked to the source cells.

q: Which of the following is the best description of using the "Find" feature when editing a spreadsheet with many entries?
o: It changes all fonts to the same style
It searches for specific text or values so the user can review or edit those cells
It deletes all cells that do not match a certain value
exp:
When working on a large spreadsheet with thousands of rows, Excel's Find tool (Ctrl + F, or Home > Find & Select > Find) searches across cells/formulas to locate specific text or numbers quickly so the user can jump to, inspect, or edit those matching cells.
★ Exam Points:
• Clicking Find All lists every matching cell address in a clickable table at the bottom of the dialog box.

q: Which of the following correctly explains the role of brackets in the formula =(A1+A2)(B1-B2):
o: They have no effect on the result
They change the natural order so A1+A2 is done before multiplying by (B1-B2)
They force subtraction to happen last
They convert all values inside them to text
exp:
In Excel's operator hierarchy, multiplication normally happens BEFORE addition and subtraction. Placing parentheses in =(A1+A2)*(B1-B2) (printed as =(A1+A2)(B1-B2)) overrides default precedence so Excel evaluates (A1+A2) and (B1-B2) inside the brackets first before multiplying the two results.
★ Exam Points:
• Without parentheses, =A1+A2*B1-B2 would compute A2*B1 first!
• Note: In actual Excel syntax, always write the explicit asterisk * between parenthesized groups: =(A1+A2)*(B1-B2).

q: The ________ in Excel allows you to add, edit, and delete records (rows) and display only those records that meet certain criteria.
exp:
MS Excel's built-in Data Form dialog box (accessible by adding the Form button to the Quick Access Toolbar) displays one table row at a time as a clean dialog card—allowing users to add new records, edit or delete existing rows, and search/filter records matching specific field criteria.
★ Exam Points:
• Data Form works cleanly on tables with up to 32 columns (fields).

q: Which of the following would you use to protect a cell from editing in Excel?
exp:
Preventing edits to cells in MS Excel relies on Cell Protection—a two-step mechanism: 1. Check the Locked attribute under Format Cells (Ctrl + 1) > Protection (enabled by default on all cells; uncheck it on input cells you want editable). 2. Activate Review > Protect Sheet so the cell lock actually takes effect.
★ Exam Points:
• Important exam trap: Locking cells in Format Cells has zero effect until Protect Sheet is turned on!

q: In MS Excel, which of the following correctly identifies how rows and columns are labeled as elements of a worksheet?
o: Rows use letters and columns use numbers
Rows use numbers and columns use letters.
Rows and columns both use letters
Rows and columns both use numbers
exp:
In every standard MS Excel worksheet (default A1 reference style), horizontal Rows are labeled with sequential numbers (1, 2, 3, ... up to 1,048,576) and vertical Columns are labeled with letters (A, B, C, ... Z, AA ... up to XFD).
★ Exam Points:
• Note: Excel also has an optional R1C1 reference style (enabled in File > Options > Formulas) where both rows and columns use numbers (e.g., R2C3 for C2), but standard worksheets use numbers for rows and letters for columns.

q: Which statement best describes why using cell references in formulas is better than typing actual numbers directly when editing a spreadsheet?
o: It makes formulas harder to read and understand
It ensures that formulas automatically update when the referenced cells change
It prevents any further editing of the worksheet
It stops the use of functions like SUM and AVERAGE
exp:
Using cell references (like =B2*C2) instead of hard-coding literal numbers (like =250*18) makes a spreadsheet dynamic—whenever a value in any referenced input cell changes, Excel automatically recalculates and updates every dependent formula without manual re-editing.
★ Exam Points:
• Cell references also allow copying a single formula down thousands of rows cleanly via the Fill Handle.

q: Which of these statements best describes how to select multiple non-adjacent cells or ranges for editing in Excel?
o: Click and drag across all cells to be selected
Hold down the Ctrl key and click each cell or range separately
Use the Tab key repeatedly to move and select cells
Use Shift + Enter on each cell
exp:
To select multiple non-adjacent (non-contiguous) cells or cell ranges simultaneously in MS Excel, select the first cell/range, then hold down the Ctrl key while clicking or dragging across each additional cell or range.
★ Exam Points:
• Contrast: Holding Shift while clicking selects a continuous rectangular block between the first and second clicked cell, whereas holding Ctrl selects non-adjacent scattered cells.
• Keyboard-only non-adjacent selection mode in Excel: Shift + F8 ('Add or Remove Selection').

q: What is the function of Ctrl+0?
exp:
In MS Excel, pressing Ctrl + 0 (Ctrl + zero) hides the entire column(s) containing the currently selected cell(s).
★ Exam Points:
• Memory pair: Ctrl + 9 = Hide selected Row(s); Ctrl + 0 = Hide selected Column(s).

q: What is a function of Shift + F9?
o: Calculate active/selected worksheets in the active workbook.
Calculates All the worksheets in All the open workbooks.
Full calculation of "all" the cells in just the "active" workbook.
exp:
In MS Excel (especially when Workbook Calculation is set to Manual), pressing Shift + F9 recalculates formulas only on the currently active/selected worksheet(s) inside the active workbook.
★ Exam Points:
• Excel Calculation Shortcut | Exact Scope
• F9 | Calculates ALL worksheets in ALL open workbooks
• Shift + F9 | Calculates ONLY the active worksheet
• Ctrl + Alt + F9 | Forces a full recalculation of all cells in all open workbooks

q: What is the maximum number of rows allowed in an Excel worksheet?
exp:
In modern MS Excel (Excel 2007, 2010, 2013, 2016, 2019, 2021, and Microsoft 365), a single worksheet supports a (220 maximum of 1,048,576 rows ) and 16,384 columns ( 2¹⁴, from A to XFD).
★ Exam Points:
• Legacy Excel 97–2003 (.xls) worksheets supported (216 65,536 rows ) and 256 columns (A to IV).
• Shortcut to jump instantly to the last row (Row 1,048,576): Ctrl + Down Arrow from an empty column.

q: In Excel, when a formula containing relative references is copied from one cell to another, which statement best describes the editing behavior of the references?
o: The references remain exactly the same in every copied cell
The references adjust based on the relative position of the new cell
The references change only if the destination is in a different worksheet
The references always change to A1
exp:
In MS Excel, relative cell references (like A1 or B2, without $ signs) store relative offsets rather than fixed coordinates —so when copied to another cell, the references automatically shift and adjust based on the relative row and column offset of the new cell.
★ Exam Points:
• For example, copying =A1+B1 from cell C1 down one row into C2 automatically adjusts it to =A2+B2.

q: To move the contents of a cell or range to a new location, which commands would you typically use?
exp:
To move the contents of a cell or range from its current position to a new destination (clearing the source cells), use Cut and Paste (Ctrl + X followed by Ctrl + V, or drag the cell border directly).
★ Exam Points:
• Remember: Move = Cut + Paste (Ctrl + X, Ctrl + V); Duplicate = Copy + Paste (Ctrl + C, Ctrl + V).

q: You enter a number into a cell, but the cell displays: #####, instead of the number. What does this most likely indicate?
o: The formula contains an incorrect name for a function.
The cell is not wide enough to display the entire number or date.
The number contains a division-by-zero error.
The cell contains non-numeric data that cannot be calculated.
exp:
When an Excel cell displays a string of hash/pound signs— #####—after entering a number, currency, date, or time, it almost always indicates that the column is not wide enough to display the full formatted number or date (widening/AutoFitting the column immediately reveals the number).
★ Exam Points:
• Second cause of ##### in Excel: a formula producing a negative date or negative time value.
• Compare real formula errors: #NAME? = misspelled function; #DIV/0! = division by zero; #VALUE! = wrong data type.

q: Which of the following editing operations is best when the user wants to remove a few inner columns and shift the remaining data left to close the gap?
o: Use Clear Contents on the selected columns
Use Delete Columns in the Cells group
Use Merge & Center on the columns
exp:
When you want to completely remove inner columns and have the columns on their right automatically slide left to close the empty gap, select those columns and use Delete Columns in the Cells group on the Home tab (or right-click column headers → Delete, or press Ctrl + -).
★ Exam Points:
• Contrast: Clear Contents leaves empty blank columns behind; Hide merely conceals them without removing their data.

q: Which function in Excel is most suitable for calculating cumulative total such that cell C3 contains C2 plus B3 (where B column has new values added)?
exp:
To maintain a running (cumulative) total in Column C where Column B holds each row's new transaction/entry and cell C2 already holds the previous cumulative total, the exact formula in cell C3 is =C2+B3 (previous running total + current row's new value).
★ Exam Points:
• Alternative anchored-range cumulative sum formula in C2 dragged down: =SUM($B$2:B2) (becomes =SUM($B$2:B3) in C3).
• Note why Option 2 fails: =SUM(C2:B3) spans a 2×2 rec-tangle (B2, C2, B3, C3), creating a circular reference in C3!

q: Which of the following is the correct Excel formula to calculate the square root of 25?
exp:
Excel's dedicated built-in mathematical function for finding the positive square root of a number is =SQRT(25), which returns 5. (Excel has no functions named ROOT or SQUARE; while =POWER(25, 0.5) also computes 25⁰.⁵ = 5 via general exponentiation, =SQRT() is Excel's specific square-root function.)
★ Exam Points:
• Passing a negative number to =SQRT(-25) returns the #NUM! error (use =SQRT(ABS(-25)) if magnitude is desired).

q: In MS Excel, what is the intersection of a row and a column on a worksheet called?
exp:
In MS Excel, the rectangular box formed where a horizontal row and a vertical column meet on a worksheet is called a Cell.
★ Exam Points:
• Compare terms: Cell = single row-column intersection (e.g., B4); Range = group of cells (e.g., B4:D10); Sheet = entire worksheet grid; Field = column in a database table.

q: When using AutoFill for a text like "Mon" in a cell, which setting should be applied or accepted so that dragging the Fill Handle downward continues the series to "Tue", "Wed", and so on?
o: Choose "Copy Cells" in the AutoFill options
Choose "Fill Series" in the AutoFill options
Choose "Fill Formatting Only" in the AutoFill options
Choose "Clear Contents" in the AutoFill options
exp:
Excel recognizes built-in chronological lists like Mon, Tue, Wed... and Jan, Feb, Mar.... Dragging the Fill Handle downward on "Mon" with "Fill Series" selected in the AutoFill Options smart tag advances the weekday sequence automatically to "Tue", "Wed", "Thu"....
★ Exam Points:
• By contrast, choosing Copy Cells repeats "Mon", "Mon", "Mon" in every cell, and Fill Formatting Only copies cell styling without any text.

q: In Excel, which element of the spreadsheet visually indicates which cell is currently active and ready for editing?
o: The dotted grid lines around the worksheet
The bold border around a single cell (active cell)
exp:
In MS Excel, the Active Cell—the cell currently selected to receive keyboard input or editing—is visually distinguished on the grid by a thick bold (green/dark) rectangular border around that single cell (with the small square Fill Handle at its bottom-right corner).
★ Exam Points:
• The address of the Active Cell (e.g., C5) is simultaneously displayed in the Name Box to the left of the Formula Bar.

q: While editing, which feature is most appropriate for visually indicating duplicate values in a column, so that they can be reviewed or changed?
o: Conditional Formatting with a "Duplicate Values" rule
exp:
To highlight repeated entries (such as duplicate roll numbers, Aadhaar numbers, or invoice IDs) visually without deleting them first so an editor can inspect them, apply Conditional Formatting with a "Duplicate Values" rule (Home > Conditional Formatting > Highlight Cells Rules > Duplicate Values).
★ Exam Points:
• Contrast: Data > Remove Duplicates immediately deletes duplicate rows, whereas Conditional Formatting > Duplicate Values safely highlights them in colour for manual review!

q: What is the maximum number of columns allowed in an Excel worksheet?
exp:
In modern MS Excel (Excel 2007 and later, .xlsx format), the maximum number of columns allowed in a single worksheet is 16,384 (2¹⁴), labeled alphabetically from A to XFD.
★ Exam Points:
• Quick summary of Excel 2007+ sheet limits: (220
• Maximum Rows = 1,048,576 ) (214
• Maximum Columns = 16,384 , last column = XFD)
• Legacy Excel 97–2003 had only 256 columns (last column = IV).

q: In MS Excel, which component is used to display and edit the contents or formula of the selected cell, even if the content is longer than the visible width of the cell?
exp:
Located between the Ribbon and the worksheet column headers (to the right of the Name Box and fx button), MS Excel's Formula bar displays and lets you edit the complete raw contents or underlying formula of the selected cell— even when the cell itself is narrow or displays only the calculated result.
★ Exam Points:
• Pressing Ctrl + Shift + U expands or collapses the Formula Bar vertically for multi-line formulas.

q: Which description best explains the difference between hiding a column and deleting a column when editing a spreadsheet?
o: Hiding removes data permanently, deleting keeps data temporarily
Hiding makes the column invisible without removing data, deleting removes the column and its data
Both hiding and deleting remove the column permanently
Hiding is only for rows and deleting only for columns
exp:
Comparing Hide Column vs Delete Column in MS Excel: • Hiding a column (Ctrl + 0) merely makes that column visually invisible on screen and printouts while keeping all its values intact and usable by formulas. • Deleting a column permanently removes the column and its data (shifting right-hand columns left and causing #REF! in formulas pointing purely to deleted cells).
★ Exam Points:
• Hidden columns can be restored anytime via Right-click adjacent headers → Unhide.

q: Which of the following correctly identifies how rows and columns are labeled in a standard MS Excel worksheet?
o: Rows by letters, columns by numbers
Rows by numbers, columns by letters
Both rows and columns by letters
Both rows and columns by numbers
exp:
In a standard MS Excel worksheet, horizontal Rows are labeled sequentially by numbers (1, 2, 3, ... 1,048,576) and vertical Columns are labeled alphabetically by letters (A, B, C, ... Z, AA ... XFD).
★ Exam Points:
• In every standard cell address (e.g., F12), the column letter (F) always comes first, followed by the row number (12).

q: Which of the following actions is most suitable if a user wants to check how the worksheet will look on paper before actually printing, so that further editing can be done if alignment is poor?
exp:
Before sending an Excel worksheet to a physical printer, opening Print Preview (via File > Print or keyboard shortcut Ctrl + F2 / Ctrl + P) shows exactly how columns, rows, margins, orientation, and page breaks will fit on paper—allowing you to adjust scaling or alignment without wasting paper.
★ Exam Points:
• Useful scaling options in Excel's Print Preview: Fit Sheet on One Page, Fit All Columns on One Page, and Fit All Rows on One Page.

q: In Excel, which operation is best suited when the user wants to quickly adjust all columns so that their contents are fully visible after editing various cell entries?
o: Select all columns and use AutoFit Column Width
Use Clear Contents on all columns
Use AutoFill to repeat column headers
exp:
When cell entries across many columns have been edited and several columns are too narrow or unevenly wide, the fastest clean fix is to select all columns (e.g., Ctrl + A or clicking the top-left Select All triangle) and apply AutoFit Column Width (via Home > Format > AutoFit Column Width or double-clicking any selected column boundary).
★ Exam Points:
• Keyboard Ribbon sequence to AutoFit all selected columns in Excel: Alt → H → O → I.

q: What function would you use to get the current month in Excel?
exp:
In MS Excel, =TODAY() returns the current system date, and wrapping it inside =MONTH(serial_number) extracts the integer month number (from 1 for January to 12 for December)—giving the nested formula =MONTH(TODAY()).
★ Exam Points:
• Similarly, for the current year use =YEAR(TODAY()), and for the current day of the month (1–31) use =DAY(TODAY()).
• Excel has no built-in functions named CURRENTMONTH() or CURRENTDATE().

q: Why is it useful to have clear column headings (Name, Quantity, Price) at the top of each column?
o: Headings describe the data in each column
exp:
Headings explain the contents and are used by filters, tables and PivotTables.
★ Exam Points:
• Freeze top row to keep headings visible.
• Tables use headers in structured references.
• Print Titles repeat headings.

q: What happens when you select an entire row and choose Insert from the right-click menu?
o: A new blank row is inserted above the selected row and existing rows shift down
A row is inserted below without shifting
exp:
Insert adds a blank row above the selection; rows below move down.
★ Exam Points:
• Ctrl + Shift + + also inserts.
• Formatting is copied from above by default.
• Insert Options button appears.

q: Which is the safest method to close only the current workbook while keeping Excel open?
exp:
File → Close (Ctrl + W / Ctrl + F4) closes the workbook but leaves Excel running.
★ Exam Points:
• File → Exit (Alt + F4) closes Excel.
• Excel prompts to save changes.
• AutoRecover saves periodic copies.

q: A workbook has sheets named "Data", "Summary" and "Charts". What does this naming practice show?
o: It indicates a deliberate, organised structure
exp:
Descriptive sheet names show the purpose of each sheet and make navigation easy.
★ Exam Points:
• Sheet names up to 31 characters.
• Tab colours aid organisation.
• Formulas use names like Data!A1.

q: Why is inserting a new row just above a grand-total row safer than typing new records below the total?
o: Total formulas usually refer to the rows above them, so inserted rows are automatically included
exp:
A SUM range like B2:B20 expands when rows are inserted inside it, so the total stays correct.
★ Exam Points:
• Rows added below the total are not included.
• Excel Tables auto-expand.
• Check totals after inserting.

q: Which Paste Special option copies calculated results from one range to another without copying the formulas?
exp:
Paste Values pastes only the results, converting formulas to fixed values.
★ Exam Points:
• Ctrl + Alt + V, V.
• Useful before deleting source data.
• Values + Number Formats keeps formatting of numbers.

q: Which function finds the average of numbers in B2:B20 while ignoring empty cells automatically?
exp:
AVERAGE ignores blank cells and text; it divides by the count of numeric cells only.
★ Exam Points:
• Zeros are included in AVERAGE.
• AVERAGEA treats text as 0.
• MEAN/AVG are invalid names.

q: Which option under the File tab shows information like file size, author and last modified date and also provides commands to protect or inspect the workbook?
exp:
File → Info shows properties and offers Protect Workbook, Inspect Workbook and Manage Workbook.
★ Exam Points:
• Properties can be edited.
• Check for Issues → Inspect.
• Version history appears for cloud files.

q: A user wants to prevent anyone from adding, deleting or moving worksheets but still allow data editing in cells. Which command should be applied?
exp:
Review → Protect Workbook protects the workbook structure (sheets) while cell editing remains allowed.
★ Exam Points:
• Protect Sheet controls cell editing.
• A password is optional.
• Encrypt with Password controls opening.

q: When an Excel formula displays #DIV/0!, what does it indicate?
o: The formula is dividing a number by zero or by an empty cell
The cell is formatted as percentage
exp:
#DIV/0! occurs when the divisor is 0 or blank.
★ Exam Points:
• Use IFERROR to handle it.
• =IF(B1=0,"",A1/B1) avoids it.
• #NAME? is for misspelt names.

q: What information is normally shown in Excel's Status Bar?
o: Information such as average/sum of selected cells, view buttons and zoom
exp:
The status bar shows mode, quick calculations (Average, Count, Sum), view buttons and zoom slider.
★ Exam Points:
• Right-click to customise.
• Shows Caps Lock status.
• Shows page number in Page Layout view.

q: Why does using a consistent number format for a column of amounts make editing and checking easier?
o: It displays all amounts in a uniform style, making mistakes easier to spot
exp:
Uniform formats (e.g., ₹#,##0.00) make values easy to compare and errors stand out.
★ Exam Points:
• Ctrl + Shift + 4 – currency.
• Accounting format aligns symbols.
• Formats don't change values.

q: You want to enter the same heading in several non-adjacent cells at once. Which method works?
o: Select all the required cells, type the heading and press Ctrl + Enter
Type in one cell and press Shift + Delete
Drag the fill handle without selection
exp:
Ctrl + Enter fills the typed entry into every selected cell simultaneously.
★ Exam Points:
• Use Ctrl + click to select non-adjacent cells.
• Works with formulas too.
• Ctrl + D fills down.

q: In MS Excel, what category of cell reference is $C7?
exp:
$ before C fixes the column; row 7 remains relative.
★ Exam Points:
• C$7 – relative column, absolute row.
• $C$7 – fully absolute.
• F4 toggles types.

q: Which print option adjusts how much of the worksheet prints on each page without changing the data?
o: Using Page Setup to adjust scaling or fit options
exp:
Scaling (Adjust to % or Fit to pages wide/tall) resizes the printout only.
★ Exam Points:
• Page Layout → Scale to Fit.
• Doesn't affect cell values.
• Print preview checks result.

q: Someone copies a sheet and experiments with new assumptions on the copy while preserving the original. Which principle does this illustrate?
o: Separation of experimental changes from the trusted base version to reduce risk
exp:
Working on a copy protects the original model from accidental errors.
★ Exam Points:
• Ctrl + drag a sheet tab copies it.
• Move or Copy dialog also works.
• Scenario Manager stores alternatives.

q: In a large Excel worksheet you need to move quickly to cell Z500. Which method is most efficient?
o: Type Z500 in the Name Box (or Go To, Ctrl + G) and press Enter
exp:
Typing an address in the Name Box or Go To jumps directly to that cell.
★ Exam Points:
• F5 also opens Go To.
• Ctrl + Home – cell A1.
• Ctrl + End – last used cell.

q: Why is it better to use separate columns "Item" and "Quantity" instead of writing "5 pens" in one cell?
o: Excel cannot store text and numbers separately
Separate columns allow numeric operations like SUM and sorting
"5 pens" is the only valid format
exp:
Quantities stored as numbers can be added, averaged and charted; text like "5 pens" cannot.
★ Exam Points:
• One fact per cell is a data rule.
• Text numbers are left-aligned.
• Use units in headers.

q: Which feature combines adjacent cells into one larger cell and centres the content?
exp:
Merge & Center joins cells and centres the text – commonly used for titles.
★ Exam Points:
• Merge Across merges row-wise.
• Unmerge Cells reverses it.
• Center Across Selection avoids merging.

q: In the Excel function =SUM(A1:A5), how is A1:A5 classified?
exp:
Values or ranges given inside a function’s brackets are its arguments.
★ Exam Points:
• SUM can take up to 255 arguments.
• Arguments are separated by commas.
• Colon is the range operator inside the argument.

q: How does strong command over functions and formulas in Excel improve work with data?
o: It removes the need to plan structure
It allows data to be calculated, checked and summarised accurately
exp:
Functions automate calculations and summaries, reducing manual errors.
★ Exam Points:
• Use auditing tools to check formulas.
• Errors can still occur from bad inputs.
• Functions save time.

q: Which is an advantage of using Excel instead of doing calculations on paper?
o: Only one value can be stored
Formulas can be updated and recalculated automatically
exp:
Changing an input automatically recalculates all dependent results.
★ Exam Points:
• What-If Analysis tests scenarios.
• Charts update automatically.
• Reduces arithmetic errors.

q: Why is it helpful to understand Page Layout options (margins, orientation, scaling) even when working mainly on screen?
o: They determine how the worksheet will appear when printed
exp:
Page Layout settings decide margins, orientation and fit when printing.
★ Exam Points:
• Fit to 1 page wide is common.
• Print Titles repeat headers.
• Page Break Preview helps adjust.

q: When you use Wrap Text on a selected cell, how are the contents displayed?
o: Displayed on multiple lines within the same cell
exp:
Wrap Text breaks long text into multiple lines inside the cell, increasing row height.
★ Exam Points:
• Alt + Enter inserts manual breaks.
• Row height auto-adjusts.
• Found in Home → Alignment.

q: Why is it useful to clearly separate input cells, calculation cells and output cells in a worksheet?
o: It makes the sheet harder to read
It helps users know where to enter data, where formulas are and where results appear
exp:
Clear layout reduces errors and makes models easier to audit and update.
★ Exam Points:
• Colour-code input cells.
• Protect formula cells.
• Document assumptions.

q: Why is it important to understand operator precedence when creating complex Excel formulas?
o: It determines the order of operations and can change the result
exp:
Excel evaluates ^ before * and /, then + and −; brackets override this order.
★ Exam Points:
• =2+3*4 = 14 but =(2+3)*4 = 20.
• Comparison operators are evaluated last.
• & (concatenation) comes before comparisons.

q: A worksheet column mixes numeric codes and text comments; later it is difficult to sort and analyse the codes. What does this illustrate?
o: Mixing different types of data in the same field causes analysis problems
Comments must be in a separate workbook
exp:
Each column should hold one type of data; mixing text and numbers breaks sorting and calculations.
★ Exam Points:
• Keep comments in a separate column.
• Use Data Validation to control types.
• Tables work best with clean columns.

q: When saving a workbook for the first time, what does the Save As command allow the user to do?
o: Choose a file name and storage location for the workbook
exp:
Save As lets you specify name, folder and file type.
★ Exam Points:
• First Ctrl + S also opens Save As.
• Choose .xlsx, .xlsm, .csv, .pdf.
• F12 opens Save As.

q: A user wants to insert a new column between existing columns B and C. Which method is correct?
o: Right-click column B → Insert; the new column appears right of B
Right-click column C → Insert; the new column appears to the left of column C
Select column A and press Delete
exp:
Insert adds a column to the left of the selected column, so inserting at C places it between B and C.
★ Exam Points:
• Ctrl + Shift + + inserts.
• Old column C becomes D.
• Formulas adjust automatically.

q: Why do meaningful names for important cells or ranges make formulas easier to work with?
exp:
=Sales*GST is easier to understand than =B7*$F$2.
★ Exam Points:
• Names appear in formula AutoComplete.
• Manage with Name Manager.
• Scope can be workbook or sheet.

q: When a long number or text does not fit within a column, which basic action can increase the visible width of that column?
o: Dragging the column boundary to the right on the column header
Dragging the boundary on a column footer
exp:
Dragging the right edge of the column header widens the column.
★ Exam Points:
• Double-click boundary to AutoFit.
• Format → Column Width sets exact width.
• ##### shows when numbers don't fit.

q: What is the main advantage of using multiple worksheets within one workbook?
o: It groups related data in one file
exp:
Keeping related tables on different sheets of one workbook keeps data organised and linkable.
★ Exam Points:
• Formulas can refer to other sheets (Sheet2!A1).
• 3D references summarise across sheets.
• Sheets can be colour-coded.

q: Why does converting a key input cell such as a tax rate into a named range like "TaxRate" make future formula editing easier?
o: The name makes formulas readable and lets the input move without rewriting formulas
exp:
Named ranges make formulas self-explanatory (=Amount*TaxRate) and update automatically if the cell moves.
★ Exam Points:
• Define names via Name Box or Name Manager.
• Names are absolute by default.
• Names can't contain spaces.

q: Which error appears when a lookup or reference function cannot find the requested value?
exp:
#N/A ("not available") is returned by VLOOKUP, MATCH, XLOOKUP when no match exists.
★ Exam Points:
• IFNA handles #N/A.
• #REF! – invalid reference.
• #DIV/0! – divide by zero.

q: Which practices best support a workbook prepared for long-term use?
o: Random sheet names, mixed data, no backups
Clear sheet names, structured tables with headings and regular backups in more than one location
Everything on one sheet with no headings
exp:
Good structure and backups make data understandable and safe over time.
★ Exam Points:
• Follow 3-2-1 backups.
• Use Excel Tables for data.
• Document assumptions on a separate sheet.

q: Which shortcut is used to close a workbook in MS-Excel 2010?
exp:
Ctrl + F4 (or Ctrl + W) closes the active workbook window.
★ Exam Points:
• Alt + F4 closes Excel.
• Ctrl + F3 – Name Manager.
• Ctrl + F1 – collapse Ribbon.

q: The formula =B2+4 is in cell A1 of MS-Excel 2010. If A1 is copied and pasted into D4, what will be the formula in D4?
exp:
From A1 to D4 is +3 columns and +3 rows, so B2 becomes E5; constants stay the same.
★ Exam Points:
• Relative references adjust on copy.
• Constants (4) never change.
• =$B$2+4 would remain the same.

q: In MS-Excel 2010, the ____ function returns the year corresponding to a date.
exp:
=YEAR(date) returns a four-digit year, e.g. =YEAR(TODAY()).
★ Exam Points:
• MONTH and DAY extract month and day.
• DATE(y,m,d) builds a date.
• DATEDIF finds differences (hidden function).

q: Choose the wrong option with respect to MS-Excel 2010.
o: Alt + 0 is used to hide columns.
Ctrl + 9 is used to hide rows.
Ctrl + 0 is used to hide columns.
The Home tab contains the most frequently used commands.
exp:
Columns are hidden with Ctrl + 0, not Alt + 0.
★ Exam Points:
• Ctrl + 9 – hide rows.
• Ctrl + Shift + 9 – unhide rows.
• Ctrl + Shift + 0 – unhide columns.

q: What will be the address of the cell at the intersection of the seventh row and tenth column in MS-Excel 2010?
exp:
The tenth column is J; with row 7 the address is J7.
★ Exam Points:
• A=1, B=2 … J=10.
• Absolute form: $J$7.
• Column letters come first.

q: The ____ tab in MS-Excel 2010 provides tools to manage worksheet appearance, both onscreen and printed – themes, gridlines, margins, alignment and print area.
exp:
Page Layout tab has Themes, Page Setup (Margins, Orientation, Size, Print Area), Scale to Fit and Sheet Options.
★ Exam Points:
• Print Titles repeat headers on every page.
• Alt + P opens Page Layout.
• Gridlines can be printed via Sheet Options.

q: Which MS-Excel function rounds a number up to the nearest integer or to the nearest multiple of significance?
exp:
CEILING (CEILING.MATH) rounds a number up to the nearest multiple of significance.
★ Exam Points:
• =CEILING(7,5) → 10.
• FLOOR rounds down.
• ROUNDUP rounds away from zero to given digits.

q: The Data Validation option is present in the ____ tab of MS-Excel 2010.
exp:
Data → Data Tools → Data Validation restricts what can be entered in cells (lists, ranges, dates).
★ Exam Points:
• Drop-down lists are made with validation.
• Circle Invalid Data highlights wrong entries.
• Input and error messages can be set.

q: Which formula will give an error in Microsoft Excel 2016?
exp:
A9:15 is an invalid range (mixes a cell with a row number), so Excel shows an error.
★ Exam Points:
• Valid ranges: A9:A15 or 9:15 (full rows).
• #NAME? / #REF! / #VALUE! are common errors.
• Excel will show a formula error message.

q: What is the result of the MS-Excel formula =FLOOR(3,3)+CEILING(4,4)?
exp:
FLOOR(3,3) = 3 and CEILING(4,4) = 4, since both numbers are already multiples; 3 + 4 = 7.
★ Exam Points:
• FLOOR rounds down to a multiple.
• CEILING rounds up to a multiple.
• =CEILING(4.1,4) → 8.

q: What is the result of the MS-Excel formula =256/8/4/2?
exp:
Division is evaluated left to right: 256/8 = 32, 32/4 = 8, 8/2 = 4.
★ Exam Points:
• Same-precedence operators go left to right.
• =256/(8/4/2) = 256.
• Excel uses BODMAS-like precedence.

q: What is the result of the MS-Excel formula =CEILING(7,5)?
exp:
CEILING rounds 7 up to the nearest multiple of 5, which is 10.
★ Exam Points:
• =FLOOR(7,5) → 5.
• =MROUND(7,5) → 5.
• =ROUNDUP(7.1,0) → 8.

q: Which key is used to select a range of continuous cells in MS-Excel?
exp:
Click the first cell, hold Shift and click the last cell (or use Shift + arrow keys) to select a continuous range.
★ Exam Points:
• Ctrl + click selects non-adjacent cells.
• F8 turns on Extend Selection mode.
• Shift + F8 adds non-adjacent selections.

q: Which of the following appears at the top of a worksheet (below the Ribbon) in MS-Excel?
exp:
The formula bar appears above the column headings; scroll bars are on the right/bottom and the status bar at the bottom.
★ Exam Points:
• Formula bar shows active cell contents.
• Name Box is to its left.
• Can be hidden from View tab.

q: What is the address of the cell at the intersection of the fifth row and fifth column in MS-Excel 2010?
exp:
The fifth column is E, so the cell is E5 (relative reference).
★ Exam Points:
• $E$5 is the absolute form.
• Column letter always comes first.
• Name Box shows E5 when selected.

q: When the contents of a cell are being edited in MS-Excel 2010, they are displayed in the ____.
exp:
The formula bar shows (and allows editing of) the actual contents or formula of the active cell.
★ Exam Points:
• Ctrl + Shift + U expands the formula bar.
• fx button opens Insert Function.
• Status bar shows "Edit" mode.

q: Which of the following is a wrong declaration in MS-Excel 2010?
exp:
TIMEVALUE accepts recognised date-time text; a string starting with the weekday name is not recognised and returns #VALUE!.
★ Exam Points:
• TIMEVALUE returns a decimal 0–0.99999.
• Date part in the text is ignored.
• DATEVALUE converts a date text to a serial number.

q: Which of the following is a function in MS-Excel 2010?
exp:
SUM is a built-in Excel function; RANGE, ADD and FORMULA are not functions.
★ Exam Points:
• Functions start with = sign in a formula.
• Excel has 400+ functions.
• Shift + F3 opens Insert Function.

q: The Header & Footer option is present in the ____ tab of the MS-Excel 2010 ribbon.
exp:
Insert → Text group → Header & Footer switches to Page Layout view to add headers/footers.
★ Exam Points:
• Page Layout view shows headers on screen.
• Can add page numbers, date, file name.
• Also via Page Setup dialog.

q:
What is the value of the following expression in MS-Excel 2010?
=22-12/3/2+4
exp:
Division is done first, left to right: 12/3 = 4, 4/2 = 2; then 22 − 2 + 4 = 24.
★ Exam Points:
• Excel order: () → ^ → * / → + −.
• Same-level operators go left to right.
• Negation (−) has highest priority after reference operators.

q: In MS-Excel 2010, to select two or more non-adjacent worksheets, click the first sheet tab and hold down the ____ key while clicking the other tabs.
exp:
Ctrl + click selects non-adjacent sheets; Shift + click selects adjacent ones.
★ Exam Points:
• Grouped sheets show [Group] in the title.
• Edits apply to all grouped sheets.
• Right-click → Ungroup Sheets.

q: Choose the wrong option with respect to MS-Excel 2010.
o: We can insert comments in a cell.
Ctrl + O is used to open an existing file.
We can save the file using F2.
We can insert a table from the Insert tab.
exp:
F2 edits the active cell; saving uses Ctrl + S or Shift + F12 (F12 for Save As).
★ Exam Points:
• F2 – edit mode.
• Ctrl + S – save.
• Ctrl + O – open.

q: The ____ function in MS-Excel changes all characters of the text to uppercase.
exp:
=UPPER(text) converts all letters to capitals.
★ Exam Points:
• =UPPER("delhi") → DELHI.
• LOWER makes all small letters.
• PROPER capitalises the first letter of each word.

q: Which MS-Excel 2010 function converts a date stored as text into a serial number that Excel recognises as a date?
exp:
DATEVALUE("15-08-2026") returns the date serial number.
★ Exam Points:
• EDATE adds months to a date.
• TIMEVALUE converts time text.
• Excel date 1 = 01-01-1900.

q: The ____ formula in MS-Excel 2010 has the primary function of adding specific cells.
exp:
=SUM() adds numbers in cells or ranges.
★ Exam Points:
• AutoSum shortcut: Alt + =.
• SUMIF/SUMIFS add with conditions.
• SUMPRODUCT multiplies and adds arrays.

q: In MS-Excel 2010, the ____ function provides the current system date and time.
exp:
=NOW() returns both the current date and time and updates on recalculation.
★ Exam Points:
• TODAY() returns only the date.
• YEAR() extracts the year from a date.
• F9 recalculates the workbook.

q: Choose the wrong option with respect to MS-Excel 2010.
o: Ctrl + F is used to find text within the sheet.
The Home tab contains the most frequently used commands like copy, paste, sort, filter and formatting.
Alt + Enter starts a new line of text within a worksheet cell.
We can save the file by pressing F3.
exp:
F3 opens the Paste Name dialog; files are saved with Ctrl + S or F12 (Save As).
★ Exam Points:
• Shift + F12 also saves.
• F3 works only when named ranges exist.
• Ctrl + H – Replace.

q: In MS-Excel 2010, we can collapse the ribbon to get extra space by right-clicking it and choosing Minimize the Ribbon, or by pressing ____.
exp:
Ctrl + F1 shows or hides (collapses) the Ribbon.
★ Exam Points:
• Double-clicking a tab also collapses the Ribbon.
• Alt + F1 creates an embedded chart.
• Ctrl + Shift + F1 toggles full-screen ribbon mode in Excel 365.

q: When you select the range B3:G9 starting from B3 in an MS-Excel 2010 worksheet, what will be displayed in the Name Box?
exp:
After selection, the Name Box shows the active cell, which is the cell where selection started (B3).
★ Exam Points:
• While dragging, the Name Box briefly shows rows × columns (e.g., 7R x 6C).
• Active cell stays white inside the selection.
• Name Box can define a named range.

q: What is the maximum number of characters that can be typed in a cell of MS-Excel?
exp:
An Excel cell can hold up to 32,767 characters; only 1,024 are displayed in the cell (all appear in the formula bar).
★ Exam Points:
• Maximum formula length: 8,192 characters.
• Column width max: 255 characters.
• Rows: 1,048,576; Columns: 16,384.

q: Choose the wrong option with respect to MS-Excel 2010.
o: Ctrl + H is used for replacing text within the sheet.
Ctrl + R is used for replacing text within the sheet.
Alt + Enter enters a new line in the text of a particular cell.
The Home tab contains the most frequently used commands.
exp:
Ctrl + R is Fill Right (copies the left cell into selected cells); Replace is Ctrl + H.
★ Exam Points:
• Ctrl + D – Fill Down.
• Ctrl + F – Find.
• In Word, Ctrl + R is right-align.

q: In MS-Excel 2010, the ____ operation is used to arrange data in a particular order.
exp:
Sorting arranges data in ascending (A–Z, smallest–largest) or descending order.
★ Exam Points:
• Sort is in Data tab and Home → Editing.
• Custom sort can use multiple levels.
• Filter shows only matching rows.

q: Which option is correct for enabling Edit mode directly in cells of MS-Excel 2010 and above?
o: File > Options > Customize Ribbon, then under Editing options select Allow editing directly in cells
File > Options > Customize Ribbon and select Allow editing directly in cells
File > Options > Advanced, then under Editing options select Allow editing directly in cells
File > Options > Trust Center and select Allow editing directly in cells
exp:
The "Allow editing directly in cells" check box is in File → Options → Advanced → Editing options.
★ Exam Points:
• When disabled, editing happens only in the formula bar.
• F2 starts editing the active cell.
• Trust Center deals with security/macros.

q: ____ shortcut key is used in MS-Excel 2010 to go to the View tab.
exp:
Alt + W activates the View tab (Window); Alt + N – Insert; Alt + A – Data.
★ Exam Points:
• Alt + H – Home; Alt + M – Formulas; Alt + P – Page Layout.
• Alt + R – Review.
• KeyTips appear when you press Alt.

q: In MS-Excel 2010, ____ are named from A onwards and ____ are named from 1 onwards.
exp:
Columns are labelled with letters (A, B, … XFD) and rows with numbers (1 to 1,048,576).
★ Exam Points:
• Total columns: 16,384.
• After Z come AA, AB … .
• R1C1 notation numbers both.

q: The Hide (window) option is present in the ____ tab of the MS-Excel 2010 ribbon.
exp:
View → Window group has Hide and Unhide for workbook windows.
★ Exam Points:
• Hide rows/columns: Home → Format → Hide & Unhide.
• Freeze Panes is also in the View tab.
• New Window and Split are in the Window group.

q: In MS-Excel 2010, ____ is used for hiding columns within the sheet.
exp:
Ctrl + 0 (zero) hides selected columns; Ctrl + 9 hides selected rows.
★ Exam Points:
• Ctrl + Shift + 9 unhides rows.
• Ctrl + Shift + 0 unhides columns (if allowed).
• Hidden columns can also be unhidden by double-clicking the border.

q: In MS-Excel 2010, the ____ function provides only the current system date.
exp:
=TODAY() returns the current date without time.
★ Exam Points:
• NOW() returns date and time.
• Ctrl + ; enters today’s date as a fixed value.
• TODAY is volatile (recalculates).

q: The ____ function in MS-Excel 2010 returns the total number of characters in a string.
exp:
=LEN(text) counts all characters including spaces.
★ Exam Points:
• LEN("India 2026") = 10.
• TRIM removes extra spaces.
• COUNTA counts non-empty cells, not characters.

q: The ____ is the lower edge of the worksheet window that displays various information about an Excel worksheet.
exp:
The status bar at the bottom shows mode indicators, quick statistics (Average, Count, Sum), zoom and view buttons.
★ Exam Points:
• Status bar can be customised by right-clicking.
• Title bar is at the top.
• Ribbon holds the command tabs.

q:
Consider the following statements about the EXACT() function of MS-Excel.
P: It compares two text strings and returns TRUE if they are exactly the same.
Q: It returns 1 if they are not exactly the same.
R: It returns FALSE if they are not exactly the same.
Which is/are true?
exp:
EXACT is case-sensitive and returns TRUE for identical strings and FALSE otherwise; it never returns 1.
★ Exam Points:
• =EXACT("Delhi","delhi") → FALSE.
• The = operator is not case-sensitive.
• EXACT ignores formatting differences.

q: The Unhide (window) option is present in the ____ tab of the MS-Excel 2010 ribbon.
exp:
Unhide for hidden workbook windows is in View → Window group.
★ Exam Points:
• Hide sheet: right-click sheet tab → Hide.
• Unhide sheet: right-click any tab → Unhide.
• Very hidden sheets need VBA.

q: ____ shortcut key is used to move to the previous sheet in MS-Excel 2010.
exp:
Ctrl + Page Up moves to the previous (left) worksheet; Ctrl + Page Down to the next sheet.
★ Exam Points:
• Alt + Page Up/Down scrolls one screen left/right.
• Shift + F11 inserts a new sheet.
• Right-click the navigation arrows to list all sheets.

q: ____ shortcut key is used to move to the next sheet in an MS-Excel 2010 workbook.
exp:
Ctrl + Page Down activates the next worksheet to the right.
★ Exam Points:
• Ctrl + Page Up – previous sheet.
• Ctrl + Shift + Page Down selects the current and next sheet.
• Sheet tabs appear at the bottom-left.

q: The ____ tab of the MS-Excel 2010 ribbon opens Backstage view, containing essential file-related commands and Excel Options.
exp:
The File tab opens Backstage view with New, Open, Save, Print, Share, Export and Options.
★ Exam Points:
• Backstage view introduced in Office 2010.
• Office 2007 had the Office Button instead.
• Alt + F opens the File tab.

q: In MS-Excel 2010, the ____ feature helps us quickly add the numeric values of a range.
exp:
AutoSum (Σ) automatically inserts a SUM formula for adjacent numbers.
★ Exam Points:
• Shortcut: Alt + =.
• AutoSum dropdown offers Average, Count, Max, Min.
• AutoFill copies or extends series.

q: What is the maximum zoom percentage in MS-Excel 2010?
exp:
Excel zoom ranges from 10% to 400%.
★ Exam Points:
• Word zoom ranges from 10% to 500%.
• Zoom slider is on the status bar.
• Ctrl + mouse scroll also zooms.

q: Counting the number of cells in a range that meet a specific criterion in MS-Excel 2010 can be done using ____.
exp:
=COUNTIF(range, criteria) counts cells meeting one condition, e.g. =COUNTIF(A1:A10,">50").
★ Exam Points:
• COUNTIFS handles multiple criteria.
• COUNT counts numeric cells.
• SUMIF adds cells meeting a condition.

q: In a worksheet the number 10 is stored in cell B2. What is the absolute address of this cell?
exp:
An absolute reference places $ before both column and row: $B$2.
★ Exam Points:
• $B2 – column absolute.
• B$2 – row absolute.
• Press F4 to toggle.

q: Tables created through the Table feature of MS-Excel 2010 allow users to filter by different values of each ____.
exp:
Each column header in an Excel table gets a filter drop-down to filter or sort that column.
★ Exam Points:
• Ctrl + Shift + L toggles filters.
• Total Row can be added from Table Design.
• Tables auto-expand when new data is added.

q: Which shortcut key is used to insert a new worksheet in an existing workbook?
exp:
Shift + F11 (or Alt + Shift + F1) inserts a new worksheet before the active sheet.
★ Exam Points:
• F11 creates a chart sheet.
• Shift + F10 opens the shortcut (right-click) menu.
• New sheet button (+) is next to sheet tabs.

q: In MS-Excel 2010, ____ is used for replacing text within the sheet.
exp:
Ctrl + H opens Find and Replace on the Replace tab.
★ Exam Points:
• Ctrl + F – Find tab.
• Replace All changes all matches at once.
• Wildcards * and ? can be used.

q: Which font style is NOT available in the MS-Excel 2010 Font dialog box?
exp:
Font styles are Regular, Italic, Bold and Bold Italic; there is no Superbold.
★ Exam Points:
• Effects: Strikethrough, Superscript, Subscript.
• Underline types: Single, Double, Single Accounting, Double Accounting.
• Ctrl + Shift + F opens Font tab.

q: In MS-Excel 2010, a ____ is a table of grouped values that aggregates the items of a more extensive table within one or more discrete categories.
exp:
A PivotTable summarises large data by grouping and aggregating (sum, count, average) across categories.
★ Exam Points:
• Insert → PivotTable.
• Fields go into Rows, Columns, Values, Filters.
• PivotChart is its graphical form.

q: Choose the wrong option in relation to a cell.
o: Cells can contain formatting attributes that change how letters, numbers and dates are displayed.
Cells can contain text and numbers but not dates.
Any information entered in a spreadsheet is stored in a cell.
Cells can contain text, numbers and dates.
exp:
Cells can store dates (as serial numbers) as well as text, numbers and formulas.
★ Exam Points:
• Dates are right-aligned like numbers.
• Excel date serial 1 = 1 January 1900.
• Ctrl + ; enters today’s date.

q: The ____ function is used in MS-Excel 2010 for rounding a number down to the nearest multiple of significance.
exp:
=FLOOR(number, significance) rounds down; CEILING rounds up.
★ Exam Points:
• ROUNDDOWN rounds down to given digits.
• INT rounds down to the nearest integer.
• MROUND rounds to the nearest multiple.

q: In MS-Excel 2010, which shortcut key is used to bold the selected text?
exp:
Ctrl + B (or Ctrl + 2) toggles bold formatting.
★ Exam Points:
• Ctrl + 0 hides columns.
• Ctrl + I – italic; Ctrl + U – underline.
• Ctrl + 5 – strikethrough.

q: Choose the wrong option with respect to MS-Excel 2010.
o: Ctrl + N is used to open a new file.
We cannot insert a comment in a cell.
We can save the file using F12.
We can insert a table from the Insert tab.
exp:
Comments can be inserted using Review → New Comment or Shift + F2.
★ Exam Points:
• Cells with comments show a red triangle.
• Excel 365 has threaded comments and Notes.
• Ctrl + Shift + O selects cells with comments.

q: In MS-Excel 2010, the ____ operation is used to open an already existing file.
exp:
Open (Ctrl + O / Ctrl + F12) opens an existing workbook.
★ Exam Points:
• Recent workbooks appear in File → Open/Recent.
• Excel can open .csv and .txt files too.
• New creates a blank workbook.

q: In MS-Excel 2010, ____ looks up values in a reference or array and returns their relative position.
exp:
Excel describes MATCH as "looks up values in a reference or array" – it returns the position of the item.
★ Exam Points:
• VLOOKUP returns a value from a column of a table.
• INDEX returns a value at a given position.
• XLOOKUP combines both in Excel 365.

q: A formula =A3+B4 is typed in cell A5. If A5 is copied and pasted into E9, what will be the formula in E9?
exp:
Relative references shift by the same offset: from A5 to E9 is +4 columns and +4 rows, so A3 → E7 and B4 → F8.
★ Exam Points:
• Use $ to stop references from changing.
• Moving (cut-paste) a formula does not change references.
• Copying across shifts columns; copying down shifts rows.

q: The ____ tab of the MS-Excel 2010 ribbon contains the most frequently used commands such as copying, pasting, sorting, filtering and formatting.
exp:
The Home tab has Clipboard, Font, Alignment, Number, Styles, Cells and Editing groups.
★ Exam Points:
• Sort & Filter is in Home → Editing and Data tab.
• Conditional Formatting is in Home → Styles.
• Alt + H activates Home.

q: In an MS-Excel 2010 sheet, a cell with a text overflow problem can be dealt with using ____.
exp:
Wrap Text displays long text on multiple lines within the cell.
★ Exam Points:
• Wrap Text is in Home → Alignment.
• Alt + Enter inserts a manual line break.
• Shrink to Fit reduces font size instead.

q: ____ shortcut key is used in MS-Excel 2010 to select the entire worksheet.
exp:
Ctrl + A selects the current region; pressing it again selects the entire sheet.
★ Exam Points:
• Ctrl + Shift + Spacebar also selects all.
• Clicking the Select All button (top-left corner) selects the sheet.
• Ctrl + R – Fill Right.

q: Choose the wrong option with respect to MS-Excel 2010.
o: We can insert a comment to a cell.
We can save the file using F12.
To open a new blank file, Ctrl + O is used.
We can insert a table from the Insert tab.
exp:
Ctrl + O opens an existing file; a new blank file is created with Ctrl + N.
★ Exam Points:
• F12 opens Save As.
• Shift + F2 inserts a comment.
• Insert → Table (Ctrl + T).

q: In the MS-Excel 2010 ribbon, the ____ tab is used for adding different objects to a worksheet.
exp:
The Insert tab adds tables, pictures, shapes, charts, SmartArt, text boxes, headers & footers, symbols, etc.
★ Exam Points:
• Alt + N activates Insert.
• Sparklines are in the Insert tab.
• Hyperlink (Ctrl + K) is also there.

q: The ____ tab in the MS-Excel 2010 ribbon contains tools for inserting functions and controlling calculation options.
exp:
The Formulas tab contains Function Library, Defined Names, Formula Auditing and Calculation groups.
★ Exam Points:
• Alt + M activates Formulas.
• Shift + F3 – Insert Function.
• Calculation Options: Automatic or Manual.

q: Which font effect is NOT available in the MS-Excel 2010 Font dialog box?
exp:
There is no "Super Italic" style in Excel.
★ Exam Points:
• Available effects: Strikethrough, Superscript, Subscript.
• Styles: Regular, Italic, Bold, Bold Italic.
• Ctrl + 1 → Font tab.

q: In MS-Excel 2010, ____ are used to make a graphical representation of any set of data.
exp:
Charts present data graphically for easy comparison and trend analysis.
★ Exam Points:
• Chart types: Column, Bar, Line, Pie, Area, Scatter.
• F11 – chart sheet; Alt + F1 – embedded chart.
• Sparklines are mini charts in a cell.

q: ____ shortcut key is used in MS-Excel 2010 to select a column.
exp:
Ctrl + Spacebar selects the entire column of the active cell.
★ Exam Points:
• Shift + Spacebar – entire row.
• Ctrl + Shift + Spacebar – entire sheet.
• Ctrl + Shift + Arrow – extend to last filled cell.

q: In MS-Excel 2010, the ____ operation displays only the rows that meet certain conditions while other rows get hidden.
exp:
Filter (AutoFilter) shows only rows matching criteria and temporarily hides the rest.
★ Exam Points:
• Ctrl + Shift + L toggles filter.
• Advanced Filter can copy results elsewhere.
• Status bar shows "x of y records found".

q: Which of the following is NOT a function in MS-Excel 2010?
exp:
Excel has AVERAGE, not AVG; AVG() would return #NAME? error.
★ Exam Points:
• #NAME? appears for unrecognised function names.
• MAX/MIN return the largest/smallest value.
• AVERAGEA counts text as zero.

q: In MS-Excel 2010, ____ is used for finding text within the sheet.
exp:
Ctrl + F opens the Find tab of the Find and Replace dialog.
★ Exam Points:
• Shift + F5 also opens Find.
• Shift + F4 repeats the last find.
• Ctrl + H – Replace.

q: ____ shortcut key is used in MS-Excel 2010 to go to the Data tab.
exp:
Alt + A activates the Data tab.
★ Exam Points:
• Alt + N – Insert; Alt + F – File.
• Alt + M – Formulas; Alt + W – View.
• Alt + R – Review.

q: How many rows and columns are there in a worksheet of MS-Excel 2010?
exp:
From Excel 2007 onwards a sheet has 1,048,576 (2^20) rows and 16,384 (2^14) columns, last column XFD.
★ Exam Points:
• Excel 2003: 65,536 rows × 256 columns (IV).
• Total cells ≈ 17.18 billion.
• Ctrl + Down arrow jumps to the last row of data.

q: In MS-Excel 2010, rows are identified by ____.
exp:
Rows are numbered 1, 2, 3 … and columns are lettered A, B, C ….
★ Exam Points:
