• Row headers are at the left.
• Column headers are at the top.
• Cell address = column + row (e.g. C7).

q: A ____ is a tool used in MS-Excel 2010 to calculate, summarise and analyse data and see comparisons, patterns and trends.
exp:
A PivotTable summarises and analyses large data sets interactively.
★ Exam Points:
• Drag fields into Rows, Columns, Values, Filters.
• Refresh updates PivotTable after data change.
• Slicers filter PivotTables visually.

q:
What will the following function return in MS-Excel 2010?
=EXACT("Word","word")
exp:
EXACT is case-sensitive; "Word" and "word" differ in the first letter's case, so it returns FALSE.
★ Exam Points:
• ="Word"="word" returns TRUE (not case-sensitive).
• EXACT returns only TRUE/FALSE.
• FIND is case-sensitive; SEARCH is not.

q: The ____ function in MS-Excel 2010 capitalises the first letter of each word in a text value.
exp:
=PROPER("aimers qila") → SSC Restart.
★ Exam Points:
• UPPER – all caps.
• LOWER – all small.
• Word equivalent: Shift + F3 (Capitalize Each Word).

q:
Which of the following are correct ways to start Edit mode in an MS-Excel 2010 cell?
P: Double-click the cell containing the data.
Q: Click the cell and press F2.
R: Click the cell and press Shift.
S: Click the cell and press Ctrl.
exp:
Double-clicking a cell or pressing F2 enters Edit mode; Shift or Ctrl alone do not.
★ Exam Points:
• Clicking in the formula bar also allows editing.
• Status bar shows "Edit".
• Esc cancels the edit.

q: In MS-Excel 2010, the ____ operation is used to save an already saved file under a different name.
exp:
Save As (F12) saves a copy with a new name, location or file type.
★ Exam Points:
• Original file remains unchanged.
• Save As can create PDF or CSV.
• Ctrl + S just updates the same file.

q: The ____ tab in MS-Excel 2010 provides commands for switching worksheet views, freezing panes and arranging multiple windows.
exp:
The View tab has Workbook Views, Show (gridlines, headings), Zoom, Window (Freeze Panes, Split, Arrange All) and Macros.
★ Exam Points:
• Views: Normal, Page Layout, Page Break Preview.
• Freeze Top Row keeps headers visible.
• Alt + W opens View.

q: The ____ tab of MS-Excel 2010 lets you check spelling, track changes, add comments and protect worksheets and workbooks.
exp:
The Review tab includes Proofing, Comments and Changes (Protect Sheet, Protect Workbook, Track Changes).
★ Exam Points:
• F7 – Spelling in Excel.
• Shift + F2 – insert comment.
• Alt + R opens Review.

q: In MS-Excel 2010, what will be the value of the expression =656/4^2?
exp:
Exponent is calculated first: 4^2 = 16; then 656 ÷ 16 = 41.
★ Exam Points:
• ^ has higher precedence than / and *.
• Use brackets to change order.
• =(656/4)^2 = 26896.

q: In MS-Excel 2010, ____ is used to hide rows within the sheet.
exp:
Ctrl + 9 hides the selected rows; Ctrl + Shift + 9 unhides them.
★ Exam Points:
• Ctrl + 0 hides columns.
• Hidden rows show a double line between numbers.
• Format → Hide & Unhide menu also works.

q: Choose the wrong option related to a cell of MS-Excel 2010.
o: Cells can contain text, numbers and dates.
The intersection of a row and column is a cell.
Cell addresses are written like A1, A2, A3.
exp:
A cell address must include the column letter and row number (e.g., A1); a number alone is a row number.
★ Exam Points:
• Range example: A1:C5.
• Active cell has a thick border.
• Name Box shows the address.

q: Which of the following is NOT a valid MS-Excel 2010 Math function?
exp:
MOD, ODD and BASE are Math & Trig functions; OFF() does not exist.
★ Exam Points:
• MOD returns the remainder.
• ODD rounds up to the nearest odd integer.
• BASE converts a number to another base (Excel 2013+).

q: Which shortcut key adds an outline border to selected cells in MS-Excel?
exp:
Ctrl + Shift + & applies an outline border; Ctrl + Shift + _ removes borders.
★ Exam Points:
• Ctrl + 1 → Border tab for more options.
• Ctrl + Shift + ~ – General number format.
• Ctrl + Shift + ! – number format with 2 decimals.

q: To quickly zoom a workbook in MS-Excel 2010, use the minus and plus symbols in the ____.
exp:
The zoom slider with − and + buttons is on the right side of the status bar.
★ Exam Points:
• Zoom range: 10%–400%.
• View → Zoom to Selection.
• Ctrl + scroll wheel zooms.

q: Columns in MS-Excel 2010 are identified by ____.
exp:
Columns are labelled with letters A, B, C … XFD.
★ Exam Points:
• 16,384 columns in total.
• After Z: AA … AZ, BA ….
• Rows use numbers.

q: ____ is one of the most popular functions in MS-Excel and allows you to make logical comparisons between a value and what you expect.
exp:
=IF(condition, value_if_true, value_if_false) performs a logical test.
★ Exam Points:
• IFS handles multiple conditions.
• IFERROR handles errors.
• Nested IFs allowed up to 64 levels.

q: When you open a new workbook in MS-Excel 2010, which appears at the topmost position of the screen?
exp:
The title bar is at the very top and shows the workbook name, e.g., Book1 – Microsoft Excel.
★ Exam Points:
• Status bar is at the bottom.
• Scroll bars are at right and bottom.
• Ribbon is below the title bar.

q: What happens when you select a cell of an MS-Excel 2010 worksheet and press F2?
o: The cell switches to Edit mode so its content can be modified
exp:
F2 enters Edit mode with the cursor at the end of the cell content.
★ Exam Points:
• Delete key clears content.
• Esc cancels editing.
• Enter confirms.

q: The fx button in MS-Excel 2010 represents the ____ operation.
exp:
The fx button next to the formula bar opens the Insert Function dialog.
★ Exam Points:
• Shortcut: Shift + F3.
• × (cancel) and ✓ (enter) buttons are beside it.
• Function Arguments dialog guides input.

q: What is the result of the expression =8/8^2*16 in MS-Excel?
exp:
8^2 = 64 first; then 8/64 = 0.125; 0.125 × 16 = 2.
★ Exam Points:
• Precedence: ^ before * and /.
• * and / are evaluated left to right.
• Use brackets for clarity.

q: What is the default name of the first worksheet in an MS-Excel 2010 workbook?
exp:
The first worksheet is named Sheet1 (Excel 2010 workbooks had Sheet1–Sheet3 by default).
★ Exam Points:
• Excel 2013+ starts with one sheet.
• Rename by double-clicking the tab.
• Max sheet name length: 31 characters.

q: What is the main advantage of using multiple worksheets within one workbook instead of keeping each table in separate workbook files?
o: It prevents the file from being saved
It groups related data in one file
It limits the number of rows available
It stops formulas from working across tables
exp:
Utilizing multiple worksheets in a single Excel workbook allows users to organize and group related data logically within one file. This simplifies file management, streamlines navigation, and enables easy cross-sheet formula linking.
★ Exam Points:
• An Excel file is referred to as a Workbook, which contains one or more Worksheets.
• Formulas can reference other worksheets using the syntax SheetName!CellAddress (e.g., Sheet2!A1).
• Grouping tables in one file eliminates the need to manage multiple separate file paths.
• New sheets can be added quickly using the + icon next to sheet tabs or using Shift+F11.

q: Which arrangement best supports clear analysis when keeping sales data for different months in Excel?
o: All months are kept together in the same column without any separation or labels, this makes it difficult to distinguish or organize the data by month
Using one column for "Month" and other columns for quantities and values, with each row representing one record
Storing each sale randomly in any empty cell
Using a separate workbook for each individual sale
exp:
Structuring data in a flat table format—where each column represents an attribute/variable (e.g., Month, Region, Sales Amount) and each row represents an individual record— follows standard database principles. This enables efficient sorting, filtering, and PivotTable creation.
★ Exam Points:
• Standardized tabular structures with clear column headers enable features like PivotTables.
• Storing uniform data types per column maintains data integrity.
• Empty rows and columns within data sets should be avoided as they break dynamic ranges.
• Excel Tables (Ctrl + T) automatically apply structured references and easy filtering.

q: A workbook with important data is being prepared for long-term use. Which combination of practices best supports reliability and maintainability?
o: Using random sheet names, mixing data and notes in the same cells, no backups
Using clear sheet names, structured tables with headings and regular backups in more than one location
Keeping everything on one sheet with no headings and no backups
Printing only, without saving the file
exp:
Maintaining data integrity and long-term usability in Excel requires using descriptive sheet names, structured data tables with headers, and enforcing redundant backups (local and cloud). This ensures quick data auditing and protects against data corruption.
★ Exam Points:
• Meaningful worksheet names make formula references readable (e.g., =Sales2025!A1).
• Structured tables reduce formula errors and dynamically expand as data grows.
• The 3-2-1 backup strategy recommends keeping 3 copies of data on 2 different media with 1 offsite copy.
• Documentation or instruction tabs help maintain complex workbooks for multiple users.

q: Which part of the Excel window displays the address of the active cell and can be used to jump to another cell by typing its reference?
exp:
The Name Box is located to the left of the Formula Bar in Excel. It displays the cell reference of the currently selected cell (e.g., A1) and allows users to quickly navigate to any cell or named range by entering its address directly.
★ Exam Points:
• The Name Box can also be used to assign custom names to selected cells or cell ranges.
• Typing a range reference (e.g., A1:B10) into the Name Box highlights that entire block.
• The Formula Bar, located right next to the Name Box, shows cell content or underlying formulas.
• The active cell address highlighted in the Name Box updates dynamically as you move the cursor.

q: What happens when an Excel workbook is closed without saving after changes have been made and the user chooses "Don't Save"?
o: Changes are discarded, only the last saved version remains
The workbook is deleted from disk
Excel creates a backup copy automatically
exp:
Selecting "Don't Save" ignores all edits performed since the file was last opened or saved. The file on the disk reverts entirely to its previously saved state.
★ Exam Points:
• AutoRecover may retain an unsaved temporary draft if configured, but default unsaved changes are discarded.
• Clicking Save (Ctrl + S) overwrites the existing disk file with the newest changes.
• AutoSave is an automatic feature active when working on cloud-stored files (OneDrive/SharePoint).
• Pressing Esc during a save prompt cancels the closing action and keeps the document open.

q: Which basic precaution helps protect against data loss when entering large amounts of data in Excel?
o: Saving the workbook regularly under a meaningful file name
Using only one worksheet for all tasks
exp:
Regularly executing the Save command (Ctrl + S) under an identifiable file name ensures that recent modifications are continuously written to the storage drive, preventing work loss caused by unexpected system crashes or power outages.
★ Exam Points:
• Ctrl + S is the standard keyboard shortcut to quickly save a file.
• AutoRecover interval settings can be configured under Excel Options -> Save.
• Storing files with descriptive names prevents accidental overwriting of crucial work.
• Utilizing cloud storage enables real-time AutoSave functionality.

q: What is the key difference between using the Clear Contents command and using the Delete command from the right click menu on a selected cell?
o: Clear Contents removes the cell and shifts other cells, while Delete only clears the text
Clear Contents clears only the data inside the cell, while Delete removes the cell itself and may shift surrounding cells
Clear Contents removes formatting but Delete keeps formatting unchanged
There is no difference because both commands perform exactly the same operations
exp:
Clear Contents (or pressing the Delete key) removes values/data inside a cell while keeping the cell grid structure and formatting intact. Selecting Delete... removes the actual cell structure itself, shifting neighboring cells left or up.
★ Exam Points:
• Shortcut key to clear contents is the Delete key on the keyboard.
• Using Delete... prompts options to "Shift cells left", "Shift cells up", "Entire row", or "Entire column".
• Clear All (Home tab) removes cell contents, formatting, and comments simultaneously.
• Clearing contents does not alter formulas pointing to that cell address (they evaluate to zero/blank).

q: Why is it important to understand the order of operations (operator precedence) when creating complex Excel formulas?
o: Because it determines the order in which Excel performs operations and can change the final result
Because it controls how worksheets are renamed and can not change the final result
Because it changes the default font of formulas
Because it decides how many worksheets can be created
exp:
Excel evaluates mathematical operators following standard rules of algebraic precedence (BODMAS/PEMDAS). Failing to structure operations correctly—such as omitting parentheses—alters the sequence of calculation, yielding mathe-matically incorrect output.
★ Exam Points:
• Precedence order: Parentheses () → Exponents ^ → Multiplication * / Division / → Addition + / Subtraction -.
• Parentheses () override standard precedence, forcing nested operations to calculate first.
• Operators with equal precedence are evaluated from left to right.
• Formulas must always begin with an equals sign (=).

q: In a shared environment, why is it advisable to avoid storing all important Excel workbooks only on one computer without backup?
o: Because Excel cannot run on a single machine
Because if that computer fails, all those workbooks may be lost
Because Excel stops saving when backups exist
exp:
Relying on a single local device creates a single point of failure. Hardware corruption, system crashes, or malware infection can permanently destroy unbacked files, empha-sizing the need for structured data redundancy.
★ Exam Points:
• The 3-2-1 backup strategy recommends 3 copies on 2 different media with 1 offsite.
• Cloud auto-save services (e.g., SharePoint, OneDrive) protect against physical hardware failures.
• Version history features prevent permanent data corruption from manual user errors.
• Regular automated backups minimize organizational downtime and data loss.

q: In MS Excel, what does the term "cell" specifically refer to within a worksheet?
o: A full page of text and images stored in one file
The entire worksheet containing multiple rows and columns
A single rectangular box at the intersection of a row and a column
A group of workbooks stored together in a folder
exp:
A cell is the fundamental unit of data storage in Excel, formed by the intersection of a horizontal row and a vertical column. Each cell is uniquely identified by its column letter and row number (e.g., B5).
★ Exam Points:
• A selected cell currently active for editing is called the Active Cell.
• Cells can contain constants (text/numbers) or dynamic formulas.
• An individual cell in Excel can store up to 32,767 characters of text.
• The address of the active cell is displayed in the Name Box.

q: What is a potential risk of renaming an Excel file with a completely unrelated name such as "abc.xlsx" after building a detailed worksheet?
o: It becomes harder to identify the content later
exp:
Assigning non-descriptive or generic filenames (like abc.xlsx or Document1.xlsx) creates organizational confusion, making it difficult for users to search, identify, or retrieve specific data content without opening every file manually.
★ Exam Points:
• Filenames should clearly reflect document contents, dates, or project titles (e.g., Q1_Sales_Report_2026.xlsx).
• Non-descriptive names complicate file management in shared team directories.
• File naming conventions improve productivity and file searchability.
• Changing the file name does not corrupt the internal data structure or formulas.

q: A user wants to insert a new column between existing columns B and C in an Excel worksheet. Which of the following sequences of actions will correctly perform this task?
o: and choose Insert; the new column appears to the right of column B B Right click column
and choose Insert; the new column appears to the left of column C C Select column A and press Delete; then type the new column heading
Double click between columns B and C; the new column appears automatically
exp:
blank column to the left of the currently selected column header. Therefore, to insert a column between B and C, right-clicking Column C and choosing Insert correctly places it between them.
★ Exam Points:
• Excel inserts new columns to the left of the selected column.
• Excel inserts new rows above the selected row.
• Keyboard shortcut to insert a new column/row after selecting it is Ctrl + Shift + "+".
• Keyboard shortcut to delete a selected column/row is Ctrl + "-".

q: When entering data into Excel, why is it better to keep one logical item in each cell rather than mixing multiple items in a single cell?
o: It reduces the number of rows available
It makes sorting, filtering and analysis easier
It prevents the workbook from opening
It stops printing of the sheet
exp:
Storing discrete atomic data points per cell adheres to standard database structure practices. It enables Excel’s computational engine to perform precise sorting, filtering, PivotTable aggregation, and formula calculations seamlessly.
★ Exam Points:
• Combined text in single cells complicates querying via functions like VLOOKUP or XLOOKUP.
• The Text to Columns tool helps break down combined data into distinct cells.
• Atomic data design is essential for building accurate dynamic dashboards.
• Prevents data contamination and invalid results during custom formula execution.

q: A table in Excel tracks items and quantities. Why is it more reliable to use separate columns "Item" and "Quantity" instead of writing both in a single text cell such as "5 pens"?
o: Because Excel cannot store text and numbers in separate cells
Because separate columns allow numeric operations
Because "5 pens" is the only valid format
Because charts cannot be created from separate columns
exp:
Excel treats text strings like "5 pens" as text entries, which prevents mathematical functions (SUM, AVERAGE) from performing arithmetic. Placing "5" in a dedicated numeric column enables numeric operations and computational aggregation.
★ Exam Points:
• Mathematical functions ignore cells formatted as text or containing non-numeric characters.
• Custom Cell Formatting can display units (e.g., 0 "pens") while preserving raw numbers.
• Separating fields prevents #VALUE! errors in downstream formulas.
• Facilitates automated mathematical calculations and accurate charting.

q: Which action will select an entire column so that formatting or editing applies to all its cells at once?
o: Double-clicking any cell in the column
Clicking the column letter at the top of the worksheet
Clicking the row number on the left edge
exp:
Left-clicking a column header letter (e.g., Column A, B) selects every cell from row 1 down to row 1,048,576 instantly. This allows universal formatting, style modifications, or deletion across the entire column.
★ Exam Points:
• Keyboard shortcut to select an entire current column is Ctrl + Spacebar.
• Keyboard shortcut to select an entire current row is Shift + Spacebar.
• Excel worksheets contain 1,048,576 rows and 16,384 columns (A to XFD).
• Clicking the top-left gray corner box selects the entire worksheet.

q: In the Excel function =SUM(A1:A5), how is the notation A1:A5 described or classified?
exp:
Inputs supplied inside the opening and closing parentheses of an Excel function are called arguments. In =SUM(A1:A5), the range A1:A5 serves as the range argument that specifies which values the function must process.
★ Exam Points:
• Multiple arguments in Excel functions are separated by commas (,).
• Arguments can consist of cell ranges, numbers, text, or nested functions.
• The colon operator (:) defines a continuous cell range.
• Functions without required input parameters still retain empty parentheses (e.g., =TODAY()).

q: When you use the Wrap Text option for a selected cell what change occurs to the way the cell contents are displayed?
o: The text is converted into uppercase letters only
The text automatically moves to the next cell on the right when it reaches the cell border
The text is displayed on multiple lines within the same cell
The text is hidden completely and only the cell border remains
exp:
Enabling Wrap Text forces long text strings that exceed the current column width to expand vertically across multiple lines within the same cell, adjusting row height automatically to keep content fully visible without widening the column.
★ Exam Points:
• Located under Home tab > Alignment group > Wrap Text.
• Prevents text truncation or spilling over into neighboring empty cells.
• Manual line breaks inside a wrapped cell can be inserted using Alt + Enter.
• Automatically increases row height to fit wrapped multi-line text.

q: Why is it useful to separate input cells, calculation cells and output cells clearly when designing a worksheet of formulas and functions?
o: It makes the sheet harder to read but faster to calculate
It helps users know where to enter data, formulas live, final results appear
It disables the use of functions in calculation cells
exp:
Logically segmenting raw input data, intermediate formula calculations, and final summary outputs creates a structured model. It guides end users where data entry is required, protects core formulas from being overwritten, and simplifies spreadsheet auditing.
★ Exam Points:
• Supports spreadsheet protection models where calculation cells are locked.
• Reduces accidental formula destruction during manual data entry operations.
• Improves auditability and makes complex Financial models easier to debug.
• Cell Styles (e.g., Input, Calculation, Output presets) help visually differentiate segments.

q: In Excel, which basic action is used to copy the content of one cell to another location using the mouse and the Ctrl key?
o: Dragging the cell border without keys
Dragging the fill handle while holding Ctrl
exp:
Dragging the fill handle (the small solid square at the bottom-right corner of an active cell) while holding down the Ctrl key duplicates exact cell contents or fills a calculated series into adjacent destination cells.
★ Exam Points:
• The fill handle is located at the bottom-right corner of the active cell border.
• Dragging without Ctrl triggers AutoFill (e.g., extending days, months, or standard linear series).
• Double-clicking the fill handle automatically fills data down to match the adjacent column length.
• Holding Ctrl prevents incremental series expansion when copying plain numbers.

q: Why is it beneficial to understand that Excel recalculates values automatically when underlying numbers change?
o: It requires that all formulas be typed again each time they are needed, this increases work and the chance of errors in the document
It allows building worksheets where changing input cells instantly updates results, supporting "what-if" analysis
It disables data entry in other cells
exp:
Excel’s dynamic recalculation engine updates dependent outputs instantly when input variables change. This under-pins "what-if" analysis, enabling decision-makers to simu-late scenarios and see instant updates across complex calculations.
★ Exam Points:
• Features built-in analysis tools like Goal Seek, Scenario Manager, and Data Tables.
• Eliminates manual recalculation work across interconnected financial models.
• Recalculation can be set to Manual for extremely large workbooks to increase performance.
• Pressing F9 forces a complete recalculation of all open workbooks manually.

q: Which visual feature on the worksheet helps the eye recognise boundaries of cells while viewing or editing data on screen?
exp:
Gridlines are faint light-gray intersecting lines displayed across an Excel worksheet that visually delimit individual rows and columns, making data structure scannable without adding explicit cell borders.
★ Exam Points:
• Gridline visibility can be toggled via View tab > Show group > Gridlines.
• By default, gridlines are visible on screen but do not print unless configured in Page Setup.
• Explicit Cell Borders applied by users are separate and override default gridlines.
• Gridline color can be customized inside Excel Advanced Options.

q: A user has entered the same wrong spelling of a product name in many cells across a worksheet. Which Excel command is most appropriate to quickly correct this spelling in all those cells at once?
exp:
The Find and Replace feature enables automated text sub-stitution across an entire worksheet or workbook. Clicking "Replace All" replaces every instance of the targeted mis-spelling simultaneously.
★ Exam Points:
• Keyboard shortcut to open Find and Replace is Ctrl + H (or Ctrl + F for Find only).
• Supports wildcard characters: question mark (?) for single char, asterisk (*) for string.
• Option allows restricting replace operations to Match case or Entire cell contents.
• Can search across the current active worksheet or the entire workbook.

q: In Excel formulas, what is the primary reason or purpose for using parentheses around parts of an expression?
o: They are required in every formula but have no effect
They group parts of an expression and can change the order of evaluation
They are used only in text entries
They are only allowed inside functions, never in simple formulas
exp:
Parentheses () override standard mathematical operator precedence (BODMAS/PEMDAS). Expressions enclosed inside parentheses are evaluated first, altering the calculation order in complex expressions.
★ Exam Points:
• Standard operator precedence without parentheses: Exponentiation, Multiplication/Division, Addition/Subtraction.
• Nested parentheses compute from the innermost set out to the outermost set.
• Mismatched or unclosed parentheses trigger an automatic formula correction prompt.
• Used in functions to enclose arguments and range specifi-cations (e.g., =SUM(A1:A10)).

q: In an examination report you have marks for three tests in cells B2, C2 and D2. You want to assign a result "Pass" only if the average of the three marks is at least 40 and none of the individual marks is below 35. Which of the following Excel formulas most accurately implements this logic in a single cell?
exp:
The AND() function evaluates multiple logical conditions and returns TRUE only if all conditions are met. Wrapping AND() inside IF() ensures that "Pass" is returned strictly when AVERAGE(B2:D2)>=40 AND all three test scores are individually >=35.
★ Exam Points:
• AND returns TRUE if all arguments evaluate to TRUE.
• OR returns TRUE if at least one argument evaluates to TRUE.
• Syntax structure: =IF(logical_test, value_if_true, value_if_false).
• Nesting logical functions allows complex multi-conditional business rules to be executed.

q: In MS Excel, what types of information or indicators are normally shown in the Status Bar located at the bottom of the window?
o: Information such as average of selected cells, view, zoom details
The list of all installed applications
Only the current date and time
exp:
The Status Bar at the bottom of the MS Excel window provides real-time information regarding the current selection, such as Average, Count, and Sum. It also houses view shortcuts (Normal, Page Layout, Page Break Preview) and the Zoom control slider.
★ Exam Points:
• Right-clicking the Status Bar allows users to customize displayed metrics like Minimum, Maximum, and Numerical Count.
• Key mode indicators like Ready, Edit, and Enter appear on the far-left side of the Status Bar.
• Caps Lock and Num Lock status indicators can also be enabled on the bar.
• Quick calculations on the Status Bar do not alter cell contents or insert formulas.

q: When designing a worksheet that others will read, why is consistent use of text alignment, fonts and number formats important?
o: It improves readability, gives a professional appearance
exp:
Maintaining consistent formatting across a worksheet enhances visual hierarchy and readability, making complex data easy to interpret. Uniform alignment, clear fonts, and standardized number formats present data professionally and reduce reader cognitive strain.
★ Exam Points:
• Text is usually left-aligned by default, while numbers are right-aligned in MS Excel.
• Using cell styles and themes helps maintain design con-sistency across multiple sheets.
• Over-formatting with too many colors or mismatched fonts creates clutter and reduces legibility.
• Proper number formatting (e.g., Currency, Percentage) clarifies data context without changing cell values.

q: In an Excel worksheet you want to enter the same heading text into several non adjacent cells at once without typing it repeatedly. Which method can be used to achieve this?
o: Select all the required cells, type the heading and then press Ctrl + Enter
Type the heading in one cell and press Shift + Delete
Type the heading in one cell and drag its fill handle without selecting any other cells
Type the heading in each cell separately one by one
exp:
Pressing Ctrl + Enter populates all currently selected cells— whether contiguous or non-adjacent—with the entry made in the active cell. Holding Ctrl while clicking cells enables the selection of non-adjacent ranges prior to entry.
★ Exam Points:
• Selecting multiple non-adjacent cells is performed by holding down the Ctrl key while clicking each target cell.
• The Ctrl + Enter shortcut works for text, numbers, and formulas across selected ranges.
• Using Ctrl + Enter prevents the active cell focus from shifting to the next row below.
• Fill Handle dragging is generally suitable for contiguous ranges, whereas Ctrl + Enter works seamlessly on non-adjacent selections.

q: While building a financial model, someone copies a sheet and experiments with new assumptions on the copy while preserving the original sheet. Which principle of using Excel does this illustrate?
o: The document is created without following any particular structure or organization, this can make it harder to read, understand and navigate
Separation of experimental changes from the trusted base version to reduce risk
exp:
Duplicating a worksheet before applying speculative changes demonstrates version isolation and risk management. Keeping the base model untouched ensures that trusted calculations remain safe while scenario testing or formula modifications occur on the copy.
★ Exam Points:
• Excel's Scenario Manager (Data tab) allows saving and switching between different input variable sets on a single sheet.
• Right-clicking a sheet tab provides the Move or Copy option with a "Create a copy" checkbox.
• What-If Analysis tools like Goal Seek and Data Tables aid scenario modeling without destroying original inputs.
• Creating backups or working on copies prevents accidental overwriting of baseline financial data.

q: In a large Excel worksheet you need to quickly move the active cell to cell Z500 without scrolling manually. Which method is most efficient to reach this specific cell?
o: Type Z500 in the Name Box and press Enter
Double click the top left corner of the worksheet
exp:
Typing a target cell coordinate (such as Z500) into the Name Box (located to the left of the Formula Bar) and pressing Enter immediately jumps the selection focus directly to that cell, bypassing manual scrolling.
★ Exam Points:
• Pressing F5 or Ctrl + G opens the Go To dialog box, where entering a cell address jumps to it.
• Ctrl + Home moves active selection directly to cell A1.
• Ctrl + End moves active selection to the bottom-right used cell in the worksheet.
• The Name Box also displays defined range names and allows quick range creation.

q: Why is it useful to use clear column headings (such as "Name", "Quantity", "Price") at the top of each column in a worksheet?
o: Headings describe the data in each column
exp:
Column headings clearly define the data type and purpose of the values stored in the rows beneath them. They provide crucial context for human readers and are utilized by Excel functions like sorting, filtering, and PivotTables to identify data attributes.
★ Exam Points:
• Freeze Panes locks top row headings on screen so they remain visible while scrolling down large datasets.
• Excel Tables (Ctrl + T) convert top entries automatically into functional table headers with built-in filter drop-downs.
• Column headings ensure correct data mapping when exporting data to databases or performing mail merges.
• Using descriptive headers prevents data entry errors and misinterpretation of raw numbers.

q: Why is it important to understand the difference between saving a workbook with a new name and simply overwriting an existing file?
o: Both actions always delete the data
Saving with a new name stops formulas working
exp:
Using Save overwrites and replaces the existing file on disk with current updates, permanently erasing the prior version's state. Using Save As creates a brand-new separate file under a different name or path, preserving the original file intact.
★ Exam Points:
• Save As (F12 shortcut) is essential when creating template variations or preserving baseline audit copies.
• Overwriting a file without a backup makes recovering accidentally deleted data or broken formulas difficult.
• Cloud services like OneDrive offer Version History to restore previous overwritten file instances if needed.
• AutoSave continuously overwrites cloud-stored files as changes occur in real time.

q: Which operation is performed when you select an entire row and then choose Insert from the right click context menu?
o: The selected row is deleted and all data below it moves up
A new blank row is inserted above the selected row and existing rows shift down
A new blank row is inserted below the selected row but no data shifts
All cells in the row are cleared but the row structure remains unchanged
exp:
Inserting a row via the context menu when an entire row is selected shifts the selected row and all lower rows downward by one position, creating a new empty row immediately above the original selection.
★ Exam Points:
• The keyboard shortcut to insert a new row after selecting an entire row is Ctrl + Plus sign (+).
• Inserting rows automatically adjusts formula cell references across the worksheet to maintain calculation integrity.
• Selecting multiple rows before clicking Insert adds an equivalent number of new blank rows at once.
• To insert a new column, the process inserts the blank column to the left of the selected column.

q: Which of these actions is the safest method to close only the current workbook while keeping Excel itself open?
o: Remove the workbook file from the disk
exp:
Selecting File > Close (or pressing Ctrl + W) closes the active workbook tab or window safely while leaving the main Microsoft Excel application interface open to create or edit other workbooks.
★ Exam Points:
• The keyboard shortcut Ctrl + W or Ctrl + F4 closes the active workbook.
• File > Exit or Alt + F4 completely closes the entire Excel application along with all open workbooks.
• If unsaved changes exist, Excel prompts the user to save before completing the close command.
• Closing individual workbooks frees system RAM without needing to restart the application.

q: A workbook contains multiple sheets named "Data", "Summary" and "Charts". What does this naming practice show about worksheet organisation?
o: It is mandatory for Excel to operate
exp:
Replacing default sheet labels (Sheet1, Sheet2) with descriptive names like "Data", "Summary", and "Charts" reflects a deliberate structural design. Separating raw data inputs, summary calculations, and visual charts improves navigation and auditability.
★ Exam Points:
• Double-clicking a sheet tab allows users to rename it quickly.
• Descriptive sheet names make 3D formulas and cross-sheet references (e.g., =Summary!A1) easier to read.
• Tab colors can also be assigned to sheet tabs for visual categorization.
• Sheet names cannot exceed 31 characters and cannot contain certain characters like : \ / ? * [ ].

q: Which option under Paste Special is most appropriate if you want to copy the calculated results from one range to another but do not want to copy the original formulas themselves?
exp:
The Paste Values option converts dynamic formula outputs into static, constant numbers or text strings. This isolates calculation outputs from underlying dependencies, allowing users to copy results without carrying over dynamic formulas.
★ Exam Points:
• The keyboard shortcut for Paste Values in Excel is Alt + E + S + V + Enter or Ctrl + Alt + V then selecting Values.
• Paste Formulas copies underlying formula statements while adjusting relative references.
• Paste Formats transfers only visual styling, font colors, and number formats without cell contents.
• Converting formulas to static values prevents reference errors like #REF! when source sheets are removed.

q: A user is working with a large financial model and wants to protect the structure of the workbook so that no one can accidentally add delete or move worksheets, but still allow data editing inside existing cells. Which command should the user apply after setting a password if needed?
exp:
The Protect Workbook Structure command (found on the Review tab) locks the organization of the workbook. It pre-vents users from inserting, deleting, renaming, hiding, un-hiding, or moving worksheet tabs while keeping cell contents editable.
★ Exam Points:
• Protect Sheet locks individual cell ranges and prevents editing cell values or formatting.
• Protecting workbook structure requires setting an optional password to prevent unauthorized structural edits.
• When workbook structure is protected, tab right-click options (Insert, Delete, Rename) are grayed out.
• It is located in the Protect group on the Review tab in Excel.

q: Which bar is designed specifically to display and edit the formula or full contents of the active cell, even when the cell appears narrow on the grid?
exp:
The Formula Bar is positioned directly above the worksheet grid. It displays the underlying formula, text, or constant value of the active cell, allowing users to view and edit lengthy cell contents easily even if the cell width is restricted.
★ Exam Points:
• The fx button adjacent to the Formula Bar launches the Insert Function wizard.
• Pressing Ctrl + Shift + U expands or collapses the Formula Bar height to view multi-line formulas.
• While a cell displays the calculated output on the grid, the Formula Bar shows the raw formula logic.
• The Name Box is located to the immediate left of the Formula Bar.

q: When an Excel formula displays the error value #DIV/0! what does this generally indicate about the calculation?
o: A text string is too long for the cell
The formula is trying to divide a number by zero or by an empty cell
The function name has been typed incorrectly
The cell formatting is set to percentage
exp:
The #DIV/0! error occurs when a formula attempts to divide a number by zero (0) or by an empty cell evaluated as zero. Mathematical division by zero is undefined, triggering this standard error flag in Excel.
★ Exam Points:
• Wrapping formulas with IFERROR (e.g., =IFERROR(A1/B1, 0)) suppresses #DIV/0! displays smoothly.
• #VALUE! error occurs when a formula encounters wrong data types (e.g., text in math operations).
• #NAME? error indicates an unrecognized or misspelled function name.
• Error | Meaning / Cause
• #DIV/0! | Division by zero or empty cell
• #VALUE! | Wrong data type in formula (e.g., text + number)
• #NAME? | Misspelled function or unrecognized range name
• #REF! | Deleted or invalid cell reference
• #N/A | Lookup value not found (VLOOKUP/MATCH)
• ##### | Column too narrow or negative date/time

q: The keyboard shortcut to open the Format Cells dialog box in MS-Excel 2010 is ____.
exp:
Ctrl + 1 opens Format Cells with tabs Number, Alignment, Font, Border, Fill and Protection.
★ Exam Points:
• Ctrl + Shift + F opens Format Cells on the Font tab.
• Ctrl + Shift + $ – currency format.
• Ctrl + Shift + % – percentage format.

q: Which is the correct way to refer to the range of cells in columns A through E and rows 10 through 20 in an MS-Excel 2010 formula?
exp:
A rectangular range is written as top-left cell : bottom-right cell, i.e. A10:E20.
★ Exam Points:
• Range A10:E20 has 5 × 11 = 55 cells.
• Colon (:) is the range operator.
• Comma joins separate ranges.

q: In MS-Excel 2010, which function converts text to Title (Proper) case?
exp:
=PROPER(text) capitalises the first letter of each word and makes other letters lowercase.
★ Exam Points:
• UPPER converts to all capitals; LOWER to small letters.
• There is no TITLE function in Excel.
• In Word, Shift + F3 changes case.

q: The keyboard shortcut to open a new workbook in MS-Excel 2010 is ____.
exp:
Ctrl + N creates a new blank workbook.
★ Exam Points:
• Ctrl + S saves; Ctrl + O opens; Ctrl + W closes.
• Shift + F11 adds a new worksheet.
• F12 – Save As.

q: In MS-Excel 2010, the Remove Duplicates function is found in the ribbon under the ____ tab.
exp:
Remove Duplicates is in Data → Data Tools group.
★ Exam Points:
• Highlight duplicates via Conditional Formatting.
• UNIQUE function (Excel 365) lists distinct values.
• Data Validation is also in Data Tools.

q: A ____ consists of a matrix of rectangular cells grouped in rows and columns.
exp:
A spreadsheet arranges data in a grid of cells formed by rows and columns.
★ Exam Points:
• First spreadsheet program: VisiCalc (1979).
• Lotus 1-2-3 was popular in the 1980s.
• Excel, Google Sheets, LibreOffice Calc are spreadsheets.

q: In MS-Excel 2010, the ____ displays the name of the spreadsheet (workbook).
exp:
The title bar at the top shows the workbook name and program name (e.g., Book1 – Excel).
★ Exam Points:
• Default new workbook name: Book1.
• Status bar shows mode (Ready, Edit, Enter) and quick totals.
• Taskbar belongs to Windows, not Excel.

q: The ____ command in MS-Excel 2010 saves the changes made in the primary file into a new file.
exp:
Save As (F12) saves the workbook with a new name, location or format, leaving the original unchanged.
★ Exam Points:
• Save (Ctrl + S) overwrites the same file.
• Save As can save as PDF, CSV, XLS.
• First Save of a new file opens Save As.

q: Which option gives more control over how content is displayed or functions when pasted?
exp:
Paste Special lets you paste only values, formats, formulas, comments, or transpose data.
★ Exam Points:
• Shortcut: Ctrl + Alt + V.
• Paste Special can also perform operations (add, multiply).
• Paste Link creates a link to the source.

q: In MS-Excel 2010, click the cell containing data you want to edit and press the ____ key to enter Edit mode with the cursor at the end of the cell content.
exp:
F2 puts the active cell into Edit mode.
★ Exam Points:
• F4 repeats last action / toggles references.
• F7 – Spelling.
• F3 – Paste Name.

q: Which function in MS-Excel 2010 converts a text string to all lowercase letters?
exp:
=LOWER(text) converts all letters to lowercase.
★ Exam Points:
• UPPER – all capitals.
• PROPER – first letter of each word capital.
• TEXT formats a number as text.

q: In MS-Excel 2010, which function returns the serial number of the current date and time?
exp:
=NOW() returns the current date and time; it updates whenever the sheet recalculates.
★ Exam Points:
• TODAY() returns only the current date.
• Ctrl + ; inserts static date; Ctrl + Shift + ; static time.
• Excel stores dates as serial numbers from 1 Jan 1900.

q: Which shortcut key is used to bold text in MS-Excel 2010?
exp:
Ctrl + B (or Ctrl + 2) applies or removes bold formatting.
★ Exam Points:
• Ctrl + I / Ctrl + 3 – italic.
• Ctrl + U / Ctrl + 4 – underline.
• Ctrl + 5 – strikethrough in Excel.

q: In MS-Excel 2010, the ____ is at the bottom, where information about the current mode or special keys engaged can be seen.
exp:
The status bar shows the mode (Ready, Enter, Edit), Caps Lock status, and quick calculations like Sum and Average.
★ Exam Points:
• Zoom slider and view buttons are on the status bar.
• Right-click the status bar to customise it.
• Title bar is at the top.

q: Which shortcut key is used to select the entire row in MS-Excel 2010?
exp:
Shift + Spacebar selects the whole row of the active cell.
★ Exam Points:
• Ctrl + Spacebar – entire column.
• Ctrl + Shift + Spacebar – whole sheet.
• Alt + Spacebar – window control menu.

q: In MS-Excel 2010, if A3 = 300, B3 = 225, C3 = 180, D3 = 350 and E3 = 400, then =AVERAGE(A3,B3,C3,D3,E3) in F3 gives ____.
exp:
Sum = 300 + 225 + 180 + 350 + 400 = 1455; 1455 ÷ 5 = 291.
★ Exam Points:
• AVERAGE ignores empty cells and text.
• =AVERAGE(A3:E3) gives the same result.
• MEDIAN of these values = 300.

q: In MS-Excel 2010, which shortcut opens the Delete dialog box to delete selected cells?
exp:
Ctrl + minus (-) opens the Delete dialog to shift cells left/up or delete entire rows/columns.
★ Exam Points:
• Ctrl + Shift + + (plus) inserts cells.
• F4 repeats the last action.
• Delete key clears contents only.

q: The ____ function in MS-Excel 2010 is used to find the average (mean) of numbers.
exp:
=AVERAGE(range) returns the arithmetic mean of the numbers.
★ Exam Points:
• AVERAGEIF/AVERAGEIFS – conditional average.
• MEDIAN – middle value; MODE – most frequent value.
• AVERAGEA also counts text as 0.

q: The dollar sign ($) is used to make ____ references in MS-Excel 2010.
exp:
A $ before the column and row (e.g. $A$1) makes the reference absolute so it does not change when copied.
★ Exam Points:
• F4 cycles through absolute/mixed/relative references.
• $A1 – column fixed; A$1 – row fixed.
• Relative reference (A1) changes when copied.

q: The keyboard shortcut to paste special values in a worksheet in MS-Excel 2010 is ____.
o: Ctrl + Alt + V, then press V
Ctrl + Shift + V, then press V
exp:
Ctrl + Alt + V opens the Paste Special dialog; pressing V selects Values.
★ Exam Points:
• Paste Special can paste values, formats, formulas, transpose.
• Ctrl + Shift + V pastes as plain text in Excel 365.
• Transpose switches rows and columns.

q: A ____ is a visual representation of data in a worksheet of MS-Excel 2010.
exp:
Charts/graphs present worksheet data visually, e.g. column, line, pie charts.
★ Exam Points:
• F11 creates a chart on a new chart sheet.
• Alt + F1 creates an embedded chart.
• Pie chart shows parts of a whole.

q: In MS-Excel 2010, the ____ keyboard shortcut is used to undo changes.
exp:
Ctrl + Z undoes the last action.
★ Exam Points:
• Ctrl + Y redoes; Ctrl + U underlines.
• Excel keeps up to 100 undo levels.
• Undo is on the Quick Access Toolbar.

q: Which reference is used to refer to all cells in columns H through J in an MS-Excel 2010 formula?
exp:
A full-column range is written with a colon between column letters, e.g. H:J.
★ Exam Points:
• Full rows: 5:10.
• =SUM(H:J) adds everything in columns H to J.
• Union of ranges uses a comma; intersection uses a space.

q: Which of the following is available under the Data tab of MS-Excel 2010?
exp:
The Data tab contains Sort & Filter, Data Tools (Text to Columns, Remove Duplicates, Data Validation), Outline, etc.
★ Exam Points:
• Filter shortcut: Ctrl + Shift + L.
• Paste is in Home tab; Table is in Insert tab.
• What-If Analysis is also in Data tab.

q: Which MS-Excel function is used to sort the contents of a range or an array?
exp:
The SORT dynamic-array function returns a sorted copy of a range or array (Excel 365/2021).
★ Exam Points:
• SORTBY sorts by another range.
• FILTER returns rows meeting a condition.
• UNIQUE returns distinct values.

q: The ____ function in MS-Excel 2010 is used to join several text items into one text item.
exp:
CONCATENATE (or the & operator, CONCAT and TEXTJOIN in newer versions) joins text strings.
★ Exam Points:
• =A1&" "&B1 also joins text.
• TEXTJOIN can add a delimiter and ignore blanks.
• CONCAT replaced CONCATENATE in Excel 2016+.

q: Which small customisable toolbar at the top-left corner of the window contains a set of frequently used commands in MS-Excel 2010?
exp:
The Quick Access Toolbar holds frequently used commands like Save, Undo and Redo and can be customised.
★ Exam Points:
• Status bar is at the bottom.
• Ribbon contains tabs and groups.
• QAT can be moved below the Ribbon.

q: The keyboard shortcut in MS-Excel 2010 to preview the worksheet before printing is ____.
exp:
Ctrl + F2 opens Print Preview (Backstage Print view).
★ Exam Points:
• Ctrl + P also shows the print preview.
• Shift + F3 opens Insert Function.
• Alt + F2 – Save As in Excel.

q: In MS-Excel 2010, which shortcut is used to display the Create Table dialog box?
exp:
Ctrl + T (or Ctrl + L) opens the Create Table dialog box.
★ Exam Points:
• Table adds header filters and banded rows.
• Table Tools → Design tab appears for tables.
• Structured references use table/column names.

q: In MS-Excel 2010, which option in the File tab is used to create a new workbook?
exp:
File → New creates a blank workbook or one from a template.
★ Exam Points:
• Shortcut: Ctrl + N.
• Open – Ctrl + O.
• Templates include budgets, calendars, invoices.

q: Which of the following shows the address of the current selection or active cell in MS-Excel 2010?
exp:
The Name Box, left of the formula bar, displays the active cell address or the name of a selected range.
★ Exam Points:
• Formula bar shows the content/formula of the active cell.
• You can type a cell address in the Name Box to jump to it.
• Named ranges are also managed by Name Manager (Ctrl + F3).

q: In MS-Excel 2010, ____ is a tool that applies formatting to data depending on conditions you specify.
exp:
Conditional Formatting (Home tab) changes cell appearance – colours, data bars, icon sets – based on rules.
★ Exam Points:
• Examples: highlight duplicates, top 10 values.
• Data bars, colour scales and icon sets are visual rules.
• Rules managed via Manage Rules.

q: Which part of the Excel window displays sheet tabs such as Sheet1, Sheet2 and allows switching between them?
exp:
The sheet tab bar at the bottom-left lists worksheet tabs.
★ Exam Points:
• Right-click tabs for options.
• New sheet (+) button is next to tabs.
• Ctrl + Page Up/Down switches sheets.

q: A user wants to share structured Excel data with another application that expects a plain-text table. Which save approach is suitable?
exp:
CSV stores rows as plain text with commas separating columns, readable by most programs.
★ Exam Points:
• Only the active sheet is saved.
• Formatting and formulas are lost.
• Text (Tab delimited) .txt also works.

q: When editing inside a cell, which key removes characters one by one to the left of the insertion point?
exp:
Backspace deletes characters to the left; Delete removes characters to the right.
★ Exam Points:
• F2 enters edit mode.
• Esc cancels editing.
• Ctrl + Backspace scrolls to active cell.

q: In an Excel formula, what is the function of the dollar signs in $A$1?
o: It converts the cell into text
It locks both the column and row so the reference does not change when copied
exp:
$A$1 is an absolute reference fixed in both column and row.
★ Exam Points:
• $A1 – column fixed.
• A$1 – row fixed.
• F4 toggles types.

q: Which formula correctly nests functions to find the square root of the largest value in A1:A5?
exp:
MAX finds the largest value first, then SQRT takes its square root.
★ Exam Points:
• Inner function is evaluated first.
• Up to 64 levels of nesting.
• =POWER(MAX(A1:A5),0.5) is equivalent.

q: In a large worksheet you want to see how the data will be divided into printed pages, including margins. Which view should you select?
exp:
Page Layout view shows pages with margins, headers and footers as they will print.
★ Exam Points:
• Page Break Preview shows page divisions with blue lines.
• Normal is default view.
• Views are in the View tab and status bar.

q: A1:A10 contains numbers and B1:B10 contains status text. Which function adds values from A1:A10 only where B1:B10 equals "YES"?
exp:
SUMIF(range, criteria, sum_range) checks B1:B10 for "YES" and adds corresponding values in A1:A10.
★ Exam Points:
• SUMIFS allows multiple criteria (sum_range first).
• COUNTIF counts, not sums.
• Criteria are not case-sensitive.

q: What best practice helps clarity when naming Excel workbooks meant for long-term use?
o: Names that briefly describe the content
exp:
Descriptive names (e.g., Sales_Report_FY2025-26.xlsx) make files easy to find later.
★ Exam Points:
• Add dates/versions in names.
• Avoid special characters like / \ : * ?.
• Keep a consistent naming convention.

q: Data copied from external sources sometimes gets interpreted as text instead of numbers, causing formulas to fail. Which concept needs attention?
exp:
Numbers stored as text cannot be calculated; correct data types are essential.
★ Exam Points:
• Convert using Text to Columns or VALUE().
• Green triangle indicates number stored as text.
• Paste Special → Multiply by 1 converts.

q: When a cell or range is selected (not in edit mode), what does pressing Delete do?
o: Clears the contents of the selected cells but leaves the cells and formatting in place
Removes the cells and shifts others
exp:
Delete key clears contents only; formatting and comments remain.
★ Exam Points:
• Clear All removes everything.
• Ctrl + - removes cells.
• Backspace clears and enters edit mode.

q: What does the formula =SUM(B1:B5)-SUM(C1:C5) do?
o: Subtracts the sum of C1:C5 from the sum of B1:B5
exp:
It calculates two totals and finds their difference.
★ Exam Points:
• Useful for income − expense.
• Order matters in subtraction.
• Could also be =SUM(B1:B5,-C1:C5) as array.

q: Which Excel function returns the absolute value of a number (removes any negative sign)?
exp:
ABS returns the non-negative value, e.g., =ABS(-25) → 25.
★ Exam Points:
• SIGN returns 1, 0 or -1.
• ABS is a Math & Trig function.
• NEG and POS don't exist.

q: Which control on the status bar can be dragged to zoom in or out of the worksheet without opening any dialog?
exp:
The zoom slider at the bottom-right changes magnification instantly.
★ Exam Points:
• Range 10%–400%.
• Clicking % opens Zoom dialog.
• Ctrl + mouse wheel also zooms.

q: How can you compute the average of A1:A10 using SUM and COUNT instead of AVERAGE?
exp:
Average = total ÷ number of values.
★ Exam Points:
• COUNT counts numeric cells only.
• Same result as AVERAGE.
• Empty cells are ignored by both.

q: A workbook with many sheets is becoming confusing. Which approach best improves navigation without changing the data?
exp:
Descriptive sheet names (and tab colours) make it easy to find information.
★ Exam Points:
• Add a contents/index sheet with hyperlinks.
• Group related sheets together.
• Right-click arrows list all sheets.

q: Which best describes the main purpose of Microsoft Excel?
o: A word processor for long documents
A spreadsheet program used to organise and calculate data in rows and columns
exp:
Excel is a spreadsheet application for data entry, calculation, analysis and charts.
★ Exam Points:
• Part of Microsoft Office (1985 for Mac).
• File extension: .xlsx.
• Rival: Google Sheets, LibreOffice Calc.

q: Which function counts how many cells in A1:A50 contain the word "YES" exactly?
exp:
COUNTIF counts cells matching the criterion "YES".
★ Exam Points:
• COUNT counts numbers only.
• COUNTA counts all non-empty cells.
• Not case-sensitive.

q: If A1 = 10 and B1 = 4, what is the output of =MOD(A1,B1)?
exp:
MOD returns the remainder: 10 ÷ 4 = 2 remainder 2.
★ Exam Points:
• =QUOTIENT(10,4) → 2.
• MOD sign follows divisor.
• Useful for odd/even checks (MOD(n,2)).

q: Which File-tab option creates a new workbook based on a ready-made design such as an expense report or calendar?
exp:
File → New shows templates (budgets, calendars, invoices) to start with a pre-designed workbook.
★ Exam Points:
• Templates have extension .xltx.
• Custom templates can be saved.
• Online templates need Internet.

q: Which function finds the largest value in A1:A10 that is less than 500, assuming a conditional maximum function is available?
exp:
A conditional maximum function (MAXIFS in Excel 2019+) returns the largest value meeting the criterion.
★ Exam Points:
• Actual syntax: =MAXIFS(A1:A10,A1:A10,"<500").
• MINIFS is the minimum version.
• MAX ignores criteria text.

q: A user wants to share structured data from Excel with another application that expects a plain text table. Which simple export or save approach is more suitable?
o: Save as a macro-enabled workbook only
exp:
Saving or exporting the worksheet as .txt (Tab-delimited) or .csv (Comma-Separated Values) strips proprietary binary/XML formatting and stores rows as plain-text lines with delimiters, making structured tabular data universally readable by databases, scripts, and external software.
★ Exam Points:
• CSV separates columns using commas (,), whereas TSV / .txt separates columns using tab characters.
• A .csv file saves only the active worksheet's values—formulas, charts, multiple sheets, and cell colours are not pre-served.
• Standard Excel extensions: .xlsx (default workbook), .xlsm (macro-enabled), .xltx (template), .xls (Excel 97–2003).

q: A workbook is to be shared widely within an organisation. Why is documenting the purpose of key sheets and critical cells (for example, using comments or a separate documentation sheet) valuable?
o: Using clear sheet names, structured tables with headings and regular backups in more than one location
It helps future users understand the structure and logic, reducing errors and misuse
It stops others from opening the workbook
exp:
Adding clear documentation—via cell comments/notes or a dedicated 'Overview' sheet—explains input assumptions, units, and formula logic so future users understand the workbook's structure, reducing accidental formula edits and misinterpretation.
★ Exam Points:
• Shortcut to insert/edit a cell Note (legacy Comment) in Excel: Shift + F2.
• A cell containing a Note displays a small red/purple indicator triangle in its top-right corner.
• Combining documentation with Protect Sheet on formula cells prevents accidental overwriting in shared models.

q: In an Excel formula, what is the function of the dollar sign when used in a reference like $A$1?
o: It converts the cell into a text label
It locks both the column and row so that the reference does not change when the formula is copied
It does not locks both the column and row so that the reference will change when the formula is copied
It makes the formula calculate faster than normal
exp:
In an Excel formula, placing dollar signs before both the column letter and row number—$A$1—creates an absolute cell reference that locks both the column and the row so neither changes when the formula is copied or dragged to any other cell.
★ Exam Points:
• Reference | Type | Locked Part (F4 cycles)
• A1 | Relative | Neither column nor row changes lock; both adjust
• $A$1 | Absolute | Both column A and row 1 locked
• $A1 | Mixed | Column A locked, row 1 relative
• A$1 | Mixed | Column A relative, row 1 locked
• Pressing F4 while editing a cell reference in the Formula Bar cycles through A1 → $A$1 → A$1 → $A1.

q: In a large Excel worksheet you want to see how the data will be divided into pages when printed including margins and page breaks. Which view should you select from the View tab to get this page based overview?
exp:
In MS Excel, Page Layout view (View tab > Workbook Views) displays the worksheet divided into actual printed pages complete with margins, headers, footers, rulers, and page breaks.
★ Exam Points:
• Normal view is best for fast continuous data entry and formula creation.
• Page Break Preview gives a zoomed-out overview with draggable blue lines to adjust where pages split.
• Print Preview shortcut across Excel and Word: Ctrl + F2 (or Ctrl + P).

q: In MS Excel, what action happens when you press the F2 key while a cell is currently selected?
o: Enters edit mode for the active cell, allowing modification
exp:
Selecting a cell in MS Excel and pressing the F2 function key switches Excel into cell Edit Mode, placing the cursor at the end of the active cell's contents so partial edits can be made without overwriting the whole cell.
★ Exam Points:
• Other ways to edit a cell without overwriting: double-click the cell or click directly inside the Formula Bar.
• Simply typing on a selected cell (without pressing F2) replaces the entire existing content.
• In Windows File Explorer, F2 renames the selected file or folder.

q: What best practice helps ensure clarity and easy identification when assigning names to Excel workbooks meant for long-term use?
o: Using very short, unclear names like "x1" or "file"
Using names that briefly describe the content
Using only random characters to make names difficult to read
exp:
Giving Excel workbooks clear, descriptive names (such as Sales_Report_2026_Q1.xlsx instead of vague labels like x1.xlsx or Book1.xlsx) makes files easy to identify, search, sort chronologically, and audit over long-term use.
★ Exam Points:
• Default unsaved workbook name in MS Excel: Book1 (default Word document name: Document1; PowerPoint: Presentation1).
• Shortcut for Save As in MS Excel & Word to rename/save a copy: F12.

q: A person regularly copies data from external sources into Excel. Sometimes values are interpreted as text instead of numbers, causing formulas to fail. Which underlying concept needs attention?
exp:
When external numbers are pasted with leading spaces, apostrophes ('), or non-numeric symbols, Excel stores them as the Text data type instead of numeric values—causing math/aggregation functions like SUM() and AVERAGE() to ignore them or formulas to fail.
★ Exam Points:
• Default Excel alignment clue: Numbers & Dates align right, Text aligns left, and Logical/Error values center.
• Fixes to convert text-numbers to real numbers: VALUE() function, Text to Columns, or the green error-indicator Convert to Number option.

q: A student enters the formula =SUM(B1:B5)-SUM(C1:C5) in Excel. What overall operation is this formula performing?
o: It adds all values in B1:B5 and C1:C5 together
It subtracts the sum of C1:C5 from the sum of B1:B5
It multiplies the sum of B1:B5 by the sum of C1:C5
It divides the sum of B1:B5 by the sum of C1:C5
exp:
In =SUM(B1:B5)-SUM(C1:C5), Excel first computes the total of cells B1 through B5, computes the total of cells C1 through C5, and then subtracts the sum of C1:C5 from the sum of B1:B5.
★ Exam Points:
• All Excel formulas must begin with an equals sign (=).
• Shortcut for AutoSum in MS Excel: Alt + =.
• A colon (:) is the range operator (e.g., B1:B5), whereas a comma (,) is the union operator separating multiple arguments.

q: When you want to zoom in or zoom out of the worksheet view without opening any dialog box which control on the status bar can you drag to change the zoom level?
exp:
At the bottom-right corner of the MS Excel Status Bar sits the Zoom slider (with – and + buttons), which can be dragged smoothly to zoom the worksheet view in or out without opening any dialog box.
★ Exam Points:
• Excel's allowed zoom range is 10% to 400% (whereas MS Word's zoom range is 10% to 500%).
• Mouse/keyboard alternative: hold Ctrl and scroll the mouse wheel up/down.
• Zooming only changes on-screen magnification—it has no effect on printed font size.

q: A workbook with many sheets is becoming confusing. Which approach is most effective for improving navigation without changing the data?
o: Reducing zoom to the smallest level
exp:
When a workbook contains many worksheets, renaming sheet tabs with clear, descriptive titles (e.g., Jan_Sales, Summary, Tax_Calc instead of Sheet1..Sheet20) dramatically improves navigation without altering any cell data.
★ Exam Points:
• To rename a sheet tab quickly: double-click the sheet tab (or right-click the tab → Rename).
• Right-clicking the sheet navigation arrows (bottom-left) opens a popup list of all sheets in a large workbook for instant jumping.

q: A workbook is designed to calculate totals automatically, yet some cells have been typed with spaces causing them to be treated as text. What does this reveal about careful data entry in Excel?
o: That extra characters such as leading spaces can change how Excel interprets an entry and affect results
Excel is unable to process or recognize any numeric values, this prevents calculations, formulas and numerical analysis from being performed
exp:
Typing accidental leading/trailing spaces alongside digits (e.g., " 250" or "1 00") causes Excel to interpret the entry as a text string rather than a number, demonstrating that invisible extra characters alter data interpretation and break numeric calculations.
★ Exam Points:
• =TRIM(text) removes leading, trailing, and duplicate spaces from text strings.
• Data Validation (Data tab > Data Tools) can restrict a column strictly to whole numbers or decimals to prevent invalid text entry.

q: In the context of office productivity software which of the following best describes Microsoft Excel from the point of view of its main purpose?
o: It is a word processing program used mainly to create long documents
It is a spreadsheet program used to organise data in rows and columns
It is a graphics editor used only for drawing pictures and logos
It is an email client used for sending and receiving messages
exp:
Microsoft Excel is a spreadsheet application designed to organize, calculate, analyze, and visualize structured data arranged in tabular rows and columns.
★ Exam Points:
• Modern Excel worksheet dimensions (Excel 2007+): 1,048,576 rows (2²⁰) and 16,384 columns (2¹⁴, from A to XFD).
• Other spreadsheet programs: Google Sheets, LibreOffice Calc, and Apple Numbers (historic first electronic spreadsheet: VisiCalc, 1979).

q: Which method lets you modify part of the existing text or number in a cell without retyping the whole entry?
o: Select the cell, press F2 to enter edit mode
Select the cell and press Delete
Select the row number on the left edge
Select the column letter at the top
exp:
To modify only part of an existing cell entry without retyping everything from scratch, select the cell and press F2 to enter Edit Mode (or double-click the cell / edit in the Formula Bar).
★ Exam Points:
• Once in Edit Mode, use the Left/Right arrow keys, Home (start of entry), and End (end of entry) to position the cursor precisely.
• Press Enter to save the change or Esc to discard the edit.

q: If cell A1 contains 10 and cell B1 contains 4, what output will the formula generate? =MOD(A1,B1)
exp:
The MOD(number, divisor) function returns the remainder after dividing number by divisor: With A1 = 10 and B1 = 4, dividing 10÷4 gives quotient 2 ( 4×2 = 8) and remainder 10−8 = 2. Thus =MOD(A1,B1) outputs 2.
★ Exam Points:
• To get only the integer quotient without remainder, Excel provides =QUOTIENT(10, 4) → returns 2.
• If the divisor (second argument) in =MOD(A1, B1) is 0, Excel returns the #DIV/0! error.

q:
In MS-Excel 365, which of the following is/are true about naming worksheets?
(i) The keyboard shortcut to add a new sheet is Shift + F11.
(ii) A worksheet name can contain the characters / \ ? * : [ ].
(iii) A worksheet can be renamed by right-clicking the sheet tab and choosing Rename.
(iv) A worksheet can be renamed by double-clicking the sheet tab.
exp:
Sheet names cannot contain / \ ? * : [ ]; the other three statements are true.
★ Exam Points:
• Sheet name maximum length: 31 characters.
• Sheet name cannot be blank or "History".
• Alt + H, O, R also renames a sheet.

q:
Identify whether the following statements are true or false.
(i) If A15 = 4 and A16 = 3 and =A15*A16 is entered in A17, the value in A17 will be 64.
(ii) In MS-Excel 365, NETWORKDAYS() returns the number of whole workdays between two dates.
(iii) In MS-Excel 365, a radar chart is also known as a spider chart or web chart.
exp:
4 × 3 = 12, not 64 (64 would be 4^3), so (i) is false; (ii) and (iii) are true.
★ Exam Points:
• Exponent operator in Excel is ^ (e.g. =4^3).
• NETWORKDAYS excludes weekends and listed holidays.
• Radar chart compares several variables from a central point.

q:
Match List-I (Excel formula) with List-II (output).
(a) =REPLACE("1101010",6,2,"11") (b) =(11+1010101) (c) =DEC2HEX(10) (d) =BIN2DEC(100)
(i) 4 (ii) 1101011 (iii) 1010112 (iv) A
exp:
REPLACE swaps characters 6–7 ("10") with "11" → 1101011; 11 + 1010101 = 1010112 (decimal addition); decimal 10 = hex A; binary 100 = 4.
★ Exam Points:
• DEC2BIN, BIN2DEC, DEC2HEX, HEX2DEC are Engineering functions.
• REPLACE(old_text, start_num, num_chars, new_text).
• SUBSTITUTE replaces by matching text, not position.

q: In MS-Excel 365, the cell address D101 indicates ____.
exp:
A cell address gives the column letter first and then the row number, so D101 is column D, row 101.
★ Exam Points:
• Columns are labelled with letters, rows with numbers.
• R1C1 style shows both as numbers (R101C4).
• Ctrl + G (F5) – Go To a cell address.

q:
Match the Excel formula with its output.
(a) =MID("mumbai metro",8,5) (b) =REPT("mumbai metro",3) (c) =CHAR(66) (d) =PROPER("mumbai metro")
(i) Mumbai Metro (ii) metro (iii) mumbai metromumbai metromumbai metro (iv) B
exp:
MID takes 5 characters from position 8 ("metro"); REPT repeats text 3 times; CHAR(66) = "B"; PROPER capitalises each word.
★ Exam Points:
• MID(text, start_num, num_chars).
• CHAR returns the character for an ASCII/ANSI code; CODE does the reverse.
• UPPER/LOWER change all letters.

q: Which option is used to save a file in CSV format in MS-Excel 365?
exp:
Use File → Save As (F12) and choose "CSV (Comma delimited) (*.csv)" as the file type.
★ Exam Points:
• CSV = Comma-Separated Values (plain text).
• CSV saves only the active sheet and no formatting.
• Default Excel format: .xlsx.

q:
Identify whether the statements are true or false.
(i) The Excel function that counts cells with text or values but not blanks is COUNT_NONE_BLANK.
(ii) CHOOSE comes under Lookup & Reference functions.
(iii) A bar chart illustrates comparisons among individual items.
exp:
The correct function is COUNTA; there is no COUNT_NONE_BLANK, so (i) is false.
★ Exam Points:
• COUNT – numbers only; COUNTA – non-empty; COUNTBLANK – empty cells.
• CHOOSE(index, value1, value2, …).
• Bar chart = horizontal bars; column chart = vertical bars.

q: Which keyboard shortcut is used to format a worksheet range using the ‘Format as Table’ style in MS-Excel 2019?
exp:
Alt, H, T opens the Format as Table gallery on the Home tab (Ctrl + T creates a table directly).
★ Exam Points:
• Ctrl + T / Ctrl + L – Create Table.
• Ctrl + 1 opens Format Cells.
• Tables give banded rows, filters and structured references.

q: Which keyboard shortcut is used to enter a new line in the same cell in an MS-Excel 2010 worksheet?
exp:
Alt + Enter inserts a line break inside the cell; Wrap Text is turned on automatically.
★ Exam Points:
• Ctrl + Enter fills the selected cells with the same entry.
• Shift + Enter moves to the cell above.
• Tab moves to the cell on the right.

q: What is the default alignment of numeric values entered into a cell of an MS-Excel worksheet?
exp:
Numbers, dates and times are right-aligned by default; text is left-aligned.
★ Exam Points:
• Logical values TRUE/FALSE and errors are centre-aligned.
• Numbers stored as text appear left-aligned with a green triangle.
• Default font in Excel 365: Aptos 11 (earlier Calibri 11).

q: In MS-Excel 2010, to print multiple worksheets, click the first worksheet, hold the ____ key and then click the other worksheets you want to select.
exp:
Ctrl + click selects non-adjacent sheet tabs; Shift + click selects adjacent ones; selected sheets form a group.
★ Exam Points:
• Grouped sheets show [Group] in the title bar.
• Ctrl + Page Down/Up moves between sheets.
• Print → "Print Entire Workbook" prints all sheets.

q: In the MS PowerPoint 2019 interface, which of the following icons should you click to save changes to the current presentation quickly?
exp:
The floppy disk icon on the Quick Access Toolbar saves the presentation.
★ Exam Points:
• Floppy disk icon = Save.
• Curved left arrow = Undo; circular arrow = Redo.
• QAT is customisable.

q: In Microsoft PowerPoint, which view is best suited for reorganising slides and getting an overview of the entire presentation structure?
exp:
Slide Sorter view is best for reorganising slides and viewing the overall structure.
★ Exam Points:
• Slide Sorter – reorder slides by dragging.
• Normal – editing.
• Reading View – preview in window.

q: Which keyboard shortcut is used in MS PowerPoint 365 to start editing text inside a selected shape or text box?
exp:
F2 enters edit mode inside a selected shape or text box in PowerPoint.
★ Exam Points:
• F2 toggles text edit in a selected shape.
• Esc exits text editing.
• F5 starts slide show.

q: When initiating a new presentation in MS PowerPoint, which of the following is the most accurate description of the 'Design Ideas' feature's primary function?
o: To automatically populate slides with relevant content based on the presentation topic
To provide real-time collaboration tools for multiple users working on the same presentation simultaneously
To suggest various pre-designed templates and layouts based on the content on the current slide
To automatically translate the presentation content into multiple languages
exp:
Design Ideas suggests pre-designed templates and layouts for slides.
★ Exam Points:
• Design Ideas (Designer) suggests layouts automatically.
• Found in Design tab.
• Requires Microsoft 365 (online feature).

q: What is the significance of PowerPoint’s "Protected View", while opening a downloaded file?
o: It opens the file in a read-only mode, disabling most editing features
The presentation is encrypted and cannot be viewed
exp:
Protected View opens a downloaded file in read-only mode with most editing disabled to protect from threats.
★ Exam Points:
• Protected View = read-only sandbox for files from the Internet.
• Click "Enable Editing" to edit.
• Protects against malicious macros.

q: What happens if you start a new blank presentation while another presentation is already open in MS PowerPoint?
o: The slides from the current presentation are copied to the new one.
A new MS PowerPoint window opens with the blank presentation.
MS PowerPoint displays an error message.
exp:
A new PowerPoint window opens with the blank presentation; the existing presentation stays open.
★ Exam Points:
• Ctrl + N creates a new presentation.
• Switch windows with Alt + Tab.
• Each presentation is a separate window.

q: When saving an MS PowerPoint presentation, what is the primary purpose of the 'Save as Picture Presentation' option?
o: To optimise the presentation for viewing on low-bandwidth internet connections
To prevent any further editing of the presentation content
To save each slide as a separate image file within a folder
To embed a static image of the first slide as a preview
exp:
Save as Picture Presentation turns slides into pictures, preventing further editing of the content.
★ Exam Points:
• Picture presentation converts each slide into an image.
• Text can no longer be edited.
• Helps protect content.

q: What happens when you press 'Ctrl + M' in MS PowerPoint 365?
o: A new slide is inserted with the same layout as the previous slide.
A new blank slide is inserted regardless of the previous layout.
A duplicate of the current slide is created.
The slide master view is opened.
exp:
Ctrl + M inserts a new slide with the same layout as the current slide.
★ Exam Points:
• Ctrl + M – new slide.
• Ctrl + D – duplicate slide.
• New slide normally follows the current slide's layout.

q: When you reuse slides from another presentation in MS PowerPoint 365, which of the following options ensures the imported slides retain their original formatting?
o: Import slides as images to lock their look
Apply the destination theme after inserting
Click 'Keep Source Formatting' in the Reuse Slides pane
exp:
'Keep Source Formatting' in Reuse Slides keeps the imported slides' original look.
★ Exam Points:
• Keep Source Formatting preserves original design.
• Default uses destination theme.
• Reuse Slides pane has this checkbox.

q: Which of the following options in PowerPoint allows you to see all the slides at once as thumbnails?
exp:
Slide Sorter view shows all slides as thumbnails for reordering, copying or deleting.
★ Exam Points:
• Normal view – editing.
• Reading View – window slide show.
• Outline View – text only.

q: Which of the following methods is the quickest way to open an existing MS PowerPoint presentation?
o: Double-click the .pptx file in File Explorer
Open MS PowerPoint and click Blank Presentation
exp:
Double-clicking the .pptx file in File Explorer opens it fastest.
★ Exam Points:
• Double-click the file to open it with its default program.
• Ctrl + O from inside PowerPoint.
• Recent list in File → Open.

q: What is the main function of MS PowerPoint?
exp:
PowerPoint is used to create and present slideshows.
★ Exam Points:
• PowerPoint – presentation software (Microsoft, 1987; originally Forethought).
• Slides contain text, images, media.
• File format: .pptx.

q: Which of the following MS PowerPoint features allows you to record the timing for each slide and any narration or laser pointer movements to be replayed automatically during a slideshow?
exp:
Record Slide Show records timings, narration and laser-pointer movements for automatic replay.
★ Exam Points:
• Record Slide Show records narration, timings and ink.
• Rehearse Timings records only timings.
• Found in Slide Show tab.

q: In MS PowerPoint, which of the following keyboard combinations is used to create a new blank presentation?
exp:
Ctrl + N creates a new blank presentation.
★ Exam Points:
• Ctrl + N – new presentation.
• Ctrl + O – open.
• Ctrl + B – bold.

q: What happens when you apply a template to an existing MS PowerPoint presentation?
o: It only changes the background, without affecting text formatting.
It applies a new design while keeping the existing slide content.
It converts the PowerPoint presentation into a read-only format.
It completely replaces all slides and content.
exp:
Applying a template gives a new design while keeping the existing slide content.
