• Design tab → Themes.
• Variants change colour schemes.

q: Which keyboard shortcut is used to save an MS PowerPoint presentation quickly?
exp:
Ctrl + S saves the presentation.
★ Exam Points:
• Ctrl + S – save.
• Ctrl + O – open; Ctrl + P – print.
• Ctrl + N – new presentation.

q: Which shortcut key is used to create a new blank presentation quickly in MS PowerPoint 365?
exp:
Ctrl + N creates a new blank presentation.
★ Exam Points:
• Ctrl + N – new presentation.
• Ctrl + O – open; Ctrl + P – print.
• Ctrl + M – new slide.

q: Which sequence of steps correctly initiates a blank presentation in MS PowerPoint 2016 or later?
exp:
File, New, then Blank Presentation starts a blank presentation.
★ Exam Points:
• File → New → Blank Presentation.
• Templates available in New.
• Ctrl + N shortcut.

q: Which of the following is the main purpose of using the 'Ctrl + S' keyboard shortcut while working on an MS PowerPoint presentation?
o: To save the current changes made to the file
To close the presentation window immediately
To share the presentation via email
To start a slideshow from the beginning

Ctrl + S saves the current changes.

q: In MS PowerPoint's Slide Master view, what is the primary benefit of customising the top-level master slide versus individual layout masters?
o: The top-level master is only relevant when exporting the presentation to other formats
Customising the top-level master ensures consistency of universal elements across all slide layouts
Changes to the top-level master overrides all formatting on individual layout masters
Individual layout masters cannot be edited unless the top-level master is modified first

Customising the top-level master ensures consistency across all layouts.

• Top-level master affects all layouts.
• Layout masters control specific layouts.
• Ensures consistent fonts and colours.

q: If you want your audience to NOT see your notes in the MS PowerPoint 365 slides, which view should you use during slide show?
exp:
Presenter View shows speaker notes to the presenter only, not to the audience.
★ Exam Points:
• Presenter View shows notes, next slide, timer only to presenter.
• Audience sees only the slide.
• Alt + F5 starts Presenter View.

q: Which shortcut key combination is used to insert a hyperlink in MS PowerPoint 365?
exp:
Ctrl + K inserts a hyperlink.
★ Exam Points:
• Ctrl + K – insert hyperlink.
• Links can point to slides or URLs.
• Action buttons also link.

q: In MS PowerPoint, which of the following keys must be pressed to start a new line while typing inside a text box?

Pressing Enter starts a new paragraph/line inside a PowerPoint text box (Shift + Enter inserts a line break within the same paragraph).
★ Exam Points:
• Tab increases list level.
• Shift + Tab decreases list level.
• AutoFit shrinks text to fit.

q: On the MS PowerPoint 2019 home screen, which option or section should you click to start a new blank presentation when the 'Start Screen' is enabled?
o: The Open button at the bottom left corner
The Recent tab in the left sidebar
The Design tab from the ribbon
The tile labeled 'Blank Presentation' on the right panel

On the Start Screen, click the 'Blank Presentation' tile to begin a new blank presentation.

• Start screen shows templates and Blank Presentation.
• Ctrl + N also creates blank.
• Start screen can be disabled in Options.

q: When saving an MS PowerPoint presentation, which of the following options would be most suitable if the primary goal is to ensure the presentation opens in slideshow view by default for recipients who may not have MS PowerPoint installed?
exp:
Saving as PowerPoint Show (.ppsx) makes the file open in slide-show view.
★ Exam Points:
• .ppsx opens straight into slide show.
• .pdf preserves layout but no animations.
• .odp is OpenDocument format.

q: Which of the following keyboard shortcuts is used to insert a new slide in PowerPoint 2019?
exp:
Ctrl + M inserts a new slide in PowerPoint.
★ Exam Points:
• Ctrl + M – new slide.
• Ctrl + D – duplicate.
• Ctrl + K – hyperlink.

q: What is the main advantage of saving an MS PowerPoint presentation as a .pdf file?
o: It enables users to modify slides in any PDF viewer.
It reduces file size and prevents unwanted editing.
It allows all MS PowerPoint animations to run.
It automatically translates text into different languages.

Saving as PDF reduces file size and prevents unwanted editing.

q: Which feature in MS-PowerPoint 2019 allows you to reuse slides from another presentation without copying content manually?
exp:
Reuse Slides (Home, New Slide) lets you insert slides from another presentation.
★ Exam Points:
• Home → New Slide → Reuse Slides.
• Keep Source Formatting option available.
• Saves time across presentations.

q: What happens when you press F5 in MS PowerPoint 2019?
o: Starts the slide show from the beginning
exp:
F5 starts the slide show from the beginning.

• F5 – start from beginning.
• Shift + F5 – from current slide.

q: Which file format is used for saving MS PowerPoint templates?
exp:
PowerPoint templates are saved as .potx files.

• .potx – template; .pptx – presentation.
• .ppsx – show; .pptm – macro-enabled.

q: What is the primary purpose of the .ppsx file format in MS PowerPoint 365?
o: To save the presentation in a read-only format
To save the presentation in a format that opens directly in Slide Show mode
To save the presentation as a template for future use
To compress the presentation file size

q: A user wants to have a bulleted list in MS PowerPoint. After typing a list item and pressing Enter, they want to create a sub-bullet point (a lower-level bullet). Which of the following actions will reliably achieve this?

Clicking the 'Decrease List Level' button in the Paragraph group

q: In MS PowerPoint 2019, when you press the Enter key while typing in a text box, what happens?

The cursor moves to the next line within the same text box.
The text is entered into a new slide.
exp:
Pressing Enter in a text box moves the cursor to the next line within the same text box.

q: What is the standard method to save your work in PowerPoint?
o: Use the File tab and select 'Save' or press Ctrl + S
exp:
Use File then Save, or press Ctrl + S, to save in PowerPoint.
★ Exam Points:
• Ctrl + S saves; F12 Save As.
• Default format .pptx.
• AutoSave works with OneDrive.

q: What happens if you paste text into MS-PowerPoint 2019 with the Keep Source Formatting option?
o: The text adopts the destination slide’s theme fonts/colors.
The text retains its original formatting from the source.
The text is converted into an image.
The text size automatically adjusts to fit the slide.

Keep Source Formatting retains the original formatting of the copied text.

• Keep Source Formatting – retains original.
• Use Destination Theme – adopts slide's theme.
• Keep Text Only – plain text.

q: Which of the following is the correct way to add a new slide in an MS-PowerPoint 2019 presentation?
o: Go to the Home tab Click New Slide
exp:
On the Home tab, click New Slide to add a slide.
★ Exam Points:
• Home → New Slide (Ctrl + M).
• Layout can be chosen from the drop-down.
• Duplicate slide: Ctrl + D.

q: Which method CANNOT be used to create a new slide in MS PowerPoint 365?
o: Clicking 'New Slide' on the Home tab
Right-clicking in the slide sorter pane and selecting 'New Slide'
exp:
Ctrl + N creates a new presentation, not a new slide; Ctrl + M adds a slide.
★ Exam Points:
• Ctrl + N opens a new presentation.
• New slide: Ctrl + M, Home → New Slide, right-click → New Slide.
• Enter in thumbnails pane also adds a slide.

q: What is the shortcut to open an MS PowerPoint file directly from the application?
exp:
Ctrl + O opens an existing file.
★ Exam Points:
• Ctrl + O opens existing file.
• Ctrl + N new; Ctrl + S save.
• Ctrl + P print.

q: In MS PowerPoint 2019, which of the following tabs must you first select to access the 'Open' option for loading a saved PowerPoint file?
exp:
The File tab leads to the Open option.
★ Exam Points:
• File tab → Open (Ctrl + O).
• Recent presentations listed there.
• Backstage view holds file commands.

q: Which of the following shortcut keys can be used to quickly open a presentation in PowerPoint?
exp:
Ctrl + O opens a presentation.
★ Exam Points:
• Ctrl + O – open presentation.
• Ctrl + F12 – Open dialog.
• Recent files on Start screen.

q: Which of the following is the correct way to start a new blank presentation in MS PowerPoint?
exp:
Ctrl + N starts a new blank presentation in PowerPoint.
★ Exam Points:
• Ctrl + N – new presentation.
• Ctrl + O – open.
• Ctrl + M – new slide.

q: When using the 'Replace' function (Ctrl + H) in MS PowerPoint, which of the following options allows users to replace only whole words and not parts of words?
exp:
The 'Find whole words only' option replaces only complete words.
★ Exam Points:
• Find whole words only avoids partial matches.
• Match case respects capitals.
• Ctrl + H – Replace in PowerPoint.

q: How do you add text to a slide in MS PowerPoint?
o: Click inside a text placeholder and start typing
Drag an image onto the slide
exp:
Click inside a text placeholder and type to add text to a slide.
★ Exam Points:
• Text placeholders appear in slide layouts.
• Text boxes can be inserted from Insert tab.
• Outline view also allows typing.

q: Which of the following elements, when poorly implemented, is most likely to undermine the credibility and impact of an otherwise well-researched MS PowerPoint presentation?
o: The inclusion of speaker notes for reference
Inconsistent use of slide masters and templates
Embedding multimedia elements such as videos
The choice of transition effects between slides
exp:
Inconsistent use of slide masters and templates makes a presentation look unprofessional and hurts credibility.
★ Exam Points:
• Consistent masters/templates make slides professional.
• Avoid mixing many fonts/colours.
• Use Slide Master for uniform design.

q: What happens if you try to open a MS PowerPoint presentation created in a newer version (e.g., MS PowerPoint 2021) in an older version (e.g., MS PowerPoint 2010)?
o: The file will be automatically converted to a PDF.
The file will open normally with all features intact.
MS PowerPoint will display an error and refuse to open the file.
The file will open in Compatibility Mode with limited features.
exp:
A newer-version PowerPoint file opens in an older version, but newer features may be unavailable or changed.
★ Exam Points:
• Older versions open newer files in Compatibility Mode or with limited features.
• Office 2007+ share .pptx format.
• Unsupported features may display as images.

q: What is the purpose of the Slide Master in MS PowerPoint?
o: To apply consistent formatting, fonts, and layouts to all slides
To delete multiple slides at once
exp:
The Slide Master applies consistent formatting, fonts and layouts across all slides.
★ Exam Points:
• Slide Master controls themes, fonts, placeholders for all slides.
• View → Slide Master.
• Changes apply to all slides using that layout.

q: In Microsoft PowerPoint, which keyboard shortcut inserts a new slide (with the layout of the previous slide)?
exp:
Ctrl + M adds a new slide after the current one.
★ Exam Points:
• Ctrl + D duplicates the current slide.
• Ctrl + N creates a new presentation.
• Layouts can be changed via Home → Layout.

q: What are the correct steps to create a blank presentation in MS PowerPoint?
exp:
Choose File, then New, then Blank Presentation (or press Ctrl + N).
★ Exam Points:
• Default first slide layout: Title Slide.
• Presentations save as .pptx.
• Templates are listed under New.

q: How can you exit a slide show and return to editing mode in MS PowerPoint?
exp:
Esc (or the hyphen key) ends the slide show.
★ Exam Points:
• F5 – start from the beginning.
• Shift + F5 – start from current slide.
• B blacks out the screen; W whites it.

q: What is the main purpose of using a template when creating a presentation in MS PowerPoint?
exp:
Templates provide predefined layouts, themes, fonts and colours so all slides look consistent and professional.
★ Exam Points:
• PowerPoint template extension: .potx.
• Slide Master controls the overall design.
• Themes are in the Design tab.

q: What is the primary advantage of being able to insert and delete slides in an MS PowerPoint presentation?
o: To allow dynamic content adjustment and organisation
To apply different templates to individual slides
exp:
Adding and removing slides lets the presenter organise and adjust the content flow as needed.
★ Exam Points:
• New slide: Ctrl + M.
• Duplicate slide: Ctrl + D.
• Slide Sorter view helps reorder slides.

q: During a presentation, text shifts out of place when editing content. Which design mistake is the most likely cause of this issue?
o: Using placeholders instead of text boxes
exp:
In presentation software like MS PowerPoint, slide layouts contain built-in placeholders tied to the Slide Master. Inserting ad-hoc floating text boxes instead of using placeholders causes text to shift unpredictably when layouts, themes, or content change.
★ Exam Points:
• Slide Master (View tab > Master Views) controls global fonts, logos, backgrounds, and placeholder positions across all slides.
• Ctrl + M inserts a new slide, whereas Ctrl + D duplicates the selected slide.
• Text typed inside placeholders automatically appears in the Outline View, while manual text box content does not.

q: In Microsoft PowerPoint, which keyboard shortcut is commonly used to insert a new slide with the same layout as the previous slide?
exp:
In Microsoft PowerPoint, pressing Ctrl + M inserts a new slide into the current presentation inheriting the layout of the preceding slide.
★ Exam Points:
• PowerPoint Shortcut | Action
• Ctrl + M | Insert a new slide in current presentation
• Ctrl + N | Create a brand-new blank presentation file
• Ctrl + D | Duplicate the currently selected slide or object
• F5 / Shift + F5 | Start Slide Show from beginning / from current slide
• Esc | End an active Slide Show

q: __________ asks you some questions during the process of presentation creation.
exp:
In classic versions of MS PowerPoint (up to PowerPoint 2003), the AutoContent Wizard guided users through a series of step-by-step questions (presentation type, output style, title/footer details) to automatically generate a structured starter presentation with suggested slide topics.
★ Exam Points:
• In modern PowerPoint (2007+), the AutoContent Wizard was replaced by ready-made Templates and Themes under File > New.

q: ____ is the keyboard shortcut to save a presentation in MS-PowerPoint 2010.
exp:
Ctrl + S saves the presentation; F12 opens Save As.
★ Exam Points:
• PowerPoint file extension: .pptx.
• Ctrl + M inserts a new slide.
• F5 starts the slide show from the beginning.

q: Which of the following best describes a LAN?
o: A storage device used to read optical discs
A network covering a small geographical area like an office or school
A code used to represent characters in numbers
exp:
A LAN (Local Area Network) connects computers within a small area such as a home, office or campus.
★ Exam Points:
• LAN uses Ethernet (IEEE 802.3) or Wi-Fi (802.11).
• Optical discs (CD/DVD) are storage, not networks.
• ASCII is a character code.

q: LAN is often used in schools and offices. This abbreviation expands to:
exp:
LAN stands for Local Area Network.
★ Exam Points:
• LAN covers a room, building or campus.
• Ethernet and Wi-Fi are LAN technologies.
• LANs offer high speed and low error rate.

q: In the context of Local Area Networks (LANs), what is the primary purpose of a MAC (Media Access Control) address?
o: To specify the network protocol being used for communication
To uniquely identify a network interface controller (NIC) at the data link layer
To define the physical layout and cabling of the network
To provide a logical address for network routing
exp:
A MAC address is a hardware address burned into a network interface controller (NIC) that uniquely identifies it on a local network. It is 48 bits (six hex pairs).
★ Exam Points:
• MAC address is 48-bit, written as 6 hex pairs (e.g., 00:1A:2B:3C:4D:5E).
• IP address = logical address (Network layer); MAC = physical address (Data Link layer).
• ARP maps an IP address to a MAC address.

q: A Local Area Network (LAN) enables resource sharing by connecting devices to the network medium through a specialized adapter called the ________.
exp:
A computer connects to a LAN through a Network Interface Card (NIC).
★ Exam Points:
• NIC = Network Interface Card (network adapter).
• Each NIC has a unique MAC address.
• Wireless NIC connects to Wi-Fi.

q: During group project file sharing in the CSE classroom, LAN connects which devices directly?
o: Local computers within the same building
Satellite phones for remote areas only
exp:
A LAN connects local computers within the same building.
★ Exam Points:
• LAN shares files, printers and Internet within a building.
• Classroom labs commonly use LAN switches.
• Bluetooth forms a PAN, not a LAN.

q: Which standard is commonly used for wired LANs?
exp:
IEEE 802.3 is the Ethernet standard for wired LANs; 802.11 is Wi-Fi, 802.15 Bluetooth, 802.16 WiMAX.
★ Exam Points:
• IEEE 802.3 – Ethernet (wired LAN).
• IEEE 802.11 – Wi-Fi (wireless LAN).
• IEEE 802.15 – Bluetooth/WPAN; 802.16 – WiMAX.

q: Which of the following is the correct full form of LAN?
exp:
LAN = Local Area Network.
★ Exam Points:
• LAN = Local Area Network; WAN = Wide Area Network.
• MAN = Metropolitan Area Network.
• PAN = Personal Area Network.

q: What does the abbreviation 'MAN' stand for in computer networking?
exp:
MAN stands for Metropolitan Area Network, covering a city; it is larger than a LAN and smaller than a WAN.
★ Exam Points:
• MAN spans a city (5–50 km), e.g., cable TV network.
• Order by size: PAN < LAN < MAN < WAN.
• WAN example: Internet.

q: In a LAN setup, which of the following statements is true?
o: LAN cannot share printers or files between devices.
LAN is used to connect computers over a large geographical area.
LAN connects computers within a limited area like a home or office.
exp:
A LAN connects computers within a limited area such as a building or campus and allows sharing of files and printers.
★ Exam Points:
• LANs do not need satellites.
• Large geographical area = WAN.
• LAN devices: switch, NIC, cables.

q: Which type of network connects branch offices in different cities using leased lines or satellite links?
o: LAN because it offers high speed
MAN because it covers a city
WAN because it spans large geographical areas
PAN because it connects personal devices
exp:
WANs link networks across cities and countries using leased lines, MPLS, satellite or the Internet.
★ Exam Points:
• Internet is the largest WAN.
• Banks use WANs for branches.
• MAN covers a single city.

q: Uploading files to the cloud is much slower than downloading the same size. What is the most appropriate reason?
o: Cloud servers limit upload for security
Internet connections usually have asymmetric bandwidth
exp:
Most consumer connections (ADSL, cable, mobile) provide higher download than upload speed.
★ Exam Points:
• ADSL "A" = Asymmetric.
• Fibre plans may be symmetric.
• Speed tests show both values.

q: A network device divides a LAN into smaller segments, reduces traffic and works with MAC addresses but not IP addresses. Which device is it?
exp:
A bridge works at the Data Link layer, filtering traffic between LAN segments using MAC addresses.
★ Exam Points:
• Switch is a multi-port bridge.
• Router uses IP addresses (Layer 3).
• Gateway converts protocols.

q: Which protocol is most commonly used for web communication?
exp:
HTTP (and HTTPS) carries web pages between browsers and web servers.
★ Exam Points:
• HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2, HTTP/3 versions.
• Port 80 / 443.
• FTP is for files.

q: What type of media is commonly used for WAN communication?
exp:
Fibre optic cables carry data as light over very long distances with high bandwidth, ideal for WANs.
★ Exam Points:
• Undersea cables are fibre optic.
• Fibre is immune to electromagnetic interference.
• Twisted pair is common in LANs.

q: Which device is commonly used to connect computers within a LAN?
exp:
A switch connects multiple devices in a LAN and forwards frames using MAC addresses.
★ Exam Points:
• Router connects different networks (LAN to Internet).
• Modem converts digital/analog signals.
• Repeater boosts signals.

q: ____ is the bit rate of available or consumed information capacity, expressed typically in metric multiples of bits per second.
exp:
Bandwidth is the maximum data transfer capacity of a channel, measured in bps, kbps, Mbps or Gbps.
★ Exam Points:
• Throughput is the actual data rate achieved.
• Latency is delay; measured in milliseconds.
• Baud rate = signal changes per second.

q: A ____ is a networking device that filters network traffic while connecting multiple computers or communicating devices.
exp:
A switch learns MAC addresses and sends frames only to the correct port, filtering traffic within a LAN.
★ Exam Points:
• Switch is an intelligent hub.
• Layer-3 switches can also route.
• Router connects different networks using IP addresses.

q: A/An ____ server acts as a set of components accessible to the software developer through an API defined by the platform itself.
exp:
An application server hosts business logic and exposes components/services to developers through a platform-defined API.
★ Exam Points:
• Examples: Apache Tomcat, JBoss/WildFly, IBM WebSphere.
• Web server serves static pages (Apache HTTP, Nginx, IIS).
• Database server stores and manages data (MySQL, Oracle).

q: Which Internet protocol specifies how data is exchanged over the Internet and how it should be broken into IP packets?
exp:
TCP (Transmission Control Protocol) breaks messages into packets, ensures reliable, ordered delivery and reassembles them at the destination.
★ Exam Points:
• TCP is connection-oriented; UDP is connectionless.
• TCP/IP was developed by Vint Cerf and Bob Kahn.
• TCP works at the Transport layer.

q: A ____ is a networking device that filters network traffic while connecting multiple computers or communicating devices.
exp:
A switch reads MAC addresses and forwards each frame only to the intended port, filtering unnecessary traffic.
★ Exam Points:
• Switch works at the Data Link layer (Layer 2).
• Hub sends data to all ports (no filtering).
• Repeater regenerates weak signals (Physical layer).

q: ____ is also known as a protocol converter.
exp:
A gateway converts data between networks that use different protocols, so it is called a protocol converter.
★ Exam Points:
• Gateway is the most complex internetworking device.
• Bridge connects two LAN segments (Data Link layer).
• Modem converts digital ↔ analog signals.

q: ____ are rules that exist at several levels in a telecommunication connection.
exp:
A protocol is a set of rules that governs how data is formatted, transmitted and received between devices at every layer of communication.
★ Exam Points:
• Examples: TCP/IP, HTTP, FTP, SMTP.
• Protocol elements: syntax, semantics and timing.
• OSI model has 7 layers; TCP/IP model has 4.

q: ____ is a passage to connect two networks that may work on different networking models.
exp:
A gateway joins networks that use different protocols or models and translates between them; hence it is called a protocol converter.
★ Exam Points:
• Gateway works at all OSI layers (can work up to the Application layer).
• Router connects networks using the same protocol (Network layer).
• Hub broadcasts to all ports (Physical layer).

q: In the OSI model, which layer is responsible for routing packets between networks using logical addressing?
exp:
In the 7-layer OSI model, the Network Layer (Layer 3) handles logical addressing (IP addresses) and routing of packets across different networks to determine the best path from source to destination.
★ Exam Points:
• OSI Layer | PDU (Unit) | Key Protocols / Devices
• Layer 4 – Transport | Segment / Datagram | TCP, UDP (End-to-end delivery, port numbers)
• Layer 3 – Network | Packet | IP, ICMP, Routers, Layer-3 Switches
• Layer 2 – Data Link | Frame | MAC address, Ethernet, Switches, Bridges
• Layer 1 – Physical | Bits | Cables, Hubs, Repeaters

q: A network device divides a LAN into smaller segments, reduces traffic and operates using MAC addresses but does not use IP addressing. Which device matches this description?
exp:
A Bridge operates at Layer 2 (Data Link Layer) of the OSI model. It inspects hardware MAC addresses to filter frames and split a large LAN into smaller collision domains without using Layer-3 IP addressing.
★ Exam Points:
• Network Device | OSI Layer | Addressing / Function
• Repeater / Hub | Layer 1 (Physical) | No addressing; regenerates/broad casts raw bits
• Bridge / Switch | Layer 2 (Data Link) | Uses 48-bit MAC addresses; breaks collision domains
• Router | Layer 3 (Network) | Uses IP addresses; routes packets across networks & breaks broadcast domains
• Gateway | All Layers (Up to L7) | Connects dissimi-lar networks using different protocol suites

q: What is the maximum transmission unit (MTU) for Ethernet frames in most networks?
exp:
Standard Ethernet MTU is 1500 bytes of payload.
★ Exam Points:
• Jumbo frames can be ~9000 bytes.
• Larger packets are fragmented.
• Ethernet frame max size 1518 bytes (with header & FCS).

q: Which protocol is used to upload or retrieve files between client and server?
exp:
FTP (File Transfer Protocol) is designed for transferring files between client and server.
★ Exam Points:
• Ports 20 (data) and 21 (control).
• Anonymous FTP needs no account.
• SFTP runs over SSH.

q: ____ is a broadband technology that transmits digital data at high bandwidth over existing phone lines to homes and businesses.
exp:
ADSL (Asymmetric Digital Subscriber Line) offers faster download than upload over copper telephone lines.
★ Exam Points:
• A splitter separates voice and data.
• Upload slower than download (asymmetric).
• VDSL is faster.

q: In IPv6, how many bits make up the address?
exp:
IPv6 addresses are 128 bits, written as eight groups of four hexadecimal digits.
★ Exam Points:
• Example: 2001:0db8::1.
• Provides about 3.4 × 10^38 addresses.
• IPv4 is 32 bits.

q: Which term describes an intermediary server that forwards requests without revealing the client's identity?
exp:
A proxy server sits between client and Internet, forwarding requests and hiding the client's IP address.
★ Exam Points:
• Proxies can cache pages.
• Used for content filtering.
• VPN encrypts traffic as well.

q: Which describes the difference between a static and a dynamic IP address?
o: Static IPs are used in the US only
Static IPs change frequently; dynamic IPs remain the same
Static IPs remain the same; dynamic IPs are assigned temporarily by a DHCP server and may change
Static IPs are free; dynamic IPs need a subscription
exp:
A static IP is manually fixed; a dynamic IP is leased by DHCP and can change.
★ Exam Points:
• Servers usually use static IPs.
• DHCP = Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol.
• Home routers assign dynamic private IPs.

q: Which term refers to a company that provides Internet access, typically for a fee?
exp:
An Internet Service Provider (ISP) supplies Internet connectivity to users.
★ Exam Points:
• Examples: Jio, Airtel, BSNL, ACT.
• ISPs assign IP addresses.
• Tier-1 ISPs form the Internet backbone.

q: Which Internet access technology is the most viable option for users in geographically isolated or remote rural areas?
exp:
Satellite Internet needs no ground cables, so it can reach remote areas where laying cables is not feasible.
★ Exam Points:
• Low-earth-orbit services: Starlink, OneWeb.
• Higher latency for geostationary satellites.
• BharatNet aims to give fibre to all gram panchayats.

q: Why would a web server hosting a large public website be assigned a static IP address?
o: Static IPs can only be used by servers
A static IP never changes, so the domain always points to the same reliable location
exp:
DNS records map the domain to a fixed address; a static IP ensures the site is always reachable at that address.
★ Exam Points:
• Dynamic IPs are assigned by DHCP and may change.
• Home users usually get dynamic IPs.
• DNS converts domain names to IP addresses.

q: Which fundamental Internet service translates human-readable website names (like google.com) into numerical IP addresses?
exp:
The Domain Name System resolves domain names into IP addresses.
★ Exam Points:
• DNS uses port 53.
• Public DNS: 8.8.8.8 (Google), 1.1.1.1 (Cloudflare).
• DNS is like a phonebook of the Internet.

q: What is the full form of ARPANET?
exp:
ARPANET – Advanced Research Projects Agency Network – started by the US DoD in 1969 and was the forerunner of the Internet.
★ Exam Points:
• First message sent on 29 Oct 1969 (UCLA to SRI).
• Adopted TCP/IP on 1 January 1983.
• Decommissioned in 1990.

q: ____ is a network protocol used on the Internet or LANs to provide a bidirectional interactive text-based communication facility (remote login).
exp:
Telnet provides interactive remote terminal access using TCP port 23.
★ Exam Points:
• Telnet is unencrypted; SSH (port 22) is secure.
• Used for remote administration.
• Developed in 1969.

q: What is DNS?
o: A system that translates domain names into IP addresses
exp:
DNS (Domain Name System) converts names like ssc.gov.in into IP addresses.
★ Exam Points:
• Root servers are at the top of DNS hierarchy.
• DNS cache speeds up lookups.
• Developed by Paul Mockapetris (1983).

q: ____ is the main protocol suite for Internet communication.
exp:
TCP/IP is the core protocol suite on which the Internet runs.
★ Exam Points:
• TCP – reliable delivery; IP – addressing/routing.
• Adopted by ARPANET on 1 Jan 1983.
• Vint Cerf is called a "father of the Internet".

q: ____ is a company that provides web access to both businesses and consumers.
exp:
An ISP provides Internet connectivity to homes and businesses.
★ Exam Points:
• India’s first ISP: VSNL (1995).
• ISPs provide e-mail/hosting too.
• Broadband, fibre, mobile data are ISP services.

q: Why would a web server that hosts a large, public website be assigned a Static IP address instead of a Dynamic one?
o: Because a Static IP address can only be used by server hardware, not by client devices.
A static IP never changes, so the domain always points to the same reliable location.
Because Dynamic IPs are inherently slower and lack the necessary security protocols for handling website traffic.
Because Static IPs use less bandwidth than Dynamic IPs.
exp:
Public web servers use a Static IP address because a static IP never changes, ensuring DNS records for the domain always resolve reliably to the exact same server location without interruption.
★ Exam Points:
• Home/mobile client devices typically receive temporary Dynamic IP addresses automatically from a DHCP (Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol) server.
• Static IPs are essential for hosting web servers, mail servers, DNS servers, and VPN gateways.

q: Which of the following describes the difference between a Static IP address and a Dynamic IP address?
o: Static IPs are used in the US, Dynamic IPs are assigned temporarily by a DHCP server and may change
Static IPs change frequently, Dynamic IPs remain the same
Static IPs remain the same, Dynamic IPs are assigned temporarily by a DHCP server and may change
Static IPs are free, Dynamic IPs require a subscription.
exp:
A Static IP address remains fixed permanently until manually reconfigured by an administrator, whereas a Dynamic IP address is leased temporarily by a DHCP (Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol) server and can change upon recon-nection or lease expiry.
★ Exam Points:
• DHCP operates over UDP ports 67 (server) and 68 (client) using the DORA process (Discover, Offer, Request, Acknowledge).

q: __________ is a network protocol used on the Internet or local area networks to provide a bidirectional interactive communications facility.
exp:
Telnet (Teletype Network) is an application-layer TCP/IP protocol (using TCP Port 23) that provides a bidirectional, interactive text-oriented terminal session to remotely log into another computer over a LAN or the Internet.
★ Exam Points:
• Security note: Because Telnet transmits usernames, passwords, and commands in unencrypted plain text, modern administration replaces Telnet with encrypted SSH (Secure Shell – Port 22).

q: ________ protocol is the main protocol for Internet communication.
exp:
TCP/IP (Transmission Control Protocol / Internet Protocol) is the foundational communication protocol suite of the Internet—IP handles addressing and packet routing across networks, while TCP ensures reliable, ordered, error-checked delivery of data packets.
★ Exam Points:
• OSI is a conceptual 7-layer reference model (not a live Internet protocol); POP3 is specifically for email retrieval; and UDP is connectionless transport.

q: In ________ communication, the two computers begin by establishing a connection via an automated process called a 'handshake.'
exp:
TCP (Transmission Control Protocol) is a connection-oriented Layer-4 protocol in which the client and server first establish a reliable session via an automated Three-Way Handshake (SYN → SYN-ACK → ACK) before transmitting application data.
★ Exam Points:
• By contrast, UDP (User Datagram Protocol) is connectionless—it sends datagrams directly with zero handshake overhead.

q: Which description best defines the Internet?
o: A single powerful computer owned by one company
A worldwide network of interconnected computers and devices that communicate using standard protocols
A private network inside one building
exp:
The Internet is a global network of networks using TCP/IP.
★ Exam Points:
• No single owner controls the Internet.
• Intranet is private.
• WWW is a service on the Internet.

q: The Internet is a group of interconnected computers across the globe. The Internet itself is a type of ____.
exp:
The Internet spans the world, so it is the largest Wide Area Network.
★ Exam Points:
• LAN – building; MAN – city; WAN – country/world.
• WAN links use leased lines, satellites, fibre.
• Internet uses TCP/IP.

q: The rules governing the sending, travelling and receiving of information on the Internet are called ____.
exp:
Protocols are standard rules for communication, such as TCP/IP, HTTP, SMTP.
★ Exam Points:
• TCP/IP is the core Internet protocol suite.
• HTTP – web; SMTP – mail; FTP – files.
• Protocols ensure interoperability.

q: A MODEM is used to connect a computer to the Internet. MODEM stands for ____.
exp:
A modem modulates digital signals into analog for transmission and demodulates incoming analog signals back to digital.
★ Exam Points:
• Modem speed is measured in bps.
• Dial-up modems max 56 kbps.
• DSL and cable modems are broadband modems.

q: Which of the following is a method of accessing fixed Internet for a home or office?
exp:
DSL provides fixed-line broadband over telephone wires to a home or office.
★ Exam Points:
• Other fixed methods: cable, fibre (FTTH).
• Mobile broadband uses cellular networks.
• ADSL is the common home DSL.

q: In dotted-decimal notation, IPv4 addresses are written using exactly ____ dot (.) symbols.
exp:
An IPv4 address has four octets separated by three dots, e.g. 192.168.1.1.
★ Exam Points:
• IPv4 = 32 bits; each octet 0–255.
• IPv6 = 128 bits written in hexadecimal with colons.
• 127.0.0.1 is the loopback address.

q: Which type of Internet service does NOT require cable or phone lines?
exp:
Satellite Internet uses a dish to communicate with satellites, so no ground cable or phone line is required.
★ Exam Points:
• Examples: Starlink, OneWeb, HughesNet.
• Higher latency for geostationary satellites.
• DSL and dial-up use phone lines.

q: An Ethernet card is a network adapter used to set up a wired network. It is also known as a ____.
exp:
An Ethernet card is a Network Interface Card (NIC); each NIC has a unique 48-bit MAC address.
★ Exam Points:
• NIC works at Physical and Data Link layers.
• RJ-45 connector is used for Ethernet cables.
• Wireless NIC = Wi-Fi adapter.

q: An IPv4 address is of ____ bits.
exp:
IPv4 addresses are 32 bits long (about 4.3 billion addresses).
★ Exam Points:
• IPv6 is 128 bits.
• MAC address is 48 bits.
• IPv4 classes: A, B, C, D (multicast), E (experimental).

q: Which is the slowest type of Internet service?
exp:
Dial-up is limited to about 56 kbps, the slowest among common Internet connections.
★ Exam Points:
• DSL and fibre are broadband.
• 4G offers up to 100 Mbps+; 5G much faster.
• Dial-up ties up the phone line.

q: Hathway is a/an ____.
exp:
Hathway is an Indian cable broadband Internet service provider.
★ Exam Points:
• Other Indian ISPs: BSNL, Jio, Airtel, ACT Fibernet.
• ISP provides access to the Internet.
• TRAI regulates telecom in India.

q: ____ is a global communication system that links together thousands of individual networks.
exp:
The Internet is a worldwide network of networks using TCP/IP.
★ Exam Points:
• Intranet is a private network within an organisation.
• Extranet gives partners limited access to an intranet.
• Internet originated from ARPANET (1969).

q: Every computer connected to the Internet needs an IP address. What is the full form of IP?
exp:
IP = Internet Protocol, which addresses and routes packets across networks.
★ Exam Points:
• IPv4 – 32 bit; IPv6 – 128 bit.
• IP works at the Network layer.
• DHCP assigns IP addresses automatically.

q: Which of the following is NOT a method of Internet access?
exp:
"Coolspot" is not a real Internet access method; broadband, wireless and Wi-Fi hotspots are.
★ Exam Points:
• Hotspot = place offering Wi-Fi access.
• Mobile hotspot shares phone data.
• Other methods: dial-up, DSL, fibre, satellite.

q: FTP stands for ____.
exp:
FTP – File Transfer Protocol – is used to transfer files between client and server.
★ Exam Points:
• FTP uses ports 20 and 21.
• SFTP/FTPS are secure versions.
• FileZilla is a popular FTP client.

q: Which type of ISP provides access to the Internet through telephone line, cable, Wi-Fi or fibre optics?
exp:
Access providers give users the actual connection to the Internet over various media.
★ Exam Points:
• Mailbox providers host e-mail.
• Hosting ISPs host websites/servers.
• Virtual ISPs resell another ISP’s services.

q: In what situation is FTP more suitable than HTTP/HTTPS?
o: Uploading and downloading large sets of files to and from a remote file server
exp:
FTP is designed for bulk file transfer and managing files on remote servers.
★ Exam Points:
• Common for website file uploads.
• SFTP adds security.
• HTTP is optimised for web pages.

q: What does the letter ‘D’ stand for in ISDN?
exp:
ISDN = Integrated Services Digital Network – digital transmission of voice and data over telephone lines.
★ Exam Points:
• Basic Rate Interface (BRI) = 2B + D channels (128 kbps data).
• ISDN is circuit-switched.
• DSL replaced ISDN for broadband.

q: Which Internet connection type uses conventional telephone lines to provide Internet access?
exp:
Dial-up uses a modem over the public telephone line (PSTN), with speeds up to 56 kbps.
★ Exam Points:
• DSL also uses telephone lines but at broadband speed.
• Cable Internet uses TV coaxial cable.
• VSNL started public Internet in India on 15 Aug 1995 (dial-up).

q:
Identify whether the statements are true or false.
(i) ADSL and SDSL are types of DSL transmission technologies.
(ii) Internet Information Server (IIS) is a high-performance web server from Microsoft.
(iii) A web server is a computer where web content is stored.
exp:
All three statements are correct.
★ Exam Points:
• ADSL – faster download than upload; SDSL – equal speeds.
• IIS now stands for Internet Information Services.
• Apache and Nginx are popular open-source web servers.

q: What is the full form of LAN?
exp:
LAN – Local Area Network – connects computers within a room, building or campus.
★ Exam Points:
• Ethernet (IEEE 802.3) is the common LAN technology.
• MAN covers a city; WAN covers a country/world.
• PAN – Personal Area Network (about 10 m).

q: What is the function of the keyboard shortcut Ctrl + Tab?
exp:
Ctrl + Tab switches between open tabs.
★ Exam Points:
• Ctrl + Tab switches tabs in browsers and Office dialogs.
• Alt + Tab switches applications.
• Ctrl + 1–8 jump to specific tabs.

q: In most web browsers, when multiple tabs are open in a web browser, pressing Ctrl + Tab performs which action?
o: Navigates to the previous tab on the left
Navigates to the next tab on the right
exp:
Ctrl + Tab moves to the next tab on the right.
★ Exam Points:
• Ctrl + Tab – next tab; Ctrl + Shift + Tab – previous tab.
• Ctrl + T – new tab; Ctrl + W – close tab.
• Ctrl + Shift + T reopens closed tab.

q: A student wants to locate a word inside a PDF. Which shortcut helps?
exp:
Ctrl + F opens find, so you can locate a word in a PDF.
★ Exam Points:
• Ctrl + F – find in PDFs and web pages.
• Adobe Reader supports advanced search (Ctrl + Shift + F).
• Ctrl + C copies.

q: Which of the following is the function of Ctrl + Shift + V in certain applications like Google Docs or web browsers?
o: Opens the Find and Replace dialog box
Reverts to the previous page in the browser
Saves the document as a new file
exp:
Ctrl + Shift + V pastes content without formatting.
★ Exam Points:
• Ctrl + Shift + V – paste as plain text.
• Works in Chrome, Google Docs.
• Word: Paste → Keep Text Only.

q: In applications with multiple tabs (like browsers or MS Word), what does Ctrl + Tab do?
exp:
Ctrl + Tab switches to the next tab.
★ Exam Points:
• Ctrl + Tab – next tab.
• Ctrl + Shift + Tab – previous tab.
• Ctrl + W – close tab.

q: What does the keyboard shortcut Ctrl + R do in web browsers?
exp:
Ctrl + R reloads (refreshes) the current page in most browsers.
★ Exam Points:
• Ctrl + R / F5 – reload page.
• Ctrl + Shift + R – hard reload.
• In Word, Ctrl + R right-aligns text.

q: Which of the following is NOT a standard protocol used for retrieval or transmission of e-mails?
exp:
SNMP (Simple Network Management Protocol) manages network devices; it is not an e-mail protocol.
★ Exam Points:
• SMTP sends mail.
• POP3/IMAP retrieve mail.
• SNMP uses UDP ports 161/162.

q: In a multipart e-mail message, what does the boundary parameter in the Content-Type header do?
o: It limits the size of each attachment
It defines the length of the message
It marks the start and end of each part in a multipart message
exp:
In MIME multipart messages the boundary string separates each part (body, attachments).
★ Exam Points:
• MIME – Multipurpose Internet Mail Extensions.
• MIME allows attachments and non-ASCII text.
• Content-Type example: multipart/mixed.

q: Which action can typically be performed in the Outbox?
o: Editing e-mails that are yet to be sent
exp:
The Outbox holds messages waiting to be sent; they can still be opened and edited before sending.
★ Exam Points:
• Messages wait in Outbox when offline.
• Sent Items stores sent mail.
• Drafts stores incomplete mail.

q: Which of the following best describes Electronic Mail (E-mail)?
o: A system for storing digital files on the cloud
A service used to make phone calls over the Internet
A method of sending messages electronically over a computer network
exp:
E-mail is a method of exchanging digital messages through computer networks.
★ Exam Points:
• Uses SMTP, POP3, IMAP.
• VoIP is for Internet calls.
• Cloud storage examples: Google Drive, OneDrive.

q: Which technology allows real-time voice and video communication over the Internet using only a web browser, without extra software?
exp:
WebRTC (Web Real-Time Communication) is built into browsers and enables audio/video calls directly in the browser.
★ Exam Points:
• Google Meet uses WebRTC.
• VoIP generally needs an app or device.
• WebRTC is an open standard by W3C/IETF.

q: In Microsoft Outlook, which action sends a received e-mail to another person while keeping the original message?
o: Use Archive and create a new e-mail
Click Reply and add the new recipient
Open the e-mail, click Forward and enter the recipient's address
Click Reply All and select Forward
exp:
Forward sends a copy of the received message (with attachments) to new recipients; the original stays in your mailbox.
★ Exam Points:
• Outlook Forward shortcut: Ctrl + F.
• Reply: Ctrl + R; Reply All: Ctrl + Shift + R.
• Forwarded subject starts with "FW:".

q: ____ was the first browser to display images inline with text instead of in a separate window.
exp:
NCSA Mosaic (1993), developed by Marc Andreessen and Eric Bina, was the first popular graphical browser to show images inline.
★ Exam Points:
• First web browser: WorldWideWeb (later Nexus) by Tim Berners-Lee, 1990.
• Lynx is a text-only browser.
• Netscape Navigator was developed by Mosaic’s creators.

q: Which of the following is a web browser created and developed by Microsoft?
exp:
Microsoft Edge (2015) replaced Internet Explorer; since 2020 it is based on Chromium.
★ Exam Points:
• Internet Explorer support ended on 15 June 2022.
• Chrome – Google (2008); Firefox – Mozilla; Safari – Apple.
• Opera originated in Norway; Brave was founded by Brendan Eich.

q: Which folder is used to store deleted e-mails?
exp:
Deleted e-mails go to the Trash (Bin/Deleted Items) folder, where Gmail keeps them for 30 days.
★ Exam Points:
• Spam folder holds suspected junk mail.
• Drafts holds unsent messages being written.
• Outbox holds messages waiting to be sent.

q: Which among the following statements is incorrect?
o: Uploading is a procedure for copying data from the device to the web server.
Downloading is a procedure for copying files from the web server to the machine.
Data travels from the user’s device to the web server while uploading.
Memory is required in the web server for downloading anything.
exp:
Downloading stores the file on the user’s own device, so storage is required on the user’s machine, not on the web server.
★ Exam Points:
• Upload = local → remote; Download = remote → local.
• FTP and HTTP are used for file transfer.
• Peer-to-peer (BitTorrent) downloads from many peers.

q: In Gmail, what do you use when you receive a mail and want to send a response to the same mail to the original sender only?
exp:
Reply sends the response only to the original sender, whereas Reply All also sends it to all other recipients in To and Cc.
★ Exam Points:
• Forward sends the received mail to a new recipient.
• Bcc recipients do not receive Reply All responses.
• Subject of a reply starts with "Re:"; forward with "Fwd:".

q: Which keyboard shortcut is used to bookmark the current web page in a web browser?
exp:
Ctrl + D adds the current page to bookmarks/favourites in Chrome, Edge and Firefox.
★ Exam Points:
• Ctrl + H opens History; Ctrl + J opens Downloads.
• Ctrl + Shift + B shows/hides the bookmarks bar.
• Ctrl + Shift + T reopens the last closed tab.

q: Which of the following options can be pressed to create a new e-mail message in Gmail?
exp:
The Compose button opens a new message window in Gmail.
★ Exam Points:
• Gmail keyboard shortcut for compose: C (when shortcuts are on).
• Drafts store unsent messages.
• Gmail was launched on 1 April 2004.

q: In a web browser, which of the following is responsible for displaying web pages?
exp:
The rendering (layout) engine interprets HTML and CSS and draws the web page on the screen.
★ Exam Points:
• Chrome/Edge use Blink; Firefox uses Gecko; Safari uses WebKit.
• JavaScript engine (e.g., V8) runs scripts.
• Search engines (Google, Bing) find web pages.

q: Some cookies are automatically recreated after a user has deleted them. These are called ____ cookies.
exp:
Zombie cookies are restored from backup storage (e.g., Flash/local storage) even after deletion, so they "come back to life".
★ Exam Points:
• Session cookies are deleted when the browser closes.
• Persistent cookies remain until their expiry date.
• Third-party cookies are set by domains other than the site visited (used for ads/tracking).

q:
Which of the following is NOT an example of an e-mail service provider?
I. Outlook
II. Gmail
III. Yahoo Mail
exp:
Outlook (Microsoft), Gmail (Google) and Yahoo Mail are all web-based e-mail service providers.
★ Exam Points:
• Gmail was launched by Google in 2004; Hotmail (1996) became Outlook.com.
• Other providers: Rediffmail, Zoho Mail, ProtonMail, iCloud Mail.
• E-mail client = program to read mail (Outlook, Thunderbird).

q: Which keyboard shortcut is used to reload the current page in a web browser (e.g., Google Chrome)?
exp:
F5 (or Ctrl + R) refreshes/reloads the current web page.
★ Exam Points:
• Ctrl + F5 / Ctrl + Shift + R = hard reload ignoring the cache.
• F3 / Ctrl + F finds text on the page.
• F11 toggles full-screen mode.

q: While ____, data transfers from the customer’s machine to the server.
exp:
Uploading copies data from the user’s device to a remote server; downloading copies data from the server to the user’s device.
★ Exam Points:
• Upload speed is usually lower than download speed on home broadband (asymmetric).
• FTP is a protocol used for uploading/downloading files.
• Speeds are measured in Mbps (megabits per second).

q: In networking, protocols define the rules for communication between devices. Which protocol is most commonly used for web communication?
exp:
HTTP (Hypertext Transfer Protocol) is the foundational application-layer client-server protocol of the World Wide Web used by web browsers and web servers to request and transmit web pages.
★ Exam Points:
• Feature | HTTP | HTTPS
• Port | Port 80 | Port 443
• Security | Plain-text (unencrypted) | Encrypted using SSL / TLS
• Use Case | Basic informational pages | Banking, logins, payments, modern web
• FTP (Ports 20/21) transfers files; SMTP (Port 25/587) sends emails; POP3 (Port 110/995) downloads emails.

q: Which of the following is NOT an e-mail service provider?
exp:
Adobe is a software company (Photoshop, Acrobat), not an e-mail provider.
★ Exam Points:
• Proton Mail is an encrypted e-mail service (Switzerland).
• GMX is a German provider.
• Outlook.com is Microsoft's.

q: What happens when we enter someone's e-mail address in the “Bcc” field?
o: Their address is visible only to To recipients
Visible only to other Bcc recipients
The recipient receives a copy, but their address is hidden from all other recipients
exp:
Bcc recipients are invisible to everyone else.
★ Exam Points:
• Bcc = Blind Carbon Copy.
• Used for privacy in group mails.
• Sender can see Bcc list in Sent mail.

q: ____ is the principle on which web page editors (visual editors) work.
exp:
WYSIWYG – What You See Is What You Get – shows the page while editing as it will appear in the browser.
★ Exam Points:
• Dreamweaver Design view is WYSIWYG.
• Word processors are WYSIWYG.
• Code editors show source code.

q: Which of the following is used by search engines to collect and index information from websites?
exp:
Crawlers automatically visit pages and follow links to gather content for the search index.
★ Exam Points:
• Googlebot is Google's crawler.
• robots.txt guides crawlers.
• Sitemaps help indexing.

q: In professional e-mails, which writing style is generally considered rude and should be avoided?
o: Using bold to highlight key information
Using ALL CAPS for the entire e-mail
exp:
Writing in all capital letters is perceived as shouting and is poor netiquette.
★ Exam Points:
• Use sentence case for e-mails.
• Bold sparingly for key points.
• Keep paragraphs short.

q: For which purpose can the “Bcc” field be used?
o: So that Reply All from one Bcc recipient reaches all others
To maintain client privacy while sending newsletters or updates to a large group
To ensure full transparency of recipients
exp:
Bcc hides recipients' addresses from one another, protecting privacy in bulk mails.
★ Exam Points:
• Bcc recipients don't see each other.
• Reduces reply-all storms.
• Prevents address harvesting.

q: Which service allows instant money transfer using a mobile number (MMID)?
exp:
IMPS enables instant 24×7 transfers using mobile number + MMID or account number + IFSC.
★ Exam Points:
• Launched by NPCI in 2010.
• UPI uses VPA/mobile number too.
• NEFT works in batches.

q: What is the primary function of a search engine?
o: To retrieve information from the web
exp:
Search engines index the web and return relevant results for user queries.
★ Exam Points:
• Examples: Google, Bing, DuckDuckGo.
• Search results pages = SERP.
• Images and news can also be searched.

q: Which of the following is NOT required for Internet banking?
exp:
Net banking needs an account, Internet and login credentials; card PIN is used at ATMs/POS, not for logging in.
★ Exam Points:
• Transaction password/OTP is used for transfers.
• Never share login details.
• Use official bank URLs.

q: What does the CSS z-index property control?
exp:
z-index decides which positioned element appears on top when elements overlap.
★ Exam Points:
• Higher z-index = closer to viewer.
• Works on positioned elements.
• Used for pop-ups and menus.

q: What is the main purpose of a clear and concise subject line in an e-mail?
o: To help the recipient quickly grasp the content and prioritise
exp:
A good subject line summarises the purpose so the recipient knows what the mail is about.
★ Exam Points:
• Keep it short and specific.
• Avoid all caps.
• Blank subjects may look like spam.

q:
Arrange the steps for sending an e-mail in logical order.
(i) Click Compose (ii) Log in to your account (iii) Enter recipient, subject and text (iv) Click Send
exp:
Log in first, click Compose, fill details, then Send.
★ Exam Points:
• Attach files before sending.
• Undo Send available briefly in Gmail.
• Check recipient address carefully.

q: Which accurately defines a CDN (Content Delivery Network)?
o: A system that delivers content only from central servers
A geographically distributed group of servers that caches content close to end users
exp:
CDNs store copies of content on edge servers worldwide to deliver it faster.
★ Exam Points:
• Examples: Cloudflare, Akamai.
• Reduces latency and server load.
• Helps absorb DDoS attacks.

q: What typically causes an "e-mail storm"?
o: A cyber-attack from a single source
An e-mail to a distribution list followed by a chain reaction of unnecessary "Reply All" responses
exp:
E-mail storms (reply-all storms) occur when many recipients of a group mail keep replying to all.
★ Exam Points:
• Use Bcc for large lists.
• Avoid unnecessary Reply All.
• Can overload mail servers.

q: Which one of the following is an instant messaging system?
exp:
WhatsApp is an instant messaging app; Gmail and Yahoo Mail are e-mail services and Bing is a search engine.
★ Exam Points:
• Other IM apps: Telegram, Signal.
• IM is real-time; e-mail is asynchronous.
• WhatsApp is owned by Meta.

q: What is the method to render text in bold using CSS?
exp:
In CSS, the font-weight property (bold or 700) makes text bold.
★ Exam Points:
• font-style: italic makes text italic.
• text-decoration: underline underlines.
• CSS = Cascading Style Sheets.

q:
When you forward a message, which parts of the original are typically included by default?
(i) Original subject (ii) Original body text (iii) Original attachments (iv) All original recipients
exp:
Forward keeps subject (with Fwd:), body and attachments, but you must enter new recipients.
★ Exam Points:
• Original header info is shown in the body.
• Reply does not include attachments.
• Forward as attachment is also possible.

q: Regarding the username part of an e-mail address, most modern e-mail systems treat case as ____.
o: case-insensitive – JohnDoe@ and johndoe@ reach the same inbox
sensitive only to the first letter
exp:
Major providers treat usernames as case-insensitive, so capitalisation does not matter.
★ Exam Points:
• Domain names are always case-insensitive.
• Gmail also ignores dots in usernames.
• Passwords, however, are case-sensitive.

q: The part of the Internet that is not indexed by search engines and needs special software (like Tor) to access is called the ____.
exp:
The Dark Web is a hidden part of the Deep Web, accessible only through anonymising networks like Tor.
★ Exam Points:
• Deep Web = all unindexed content (e-mails, banking pages).
• Surface Web = indexed by search engines.
• .onion sites are on Tor.

q: Which best explains why keywords are important in search engines?
o: They help match user queries with indexed pages
exp:
Search engines match the keywords in a query with words in their index to find relevant pages.
★ Exam Points:
• SEO uses relevant keywords.
• Long-tail keywords are specific phrases.
• Search operators refine keyword search.

q: What is the purpose of the viewport meta tag in responsive web design?
o: It specifies how a website should be displayed on different devices
exp:
<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"> makes pages scale properly on mobiles.
★ Exam Points:
• Responsive design uses CSS media queries.
• charset meta tag sets encoding.
• Mobile-first design is common today.

q: When you use Reply on an e-mail message, who receives your response?
o: Only the individual who originally sent the message
exp:
Reply sends your response only to the original sender.
★ Exam Points:
• Reply All includes To and Cc recipients.
• Forward goes to new people.
• Outlook Reply: Ctrl + R.

q: What is the default font size in most web browsers?
exp:
Browsers use 16px as the default base font size (1em = 16px).
★ Exam Points:
• rem units are relative to the root font size.
• Users can change default size.
• Zoom does not change default size.

q: What is the primary function of the “Forward” feature in e-mail?
o: To reply only to the sender
To reply only to Cc recipients
To send the entire original e-mail to a completely new recipient
To move the message to Archive
exp:
Forward sends the original message (with attachments) to new recipients.
★ Exam Points:
• Subject prefix: Fwd/FW.
• You can add your own note above.
• Attachments are included by default.

q: Which software is used to build websites?
exp:
Adobe Dreamweaver is a web development tool with code and design (WYSIWYG) views.
★ Exam Points:
• Other tools: WordPress, VS Code, Wix.
• ERP manages business processes.
• Tally is accounting software.

q: In web communication, what is the significance of HTTP?
o: It defines how web browsers fetch web pages from servers
exp:
HTTP defines the request–response rules browsers and servers use to transfer web pages.
★ Exam Points:
• Methods: GET, POST, PUT, DELETE.
• Encryption is added by HTTPS.
• DHCP assigns IP addresses.

q: You are in the To field with two others, and five people are in Cc. When you click ‘Reply All’, who receives your message?
o: Only the sender and the other To recipients
The original sender and the other recipients in both To and Cc
exp:
Reply All goes to the sender plus all visible To and Cc recipients (not Bcc).
★ Exam Points:
• Bcc addresses are never revealed.
• Overusing Reply All causes "e-mail storms".
• Your own address is excluded.

q: Which of the following is NOT required to send an e-mail?
exp:
You only need a connection, your account and the recipient's e-mail address; mail servers handle IP routing.
★ Exam Points:
• DNS MX records locate the recipient's mail server.
• Users never need IP addresses for e-mail.
• SMTP relays mail between servers.

q:
Which of the following are typically required on an e-mail account creation page?
(i) First name (ii) Last name (iii) Username (iv) Bank account number (v) Password
exp:
Sign-up asks for name, desired username and password; bank account details are never needed.
★ Exam Points:
• Recovery phone/e-mail is often asked.
• Choose a strong password.
• Never share bank details for e-mail sign-up.

q: Which HTML element is used for the highest level of heading?
exp:
HTML has six heading levels; <h1> is the most important (largest) and <h6> the least.
★ Exam Points:
• <title> sets the browser tab title.
• <header> is a page section element.
• Search engines value h1 tags.

q:
Which information is appropriate in a professional e-mail signature?
(i) Your name and job title
(ii) Your latest passport-size photograph
(iii) Your company's logo and tagline
(iv) Your company's name and contact numbers
exp:
A professional signature includes name, title, company logo and contact details; a personal photograph is generally not needed.
★ Exam Points:
• Keep signatures short.
• Avoid large images.
• Include official website link.

q: Which of the following is a benefit of e-banking?
o: Requires physical presence at the bank
exp:
E-banking services are available round the clock from anywhere.
★ Exam Points:
• Includes net banking, mobile banking, UPI.
• Saves time and travel.
• Secure with OTP and passwords.

q: Which statement is TRUE about a “read receipt”?
o: Recipients always have the option to decline sending a read receipt
All systems send it without consent
It guarantees the recipient understood the mail
exp:
Most mail clients ask the recipient whether to send a read receipt; it can be declined.
★ Exam Points:
• Not all services support read receipts.
• It does not prove understanding.
• Outlook: Options → Request a Read Receipt.

q: ____ is the organisation that oversees the development of web technologies and standards.
exp:
The W3C, founded by Tim Berners-Lee in 1994, develops web standards like HTML and CSS.
★ Exam Points:
• ICANN manages domain names and IP addresses.
• IETF develops Internet protocols.
• W3C is hosted by MIT, ERCIM, Keio, Beihang.

q: In a URL, “http” is followed by ____ and ____.
exp:
The scheme is followed by :// as in http://www.example.com.
★ Exam Points:
• Backslashes are used in Windows file paths.
• Browsers often hide http(s)://.
• https:// for secure sites.

q: Which statement about video conferencing and chat is most accurate?
o: Video conferencing is asynchronous while chat is real-time
Both bypass the need for an ISP
Both enable real-time communication; video conferencing adds audio and video streams while chat is mainly text
exp:
Both are synchronous (real-time) services; video conferencing carries audio-visual streams, chat carries text messages.
★ Exam Points:
• E-mail is asynchronous.
• Both need Internet connectivity.
• Platforms often combine both.

q: What does ‘RTGS’ stand for?
exp:
RTGS – Real Time Gross Settlement – settles each high-value transaction individually and instantly.
★ Exam Points:
• Minimum amount ₹2 lakh; no upper limit.
• 24×7 since 14 Dec 2020.
• Operated by RBI.

q: Which of the following is an example of a meta-search engine?
exp:
A meta-search engine (e.g., Dogpile, MetaCrawler) sends a query to several search engines and combines the results.
★ Exam Points:
• Google and Bing maintain their own indexes.
• Meta-search engines have no own index.
• DuckDuckGo uses Bing results among others.

q: What is the primary purpose of electronic mail?
exp:
E-mail is mainly used to send and receive digital messages and attachments.
★ Exam Points:
• E-mail address format: user@domain.
• Works store-and-forward.
• Mailbox stores incoming mails.

q:
Which of the following can the last part (domain) of an e-mail address be?
(i) Username (ii) Company domain name (iii) Website name (iv) E-mail service provider name
exp:
The part after @ is a domain – it may be a company domain, a website’s domain or an e-mail provider (gmail.com); the username is the first part.
★ Exam Points:
• Custom domains are used by businesses.
• Example: info@aimersqila.com.
• Domain must exist in DNS (MX record).

q: The Internet domain ‘.edu’ is used for ____.
exp:
.edu is a sponsored top-level domain for accredited educational institutions (mainly in the US).
★ Exam Points:
• India uses .ac.in and .edu.in.
• .gov – government; .com – commercial.
• .net – network providers.

q: Identify the correct structure of a URL.
exp:
A URL is written as protocol://domain/path, e.g., https://www.ssc.gov.in/notices.
★ Exam Points:
• Protocol examples: http, https, ftp.
• Port can follow domain (:8080).
• Query string starts with ?.

q: Which statement best explains what a URL is mainly used for?
o: It is software to view web pages
It specifies the unique address of a resource on the World Wide Web
It is a protocol for secure transfer
It is another name for homepage
exp:
A URL tells the browser exactly where a resource is located on the web.
★ Exam Points:
• Browser is the software.
• HTTPS is the secure protocol.
• Homepage is the main page.

q: What is the main function of "starring" or "flagging" an e-mail?
o: To mark it as important and needing action
exp:
Stars/flags highlight important mails for follow-up.
★ Exam Points:
• Gmail: Starred folder.
• Outlook: Follow-up flags.
• Important markers are automatic in Gmail.

q: ____ refers to the design of websites that are displayed on the Internet.
exp:
Web design covers layout, colours, typography and usability of websites.
★ Exam Points:
• Uses HTML, CSS, JavaScript.
• Responsive design adapts to screen size.
• UX focuses on user experience overall.

q: Which of the following lists contains ONLY web browsers?
o: Google Chrome, Mozilla Firefox, Microsoft Edge
exp:
Chrome, Firefox and Edge are browsers; Google, Bing and Yahoo are search engines; others are social/messaging apps.
★ Exam Points:
• Safari and Opera are also browsers.
• Search engines run inside browsers.
• Chrome has the largest share.

q: What does it mean when an e-mail is “queued”?
o: It is placed in the Outbox, waiting in line to be transmitted to the mail server
It has been delivered and waits to be read
exp:
A queued e-mail is waiting in the Outbox to be sent.
★ Exam Points:
• Happens when offline or the server is busy.
• Large attachments may delay sending.
• Gmail shows "Queued" on mobile.

q: In which order are posts usually displayed on a standard blog?
exp:
Blogs show the latest post first, i.e., reverse chronological order.
★ Exam Points:
• Archives group posts by month.
• Tags/categories organise posts.
• RSS feeds deliver new posts.

q: Which statement best characterises a blog?
o: A type of electronic bank transaction
A personal or corporate website, usually maintained by an individual, with regular posts of commentary or events
exp:
A blog is a regularly updated website with posts by an individual or group.
★ Exam Points:
• Blog = web + log.
• Vlog = video blog.
• Microblogging: X (Twitter).

q: What is the purpose of a “read receipt” in e-mail communication?
o: To inform the sender when the mail is delivered
To notify the sender when the recipient has opened/read the e-mail
To ask the receiver to delete the mail
exp:
A read receipt notifies the sender that the message was opened.
★ Exam Points:
• Delivery receipt confirms delivery, not reading.
• Recipient may decline sending it.
• Available in Outlook and Gmail Workspace.

q: Which icon usually represents the "Search" function in e-mail services?
exp:
A magnifying-glass icon universally represents search.
★ Exam Points:
• Paper clip – attachment.
• Gear – settings.
• Star – important/starred mail.

q:
In the URL http:
www.nasa.gov/news/index.html, which component is the Top-Level Domain (TLD)?
exp:
.gov is the top-level domain; nasa is the second-level domain and index.html is the file path.
★ Exam Points:
• http is the protocol.
• www is a subdomain.
• .gov is reserved for US government.

q: Which is an application-layer protocol for transmitting hypermedia documents?
exp:
HTTP transfers hypermedia (HTML pages, images, video) between web servers and browsers.
★ Exam Points:
• HTTP works at the Application layer.
• TCP works at the Transport layer.
• URL is an address, not a protocol.

q: Which of the given options is TRUE?
o: Bcc recipients can view the addresses of To and Cc recipients
To recipients can view the addresses of Bcc recipients
Cc recipients can view the addresses of Bcc recipients
Bcc recipients can view the addresses of other Bcc recipients
exp:
Bcc addresses are hidden from everyone else, but Bcc recipients still see the To and Cc lists.
★ Exam Points:
• Bcc protects recipients' privacy.
• Each Bcc recipient sees only their own address.
• Reply All from Bcc does not include other Bcc.

q: What is the difference between a web browser and a search engine?
o: A browser indexes content; a search engine views it
A browser is for video conferencing; a search engine for e-banking
A browser handles only FTP; a search engine only HTTP
A browser renders pages; a search engine locates them
exp:
A browser (Chrome) displays web pages; a search engine (Google) finds relevant pages from its index.
★ Exam Points:
• Search engines run inside browsers.
• Default search engine can be changed.
• Bing powers Edge search.

q: ____ is the name of the location address of hypertext documents.
exp:
A web address or URL is the location of a hypertext document on the web.
★ Exam Points:
• URL = Uniform Resource Locator.
• Typed in the address bar.
• Hyperlinks point to URLs.

q:
Which could be reasons for an e-mail lying in the Outbox?
(i) The e-mail has been successfully transmitted
(ii) It has a large attachment that is taking time to upload
(iii) The Internet connection is suddenly lost
(iv) There is a problem connecting to the server
exp:
Mail stays in the Outbox when it hasn't been sent yet – due to large uploads, lost connection or server problems; transmitted mail moves to Sent.
★ Exam Points:
• Outbox is common in desktop clients like Outlook.
• Check connection and retry.
• Large attachments should be shared via cloud links.

q: Which of the following is a security benefit of UPI for the user?
o: It provides insurance for every transaction
It is faster than RTGS for high-value transfers
It eliminates the need to share bank account numbers or IFSC codes with the receiver
exp:
UPI uses a Virtual Payment Address (VPA) like name@bank, so account details remain private.
★ Exam Points:
• UPI launched by NPCI on 11 April 2016.
• UPI PIN is a 4/6-digit secret.
• Never enter PIN to receive money.

q: Which technology used for sending and receiving e-mail is widely recognised and essential?
exp:
E-mail relies on the Internet and mail protocols (SMTP, POP3, IMAP).
★ Exam Points:
• E-mail predates the WWW.
• MIME supports attachments.
• Webmail uses HTTP(S) in the browser.

q: What does NEFT stand for in e-banking?
exp:
NEFT – National Electronic Funds Transfer – a nationwide payment system run by RBI.
★ Exam Points:
• Settles in half-hourly batches.
• Available 24×7 since Dec 2019.
• Needs IFSC of beneficiary bank.

q: What happens when we enter someone's e-mail address in the “Cc” field?
o: The recipient receives a copy for their information
The recipient's address is invisible to others
The recipient cannot see the primary recipient's address
exp:
Cc recipients get a copy and all recipients can see their address.
★ Exam Points:
• Cc = Carbon Copy.
• Use Bcc to hide addresses.
• Cc recipients are included in Reply All.

q: Which of the following is an example of an e-banking transaction?
o: Depositing cash at the bank counter
Standing in a queue to update a passbook
exp:
E-banking uses electronic channels like mobile banking, net banking, UPI and ATMs.
★ Exam Points:
• Mobile banking apps: YONO (SBI), iMobile (ICICI).
• Net banking uses user ID and password.
• UPI enables instant transfers.

q: What does ‘protocol’ refer to in e-mail communication?
o: A set of rules for sending and receiving e-mails
exp:
Protocols such as SMTP, POP3 and IMAP define how mail is sent and retrieved.
★ Exam Points:
• SMTP – send.
• POP3 – download.
• IMAP – sync on server.

q: Which of the following is NOT true about the National Electronic Funds Transfer (NEFT) system?
o: It allows electronic transfer of funds between accounts in different banks across India
It operates on a Deferred Net Settlement (DNS) basis in batches
It is regulated by the RBI
It is available only during traditional banking hours
exp:
Since 16 December 2019 NEFT is available 24×7×365, including holidays.
★ Exam Points:
• NEFT settles in half-hourly batches (48 per day).
• No minimum or maximum amount limit.
• Launched by RBI in November 2005.

q: What happens when you click “Move to Inbox” for an archived e-mail?
o: The e-mail reappears in the Inbox
exp:
Archived mail is only hidden from the Inbox; Move to Inbox brings it back.
★ Exam Points:
• Archive keeps mail in All Mail (Gmail).
• Archive ≠ Delete.
• Gmail shortcut to archive: E.

q:
Which of the following would typically qualify as junk or spam e-mail?
(i) A delivery update from a known shopping site
(ii) An e-mail from an unknown sender offering a "free prize"
(iii) An e-mail from your bank about a failed transaction
(iv) An e-mail from your workplace about an event
exp:
Unsolicited "free prize" offers from unknown senders are classic spam (often phishing).
★ Exam Points:
• Never click links in such mails.
• Report as spam/phishing.
• Lottery scams ask for fees or bank details.

q:
If a URL begins with ftp:
instead of http:
, what does this signify?
o: It is an unencrypted text page
It is a server optimised for storing and retrieving (transferring) files
exp:
ftp:// indicates the File Transfer Protocol, used by servers that store and share files.
★ Exam Points:
• FTP uses ports 20 and 21.
• Many browsers have dropped FTP support.
• Use FileZilla/WinSCP for FTP.

q: In what primary way does a blog differ from a static website?
o: Blogs allow frequent updates and user interaction
exp:
Blogs are regularly updated with new posts and usually allow comments, unlike fixed static pages.
★ Exam Points:
• Posts appear in reverse chronological order.
• Blogs use CMS like WordPress.
• RSS feeds notify readers of new posts.

q: Which protocol is mainly used to send e-mails?
exp:
SMTP (Simple Mail Transfer Protocol) sends and relays outgoing mail.
★ Exam Points:
• POP3/IMAP retrieve mail.
• SMTP ports: 25, 587, 465.
• HTTP is for web pages.

q: During a video-conferencing session, which factor has the greatest influence on maintaining clear and uninterrupted audio/video?
exp:
Video calls need sufficient, stable bandwidth; low bandwidth causes lag, freezing and poor quality.
★ Exam Points:
• HD video calls need about 1.5–3 Mbps.
• Latency and jitter also affect quality.
• Wired connections are more stable than Wi-Fi.

q: When we receive an e-mail, which field indicates the sender's e-mail address?
exp:
The From field shows who sent the e-mail.
★ Exam Points:
• To – main recipient.
• Cc – visible copy; Bcc – hidden copy.
• Reply-To can redirect replies.

q: Which of the following is a popular free platform specifically used for creating blogs?
exp:
WordPress (2003) is a free, open-source content management system widely used for blogs and websites.
★ Exam Points:
• Blogger is Google’s blogging platform.
• WordPress is written in PHP.
• Medium is another blogging platform.

q: Which of the following is TRUE about URLs?
o: They uniquely identify resources on the Internet
They are used only for images
exp:
A URL is the unique address of a resource (web page, image, file) on the Internet.
★ Exam Points:
• Many URLs do not use www.
• Structure: protocol://domain/path.
• URL coined by Tim Berners-Lee (1994 RFC).

q: In an e-mail window, which field is mandatory to send an e-mail?
exp:
An e-mail needs at least one recipient address (normally in To) to be sent; Subject and attachments are optional.
★ Exam Points:
• Gmail warns if the subject is empty.
• Recipients can also be only in Cc/Bcc.
• Multiple addresses are separated by commas.

q: In a video conference, what is the function of the ‘Screen Sharing’ feature?
o: It records the video to your hard drive
It allows other participants to see the content displayed on your monitor
It turns off your camera to save data
exp:
Screen sharing broadcasts your screen (or a window) to all participants.
★ Exam Points:
• Used for presentations and demos.
• Recording is a separate feature.
• Available in Meet, Zoom, Teams.

q: To transfer a high-value amount of ₹5,00,000 instantly to another bank account, which electronic fund transfer system is most appropriate?
exp:
RTGS settles high-value transactions (minimum ₹2 lakh) individually in real time.
★ Exam Points:
• RTGS is available 24×7 since Dec 2020.
• NEFT settles in half-hourly batches.
• IMPS is instant but meant for smaller amounts (limit ₹5 lakh).

q: Which e-mail option helps avoid typing the same message repeatedly?
exp:
E-mail templates (canned responses) store reusable messages.
★ Exam Points:
• Gmail calls them Templates (earlier Canned Responses).
• Signatures add fixed closing text.
• Filters auto-sort incoming mail.

q: What do we call the words or phrases typed into a search engine to find information?
exp:
A search query consists of keywords entered to retrieve relevant results.
★ Exam Points:
• Use quotes for exact phrase search.
• Use minus (-) to exclude words.
• site: limits results to a website.

q:
Which of the following is recommended for effective professional e-mails?
(i) Simple black text and standard fonts
(ii) Use of bold or italics to highlight key text
(iii) A different colour for every sentence
(iv) Fancy, differently sized fonts on each line
exp:
Professional e-mails should be clean and readable; limited bold/italics for emphasis is fine, but many colours or fancy fonts are not.
★ Exam Points:
• Keep a clear subject line.
• Use a proper signature.
• Avoid ALL CAPS.

q: What is the Junk/Spam e-mail filter used for?
o: It moves suspected spam e-mails to a separate folder
It returns junk mail to the sender
It forwards spam to the administrator
exp:
Spam filters detect suspicious mail and move it to the Spam/Junk folder for review.
★ Exam Points:
• Gmail spam auto-deletes after 30 days.
• "Not spam" restores a mail.
• Filters use content and sender reputation.

q: You are writing an important e-mail but need to continue later. In which folder will you find it?
exp:
Unsent, incomplete messages are saved in the Drafts folder.
★ Exam Points:
• Gmail auto-saves drafts.
• Drafts can be edited and sent later.
• Outbox is for mails waiting to send.

q: Which of the following is a feature of mobile banking?
exp:
Mobile banking lets customers bank anytime through apps on smartphones.
★ Exam Points:
• USSD banking (*99#) works without Internet.
• UPI apps are part of mobile banking.
• Secure with MPIN/biometrics.

q: When you delete an e-mail from your Inbox, where is it temporarily moved before being permanently removed?
exp:
Deleted mail goes to Trash/Bin (Deleted Items in Outlook) and can be restored for a period (30 days in Gmail).
★ Exam Points:
• Empty Trash to delete permanently.
• Spam is for unwanted mail.
• Archive keeps mail without deleting.

q: For what application is the HTTP protocol used?
o: To deliver data on the World Wide Web
exp:
HTTP is the foundation of data communication on the Web – browsers request pages and servers respond.
★ Exam Points:
• HTTP is a request–response protocol.
• Status 404 = Not Found; 200 = OK.
• HTTPS is the secure version.

q: Every resource (image, video, web page) on the Internet has a unique address. What is it technically called?
exp:
A URL (Uniform Resource Locator) uniquely locates a resource on the Internet.
★ Exam Points:
• URL parts: scheme, host, path, query.
• Shortened URLs redirect to long ones.
• URL ⊂ URI.

q: Why is an e-mail typically moved to the Archive folder?
o: To store an important e-mail separately for future reference
To store it temporarily before deletion
exp:
Archiving removes mail from the Inbox but keeps it safely for later reference.
★ Exam Points:
• Archive declutters the Inbox.
• Searchable in All Mail.
• Not deleted automatically.

q: If you type ‘best pizza near me’ into the address bar of a modern browser, what happens?
