o: It gives an error because it is not a valid URL
It automatically uses the default search engine to find results
exp:
Modern browsers have an "omnibox": text that is not a URL is sent as a query to the default search engine.
★ Exam Points:
• Chrome calls it the Omnibox.
• Default search engine can be changed in settings.
• Ctrl + L / Alt + D / F6 focus the address bar.

q: Which of the following is an example of a search engine algorithm's role?
o: Ranking web pages based on relevance
exp:
Search algorithms evaluate and rank indexed pages by relevance and quality for each query.
★ Exam Points:
• Google’s original algorithm: PageRank.
• Crawling → Indexing → Ranking.
• SEO aims to improve rankings.

q:
Which statement is TRUE about popular free e-mail services like Gmail and Outlook?
(i) Users can create custom folders or labels.
(ii) Users cannot create custom folders or labels.
(iii) Creating labels increases storage.
(iv) Creating labels decreases storage.
exp:
Users can create folders (Outlook) or labels (Gmail); these do not change the storage quota.
★ Exam Points:
• Gmail free storage: 15 GB (shared with Drive & Photos).
• Filters can auto-apply labels.
• A mail can have multiple Gmail labels.

q: Which of the following is an example of a web hosting (cloud) service?
exp:
Amazon Web Services provides cloud hosting for websites and applications.
★ Exam Points:
• Other hosts: Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud.
• Shared, VPS and dedicated hosting are types.
• MeghRaj is India’s government cloud.

q: A ____ is a single page of information on the World Wide Web.
exp:
A web page is a single document on the web, usually written in HTML.
★ Exam Points:
• A website is a collection of web pages.
• Home page is the first page of a site.
• Pages are linked by hyperlinks.

q: What is an e-mail signature?
o: An image of the handwritten signature
A block of text added to outgoing e-mails, usually with the sender's contact information
A tracking ID from the provider
exp:
An e-mail signature is text (and optionally a logo) automatically appended to outgoing messages.
★ Exam Points:
• Includes name, designation, phone.
• Set once in mail settings.
• Different from digital signature (encryption).

q: What do we call the words or phrases you type into a search engine to find what you are looking for?
exp:
The keywords, questions, or phrases typed by a user into a search engine's input box to locate information on the web are called Search Queries.
★ Exam Points:
• Search engines process a search query against their in-verted index to return a ranked SERP (Search Engine Results Page).
• Enclosing a search query in quotes ("...") forces an exact phrase match.

q: The 'S' in HTTPS signifies the use of which technology to encrypt data, thus making e-banking and other sensitive online activities secure?
exp:
In HTTPS (Hypertext Transfer Protocol Secure), communication is encrypted using Transport Layer Security (TLS) (the modern cryptographic successor to SSL – Secure Sockets Layer), protecting banking logins, card numbers, and session cookies in transit.
★ Exam Points:
• Feature | HTTP | HTTPS
• Port | Port 80 | Port 443
• Security | Plain-text (unencrypted) | Encrypted using SSL / TLS
• Use Case | Basic informational pages | Banking, logins, payments, modern web

q: If a URL begins with ftp:// instead of http://, what does this signify about the primary function of the website or server being accessed?
o: It must be a dynamic blog that updates its content every hour.
It is an unencrypted web page containing only text.
It requires a special satellite connection for access.
It is a server optimized for the storage and retrieval of large files.
exp:
When a URL starts with the scheme ftp:// (File Transfer Protocol) instead of http://, it indicates the destination is an FTP server optimized for storing, uploading, and downloading large files and directory archives rather than rendering standard hypertext web pages.
★ Exam Points:
• FTP uses TCP Port 21 (control) and Port 20 (data), whereas HTTP uses Port 80 and HTTPS uses Port 443.

q: __________ is NOT a web browser.
exp:
MS-Word is a word-processing application (part of Microsoft Office) used to create and format text documents —it is NOT a web browser. Internet Explorer, Google Chrome, and Mozilla Firefox are all web browsers.
★ Exam Points:
• Microsoft retired legacy Internet Explorer in June 2022 and replaced it with Chromium-based Microsoft Edge.

q: What is the key functional difference between a Web Browser (like Chrome) and a Search Engine (like Google)?
o: A browser indexes content, while a search engine lets you view it.
The browser is used for real-time video conferencing, and the search engine is used for e-banking.
The browser only handles FTP, and the search engine only handles HTTP.
A browser renders pages; a search engine locates them.
exp:
The core functional distinction is: • A Web Browser (Chrome, Firefox, Edge) is client software installed on your device that fetches and renders HTML/CSS/JS web pages. • A Search Engine (Google, Bing, DuckDuckGo) is a web service/database that crawls, indexes, and locates relevant web pages based on search queries.
★ Exam Points:
• You open a Web Browser first, and inside it you visit a Search Engine's website (or use the address bar's omnibox) to find URLs.

q: Which fundamental internet service is essential for translating human-readable website names (like google.com) into the numerical addresses (like 172.217.14.78) that computers use?
exp:
DNS (Domain Name System) acts as the 'phonebook of the Internet', automatically translating human-friendly domain names (like google.com) into machine-routable numerical IP addresses (like 172.217.14.78).
★ Exam Points:
• DNS operates primarily on Port 53 (UDP for standard queries; TCP for zone transfers and large responses).
• Common DNS record types: A record (domain → IPv4), AAAA record (domain → IPv6), MX record (mail server), and CNAME (alias).

q: What do you mean by ARPANET?
exp:
ARPANET stands for Advanced Research Projects Agency Network—established in 1969 by the U.S. Department of Defense's ARPA, it was the world's first operational packet-switching network and the direct forerunner of the modern Internet.
★ Exam Points:
• ARPANET officially adopted the TCP/IP protocol suite (designed by Vint Cerf and Bob Kahn) on 1 January 1983, marking the birth of the modern Internet.

q: What do you mean by DNS?
o: Translates domain names to IP addresses.
exp:
DNS (Domain Name System) is the hierarchical naming service of the Internet that translates human-readable domain names (such as www.india.gov.in) into numerical IP addresses used by routers and servers.
★ Exam Points:
• Without DNS, users would have to memorize raw IPv4/IPv6 numbers (e.g., 142.250.193.14) for every website.

q: Which of the following statements best explains what a URL is mainly used for?
o: It is a software application used to view web pages on the internet.
It specifies the unique address of a resource (like a document or image) on the World Wide Web.
It is a protocol used for the secure transfer of data between a web browser and a server.
It is the technical name for the main page of a website, also known as the homepage.
exp:
A URL (Uniform Resource Locator) is NOT an application or protocol—it is an address string that specifies the unique location/address of a resource (such as an HTML webpage, PDF document, or image) on the World Wide Web.
★ Exam Points:
• Compare: Web browser = software to view pages (Option 1); HTTPS = secure transfer protocol (Option 3); Index/Home page = main landing page of a site (Option 4).

q: In what order are 'posts' (articles) typically displayed on a standard blog?
exp:
On a standard blog (weblog), articles/posts are arranged in Reverse Chronological Order—meaning the most recently published post appears first at the very top, followed by progressively older posts below it.
★ Exam Points:
• This ensures returning readers immediately see the fresh-est updates without scrolling through old archives.

q: Which statement best describes the nature and purpose of a blog?
o: A Blog is a specialized network protocol that enables real-time voice and video communication over the internet.
A Blog is a type of electronic bank transaction that allows users to manage their accounts online without visiting a physical branch.
A Blog is a personal or corporate website, usually maintained by an individual, featuring regular posts of commentary, descriptions of events, or other material.
A Blog is a search engine optimization technique used to prioritize website rankings based on content quality and relevance.
exp:
A Blog (short for weblog) is an informational personal or corporate website, maintained by an individual or group, featuring regularly updated posts of commentary, tutorials, news, or event descriptions typically with reader comments enabled.
★ Exam Points:
• Common blogging platforms include WordPress, Blogger, Medium, and Ghost.

q: ________ is the organization that oversees the development of web technologies.
exp:
The World Wide Web Consortium (W3C)—founded in October 1994 by Web inventor Tim Berners-Lee—is the main international standards organization that develops open web standards such as HTML, CSS, XML, SVG, and WCAG accessibility guidelines.
★ Exam Points:
• Other key Internet bodies: IETF (Internet protocols/RFCs like TCP/IP, HTTP), ICANN / IANA (domain names & IP address allocation), and IEEE (LAN/Wi-Fi 802.3/802.11 standards).

q: "http" is followed by ________ and ________.
exp:
In a standard web URL (such as http://www.example.com), the scheme name "http" is immediately followed by a colon (:) and two forward slashes (//)—forming http://—to separate the protocol from the host domain name.
★ Exam Points:
• Note the slash direction: Web URLs ALWAYS use forward slashes (/), whereas Windows local file paths traditionally use backslashes ( \ ) (e.g., C:\Users\Documents).

q: Which statement best describes a critical characteristic distinguishing HTTP from HTTPS?
o: HTTP is always faster than HTTPS because it requires fewer data packets to be transferred.
HTTPS uses an additional security layer (SSL/TLS) to encrypt data, while HTTP transmits data in plain text.
HTTP is used for sending information from the client to the server, and HTTPS is used for receiving information from the server.
HTTPS is required only for e-banking, whereas HTTP is used for all other general web browsing.
exp:
The critical security difference between HTTP and HTTPS is that HTTPS wraps HTTP communication inside an SSL/TLS cryptographic layer to encrypt all transmitted data, whereas HTTP sends data in unencrypted plain text vulnerable to packet sniffing.
★ Exam Points:
• Feature | HTTP | HTTPS
• Port | Port 80 | Port 443
• Security | Plain-text (unencrypted) | Encrypted using SSL / TLS
• Use Case | Basic informational pages | Banking, logins, payments, modern web

q: em is relative to the font size of the parent element or the font size of the nearest parent with a defined font size.
exp:
In CSS (Cascading Style Sheets) typography and sizing, the relative unit em scales relative to the computed font-size of its direct/nearest parent element (e.g., if a parent ‹div› has font-size 20px, then 1.5em = 30px).
★ Exam Points:
• CSS Relative Unit | Relative To
• em | Font-size of the parent element
• rem (root em) | Font-size of the root ‹html› element (typically 16px)
• vw / vh | 1% of the browser viewport's width / height

q: What is full form of URL?
exp:
URL stands for Uniform Resource Locator—the unique standardized address used to locate web pages, images, videos, and files across the Internet.
★ Exam Points:
• Invented by Tim Berners-Lee, a URL has two essential components: Protocol/Scheme (e.g., https://) and Resource Name/Domain + Path.

q: __________ refers to a series of Websites that require special decryption and configuration tools to access.
exp:
The Dark Web is a hidden subset of the Deep Web hosted on encrypted overlay networks (darknets) that cannot be opened in normal browsers or indexed by Google—requiring special anonymizing/decryption routing software and configuration tools such as the Tor (The Onion Router) browser (e.g., .onion sites) or I2P.
★ Exam Points:
• Three layers of the Web:
• Surface Web: Publicly indexed by search engines.
• Deep Web: Unindexed private pages behind logins (net-banking portals, private emails, medical records).
• Dark Web: Encrypted overlay networks requiring special tools like Tor.

q: Which is a short cut key use to open the file from the computer edge?
exp:
In Microsoft Edge (as well as Chrome, Firefox, Word, and Excel), pressing Ctrl + O opens the system File Explorer dialog box so you can browse and open a local file (such as a saved HTML page, PDF, or image) from your computer directly inside Edge.
★ Exam Points:
• Compare standard shortcuts: Ctrl + N = New window; Ctrl + S = Save webpage; Ctrl + O = Open local file; Ctrl + P = Print page.

q: __________ is a principle on which Web page editors work.
exp:
Visual web page editors (like Adobe Dreamweaver or visual CMS builders) and modern word processors operate on the principle of WYSIWYG—standing for "What You See Is What You Get"—meaning the content during editing closely matches its final published/rendered appearance without manually writing raw markup tags.
★ Exam Points:
• Plain code editors (like Notepad or VS Code without pre-view) edit raw HTML tags directly rather than being WYSIWYG editors.

q: Which of the following is recommended for effective professional emails? (i) Simple black text and standard fonts for better readability (ii) The use of "bold" or "italics" to highlight key texts (iii) A different colour for every sentence to keep the reader engaged (iv) Fancy and differently sized fonts for each line to express creativity
exp:
Evaluating each statement for professional business email etiquette: • (i) Correct: Standard, clean fonts (Arial, Calibri, Times New Roman) in simple black text maximize cross-device read-ability. • (ii) Correct: Judicious use of bold or italics highlights deadlines and key action items. • (iii) & (iv) Incorrect: Rainbow sentence colours and mismatched fancy fonts look unprofessional, distract readers, and trigger spam filters. Hence, Only (i) and (ii) are recommended.
★ Exam Points:
• Recommended body font size for professional emails: 10 pt to 12 pt.
• Also avoid typing full paragraphs in ALL CAPS or adding excessive exclamation marks.

q: Which of the following is a security benefit of UPI (Unified Payments Interface) for the user?
o: It can be used even when there is no active internet connection available.
The service reliably provides insurance coverage for every transaction completed by users daily today.
It is faster than RTGS for high-value transfers.
It eliminates the need to share sensitive bank account numbers or IFSC codes with the receiver.
exp:
Developed by NPCI (National Payments Corporation of India) in 2016, UPI (Unified Payments Interface) lets users transact using a Virtual Payment Address (VPA / UPI ID like name@upi) or QR code—eliminating the need to expose sensitive bank account numbers and IFSC codes to the receiver.
★ Exam Points:
• Why other options fail: Standard smartphone UPI requires internet (offline USSD *99# / UPI 123Pay are separate modes), does not provide blanket daily transaction insurance, and UPI's standard per-transaction cap (Rs. 1 lakh; up to Rs. 5 lakh for specific categories like hospitals/education/IPO) differs from RTGS high-value corporate transfers.
• Every UPI debit requires authenticating with a secret 4- or 6-digit UPI PIN.

q: Which of the following could be the reason for an email lying in the Outbox? (i) The email has been successfully transmitted (ii) The email has a large attachment, which is taking time to upload (iii) The internet connection is lost suddenly (iv) There is a problem with connecting to the server
exp:
Evaluating why an email remains in the Outbox: • (i) False: Once successfully transmitted, an email moves out of Outbox into the Sent folder. • (ii) True: A large attachment still uploading keeps the mail in Outbox. • (iii) True: Sudden loss of internet connection queues outgoing mail in Outbox. • (iv) True: Mail server connection/SMTP error holds the message in Outbox. Therefore, Only (ii), (iii) and (iv) are valid reasons.
★ Exam Points:
• As soon as connectivity is restored and upload finishes, the email client automatically sends queued Outbox messages.

q: What is the Junk Email filter or the Spam filter used for?
o: It moves suspected incoming spam emails to a separate folder
It automatically deletes suspected incoming spam emails
It returns suspected incoming junk emails to the sender
It automatically forwards incoming spam emails to the administrator
exp:
An email client's Junk Email filter / Spam filter analyzes incoming messages (checking sender reputation, SPF/DKIM/DMARC authentication, and spam keywords) and automatically diverts suspected spam emails out of the main Inbox into a separate Spam / Junk folder so users can review false positives if needed.
★ Exam Points:
• Messages sitting inside Gmail's Spam folder are automatically purged after 30 days.

q: You are writing an important email, but need to stop and continue working on it later. In which folder would you expect to find it when you return?
exp:
An email that you have started composing or editing—but have not yet sent—is automatically saved by webmail and desktop mail clients inside the Drafts folder so you can reopen, finish, and send it later.
★ Exam Points:
• Once you click Send on a draft and delivery succeeds, it is removed from Drafts and placed in the Sent folder.

q: When you delete an email from your Inbox or another folder, where is it temporarily moved to before being permanently removed from the system?
exp:
Deleting an email from the Inbox moves it temporarily to the Deleted Items / Trash / Bin folder, allowing recovery in case of accidental deletion before the system purges it permanently (typically after 30 days or when 'Empty Trash' is clicked).
★ Exam Points:
• In desktop Windows File Explorer (similar concept), pressing Shift + Delete bypasses the Recycle Bin for immediate permanent deletion.

q: Which of the following statements is TRUE with reference to the email systems of popular free email service providers like Gmail and Outlook? (i) Users can create custom folders or labels to organise their messages. (ii) Users cannot create custom folders or labels to organise their messages. (iii) Creating custom folders or labels increases the storage limit allotted to the user. (iv) Creating custom folders or labels decreases the storage limit allotted to the user.
exp:
Evaluating each statement about Gmail and Outlook: • (i) True: Both let users create custom Labels (Gmail) or Folders (Outlook) to organize messages. • (ii) False: Directly contradicts (i). • (iii) & (iv) False: Creating folders/labels is purely organizational metadata and neither increases nor decreases your allotted cloud storage quota (e.g., 15 GB free on Google). Thus, Only (i) is TRUE.
★ Exam Points:
• Google accounts provide 15 GB of free shared cloud storage across Gmail, Google Drive, and Google Photos.

q: What does it mean when we say that an email is "queued"?
o: The email has been marked as spam and is waiting to be automatically deleted by the system.
The email has been moved to the Archives folder for long-term storage for future reference.
The email has been placed in the Outbox folder, waiting in line to be transmitted to the mail server.
The email has been sent successfully and is waiting in the recipient's inbox to be read.
exp:
When an email client reports that a message is "queued", it means the email is sitting in the Outbox queue waiting in line to be transmitted to the outgoing SMTP mail server (usually because the device is temporarily offline, syncing, or uploading attachments).
★ Exam Points:
• Once transmission finishes, its status changes from 'Queued' (in Outbox) to 'Sent' (in the Sent folder).

q: Which folder is used to temporarily save a message that you are composing but are not yet ready to send?
exp:
An email message that you are currently writing—and want to save temporarily before sending later—is stored in the Drafts folder.
★ Exam Points:
• Contrast: Drafts = unsent work-in-progress; Outbox = clicked 'Send' and waiting for server transmission; Archive = saved received mail; Junk = suspected spam.

q: Which of the following options is TRUE regarding a "Read Receipt" in email communication?
o: Read receipts are legally binding and cannot be refused by the recipient.
Recipients always have the option to decline sending a read receipt.
All email systems automatically send read receipts without the recipient's consent.
Read receipts guarantee that the recipient has fully understood the email's contents.
exp:
Under standard email protocols (RFC 8098 Message Disposition Notifications), Read Receipts are voluntary on standard consumer/external mail clients—meaning recipients generally have the prompt/option to decline sending a read receipt, and opening an email never proves the reader actually read or understood every word.
★ Exam Points:
• Even inside corporate Exchange/Workspace domains where admins can enforce internal receipts, external recipients can always block or decline read receipts.

q: Which statement is most accurate regarding the functionality of Video Conferencing and Chat?
o: Video Conferencing is primarily used for asynchronous communication, while Chat is used for synchronous, real-time messaging.
Both utilize specialized hardware that bypasses the need for an Internet Service Provider (ISP).
Both services enable real-time, synchronous communication; Video Conferencing specifically incorporates audio and visual streams, while Chat focuses mainly on text.
Chat is limited to two participants, but Video Conferencing can accommodate an unlimited number of users simultaneously.
exp:
Comparing Video Conferencing and Instant Chat: • Both are synchronous (real-time) Internet communication tools (unlike email, which is asynchronous). • Video Conferencing transmits live audio and video streams (plus screen sharing), whereas Chat focuses primarily on real-time text messaging.
★ Exam Points:
• Both services require network connectivity (via an ISP/LAN) and support both 1-to-1 and multi-participant group sessions.

q: Which of the following information is typically appropriate to include in a professional email signature? (i) Your name and job title (ii) Your latest passport-sized photograph (iii) Your company's or brand's logo and tagline (iv) Your company's name and contact numbers
exp:
Evaluating professional email signature items: • (i) Name & job title, (iii) Company logo & tagline, and (iv) Company name & contact numbers are standard corporate signature elements. • (ii) Passport-sized photograph is meant for official ID/application forms—not standard corporate email signatures. Hence, Only (i), (iii) and (iv) are appropriate.
★ Exam Points:
• Keep email signatures compact (3–5 lines) so they don't bloat reply chains.

q: What is the primary function of the "Forward" feature while sending an email?
o: To send a response back only to the original sender
To send a response back only to the 'Cc' recipients.
To send the entire original email to a completely new recipient.
To send the original message to the Archives folder.
exp:
In email clients, clicking Forward lets you send a copy of a received email (along with its original body text and attachments) to a completely new recipient who was not part of the original email thread.
★ Exam Points:
• Unlike Reply (which auto-fills the original sender in 'To'), Forward leaves the To field blank so you can enter the new recipient's address.

q: You receive an email with your address in the 'To' field along with two others. There are five recipients in the 'Cc' field. When you click 'Reply All', who will receive your message?
o: Only the original sender and the other recipients in the 'To' field
Only the original sender and the other recipients in both the 'To' and 'Cc' fields
Only the recipients originally listed in the 'To', 'Cc' and 'Bcc' fields
Only the original sender and those originally listed in the 'Bcc' field
exp:
When you click Reply All on an incoming email: • Your reply goes to the original sender PLUS everyone else listed in the visible 'To' and 'Cc' fields. • Anyone who was secretly blind-copied in Bcc is unknown to your email client and therefore never receives a 'Reply All' message. Hence, Only the original sender and the other recipients in both the 'To' and 'Cc' fields receive your reply.
★ Exam Points:
• Total people receiving your Reply All here = 1 (original sender) + 2 (other To recipients) + 5 (Cc recipients) = 8 recipients.

q: Regarding the Username part of an email address (the part before the @ symbol, e.g., John Doe in JohnDoe@example.com), most modern email systems treat case sensitivity as:
o: Case-sensitive, meaning John Doe@ is a different address from johndoe@.
Case-insensitive, meaning John Doe@ and johndoe@ deliver mail to the same inbox.
Sensitive only to the first letter, insensitive to the rest.
Determined solely by the operating system of the sender.
exp:
In practice, virtually all modern email providers (Gmail, Outlook, Yahoo, corporate Exchange servers) treat the user-name (local-part before @) as case-insensitive—meaning JohnDoe@example.com and johndoe@example.com route mail to the exact same inbox (domain names after @ are also strictly case-insensitive under DNS).
★ Exam Points:
• Note: Although technical RFC 5321 allows servers to treat local-parts case-sensitively in theory, real-world mail systems enforce case-insensitivity to prevent delivery errors (Gmail also ignores dots '.' in usernames!).

q: Which of the following can be included as an attachment in an email? (i) Photos (ii) Videos (iii) Files (iv) Hyperlinks
exp:
Checking what is attached as an email file attachment (via the paperclip icon): • (i) Photos (.jpg, .png), (ii) Videos (.mp4), and (iii) Files (.pdf, .docx, .xlsx, .zip) are actual discrete files uploaded as attachments. • (iv) Hyperlinks are clickable URL text links inserted directly inside the email body—not uploaded as file attachments. Hence, Only (i), (ii) and (iii) are included as attachments.
★ Exam Points:
• Standard attachment icon in email clients: a Paperclip; hyperlink icon: a Chain link.

q: Arrange the given steps for sending an email in the logical order. (i) Click the Compose button (ii) Log in to your email account (iii) Enter the required details and text (iv) Click the Send button
exp:
Tracing the logical workflow for sending an email from start to finish: 1. (ii) Log in to your email account (authenticate first). 2. (i) Click the Compose button (open a new blank message window). 3. (iii) Enter the required details and text (recipient in 'To', Subject line, body, and attachments). 4. (iv) Click the Send button (transmit the message). Correct sequence: (ii), (i), (iii), (iv).
★ Exam Points:
• Once step (iv) succeeds, a copy of the sent message is saved automatically in the Sent folder.

q: Which of the given options is the first part of an email address?
exp:
Every standard email address has two parts separated by the @ ('at') symbol—username@domain_name (e.g., rahul.sharma@gmail.com). The first part (before @) is the unique recipient mailbox identifier called the Username (or local-part).
★ Exam Points:
• The second part (after @) is the Domain name identifying the mail server/provider.

q: For which of the reasons given in the options can the "Bcc" field be used?
o: To ensure that a "reply-all" response from one Bcc recipient is sent to all other recipients.
To share the contact information of all recipients with everyone else on the email.
To maintain client privacy while sending newsletters or updates to a large group.
To ensure complete transparency regarding the full list of recipients of the communication.
exp:
Because Bcc (Blind Carbon Copy) hides every Bcc recipient's email address from everyone else on the message, it is ideal to protect client/subscriber privacy when sending announcements, newsletters, or updates to a large external group—and it simultaneously prevents accidental 'Reply All' storms!
★ Exam Points:
• Putting external client lists in To or Cc exposes every client's private email address to all other recipients (a major privacy/data-protection breach).

q: Why might a video conferencing application reduce video quality automatically during a call?
o: To adjust to limited available bandwidth and maintain a stable connection
exp:
Adaptive bitrate lowers resolution when bandwidth drops so the call doesn't freeze.
★ Exam Points:
• Turning off video saves bandwidth.
• Wired connection is more stable.
• Close other downloads.

q: Which best describes the main purpose of a web browser?
o: View and edit text documents offline
Send requests to web servers and display web pages on the screen
exp:
A browser requests resources via HTTP(S) and renders them as web pages.
★ Exam Points:
• Rendering engine draws pages.
• Extensions add features.
• Browsers are not antivirus.

q: In an e-mail application, what is the main purpose of the address book (contacts)?
o: To maintain a list of frequently used e-mail addresses and details
exp:
Contacts store names, addresses and phone numbers for quick addressing.
★ Exam Points:
• Auto-complete uses contacts.
• Groups/lists send to many.
• Google Contacts syncs with Gmail.

q: What is a major advantage of organising e-mails using folders or labels?
o: It makes it easier to locate messages related to specific topics or tasks
exp:
Folders/labels group related mails for quick retrieval.
★ Exam Points:
• Filters can label automatically.
• Gmail allows multiple labels per mail.
• Search works across folders.

q: Which is a benefit of using search filters (time range, content type) in a search engine?
o: They make recent information impossible to find
They narrow results to more relevant items based on selected criteria
exp:
Filters such as Tools → Past week or Images/News limit results to what you need.
★ Exam Points:
• Advanced Search offers more filters.
• filetype: and site: operators also filter.
• Saves time in research.

q: What happens after you click a search-result link in a browser?
o: The search engine sends the content from its own server only
The browser takes the URL in the link and sends a request to the target website's server
exp:
The link's URL is resolved via DNS and the browser requests the page from that site's server.
★ Exam Points:
• Search engine only provides the link.
• Server responds with HTML.
• Browser renders the page.

q: Which of the following is a search engine that helps you find information on the World Wide Web?
exp:
Google Search is a search engine; Chrome is a browser and WhatsApp is a messaging app.
★ Exam Points:
• Bing, Yahoo, DuckDuckGo are other search engines.
• Google launched in 1998.
• Chrome launched in 2008.

q: Why might someone configure multiple e-mail accounts in the same desktop e-mail client?
o: To view and manage several different mailboxes from one interface
exp:
Clients like Outlook/Thunderbird can manage many accounts in one window.
★ Exam Points:
• Unified inbox combines them.
• Each account has its own server settings.
• IMAP keeps them synced.

q: Which statement correctly explains incognito or private browsing?
o: It makes access completely anonymous everywhere
It prevents the browser from saving history, cookies and form data on the device
exp:
Private mode does not store local history/cookies after closing, but ISPs and websites can still see activity.
★ Exam Points:
• Chrome Incognito: Ctrl + Shift + N.
• Firefox/Edge private: Ctrl + Shift + P / N.
• Downloads and bookmarks are kept.

q: Why is it recommended to clear browser cache and cookies when troubleshooting web access problems?
o: They speed up browsing too much
Old cached files and cookies may interfere with loading updated pages
Clearing deletes passwords on bank server
exp:
Stale cache or corrupt cookies can show outdated or broken pages.
★ Exam Points:
• Ctrl + Shift + Delete opens clear-data dialog.
• Hard reload: Ctrl + F5.
• You may need to log in again.

q: What does the term “e-mail header” most accurately describe?
o: The portion of the e-mail that contains routing and addressing information
exp:
Headers include From, To, Cc, Subject, Date and routing details (Received lines).
★ Exam Points:
• "Show original" displays full headers.
• Headers help trace spam/phishing.
• Body follows the header.

q: Which option correctly illustrates the proper use of a browser's address bar?
o: Typing a document title expecting it to open from disk
Typing a complete URL such as https://www.example.com and pressing Enter
exp:
The address bar accepts URLs (or search terms) to navigate to websites.
★ Exam Points:
• Ctrl + Enter adds www. and .com.
• Address bar also shows security info.
• Suggestions come from history and search.

q: Which option distinguishes a static website from a dynamic website?
o: A static site serves fixed pages, while a dynamic site generates content based on user input or databases
Static uses FTP; dynamic uses SMTP
exp:
Static pages are fixed HTML files; dynamic pages are generated by server-side code (PHP, Python) and databases.
★ Exam Points:
• Blogs and e-commerce sites are dynamic.
• Static sites load fast.
• CMS creates dynamic sites.

q: In website terminology, what does "home page" generally refer to?
o: The main page of a website, opened when its domain is first visited
A page shown only when offline
exp:
The home page is the default entry page of a website, often index.html.
★ Exam Points:
• Browser home page is the start page.
• Links lead from home page to others.
• Also called landing/main page.

q: Which search technique is most effective for finding an exact phrase on the web?
o: Enclosing the phrase in double quotation marks
exp:
Quotes tell the search engine to match the exact phrase.
★ Exam Points:
• Use - to exclude a word.
• site: restricts to a domain.
• filetype:pdf finds PDFs.

q:
In the URL https:
www.example.org/about, which section identifies the domain name?
exp:
www.example.org is the host/domain; https is the protocol and /about is the path.
★ Exam Points:
• .org is the TLD.
• example is the second-level domain.
• www is a subdomain.

q: In web browsing, what is the primary purpose of cookies?
o: To store small pieces of data on the user's device related to website preferences and sessions
exp:
Cookies remember login sessions, shopping carts and preferences.
★ Exam Points:
• Session vs persistent cookies.
• Third-party cookies track across sites.
• Cookies are small text files.

q: Which feature differentiates video conferencing from text-based chatting?
o: Video conferencing uses only keyboard input
Video conferencing includes real-time audio and video, whereas text chat uses written messages
It cannot have more than two participants
exp:
Video conferencing transmits live audio/video; chat exchanges text.
★ Exam Points:
• Both are synchronous.
• Group video calls support many participants.
• Bandwidth needs are higher for video.

q: Why should you avoid repeatedly sending the same promotional e-mail to people who have not requested it?
o: Repeated unsolicited messages can be treated as spam
E-mail allows one message per day
exp:
Unsolicited bulk messages are spam and may get your domain blacklisted.
★ Exam Points:
• Include an unsubscribe option.
• Use opt-in mailing lists.
• Spam filters learn from user reports.

q: For what main reason do search engines employ web crawlers (spiders/bots)?
o: To automatically discover and index new and updated pages across the Web
exp:
Crawlers follow links to find and fetch pages for indexing.
★ Exam Points:
• robots.txt controls crawler access.
• Sitemaps help discovery.
• Googlebot is Google's crawler.

q: In a typical search engine, what happens when a user types keywords and presses Search?
o: The search engine compares the keywords with its indexed web pages and ranks results
The entire Internet is scanned live
exp:
Search engines look up their pre-built index rather than scanning the web live.
★ Exam Points:
• Crawling happens continuously in background.
• Results are ranked by algorithms.
• Ads appear as sponsored results.

q: Google Chrome was released by Google Inc. in the year ____.
exp:
Google Chrome was first released (beta) on 2 September 2008.
★ Exam Points:
• Stable Windows version: December 2008.
• Chrome is the most used browser worldwide.
• ChromeOS launched 2011.

q: What is the correct order of components in an e-mail address?
exp:
An e-mail address is written as username@domainname.
★ Exam Points:
• Example: aimersqila@gmail.com.
• No spaces allowed.
• Domain includes a TLD like .com.

q: Which of the following is NOT a component of an e-mail address?
exp:
An e-mail address contains a username, @ and domain name; the system name is not part of it.
★ Exam Points:
• Username identifies the mailbox.
• Domain identifies the mail server.
• Example: user@gmail.com.

q: Which of the following is NOT an example of a markup language?
exp:
QBE (Query By Example) is a database query method; HTML, SGML and XML are markup languages.
★ Exam Points:
• SGML is the parent of HTML and XML.
• Markup uses tags.
• QBE is used in MS-Access query design.

q: A service that lets us send messages electronically over the Internet to a unique address, offering an efficient and inexpensive means of distributing information, is ____.
exp:
E-mail sends messages to unique addresses quickly and cheaply.
★ Exam Points:
• First e-mail: Ray Tomlinson, 1971.
• Protocols: SMTP, POP3, IMAP.
• Gmail is the most used e-mail service.

q: In which component is e-mail received and managed?
exp:
Incoming e-mails arrive in the Inbox where they are read, organised and replied to.
★ Exam Points:
• Labels/folders organise mail.
• Archive removes mail from the inbox without deleting.
• Starred marks important mail.

q: What is the full form of HTTP?
exp:
HTTP – HyperText Transfer Protocol – is used to transfer web pages between servers and browsers.
★ Exam Points:
• HTTP is stateless.
• Default port 80; HTTPS uses 443.
• HTTP/3 uses QUIC (UDP).

q: What is the full form of IMPS in e-banking services?
exp:
IMPS – Immediate Payment Service – by NPCI (2010) enables instant 24×7 interbank transfers.
★ Exam Points:
• IMPS works on mobile, net banking and ATM.
• IMPS limit is ₹5 lakh per transaction.
• UPI (2016) is built on IMPS infrastructure.

q: IMAP is an e-mail protocol. What is the full form of IMAP?
exp:
IMAP – Internet Message Access Protocol – keeps e-mail on the server and syncs it across devices.
★ Exam Points:
• IMAP port: 143 (993 with SSL).
• POP3 downloads and usually deletes from server.
• SMTP sends mail (port 25/587).

q: What is the full form of HTTPS?
exp:
HTTPS – HyperText Transfer Protocol Secure – encrypts data using SSL/TLS.
★ Exam Points:
• Padlock icon indicates HTTPS.
• Port 443.
• Protects passwords and payment data.

q: POP is an e-mail protocol. What is the full form of POP?
exp:
POP – Post Office Protocol – downloads e-mail from the server to the local device.
★ Exam Points:
• POP3 uses port 110 (995 with SSL).
• IMAP keeps mail on the server.
• SMTP sends mail.

q: Which of the following is a central location of various related web pages?
exp:
A website is the central place (under one domain) where related web pages are kept.
★ Exam Points:
• Homepage is its main page.
• Websites are hosted on web servers.
• Example: ssc.gov.in.

q: Which of the following comprises the second part of an e-mail address?
exp:
After the @ sign comes the domain name (e.g., gmail.com).
★ Exam Points:
• First part = username/mailbox name.
• Domain points to mail servers via MX records.
• Organisation mail uses its own domain.

q: Unsolicited junk e-mail sent in bulk to an indiscriminate recipient list is stored in the ____ folder.
exp:
E-mail filters move such bulk unwanted messages (spam) into the Spam/Junk folder.
★ Exam Points:
• Gmail deletes spam after 30 days.
• "Report spam" trains filters.
• Phishing mails often land in spam.

q:
Consider the statements about HTML.
P: HTML was designed to store and transport data.
Q: All HTML documents must start with a document type declaration <!DOCTYPE html>.
R: HTML is the standard markup language for web pages.
Which is/are correct?
exp:
XML (not HTML) is designed to store and transport data; HTML displays data. Q and R are correct.
★ Exam Points:
• HTML = HyperText Markup Language (Tim Berners-Lee, 1991).
• HTML5 is the current version.
• Tags are written in angle brackets.

q:
Match the domain names with their meanings.
P. .net  Q. .edu  R. .org  S. .com
1. Non-profit organisations 2. Commercial 3. Educational 4. Government 5. Department of Defense 6. Network organisations
exp:
.net – network providers, .edu – education, .org – non-profit organisations, .com – commercial.
★ Exam Points:
• .mil – US military (Department of Defense).
• .gov – government.
• India: .gov.in, .ac.in, .co.in.

q: Bing is a/an ____.
exp:
Bing is Microsoft’s web search engine, launched in 2009.
★ Exam Points:
• Edge browser uses Bing by default.
• Bing replaced MSN Search/Live Search.
• Google is the most used search engine.

q: Which search engine dominates the market with the maximum number of searches?
exp:
Google handles about 90% of global web searches.
★ Exam Points:
• Google founded in 1998 by Larry Page and Sergey Brin.
• PageRank algorithm ranks pages.
• Bing is a distant second.

q: Which of the following is NOT an Internet (e-mail) etiquette?
o: Including your name at the bottom of mails
exp:
Forwarding unwanted chain mails or spam wastes others' time and is bad netiquette.
★ Exam Points:
• Netiquette = network + etiquette.
• Avoid writing in ALL CAPS (seen as shouting).
• Use a clear subject line.

q: Which of the following is NOT a part of an e-mail address?
exp:
An e-mail address = username + @ + provider’s domain name; there is no separate "user domain".
★ Exam Points:
• Example: aimers@gmail.com.
• Domain identifies the mail server.
• Username is unique within a domain.

q: The ____ command in a web browser moves to the next page from the current page (after going back).
exp:
Forward (Alt + Right arrow) moves ahead to the page you came back from.
★ Exam Points:
• Back: Alt + Left arrow.
• Refresh: F5.
• Home: Alt + Home.

q: A website containing a writer's or group of writers' own experiences, observations and opinions is known as a/an ____.
exp:
A blog is an online journal of posts on personal experiences, opinions or topics.
★ Exam Points:
• Micro-blogging: X (Twitter).
• Blogger is owned by Google.
• WordPress powers a large share of websites.

q: Copying a page onto a server is called ____ the page.
exp:
Transferring files from a local computer to a remote server is uploading.
★ Exam Points:
• Downloading is the opposite direction.
• Website files are uploaded via FTP or hosting panels.
• Upload speed is measured in Mbps.

q:
Which of the following is a valid domain name in an e-mail address?
I. gmail.com
II. outlook.com
III. yahoo.com
exp:
All three are valid e-mail domains of Google, Microsoft and Yahoo respectively.
★ Exam Points:
• Domain appears after the @ sign.
• Corporate mail uses company domains.
• Government e-mail in India uses gov.in / nic.in.

q: Which symbol must be used in an e-mail address?
exp:
Every e-mail address contains the @ symbol separating the username from the domain.
★ Exam Points:
• @ introduced by Ray Tomlinson in 1971.
• First e-mail sent on ARPANET.
• Ray Tomlinson is called the father of e-mail.

q: A markup language and file format used for storing, transmitting and reconstructing arbitrary data is known as ____.
exp:
XML (eXtensible Markup Language) is designed to store and transport data with user-defined tags.
★ Exam Points:
• HTML is designed to display data.
• XML was developed by W3C (1998).
• Office files (.docx/.xlsx) are zipped XML.

q: Which of the following is a valid e-mail address?
exp:
A valid address needs a username, one @ and a proper domain – mySchool@gmail.com.
★ Exam Points:
• Missing username or domain makes it invalid.
• Two @ signs are not allowed.
• Domain cannot start with a dot.

q: Which keyboard shortcut displays the non-editable HTML source code of the current page in Chrome?
exp:
Ctrl + U opens "View page source" in a new tab.
★ Exam Points:
• F12 / Ctrl + Shift + I opens Developer Tools.
• Ctrl + S saves the web page.
• view-source: prefix also shows source.

q: The ____ field indicates the sender's address, i.e. who sent the e-mail.
exp:
The From field shows the e-mail address of the sender.
★ Exam Points:
• To – primary recipients.
• Cc/Bcc – copy recipients.
• Reply-To can differ from From.

q: Which keyboard shortcut opens the Downloads window in Chrome?
exp:
Ctrl + J opens chrome://downloads.
★ Exam Points:
• Ctrl + H – History.
• Ctrl + D – bookmark page.
• Alt + D – focus address bar.

q: Which keyboard shortcut activates the browser tab to the left of the current tab in Chrome?
exp:
Ctrl + Page Up (or Ctrl + Shift + Tab) moves to the previous (left) tab.
★ Exam Points:
• Ctrl + Page Down / Ctrl + Tab – next tab.
• Ctrl + 1 to 8 – jump to that tab; Ctrl + 9 – last tab.
• Alt + Left arrow – go back a page.

q: Among the given folders, unsent mails are stored in the ____ folder.
exp:
Messages written but not yet sent are saved in Drafts.
★ Exam Points:
• Sent – mails already sent.
• Outbox – mails queued for sending.
• Gmail autosaves drafts.

q: Safari is a web browser developed by ____.
exp:
Safari is Apple’s browser, launched in 2003, and uses the WebKit engine.
★ Exam Points:
• Default browser on macOS and iOS.
• Chrome’s Blink was forked from WebKit (2013).
• Edge – Microsoft; Chrome – Google.

q: Which of the following is NOT a service provided by the Internet?
exp:
Ethernet is a LAN technology (IEEE 802.3), not an Internet service.
★ Exam Points:
• Internet services: e-mail, WWW, FTP, chat, VoIP, video conferencing.
• Ethernet invented by Robert Metcalfe (1973).
• Ethernet uses RJ-45 and twisted-pair cables.

q: The ____ field of an e-mail indicates the receiver of that e-mail.
exp:
The To field contains the primary recipient’s address.
★ Exam Points:
• Multiple addresses are separated by commas.
• Cc and Bcc are secondary recipients.
• From shows the sender.

q: ____ is the inter-company communication of business documents in a standard format.
exp:
EDI (Electronic Data Interchange) exchanges business documents like purchase orders and invoices electronically in standard formats.
★ Exam Points:
• EDI standards: ANSI X12, EDIFACT.
• Used heavily in B2B e-commerce.
• Reduces paperwork and errors.

q: In Gmail, what do you use to send a response to the original sender and all other recipients on the To and Cc lines?
exp:
Reply All sends the reply to the sender and every recipient in To and Cc.
★ Exam Points:
• Bcc recipients are never included.
• Use Reply All carefully in large groups.
• Forward sends to new people.

q:
Which of the following is/are services provided by the Internet?
(i) Websites (ii) Electronic mail (iii) Chat (iv) Discussion groups
exp:
All four – websites (WWW), e-mail, chat and discussion groups/forums – are Internet services.
★ Exam Points:
• Usenet newsgroups were early discussion groups.
• Instant messaging is a chat service.
• Other services: FTP, VoIP, streaming.

q: Online conversations in which you can immediately send messages back and forth are called ____.
exp:
Chat (instant messaging) allows real-time text conversation.
★ Exam Points:
• Examples: WhatsApp, Telegram, Google Chat.
• IRC was an early chat system (1988).
• E-mail is asynchronous.

q: The ____ indicates the purpose of an e-mail.
exp:
The subject line briefly states what the e-mail is about.
★ Exam Points:
• Keep subject short and specific.
• Subject is part of the header.
• Empty subject may trigger spam filters.

q: Which keyboard shortcut moves through each open tab going to the right in Chrome?
exp:
Ctrl + Tab (or Ctrl + Page Down) jumps to the next tab on the right.
★ Exam Points:
• Ctrl + Shift + Tab – previous tab.
• Ctrl + T – new tab; Ctrl + W – close tab.
• Alt + Tab switches applications.

q: Which of the following is NOT a web-mail provider?
exp:
Baidu is a Chinese search engine, not an e-mail service.
★ Exam Points:
• Outlook.com, Gmail and Yahoo Mail are web-mail services.
• Baidu founded by Robin Li (2000).
• Indian e-mail: Rediffmail, Zoho Mail.

q: Facebook is a/an ____.
exp:
Facebook (2004, Mark Zuckerberg) is a social networking site owned by Meta Platforms.
★ Exam Points:
• Meta also owns Instagram and WhatsApp.
• Facebook renamed parent company Meta in Oct 2021.
• Headquarters: Menlo Park, California.

q: Which of the following refers to a huge database of Internet resources (web pages, images, etc.) that helps locate information on the World Wide Web?
exp:
A search engine crawls and indexes web resources and lets users search them by keywords.
★ Exam Points:
• Components: crawler (spider), indexer, query processor.
• Google holds about 90% of global search share.
• Archie (1990) was the first search engine.

q: Which of the following allows the user to send files along with an e-mail?
exp:
An attachment is a file (document, image, etc.) sent with an e-mail, shown by a paper-clip icon.
★ Exam Points:
• Gmail attachment limit: 25 MB (larger files via Drive link).
• Be careful with .exe attachments.
• Snoozed hides mail temporarily.

q: In Gmail, what do you use to send a received message to someone not on the To or Cc lines?
exp:
Forward sends the received message (with attachments) to new recipients.
★ Exam Points:
• Forwarded subject begins with "Fwd:".
• Reply goes back to the sender.
• Show original displays raw headers.

q: Which keyboard shortcut shows or hides the Bookmarks bar in Google Chrome?
exp:
Ctrl + Shift + B toggles the bookmarks bar.
★ Exam Points:
• Ctrl + Shift + O opens Bookmark Manager.
• Ctrl + D bookmarks the page.
• Ctrl + Shift + D bookmarks all open tabs.

q: Internet Explorer is a web browser released in 1995 by ____.
exp:
Internet Explorer was released by Microsoft in August 1995 with Windows 95 Plus! pack.
★ Exam Points:
• IE was retired on 15 June 2022.
• Replaced by Microsoft Edge.
• IE11 was the last version.

q: Which command in a web browser helps to move to the previous page from the current page?
exp:
The Back button (Alt + Left arrow) returns to the previously visited page.
★ Exam Points:
• Forward: Alt + Right arrow.
• Backspace was the old Back shortcut.
• Home button opens the start page.

q: A/An ____ is a folder in an e-mail application that accepts incoming messages.
exp:
All incoming messages arrive in the Inbox.
★ Exam Points:
• Outbox – waiting to be sent.
• Sent – already sent.
• Gmail inbox tabs: Primary, Social, Promotions.

q: ____ is a telecommunication technology that permits two or more people in different locations to interact via simultaneous two-way video and audio.
exp:
Videoconferencing allows real-time audio-video meetings between remote participants.
★ Exam Points:
• Examples: Zoom, Google Meet, Microsoft Teams.
• Needs webcam, microphone and Internet.
• Used for e-courts and online classes.

q: Which statement is correct about Blind Carbon Copy (BCC) in Gmail?
o: It shares a copy with 10 primary recipients.
It shares a copy with all primary recipients.
It shares a copy with someone without letting the primary recipients know.
It shares a copy with 100 primary recipients.
exp:
BCC recipients receive the mail but their addresses are hidden from all other recipients.
★ Exam Points:
• Bcc protects privacy in mass mails.
• Bcc recipients are not included in Reply All.
• Cc recipients are visible.

q: Flipkart, one of the leading e-commerce marketplaces in India, belongs to the ____ segment.
exp:
Flipkart sells products from businesses directly to individual consumers, which is B2C e-commerce.
★ Exam Points:
• C2C: OLX; B2B: IndiaMART.
• G2C: government services portals.
• Flipkart was founded in 2007 by Sachin and Binny Bansal (now owned by Walmart).

q: Which icon is used to represent an attachment in e-mail?
exp:
A paper-clip icon represents attaching or the presence of attachments.
★ Exam Points:
• Attachment size limit in Gmail: 25 MB.
• Large files are shared as Drive links.
• Avoid opening unknown .exe attachments.

q: A collection of associated (related) web pages is called a ____.
exp:
A website is a set of related web pages under one domain name.
★ Exam Points:
• First page of a website = homepage.
• Web pages are written in HTML.
• Websites are stored on web servers.

q: The development of the World Wide Web began in which year?
exp:
Tim Berners-Lee proposed the WWW at CERN in March 1989; the first website went live in 1991.
★ Exam Points:
• ARPANET (Internet’s ancestor) started in 1969.
• First browser: WorldWideWeb (1990).
• W3C was founded in 1994.

q: Which keyboard shortcut resets Google Chrome browser zoom to default?
exp:
Ctrl + 0 resets zoom to 100%.
★ Exam Points:
• Ctrl + Plus zooms in; Ctrl + Minus zooms out.
• Ctrl + R reloads the page.
• Ctrl + 9 jumps to the last tab.

q: Google Chrome is a/an ____.
exp:
Chrome is Google’s web browser released in September 2008.
★ Exam Points:
• Uses the Blink engine and V8 JavaScript engine.
• Chromium is its open-source base.
• ChromeOS is Google’s operating system.

q: Which description best defines the internet in the context of modern communication technologies?
o: A single powerful computer owned by one company
A worldwide network of interconnected computers and devices that communicate using standard protocols
A private network inside one building only
A special software used only for sending emails
exp:
The Internet is a global system of interconnected computer networks that use the standard Internet Protocol suite (TCP/IP) to communicate. It connects billions of devices worldwide, facilitating data exchange and access to information services.
★ Exam Points:
• TCP/IP (Transmission Control Protocol/Internet Protocol) is the core communication protocol of the Internet.
• The Internet is a public, decentralized network, unlike private Intranets.
• ARPANET, established in 1969, is considered the foundational precursor to the modern Internet.
• It provides infrastructure for services such as the World Wide Web (WWW), email, and file transfer.

q: When a user types a web address into a browser and presses Enter, which component translates the domain name into an IP address?
exp:
The Domain Name System (DNS) acts as the internet's phonebook, translating human-readable domain names like example.com into machine-readable IP addresses. This enables web browsers to locate and connect to the correct web server hosting the website.
★ Exam Points:
• DNS operates primarily using UDP port 53 for quick querying.
• DNS caching stores IP lookups locally to speed up subsequent requests.
• HTTP handles the transfer of web content, while DNS handles resolution.
• FTP is used for file transfers, and POP is used for receiving emails.

q: What is the key distinction between HTTP and HTTPS when accessing websites?
o: HTTP is used only for images, HTTPS only for text
HTTPS includes encryption for secure communication, while HTTP does not
HTTP is newer and more secure, HTTPS is older
There is no difference; both are identical
exp:
HTTPS (Hypertext Transfer Protocol Secure) encrypts communication between the web browser and the web server using SSL/TLS. Standard HTTP transfers data in plaintext, exposing sensitive information to potential interception.
★ Exam Points:
• HTTP operates on default port 80.
• HTTPS operates on default port 443.
• HTTPS protects sensitive transmission like passwords, personal details, and banking credentials.
• Feature | HTTP | HTTPS
• Port | Port 80 | Port 443
• Security | Plain-text (unencrypted) | Encrypted using SSL / TLS
• Use Case | Basic informational pages | Banking, logins, payments, modern web

q: Which option correctly illustrates the proper use of a web browser's address bar for entering website addresses?
o: Typing a document title without a protocol or domain and expecting it to open from local disk
Typing a complete URL such as https://www.example.com and pressing Enter to open the site
Typing an email message directly into the address bar
Typing only a password into the bar
exp:
Entering a fully qualified Uniform Resource Locator (URL) containing the protocol (https://) and domain name (www.example.com) directly into the browser address bar establishes a direct connection to the intended remote web server.
★ Exam Points:
• Modern address bars act as Omniboxes, combining search engines and web addresses.
• Keyboard shortcut to highlight the address bar in browsers is Ctrl + L or F6.
• https:// indicates encrypted traffic via SSL/TLS.
• Typing an incomplete string defaults to the browser's default search engine lookup.

q: Which option accurately distinguishes between a static website and a dynamic website?
o: Both always show identical content to every visitor and never change
A static site serves fixed pages, while a dynamic site can generate content based on user inputs
A static site uses only FTP, while a dynamic site uses only SMTP
A static site is always secure, while a dynamic site is always insecure
exp:
A static website displays identical pre-written HTML content to all users, whereas a dynamic website uses server-side scripts (e.g., PHP, Node.js) and databases (e.g., MySQL) to generate tailored real-time web pages based on user interaction or inputs.
★ Exam Points:
• Static sites are built using basic HTML, CSS, and simple JavaScript.
• Dynamic sites interact with databases to display personalized content (e.g., user profiles).
• Static websites load faster as pages are pre-rendered and require no database queries.
• Content Management Systems (CMS) like WordPress operate as dynamic websites.

q: Which search technique is usually most effective when looking for an exact phrase on the Web?
o: Typing words in random order without any punctuation
Using all words in uppercase letters
Enclosing the phrase in double quotation marks
exp:
Wrapping a multi-word search string inside double quotation marks (" ") forces search engines to filter and return pages that match that exact sequence of words together, excluding variations.
★ Exam Points:
• Referred to as exact match search operator.
• Reduces search engine result noise by discarding pages where words appear separately.
• Combining operators (e.g., - to exclude words, filetype:pdf) enhances precision.
• Search engines are generally case-insensitive by default.

q: Which of the following statements correctly describes downloading in the context of internet usage?
o: Sending a file from a local device to a remote server
Transferring a file from a remote server or website to a local device
Printing a web page directly to paper
Writing data from memory onto a CD
exp:
Downloading is the process of receiving data or files from a remote central server or internet website onto a client's local storage device (such as a computer or smartphone).
★ Exam Points:
• The reverse operation—sending data from a local device to a remote server—is Uploading.
• Common protocols used for file downloads include HTTP, HTTPS, and FTP.
• Download speeds are measured in megabits per second (Mbps).
• Browser downloads are traditionally managed and viewed via Ctrl + J.

q: Which statement best explains why search engines do not show every existing web page in their results?
o: They purposely hide all useful pages
The Web is extremely large and indexing depends on crawlers discovering pages
There are only a few pages on the internet
Search engines cannot use any algorithms
exp:
The World Wide Web contains billions of dynamic pages. Search engines discover pages via automated software bots called web crawlers or spiders. Unlinked pages, pages blocked by robots.txt, or non-indexed pages on the Deep Web remain unlisted.
★ Exam Points:
• Crawling is the process where bots follow hyperlinks across the web to find pages.
• Indexing stores and categorizes parsed web page content in a massive database.
• Webmasters use a robots.txt file to explicitly instruct search crawlers which pages to skip.
• The Deep Web includes dynamic database content that crawlers cannot automatically index.

q: Which term refers to sending a file from a local computer to a remote server on the internet?
exp:
Uploading is the process of transmitting digital data or files from a local device, such as a PC or smartphone, to a remote computer or server via the internet. Common examples include attaching files to emails or publishing photos to cloud storage.
★ Exam Points:
• Downloading is the reverse process, where data is retrieved from a remote server to a local device.
• Common protocols used for file transfers include FTP (File Transfer Protocol) and HTTP/HTTPS.
• Bandwidth and upload speed provided by an ISP dictate how quickly files can be sent.
• Cloud services like Google Drive and Dropbox rely on background uploading to sync local files.

q: Which statement correctly explains the purpose of incognito or private browsing mode in web browsers?
o: A mode that makes internet access completely anonymous and untraceable everywhere
A mode that prevents the browser from saving history
A mode that blocks all websites
A mode that always speeds up downloads
exp:
Incognito or private browsing mode stops the local browser from storing browsing history, search records, cookies, and site data after the session is closed. However, it does not hide activity from ISPs, network administrators, or visited websites.
★ Exam Points:
• Private browsing automatically clears session cookies and form entries upon closing the private window.
• It does not provide total online anonymity or hide the device's IP address.
• Shortkey Ctrl + Shift + N opens a new incognito window in Google Chrome and Microsoft Edge.
• Shortkey Ctrl + Shift + P launches private browsing in Mozilla Firefox.

q: Which of the following best describes the main purpose of a web browser when you access the internet from a home or school computer?
o: View and edit text documents without an internet connection
Connect the computer to the electricity supply
Send requests to web servers and display web pages on the screen
Protect the computer from all types of viruses automatically
exp:
A web browser is a client software application designed to fetch digital resources (HTML, CSS, images) from remote web servers via HTTP/HTTPS protocols and render them into interactive graphical web pages for the user.
★ Exam Points:
• Popular modern web browsers include Google Chrome, Mozilla Firefox, Microsoft Edge, and Apple Safari.
• The core component that translates HTML/CSS code into visual layouts is called the rendering engine (e.g., Blink, Gecko, WebKit).
• Browsers manage web security through SSL/TLS verification, cookie handling, and sandbox isolation.
• URLs (Uniform Resource Locators) are entered into the browser address bar to specify web resource locations.

q: Which of the following is most closely associated with providing access to the internet over a wide area?
exp:
An Internet Service Provider (ISP) is a telecommunications company that provides individuals and organizations with access to the global internet via technologies such as fiber optics, DSL, cable, satellite, or cellular networks.
★ Exam Points:
• Prominent examples of ISPs in India include BSNL, Reliance Jio, and Airtel.
• ISPs assign public IP addresses to subscriber routers to enable WAN communication.
• Connection speeds offered by ISPs are measured in Mbps (Megabits per second) or Gbps.
• Modems and routers bridge customer local area networks (LAN) to the ISP's wide area network (WAN).

q: Which of the following is a benefit of using search filters (such as time range or content type) in a search engine?
o: They reduce the number of search results randomly
They make it impossible to find recent information
They help narrow results to more relevant items based on selected criteria
They delete the browser's history automatically
exp:
Search filters restrict query results according to specific parameters such as publishing date, content format (images, news, videos), file type, or region. This eliminates irrel-evant web pages and accelerates finding highly accurate information.
★ Exam Points:
• Common Google search filters include Past 24 hours, Past year, and exact match quotation marks (" ").
• Advanced operators like filetype:pdf or site:.gov act as targeted search parameters.
• Tools tab in search engines provides drop-down filters for licensing, date ranges, and verbatim matches.
• Filtering saves bandwidth and research time by removing redundant search results.

q: Which description best summarises the process that occurs after clicking a search result link in a browser?
o: The search engine sends the content directly from its own server only
The browser takes the URL in the link, sends a request to the target website server
The browser restarts before opening the page
The server prints the page on a remote printer
exp:
Clicking a link directs the browser to extract the destination URL, perform a DNS lookup to resolve the server's IP address, send an HTTP/HTTPS GET request to that target server, and render the returned web assets on screen.
★ Exam Points:
• DNS (Domain Name System) translates human-readable domain names into IP addresses.
• The target web server processes the incoming HTTP request and sends back HTML, CSS, and JavaScript files.
• HTTPS encrypts the connection between the user browser and the web server using TLS/SSL.
• Hyperlinks use the HTML ‹a› anchor tag with the href attribute specifying the destination web address.

q: In an email message, what is the primary purpose of the body section or message area?
o: To specify the email addresses of recipients
To contain the main text and detailed message content
To specify how large attachments can be
To store the time and date of sending
exp:
The body section of an email contains the main message content, detailed text, and written communication intended for the recipient. Headers like "To", "CC", and "Subject" hold meta-information, while the body holds the core information.
★ Exam Points:
• The email body can contain formatted text, inline images, and hyperlinks using HTML formatting.
• Header fields such as To, Cc, and Bcc specify recipient addresses.
• The Subject line summarizes the email purpose, distinct from the body section.
• Protocols like SMTP transfer email contents across the network.

q: In an email service, what is the primary purpose of using the Forward option on a message?
o: To send a copy of a received message to new recipients
To delete a message from the inbox
To move a message to the spam folder automatically
To print the message directly from the server
exp:
The Forward (Fwd) command is used to re-send an existing email message (including its contents and optional attachments) to a third party who was not part of the original recipient list.
★ Exam Points:
• Forwarded email subject lines automatically append the prefix Fwd: or Fw:.
• Reply sends a message back only to the original sender.
• Reply All sends the message to the original sender and all CC'd recipients.
• Original attachments are usually included automatically when forwarding, unlike standard replies.

q: Which setting in an email client can automatically move messages that match certain conditions into specific folders?
exp:
Message Rules (or Email Filters) are automated criteria configured by users to organize incoming emails. They automatically sort, label, forward, or move messages into designated folders based on specified parameters like sender, subject, or keywords.
★ Exam Points:
• Email filtering helps keep the main Inbox organized and clutter-free.
• Rules can be based on criteria such as "From", "Subject Contains", or "Attachment Present".
• Actions executed by filters include Move to Folder, Mark as Read, or Delete.
• Automated spam detection relies heavily on built-in server-side filtering algorithms.

q: Which action is appropriate when an email contains important information that must not be lost, but the inbox is becoming cluttered?
o: Move the message to a suitable folder or archive for long-term storage
Forward it many times to keep copies
exp:
Archiving or organizing emails into specific folders/labels removes them from the main Inbox view while keeping them stored safely in the account database for future retrieval or search queries.
★ Exam Points:
• Archiving in Gmail/Outlook removes the 'Inbox' tag without deleting the underlying message.
• Archived messages can be easily retrieved via the search bar or "All Mail" view.
• Folders/Labels provide a structured categorization for quick navigation.
• Deleting moves messages to the Trash, where they are purged permanently after 30 days.

q: Among the following options, which one represents a recommended or safe practice when sending or opening email attachments?
o: Always attach files without mentioning them in the body
Use clear file names and briefly describe the attachment in the message text
Avoid using any file names at all
Attach very large files without checking size limits
exp:
Using descriptive file names and explicitly explaining attachments in the email body verifies the file's legitimacy and purpose. This prevents the email from being flagged as spam or phishing by anti-malware filters.
★ Exam Points:
• Unrecognized or suspicious attachments should be scanned using antivirus software.
• Executable files (.exe, .bat) are often blocked by mail servers due to malware risks.
• Most email providers enforce an attachment size limit (typically 25 MB).
• Large files are better shared via cloud storage links (e.g., Google Drive, OneDrive).

q: Why is it important to avoid sending the same promotional email repeatedly to people who have not requested it?
o: Because email services are free and should not be used that way
Because repeated, unsolicited messages can be treated as spam
Because email cannot deliver more than one message a day
Because attachments will not work in such emails
exp:
Sending unsolicited bulk emails violates CAN-SPAM regula-tions and email service provider policies. Internet Service Providers (ISPs) flag repeated unwanted messages as spam, which damages domain reputation and leads to ip-blacklisting.
★ Exam Points:
• Spam filters use automated algorithms to analyze sending frequency and content.
• Compliance requires including an explicit unsubscribe link in marketing emails.
• Legitimate marketing relies on opt-in mechanisms to gather consensual recipients.
• Excessive spam complaints reduce overall email deliver-ability rates.

q: Which of these actions is commonly regarded as inappropriate or poor practice in email communication?
o: Writing in all capital letters as if shouting
exp:
Typing an email body or subject line entirely in ALL CAPITAL LETTERS is considered poor email etiquette (netiquette) because it conveys the impression of shouting or aggression. It also makes text visually difficult to read.
★ Exam Points:
• Netiquette refers to the informal network rules governing professional and polite online communication.
• Overusing "Reply All" when only responding to the sender is another common netiquette violation.
• Clear subject lines help recipients prioritize and search for messages efficiently.
• Proofreading emails for proper grammar, spelling, and tone ensures clear professional communication.

q: In an email message, what does the term "email header" most accurately describe?
o: A picture attached to the email
The portion of the email that contains routing and addressing information
A font style used in the body text
The file name of an attachment
exp:
An email header contains technical metadata associated with a message, including sender details, recipient addresses, mail server routing hops, timestamps, and authentication results (like SPF and DKIM).
★ Exam Points:
• Key standard header fields include From, To, Subject, Date, and Message-ID.
• Bcc (Blind Carbon Copy) hides recipient addresses from other message recipients.
• Full technical headers are often analyzed by IT security tools to trace email origin and detect spam or spoofing.
• Email transmission protocols like SMTP (Simple Mail Transfer Protocol) populate routing details within the header.

q: In an email application, what is the main function or purpose of the address book or contacts list?
o: To store a copy of all received messages
To maintain a list of frequently used email addresses and related details
To change the password for the email account
exp:
An address book or contacts list stores saved email addresses, full names, phone numbers, and associated recipient information. It enables quick recipient selection and automatic address completion while drafting new emails.
★ Exam Points:
• Auto-complete functionality draws directly from the address book as users start typing names in recipient fields.
• Contact Groups (or Distribution Lists) allow sending a single email message to multiple recipients simultaneously.
• Address books can be exported and imported across email platforms using vCard (.vcf) or CSV formats.
• Cloud email accounts sync contact lists seamlessly across desktop computers and mobile devices.

q: When using a desktop email client, why might someone configure multiple email accounts in the same program?
o: To prevent messages from being downloaded
To view and manage several different mailboxes from one interface
To stop any messages from being sent
To delete all old messages automatically
exp:
Configuring multiple accounts (e.g., work, personal) in a desktop email client like Microsoft Outlook aggregates dis-parate mailboxes into a unified portal. This streamlines managing incoming messages, calendar events, and communications from one interface.
★ Exam Points:
• Protocols like IMAP and POP3 enable desktop clients to retrieve emails from multiple mail servers.
• Unified Inboxes synthesize messages from distinct accounts into a consolidated view.
• SMTP settings are configured per account to ensure outgoing emails use the correct domain address.
• Desktop clients allow applying unique signatures, rules, and folders to each configured email account.

q: The URL for a secured website starts with ____.
exp:
HTTPS (HTTP Secure) encrypts communication using SSL/TLS; browsers show a padlock icon.
★ Exam Points:
• HTTPS uses port 443; HTTP uses port 80.
• TLS is the successor of SSL.
• Always check https before entering bank details.

q: Which of the following is an invalid e-mail address?
exp:
The domain part cannot contain special characters like $, so abc123@$yahoo.com is invalid.
★ Exam Points:
• Usernames may start with digits.
• Domain may contain letters, digits, hyphens and dots.
• Only one @ allowed.

q: The full form of URL is ____.
exp:
URL – Uniform Resource Locator – is the address of a resource on the web.
★ Exam Points:
• Parts: protocol, domain, path (e.g. https://www.ssc.gov.in/).
• URL concept given by Tim Berners-Lee.
• URI is the broader term.

q: The ____ of an e-mail is a single line of text that the recipient sees when the e-mail arrives.
exp:
The subject line summarises the message and is displayed in the recipient’s inbox list.
★ Exam Points:
• Subject is part of the e-mail header.
• Re: indicates reply; Fwd: indicates forward.
• Body contains the main message.

q: Cc in an e-mail stands for ____.
exp:
Cc = Carbon Copy; recipients in Cc receive a copy and are visible to all recipients.
★ Exam Points:
• Bcc = Blind Carbon Copy.
• Term comes from carbon paper used in typewriter days.
• Cc is used to keep people informed.

q: ____ is not a search engine.
exp:
Firefox is a web browser; Google, Bing and Yandex are search engines.
★ Exam Points:
• Yandex is a Russian search engine; Baidu is Chinese.
• DuckDuckGo focuses on privacy.
• Browsers display pages; search engines index them.

q: The Bing search engine is owned by ____.
exp:
Bing was launched by Microsoft in 2009 (replacing Live Search).
★ Exam Points:
• Bing powers Microsoft Copilot web results.
• Google Search launched in 1998.
• Yahoo Search has used Bing results.

q: ____ is used to send an e-mail copy to multiple recipients where no recipient can see who else received it.
exp:
Bcc (Blind Carbon Copy) hides the recipients’ addresses from each other.
★ Exam Points:
• Cc recipients are visible to all.
• Bcc recipients do not get Reply All replies.
• Useful for mass mailing to protect privacy.

q: Which of the following is a computer that hosts a website on the Internet?
exp:
A web server stores the website files and delivers them to browsers on request using HTTP/HTTPS.
★ Exam Points:
• Popular web servers: Apache, Nginx, Microsoft IIS.
• Browser is client software.
• Hosting companies rent web-server space.

q: Choose the wrong statement about a valid e-mail address.
o: A valid e-mail address consists of an e-mail prefix and an e-mail domain.
The domain appears to the right of the @ symbol.
The domain appears to the left of the @ symbol.
An e-mail address cannot contain spaces.
exp:
The username (prefix) is on the left of @ and the domain is on the right.
★ Exam Points:
• Format: username@domain.tld.
• Only one @ is allowed.
• Allowed special characters include . _ - in the username.

q: A ____ is a regularly updated website or web page, typically run by an individual or small group, written in an informal or conversational style.
exp:
A blog (weblog) is a regularly updated site with posts shown in reverse chronological order.
★ Exam Points:
• Term "weblog" coined by Jorn Barger (1997).
• Platforms: Blogger, WordPress, Medium.
• Vlog = video blog.

q: ____ is a general (generic) domain used worldwide.
exp:
.com is a generic top-level domain (gTLD) originally meant for commercial organisations and used worldwide.
★ Exam Points:
• .in is India’s country-code TLD (ccTLD).
• .ac.in – academic institutions in India.
• Other gTLDs: .org, .net, .edu, .gov.

q: Which of the following is a valid e-mail ID?
exp:
A valid e-mail ID has exactly one @ followed by a domain with a dot, as in abc@gmail.com.
★ Exam Points:
• No spaces allowed.
• Domain must contain at least one dot.
• E-mail IDs are not case-sensitive in practice.

q: ____ is an example of a web browser.
exp:
Mozilla Firefox is a web browser; Sheets is a spreadsheet, Twitter is social media and Gmail is an e-mail service.
★ Exam Points:
• Other browsers: Chrome, Edge, Safari, Opera.
• First graphical browser: Mosaic.
• Browsers use HTTP/HTTPS to fetch pages.

q: WWW stands for ____.
exp:
WWW = World Wide Web, a system of interlinked hypertext documents accessed via the Internet.
★ Exam Points:
• Invented by Tim Berners-Lee at CERN in 1989.
• Web runs on HTTP, HTML and URLs.
• Internet ≠ Web; the Web is a service on the Internet.

q: What is the main function of a web browser in the context of the World Wide Web?
o: To display, navigate and interact with web pages stored on web servers
To act as an e-mail server
exp:
Browsers fetch and render web pages and let users follow links and fill forms.
★ Exam Points:
• Popular browsers: Chrome, Edge, Firefox, Safari.
• First browser: WorldWideWeb (1990).
• Browsers support extensions.

q: When configuring a desktop e-mail client, why must the correct SMTP server details be entered?
