o: SMTP is the protocol responsible for sending e-mail
exp:
Outgoing mail is sent through the SMTP server; wrong settings stop mail from being sent.
★ Exam Points:
• Incoming: POP3/IMAP server.
• SMTP often uses port 587 with TLS.
• Authentication is required.

q: What does a “search query” mean on the Internet?
o: Full HTML code of a page
A word or group of words typed into a search engine to find information
exp:
A search query is the text/keywords a user enters into a search engine.
★ Exam Points:
• Queries can be voice-based too.
• Operators refine queries.
• Search history stores past queries.

q: Which statement most accurately describes e-mail?
o: A method of sending and receiving electronic messages over computer networks
exp:
E-mail transmits digital messages and attachments between users across networks.
★ Exam Points:
• Uses SMTP, POP3, IMAP.
• Asynchronous communication.
• Address format user@domain.

q: What is the primary purpose of search or filter tools inside an e-mail account?
o: To quickly locate specific messages by criteria such as sender, subject or date
exp:
Search and filters find and organise mails based on criteria.
★ Exam Points:
• Gmail operators: from:, subject:, has:attachment.
• Filters can auto-label or delete.
• Saves time in large mailboxes.

q: Which option accurately defines a hyperlink on a web page?
o: An element that, when clicked, leads the user to another resource
exp:
A hyperlink connects to another page, file, section or e-mail address.
★ Exam Points:
• HTML tag: <a href="URL">.
• Usually blue and underlined.
• Ctrl + K inserts hyperlinks in Office.

q: Why is it helpful to keep e-mail messages well structured with paragraphs and clear sentences?
o: It makes the message harder to read
It helps the receiver quickly grasp the main points and reduces confusion
exp:
Clear structure improves readability and communication.
★ Exam Points:
• Use bullet points for lists.
• Keep one topic per mail.
• End with a clear action request.

q: Why might IMAP be preferable to POP for a person using the same e-mail account on multiple devices?
o: IMAP keeps messages on the server and synchronises them across devices
exp:
IMAP stores mail on the server, so read status and folders stay in sync on phone, laptop and web.
★ Exam Points:
• POP3 usually downloads and removes from server.
• IMAP uses port 143/993.
• Webmail behaves like IMAP.

q: Why should large files sometimes be shared via cloud links instead of e-mail attachments?
o: Large attachments may exceed size limits or slow delivery
Cloud links delete the e-mail body
exp:
Mail services limit attachment size (Gmail 25 MB); cloud links avoid this.
★ Exam Points:
• Google Drive/OneDrive links.
• Set link permissions carefully.
• Recipients download when needed.

q: How do search engines usually display search results?
o: A ranked list of links with titles and snippets based on relevance
exp:
Results (SERP) are ranked by relevance with titles, URLs and short descriptions.
★ Exam Points:
• Ads appear as "Sponsored".
• Featured snippets answer directly.
• Pagination shows more results.

q: Why should you review the recipient list before clicking Send?
o: To make sure the message is sent to the intended people
exp:
Checking recipients prevents sending confidential information to the wrong person.
★ Exam Points:
• Auto-complete may pick wrong contacts.
• Use Undo Send as a safety net.
• Use Bcc for large groups.

q: Why is it important to correctly set the time zone and system clock on devices used for e-mail?
o: E-mail can't be sent if clock is correct
Incorrect time can cause confusion in message timestamps and ordering
exp:
Wrong clocks show incorrect sent/received times and can mis-order messages (and break HTTPS certificates).
★ Exam Points:
• Sync time automatically (NTP).
• IST = UTC+5:30.
• Calendar invites depend on time zones.

q: In e-mail terminology, what is an “e-mail client”?
o: A program or app used to send, receive and manage e-mail
exp:
E-mail clients (MUA) include Outlook, Thunderbird, Apple Mail and mobile mail apps.
★ Exam Points:
• Webmail is accessed via browser.
• Clients use SMTP/IMAP/POP3.
• Clients can work offline.

q: In the context of the World Wide Web, what is the main function of a web browser?
o: To display, navigate and interact with web pages stored on web servers
To convert sound waves into text messages
To act as an email server for organisations
exp:
A web browser is client-side application software used to request, render, display, navigate, and interact with web pages hosted on remote web servers using protocols like HTTP/HTTPS.
★ Exam Points:
• Popular browsers: Google Chrome, Mozilla Firefox, Microsoft Edge, Apple Safari, and Opera.
• The first web browser was WorldWideWeb (later renamed Nexus), created by Tim Berners-Lee in 1990; Mosaic (1993) popularized graphical browsing.
• Shortcut keys in browsers: Ctrl + T (New Tab), Ctrl + Shift + T (Reopen closed tab), Ctrl + H (History), Ctrl + J (Downloads).

q: Which option provides the most accurate description of what a "search query" means on the internet?
o: The complete HTML code of a webpage
A small piece of hardware attached to the router
A word or group of words typed into a search engine to find information
A protocol used for sending email
exp:
A search query is the exact word, phrase, or combination of keywords that a user types into a search engine's search box to retrieve relevant web pages from its index.
★ Exam Points:
• Search operators refine queries: "exact phrase" (quotes for exact match), site:gov.in (restrict to domain), filetype:pdf (specific file format), and -word (exclude term).
• A search engine matches the query against its pre-built index (built by web crawlers) rather than scanning the entire live web from scratch.

q: On the internet, what is the full form of the abbreviation "URL"?
exp:
URL stands for Uniform Resource Locator—the standardized web address used to uniquely specify the location and retrieval protocol of a resource on the Internet.
★ Exam Points:
• Standard URL anatomy: protocol://domain_name:port/path?query#fragment (e.g., https://www.india.gov.in/index.html).
• URI (Uniform Resource Identifier) is the broader superset encompassing both URL (location) and URN (Uniform Resource Name).
• URLs were standardized by Tim Berners-Lee in 1994 (RFC 1738).

q: Which of these is a sensible search query for finding basic information about video conferencing advantages?
exp:
Typing focused keywords or enclosing the exact target phrase in quotation marks—"advantages of video conferencing"—instructs the search engine to match pages containing that exact phrase together rather than scattered words.
★ Exam Points:
• Double quotation marks "..." perform an exact-phrase search in Google, Bing, and DuckDuckGo.
• Using a minus sign (e.g., jaguar -car) excludes unwanted results; OR (in caps) searches either of two terms.

q: Which statement best explains the usual way in which search engines display search results?
o: As a random list of pages with no particular order
As a single page that never changes
As a ranked list of links, often with titles based on relevance to the query
As only one link with no details
exp:
Search engines display results on a SERP (Search Engine Results Page) as a ranked list of clickable links with page titles, URLs, and short text snippets ordered by algorithmic relevance and authority for the user's query.
★ Exam Points:
• Three stages of how a search engine works: Crawling (discovering pages via bots/spiders) → Indexing (storing & categorizing content) → Ranking / Serving (ordering SERP results).
• Examples of search engines: Google, Bing, DuckDuckGo, Yahoo! Search, and Brave Search.

q: In the context of websites and e-banking which protocol in the URL normally indicates that the connection between browser and server is securely encrypted?
exp:
In a URL, the scheme https:// (Hypertext Transfer Protocol Secure) indicates that communication between the web browser and web server is encrypted using TLS/SSL, protecting login credentials and payment details from eavesdropping.
★ Exam Points:
• Feature | HTTP | HTTPS
• Port | Port 80 | Port 443
• Security | Plain-text (unencrypted) | Encrypted using SSL / TLS
• Use Case | Basic informational pages | Banking, logins, payments, modern web
• Modern browsers display a padlock/tune security indicator in the address bar for valid HTTPS certificates.

q: Which explanation most accurately describes why an email signature is used at the end of a message?
o: It stores the password of the user at the bottom of each email
It is a predefined block of text automatically appended to messages
It removes previous message content from a reply
It encrypts the entire email content
exp:
An email signature is a predefined block of text (typically containing the sender's name, designation, organisation, and contact details) that an email client automatically appends to the bottom of outgoing messages.
★ Exam Points:
• An email signature provides professional identity and saves repetitive typing—it is not a cryptographic Digital Signature (which verifies authenticity using public-key cryptography).
• Email signatures can be configured separately for new messages and replies/forwards in Gmail and Outlook.
• Keep signatures concise (3–4 lines) without sensitive credentials.

q: In digital communication, which statement most accurately describes what email is or how it functions?
o: A system for sending handwritten letters through post offices
A method of sending and receiving electronic messages over computer networks
A device used only for voice calls over telephone lines
A technique for printing documents from a computer
exp:
Email (Electronic Mail) is an asynchronous digital communication service used for composing, sending, storing, and receiving electronic messages and attachments across computer networks such as the Internet.
★ Exam Points:
• Ray Tomlinson sent the first network email on ARPANET in 1971 and introduced the @ symbol separating username@domain.
• Shiva Ayyadurai developed an inter-office electronic mail program named 'EMAIL' in 1978.
• Email operates on a store-and-forward model—the recipient does not need to be online simultaneously when the mail is sent.

q: In the context of email management, what is the primary purpose of using search or filter tools inside an email account?
o: To change the email address of the sender
To quickly locate specific messages based on criteria such as sender, subject
To permanently delete all messages at once
To reduce the capacity of the mailbox
exp:
Email search and filter tools allow users to instantly locate specific emails in large mailboxes using criteria such as sender (from:), recipient (to:), subject keywords, date range, or presence of attachments (has:attachment).
★ Exam Points:
• Automated Filters / Rules can also label, star, forward, or move incoming messages into folders automatically as they arrive.
• Archiving old mail + using search is safer than bulk deletion because important records remain retrievable.

q: Why might using IMAP be preferable to POP for a person who accesses the same email account on multiple devices?
o: Because IMAP deletes all messages automatically after reading
Because IMAP keeps messages on the server
Because IMAP works only without internet
Because IMAP can never mark messages
exp:
IMAP (Internet Message Access Protocol) stores and manages emails directly on the mail server and synchronizes read/unread flags, folders, and sent items in real time across smartphones, laptops, and tablets.
★ Exam Points:
• Protocol | Default Port (Plain / SSL) | Role
• SMTP | 25 / 587 (465 SSL) | Sending / pushing outgoing emails
• POP3 | 110 / 995 | Downloads mail locally (single-device style)
• IMAP | 143 / 993 | Syncs mail on server across multiple devices
• By contrast, traditional POP3 downloads mail to a single local device and often removes it from the server, making multi-device sync inconvenient.

q: Which step is normally required before sending or receiving emails through a web-based email service?
o: Logging into the account with a valid username and password
exp:
Before composing, sending, or reading messages in a webmail service (such as Gmail, Outlook.com, or Yahoo Mail), a user must first authenticate by logging into the email account with a valid username/email ID and password (plus 2FA if enabled).
★ Exam Points:
• Authentication verifies identity ('who you are' via user-name + password/OTP); Authorization determines permissions ('what you can access').
• Enabling Two-Factor Authentication (2FA) adds a second security layer beyond the password.

q: In email terminology, what does the term "email client" refer to or describe?
o: A server that routes messages across the internet
A program or app used by a person to send, receive and manage email
A hardware device that connects network cables
A protocol used to encrypt messages
exp:
An email client (Mail User Agent / MUA) is a software program or mobile/web application used by an end user to compose, send, receive, read, and organize emails.
★ Exam Points:
• Desktop email clients: Microsoft Outlook, Mozilla Thunderbird, and Apple Mail.
• Webmail clients (accessed inside a browser): Gmail, Outlook on the web, Proton Mail, and Yahoo Mail.

q: In email applications, what function does the Outbox folder mainly serve?
o: To store messages after they are successfully delivered
To temporarily hold messages that are waiting to be sent
exp:
In email applications, the Outbox folder acts as a temporary outgoing queue that holds messages waiting to be transmitted (for example, while offline, while uploading a large attachment, or during a server connection delay). Once successfully sent, the message moves automatically from Outbox to Sent.
★ Exam Points:
• Email Folder | Purpose
• Inbox | Stores received incoming messages
• Drafts | Stores unfinished, unsent messages saved for editing later
• Outbox | Temporarily holds outgoing messages waiting to be transmitted
• Sent | Stores copies of messages already successfully delivered to the mail server

q:
Identify whether the following statements are true or false.
(i) A CGI script is a specification for transferring information between a web server and a CGI program.
(ii) HTTP is one of the Internet programming languages.
(iii) Web Bot refers to programs used on the Internet that perform repetitive functions such as posting messages or searching.
exp:
HTTP is a protocol (HyperText Transfer Protocol), not a programming language; the other two statements are correct.
★ Exam Points:
• CGI – Common Gateway Interface.
• Web crawlers/spiders are bots used by search engines.
• HTML is a markup language, not a programming language.

q:
Identify whether the following statements are true or false.
(i) Microsoft Outlook is an e-mail application software.
(ii) Junk mail is unsolicited mail consisting mainly of promotional material and requests.
(iii) The e-mail header contains From, Date, To and Subject.
exp:
All three statements are correct.
★ Exam Points:
• Unsolicited bulk e-mail is called spam.
• E-mail header also has Cc, Bcc, Reply-To fields.
• Body and attachments come after the header.

q:
Which option best describes the truthfulness of the statements?
(i) RSS is a process that makes content on one website available to another website.
(ii) Cookies are information created by a web server and stored on a user's computer.
(iii) A web server is a type of database management system (DBMS).
exp:
A web server stores and delivers web pages over HTTP; it is not a DBMS, so (iii) is false.
★ Exam Points:
• RSS – Really Simple Syndication (web feeds).
• Cookies are small text files.
• Examples of web servers: Apache, Nginx, IIS.

q:
Which option best describes the truthfulness of the statements?
(i) Microsoft Outlook is an e-mail application.
(ii) E-mail clients use POP/IMAP to retrieve/sync e-mails from the server.
(iii) Microsoft Exchange Server is a mail and calendaring server developed by Microsoft.
exp:
All three statements are correct.
★ Exam Points:
• POP3 downloads mail; IMAP keeps mail synced on the server.
• SMTP is used to send mail.
• Exchange Server runs on Windows Server.

q:
Match the components of a mail system with their descriptions.
(a) Mail User Agent (b) Mail Submission Agent (c) Mail Delivery Agent (d) Mail Transfer Agent
(i) Backbone of the e-mail system; uses SMTP (ii) Software used to compose and read e-mails (iii) Takes e-mails from the user agent and delivers them to a mail transfer agent (iv) Takes e-mails from a mail transfer agent and delivers them to the recipient’s mailbox
exp:
MUA = client (Outlook, Gmail app); MSA accepts mail from the client; MTA relays it using SMTP; MDA stores it in the recipient's mailbox.
★ Exam Points:
• MUA examples: Outlook, Thunderbird.
• MTA examples: Sendmail, Postfix, Exim.
• POP3/IMAP are used by MUA to fetch mail.

q: Which of the following statements related to the World Wide Web is FALSE?
o: The process of storing a webpage on a web server is called ‘uploading’.
Web servers are host computers that store thousands of webpages.
The last webpage of a website is called the ‘homepage’.
The process of retrieving a webpage from a web server to the user's computer is called ‘downloading’.
exp:
The homepage is the first (main/index) page of a website, not the last.
★ Exam Points:
• WWW invented by Tim Berners-Lee at CERN (1989).
• Homepage file is commonly index.html.
• A website is a collection of related web pages.

q: The Firefox web browser was developed by which organisation?
exp:
Firefox is an open-source browser developed by the Mozilla Foundation/Corporation, released in 2004.
★ Exam Points:
• Firefox uses the Gecko rendering engine.
• Thunderbird is Mozilla’s e-mail client.
• Mozilla was founded by Netscape in 1998.

q: The first part of an e-mail address is the ____.
exp:
An e-mail address has the form username@domain; the part before @ is the username (local part).
★ Exam Points:
• The part after @ is the domain name.
• @ was first used in e-mail by Ray Tomlinson (1971).
• E-mail addresses cannot contain spaces.

q: When an e-mail is sent, it goes to the ____ belonging to the company that issued the e-mail address.
exp:
Outgoing mail is sent via SMTP to the recipient’s mail server, where it waits until the recipient retrieves it.
★ Exam Points:
• SMTP sends mail; POP3/IMAP retrieve mail.
• Mail server = MTA (Mail Transfer Agent).
• E-mail client = MUA (Mail User Agent).

q: You can choose to create a/an ____ that will appear at the end of every e-mail you send.
exp:
An e-mail signature is a block of text (name, designation, contact) added automatically at the end of outgoing messages.
★ Exam Points:
• Gmail signature: Settings → General → Signature.
• Attachments are files sent with an e-mail (Gmail limit 25 MB).
• Vacation responder sends auto-replies.

q: Which of the following is an example of an e-mail address?
exp:
An e-mail address has the format username@domainname; only kidsmart@billme.com follows it.
★ Exam Points:
• Option C is a URL; option A is a file path.
• @ is read as "at".
• Domain part may be .com, .in, .gov.in, etc.

q: A busy e-commerce website crashes after being overwhelmed by thousands of fake traffic requests at the same time. Which cyberattack is most likely?
exp:
DDoS floods a server with traffic from many sources (often a botnet), making it unavailable.
★ Exam Points:
• DoS uses a single source.
• CDNs and firewalls help mitigate DDoS.
• Mirai botnet caused major DDoS in 2016.

q: The ____ method is commonly used to verify the integrity of data.
exp:
Hashing creates a fixed-size digest (e.g., SHA-256); any change in data changes the hash, revealing tampering.
★ Exam Points:
• MD5 and SHA are hashing algorithms.
• Checksums are simple integrity checks.
• Digital signatures use hashing.

q: What is a common sign that a computer might be infected with a virus?
o: Unusual system slowdowns and unexpected errors
exp:
Malware often causes slowness, crashes, pop-ups, unexplained errors or missing files.
★ Exam Points:
• Other signs: high network usage, new toolbars, disabled antivirus.
• Run a full antivirus scan.
• Keep OS and software updated.

q: What is the purpose of enabling passwords on a PC?
o: To provide an additional layer of security
exp:
Passwords prevent unauthorised users from accessing the computer and its data.
★ Exam Points:
• Use strong passwords (12+ characters, mixed).
• Windows Hello offers PIN/biometric login.
• Lock PC quickly: Windows + L.

q: Which type of virus infects the boot sector of floppy disks or the Master Boot Record (MBR) of hard disks?
exp:
Boot sector viruses load during start-up because they reside in the boot sector/MBR.
★ Exam Points:
• Brain (1986) was a boot sector virus.
• Macro viruses infect Office documents.
• Secure Boot (UEFI) helps prevent boot infections.

q: Which method is used to protect sensitive information during data transmission?
exp:
SSL/TLS encrypts data between the browser and server so it cannot be read if intercepted.
★ Exam Points:
• TLS is the modern successor of SSL.
• HTTPS = HTTP over TLS.
• Hashing checks integrity, not confidentiality.

q: Which security mechanism ensures that system updates are installed without user intervention?
exp:
Patch management software automatically downloads and installs updates/patches across systems.
★ Exam Points:
• Windows Update installs patches automatically.
• IDS detects suspicious activity.
• Firewall filters network traffic.

q: ____ records everything you type on your PC in order to obtain your log-in name, passwords and other sensitive information.
exp:
Keyloggers capture keystrokes and send them to attackers to steal credentials.
★ Exam Points:
• Keyloggers can be software or hardware.
• Use a virtual keyboard for banking passwords.
• 2FA reduces damage from stolen passwords.

q: CryptoLocker is a form of which of the following?
exp:
CryptoLocker (2013) encrypted victims’ files and demanded ransom in Bitcoin – a classic ransomware.
★ Exam Points:
• WannaCry (2017) was a ransomware worm.
• Keep offline backups to protect against ransomware.
• Petya and Locky are also ransomware.

q: A ____ can be either software (malware) or hardware. Its main purpose is to record the keys pressed by a user on the keyboard.
exp:
A keylogger records keystrokes to steal passwords and other data; it may be a program or a small hardware device placed between keyboard and PC.
★ Exam Points:
• On-screen/virtual keyboards help protect against keyloggers.
• Spyware secretly collects user information.
• Worms replicate across networks by themselves.

q: A ____ is a contagious program or code that attaches itself to another piece of software and reproduces itself when that software is run.
exp:
A computer virus needs a host program; it activates and copies itself when the infected program is executed.
★ Exam Points:
• Term "computer virus" popularised by Fred Cohen (1983).
• First PC virus: Brain (1986), created in Pakistan.
• Worms do not need a host file.

q: ____ viruses are embedded in a system's memory so they can be reactivated even if the original virus is deleted.
exp:
A resident virus installs itself in RAM and keeps infecting files that are opened, even after the original carrier file is removed.
★ Exam Points:
• Non-resident (direct action) virus works only when the infected file runs.
• Polymorphic virus changes its code to avoid detection.
• Boot sector virus infects the MBR.

q: ____ is a type of malware that is often disguised as legitimate software.
exp:
A Trojan horse pretends to be a useful program; once the user runs it, it performs hidden malicious actions such as opening a backdoor.
★ Exam Points:
• Trojans do not self-replicate, unlike viruses and worms.
• Ransomware encrypts files and demands payment.
• Rootkit hides itself and gives an attacker admin-level control.

q: Which among the following statements about Trojans is incorrect?
o: Trojan spreads through user interaction such as opening an e-mail attachment or downloading a file from the Internet.
Some Trojans create backdoors to give malicious users access to the system.
Trojan self-replicates and infects other files.
exp:
Trojans do not replicate themselves or infect other files; self-replication is the property of viruses and worms.
★ Exam Points:
• Trojan name comes from the Greek story of the wooden horse of Troy.
• Remote Access Trojan (RAT) gives remote control of a PC.
• Worms spread automatically across networks without user action.

q: In network and information security, what is the primary purpose of a Trojan Horse?
o: Intercepting network traffic by flooding communication channels
Stealing or deleting files and creating a backdoor for hackers
Quietly copying itself across systems using network vulnerabilities
Blocking network traffic by overloading servers
exp:
A Trojan Horse is malicious software disguised as legitimate, useful software. Once executed by the user, it secretly steals or deletes files and opens a backdoor for remote unauthorized access without self-replicating.
★ Exam Points:
• Malware Type | Defining Behaviour
• Virus | Attaches to host files; spreads when host program runs
• Worm | Self-replicates automatically across networks without a host file
• Trojan Horse | Disguised as legitimate app; does NOT self-replicate; creates backdoor
• Ransomware | Encrypts victim's files and de-mands ransom for decryption key

q: Which of the following is a limitation of securing communication using Symmetric Encryption?
o: Requires more computational resources compared to asymmetric encryption
Difficulty in key distribution and management
The encryption and decryption process is extremely slow
exp:
In Symmetric Encryption (secret-key cryptography), the exact same secret key is used for both encryption and decryption. Its biggest limitation is secure key distribution and key management—sharing the secret key over an insecure channel exposes it, and n users requireⁿ⁽ⁿ−¹⁾ unique pair- 2 wise keys.
★ Exam Points:
• Feature | Symmetric Encryption | Asymmetric Encryption
• Keys Used | Single shared secret key | Public key (encrypt) + Private key (decrypt)
• Speed | Very fast (ideal for bulk data) | Slower (higher computation)
• Examples | AES, DES, 3DES, Blowfish | RSA, ECC, Diffie- Hellman

q: What is the primary benefit of enabling encryption for data in transit across a network?
o: It protects against physical theft of devices
It improves overall data transfer speed
It prevents unauthorized users from accessing the network
It makes data unreadable to attackers during transmission
exp:
Enabling encryption for data in transit (using protocols like TLS/SSL, HTTPS, or IPsec) converts plaintext traffic into ciphertext so that even if attackers intercept packets on the network (eavesdropping / Man-in-the-Middle), the data remains unreadable without the decryption key.
★ Exam Points:
• Data in transit refers to data actively moving across a network; Data at rest refers to data stored on disks/databases (protected via BitLocker, AES disk encryption).
• Encryption ensures Confidentiality, while cryptographic hashes/MACs ensure Integrity.
• TLS (Transport Layer Security) is the modern successor to SSL and secures HTTPS on Port 443.

q: Which of the following is a secure method to encrypt emails, protecting email contents from unauthorized access?
exp:
S/MIME (Secure/Multipurpose Internet Mail Extensions) is a cryptographic standard that provides end-to-end public-key encryption and digital signatures for email message contents and attachments, protecting them from unauthorized reading or tampering.
★ Exam Points:
• PGP (Pretty Good Privacy) / OpenPGP (created by Phil Zimmermann) is the other widely used standard for end-to-end email encryption.
• SMTP and IMAP are mail transfer/access protocols (not content encryption standards), while SSL/TLS encrypts only the transport hop between client and mail server rather than the stored email itself.

q: What is bot malware primarily used for by cybercriminals?
o: To take control of a device remotely and secretly use it for malicious purposes
To report browsing to a government agency
exp:
Bots turn infected computers into "zombies" in a botnet used for spam, DDoS attacks and fraud.
★ Exam Points:
• Botnet is controlled by a C&C server.
• Mirai botnet used IoT devices.
• Ransomware encrypts files.

q:
Which recipient actions do e-mails containing malware typically rely on to infect a computer?
(i) Clicking Reply (ii) Forwarding the mail to five contacts (iii) Clicking a malicious link (iv) Downloading and opening an infected attachment
exp:
Malware usually activates when the user clicks a malicious link or opens an infected attachment.
★ Exam Points:
• Avoid .exe, .js, macro-enabled attachments.
• Scan attachments with antivirus.
• Hover to check links before clicking.

q: Which technology is commonly used to secure online banking transactions?
exp:
OTPs sent to registered mobiles authorise transactions as a second factor.
★ Exam Points:
• OTP is valid for a short time.
• 3-D Secure uses OTP for cards.
• Never share OTP with anyone.

q: What is the main purpose of e-mail spoofing in phishing attacks?
o: To make the e-mail appear to come from a trusted source
exp:
Spoofing forges the sender address so the mail looks like it is from a bank or known contact.
★ Exam Points:
• SPF, DKIM and DMARC help prevent spoofing.
• Check the actual sender domain.
• Spoofing is also done with caller ID and websites.

q: Which is a typical characteristic of phishing e-mails?
o: They impersonate reputable organisations and create a false sense of urgency/panic
They always have perfect spelling and personalised greetings
exp:
Phishing mails pose as banks or companies and pressure victims with urgency ("account blocked").
★ Exam Points:
• Generic greetings and spelling errors are red flags.
• Hover over links to see the real URL.
• Never share OTP or PIN.

q: Which statement best describes a critical difference between HTTP and HTTPS?
o: HTTPS uses an additional security layer (SSL/TLS) to encrypt data, while HTTP transmits plain text
HTTP sends data, HTTPS receives data
exp:
HTTPS adds TLS encryption, protecting data integrity and privacy; HTTP is unencrypted.
★ Exam Points:
• HTTPS port 443; HTTP port 80.
• Browsers mark HTTP sites "Not secure".
• Let's Encrypt provides free certificates.

q: Which best explains why HTTPS is preferred over HTTP for e-banking?
o: It encrypts communication between client and server
exp:
HTTPS encrypts data using TLS, protecting passwords and transactions from eavesdropping.
★ Exam Points:
• Look for the padlock symbol.
• Certificates verify the website identity.
• HTTP sends data in plain text.

q: What is the primary function of a CAPTCHA?
o: To verify that the user is human
exp:
CAPTCHA presents tests easy for humans but hard for bots, preventing automated abuse.
★ Exam Points:
• CAPTCHA = Completely Automated Public Turing test to tell Computers and Humans Apart.
• reCAPTCHA is Google’s version.
• Used on login and sign-up forms.

q: The ‘S’ in HTTPS signifies the use of which technology to encrypt data?
exp:
HTTPS is HTTP secured with TLS (formerly SSL) encryption.
★ Exam Points:
• TLS 1.3 is the latest version.
• Certificates are issued by Certificate Authorities.
• Port 443.

q: In e-banking, which security measure verifies a transaction by sending a temporary code to your registered mobile number?
exp:
An OTP (One-Time Password) is valid for a single transaction/session, adding a second factor.
★ Exam Points:
• OTP is part of two-factor authentication.
• Never share OTP with anyone.
• TOTP apps generate time-based codes.

q: In e-banking security, what is phishing and how does it relate to URL basics?
o: Phishing is a fake-site scam; checking the URL helps identify fraud
Phishing is URL encryption for secure banking
Phishing is an ad technique based on URL structure
Phishing is a fast browsing method
exp:
Phishing tricks users into fake websites/e-mails to steal credentials; checking the exact domain and https helps detect it.
★ Exam Points:
• Look-alike domains (sbi-online.co) are common.
• Report phishing to cybercrime.gov.in / 1930.
• Banks never ask for OTP/PIN by e-mail.

q: In e-banking, the use of single-use verification codes is associated with which security mechanism?
exp:
One-time codes (OTP) act as a second factor in two-factor authentication.
★ Exam Points:
• Factors: something you know, have, are.
• Authenticator apps generate TOTP codes.
• SSO uses one login for many apps.

q: What is the primary goal of a phishing e-mail?
o: To trick the recipient into revealing sensitive personal and financial information
exp:
Phishing mails pretend to be trusted entities to steal passwords, card numbers, OTPs, etc.
★ Exam Points:
• Check sender domain and links carefully.
• Spear phishing targets specific people.
• Report at cybercrime.gov.in.

q: What of the given options is a typical characteristic of Phishing emails?
o: They provide legitimate phone numbers of customer service agents.
They use neutral, calm language to explain a complex system upgrade.
They impersonate reputable organisations and create a false sense of panic.
They always use highly personalised greetings and accurate spelling and grammar.
exp:
A classic hallmark of Phishing emails is social engineering through urgency and fear: they spoof/impersonate reputable banks, tax authorities, or tech companies and man-ufacture a false sense of panic (e.g., 'Your bank account will be suspended within 24 hours—click here to verify KYC!') so victims act impulsively without checking the fake URL.
★ Exam Points:
• Phishing emails frequently contain generic greetings ('Dear Valued Customer'), look-alike sender domains, and deceptive links.

q: Which of the following recipient actions do emails containing malware or viruses typically rely on to infect a computer? (i) The recipient clicks the "Reply" button to respond (ii) The recipient manually forwarding the email to five or more contacts (iii) The recipient clicks on a malicious link (iv) The recipient downloads and opens an infected attachment
exp:
Analyzing how email-borne malware/viruses infect a victim's system: • Simply clicking Reply (i) or forwarding text (ii) does not execute malicious payloads. • Malware relies on user execution via (iii) clicking a malicious URL link (leading to drive-by downloads/exploit kits) or (iv) downloading and opening an infected attachment (like a trojanized .exe, .zip, or macro-enabled .docm/.xlsm). Hence, Only (iii) and (iv) trigger infection.
★ Exam Points:
• Dangerous attachment extensions to watch out for in unknown emails: .exe, .bat, .scr, .vbs, .js, .docm, and .xlsm.

q: Why is it important to verify the correctness of a URL before entering confidential data on a website?
o: An incorrect URL may lead to a fraudulent site designed to steal information
exp:
Phishing sites use look-alike URLs to steal credentials.
★ Exam Points:
• Check spelling and https.
• Avoid clicking links in suspicious mails.
• Type bank URL directly.

q: Why is it unsafe to send confidential information through normal, unencrypted e-mail?
o: Plain e-mail is stored only locally
Plain e-mail can be intercepted by unauthorised parties
Plain e-mail cannot include a subject
exp:
Unencrypted mail can be read if intercepted or if servers are compromised.
★ Exam Points:
• Use encrypted mail (S/MIME, PGP).
• Share passwords separately.
• Password-protect attachments.

q: Which URL is correctly written to open a secure banking site (sample domain banksite.com)?
exp:
Secure sites use the https:// scheme (with colon and two slashes).
★ Exam Points:
• Padlock confirms encryption.
• Typos in domain may lead to fake sites.
• Bookmark your bank's real URL.

q: What is an important reason to avoid e-banking transactions over an unknown, unsecured Wi-Fi network?
o: Attackers may intercept data on unsecured Wi-Fi
It cannot connect to any site
exp:
On open Wi-Fi, attackers can perform man-in-the-middle attacks and sniff data.
★ Exam Points:
• Use mobile data or VPN for banking.
• Avoid "free Wi-Fi" for payments.
• Check https and padlock.

q: ____ can easily spread to computers connected to the Internet; such attacks may cause your system to crash or your important data may get deleted.
exp:
Viruses and other malware spread through downloads, attachments and networks, damaging data and systems.
★ Exam Points:
• Install antivirus and keep it updated.
• Do not open unknown attachments.
• Regular backups protect data.

q:
Secure communication is required when two parties communicate over the Internet and do not want a third party to intercept. Which is a property of secure communication?
P: Confidentiality
Q: Accuracy
exp:
Confidentiality (only intended parties can read the message) is a core property; "accuracy" is not a defined security property – integrity is.
★ Exam Points:
• CIA triad: Confidentiality, Integrity, Availability.
• Encryption provides confidentiality.
• Authentication and non-repudiation are other properties.

q: A ____ is a type of malicious software that spreads between computers and causes damage to data and software.
exp:
A virus attaches to files/programs and spreads when they are shared, corrupting data and software.
★ Exam Points:
• Viruses need user action to spread.
• Antivirus software detects and removes them.
• Examples: Melissa, ILOVEYOU (worm).

q: Which of the following actions helps maintain the security of an email account on a shared computer?
o: Selecting "Remember me" on the login screen
Staying logged in even when away from the computer
Logging out of the email account and closing the browser after use
Writing the password on a note near the computer
exp:
Logging out terminates the active session tokens of an email account, preventing subsequent unauthorized users of a shared or public computer from accessing your personal messages and private data.
★ Exam Points:
• Closing the browser window without logging out may leave active authentication cookies stored in cache.
• Avoid enabling "Remember me" or saving passwords on public or shared terminals.
• Incognito / Private Browsing mode prevents local saving of history, cookies, and temporary credentials.
• Enable Two-Factor Authentication (2FA) for an enhanced layer of user account security.

q: Why is it unsafe to allow browsers to auto-fill e-banking passwords on shared or public devices?
o: Other users of the same device may gain access to the stored credentials
exp:
Saved passwords can be used by anyone using that browser profile.
★ Exam Points:
• Use private/incognito mode on shared PCs.
• Log out after use.
• Use a password manager with master password.

q: Why is verifying the correct domain name more important than checking the design of a banking website?
o: Attackers can easily copy the visual design of a real site
exp:
Phishing sites copy logos and layouts, but cannot use the bank's real domain.
★ Exam Points:
• Check spelling: sbi.co.in vs sbi-co.in.
• Look for https and valid certificate.
• Bookmark official sites.

q: A backup method copies only files changed since the last backup, saving storage but requiring multiple sets for restoration. What is this method?
exp:
Incremental backup saves changes since the last backup of any type; restoring needs the full backup plus every incremental.
★ Exam Points:
• Differential saves changes since the last full backup.
• Full backup copies everything.
• Snapshots capture system state at a point in time.

q: Why should browser extensions or add-ons be installed cautiously, especially in the context of web browsing and ebanking?
o: Because all extensions are harmless and cannot access data
Because extensions have no effect on browsing
Because some extensions may read web content, capture data or slow down the browser
Because extensions always block viruses automatically
exp:
Browser extensions often request broad permissions (such as 'read and change all your data on all websites'). Malicious or poorly coded extensions can read webpage content, capture banking keystrokes/passwords, inject ads, or degrade browser performance.
★ Exam Points:
• Install extensions only from official stores after verifying the developer, permissions requested, and user reviews.
• Most browsers disable extensions by default inside Incognito / Private Browsing windows for extra safety during e-banking.
• Periodically review and remove unused extensions via the browser's Extensions / Add-ons manager.

q: Why is it generally unsafe to allow browsers to auto-fill sensitive fields such as e-banking passwords on shared or public devices?
o: Because auto-fill never works on any browser
Because passwords become invalid if filled automatically
Because other users on the same device may gain access to the stored credentials
Because auto-fill increases internet data usage significantly
exp:
On public or shared computers (cyber cafés, libraries, labs), saving or auto-filling passwords in the browser allows sub-sequent users of the same machine to access stored credentials or log directly into sensitive e-banking accounts.
★ Exam Points:
• Safe practices on shared PCs: use Incognito / Private Browsing, decline 'Save Password' prompts, avoid 'Remember Me', and always Log Out completely.
• Shortcut to open Incognito / InPrivate window: Ctrl + Shift + N (Chrome/Edge) or Ctrl + Shift + P (Firefox).

q: A ____ hides your IP address by letting the network redirect it through a specially configured remote server.
exp:
A Virtual Private Network creates an encrypted tunnel and routes traffic through a VPN server, so websites see the server’s IP address instead of yours.
★ Exam Points:
• VPN = Virtual Private Network.
• Useful on public Wi-Fi.
• Proxy servers also mask IP but usually without encryption.

q: What is the binary equivalent of decimal 25?
exp:
25 = 16+8+1 → 11001.
★ Exam Points:
• Divide repeatedly by 2, read remainders bottom to top.

q: The base of the hexadecimal number system is:
exp:
Hexadecimal uses 16 symbols: 0–9 and A–F.
★ Exam Points:
• Binary 2, Octal 8, Decimal 10, Hex 16.

q: Which pair of logic gates is called universal gates?
exp:
Any circuit can be built using only NAND or only NOR.
★ Exam Points:
• NAND = NOT of AND; NOR = NOT of OR.

q: Standard ASCII uses how many bits per character?
exp:
Standard ASCII is a 7-bit code (128 characters); extended ASCII uses 8 bits.
★ Exam Points:
• Unicode supports characters of all languages.

q: The output of an XOR gate is 1 when:
exp: XOR gives 1 only when the two inputs differ.

q: The decimal value of octal number 17 is:
What do you mean by SQL?
exp:
SQL stands for Structured Query Language—the standard domain-specific language used to create, query, update, and manage Relational Database Management Systems (RDBMS) such as MySQL, PostgreSQL, Oracle, and MS SQL Server.
★ Exam Points:
• SQL was originally developed at IBM in the early 1970s by Donald D. Chamberlin and Raymond F. Boyce (initially called SEQUEL).

q: A primary key in a table:
exp: A primary key uniquely identifies each row and cannot be NULL.

q: SQL stands for:
exp: SQL = Structured Query Language, used to manage relational databases.

q: Which of the following is a DDL command?
exp:
DDL (Data Definition Language): CREATE, ALTER, DROP.
★ Exam Points:
• SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE are DML.

q: A row in a database table is also called a:
exp: Row = record = tuple; column = field = attribute.

q: A foreign key is used to:
exp: A foreign key refers to the primary key of another table, creating a relationship.

q: Which of the following is NOT a DBMS?
exp: Linux is an operating system; the others are database software.

q: The term "Artificial Intelligence" was coined by:
exp: John McCarthy coined "AI" in 1956 (Dartmouth Conference).

q: Which of the following is an example of SaaS?
exp: SaaS gives ready-to-use software online (Gmail, Zoho). EC2/VM = IaaS; App Engine = PaaS.
topic: Emerging Tech: AI, Cloud, IoT & Blockchain

q: IoT stands for:
exp: Internet of Things – everyday devices connected to the internet.
topic: Emerging Tech: AI, Cloud, IoT & Blockchain

q: Blockchain is the underlying technology of:
exp: Blockchain is a distributed ledger that powers cryptocurrencies like Bitcoin.
topic: Emerging Tech: AI, Cloud, IoT & Blockchain

q: ChatGPT is an example of:
exp: ChatGPT is a generative-AI chatbot built on a large language model.
topic: Emerging Tech: AI, Cloud, IoT & Blockchain

q: Machine Learning is a subset of:
exp: AI ⊃ Machine Learning ⊃ Deep Learning.
topic: Emerging Tech: AI, Cloud, IoT & Blockchain

q: Multimedia combines which of the following?
exp: Multimedia integrates text, audio, images, animation and video.

q: Which of the following is a raster (bitmap) image format?
exp: JPEG, PNG, GIF, BMP are raster; SVG, AI, EPS are vector.

q: UPI stands for:
exp: UPI is NPCI's real-time mobile payment system.

q: The Digital India programme was launched in:
exp: Digital India was launched on 1 July 2015.

q: DigiLocker is used for:
exp: DigiLocker stores and shares government-issued documents digitally.

q: Which of the following is a video file format?
exp: MP4 is a video format; MP3 and WAV are audio; PNG is an image.
